## 2026-08-12 — **`DO10-4`: the star capstone — CLOSED** (a correctness fix; web + email + a coverage sweep)

A star row can state the **wrong rating** two ways, and the product had shipped both. This retires the O26
defect family. Full record: **§STAR-CAPSTONE** in `docs/design/MISSING-BACKEND-BY-PAGE.md`.

**The web remnant.** `owner/unit-detail:338` used `str_repeat('★', round($average))`. Rendered live **as the
owner** (DO-EMAIL-2's lesson: run as the role that can see the page) with a real unit **forced to a 4.67
average** (G10), the old code prints **five filled stars**. It now renders through `<x-star-rating>`: **four
filled + one empty**, named *"4.7 out of 5 stars"*. ⚠️ **That changes what the owner sees, and that is the
point** — the unit stops advertising itself as perfect. An honest rating, not a regression. The forced data
was restored immediately.
⚠️ **Premise correction:** the register called that line colour-only *and* round. It was **not** colour-only —
it already emitted `★` then `☆`. The defect was `round()` alone, plus a missing accessible name.

⚠️ **The sweep found a third defect nobody had named: the shared component's OWN defaults failed 3:1.**
`#E8A63A` measured **2.08** and `#B9A99A` **2.25** — *the component everything was being migrated TO drew a
star you could barely see.* That answers **`DO-G8-2`**, which had sat as "never measured".

⚠️ **And the measurement corrected me mid-pass.** The first retarget was chosen against the two card plates;
the live render then showed the row sits on the **peach hero plate `#FBD3BF`**, where the empty star still
failed at 2.76. Re-chosen against the **worst real plate**: filled `#8F5A06` (4.19 / 5.28 / 5.70), empty
`#7A6E64` (3.59 / 4.52 / 4.88), filled always stronger than empty, hues preserved so greyscale is unaffected.

⚠️ **The email star was not what the register said it was.** `DO-EMAIL-1` routed `#E8A317` here as "a
colour-only rating signal". `review-request` does not display a rating — it renders **five tappable rating
INPUTS**, each deep-linking the review page with that rating pre-selected. **★/☆ would have been wrong**: it
would show a rating the guest has not given. The real defects were (a) contrast — 2.14, and a meaningful
non-text **control** needs 3:1 → the same `#8F5A06` (4.17); and (b) **the accessible name** — each link was
named by its bare glyph "★", so a screen reader heard *"star, link"* five times with nothing to choose
between. Each now names its rating, verified on the real mailable. **The email set is 335 runs / 0 FAIL** —
the ★ was the last failing run in it.

⚠️ **The coverage sweep earned its place** (the DO-EMAIL-2 pattern — the adjacent thing nobody named): four
further sites. `operator/guest-profile:132` at **1.98** and unnamed — an operator page no star pass had ever
rendered. `owner/reviews:123` at **1.93 / 1.48**, unnamed. Two rows whose colours already passed (3.04, 6.49)
— **not "fixed"**, only named, because the measurement decides. And `NewReviewNotification` built the filled
half only, printing *"New review · ★★★"* — ambiguous between 3/5 and 3/3 — while its sibling
`LowRatingNotification` already built both; matched to the sibling. One site, `operator/reviews:70`, was a
**false flag by my own probe**: its stars are correctly `aria-hidden` beside a visible `4/5`.

⚠️ **The guard was vacuous at first (O32).** Reverting the component's filled colour left the contrast test
**green**, because it asserted hardcoded literals — arithmetic, not the component. Rewritten to read the inks
the component **actually renders**; the mutation then went red naming the value and the plate.
`StarRatingCorrectnessTest` (6 tests / 35 assertions) is **mutation-proven five ways**: `floor`→`round`,
`☆`→`★`, drop the name, revert each colour. `php -l` **and `php artisan view:clear`** after every Blade
mutation (DO-EMAIL-3's toolchain false-RED).

**Left deliberately:** `DO-STAR-1` — the owner Messages *"Starred"* flag SVGs still use `#E8A63A`; that is a
bookmark toggle, not a rating, and its state is also carried by a visible count. `DO-EMAIL-4` (the
twice-defined `--vy-amber-text`) flagged again, not fixed.

`OwnerUnitDetailViewTest` remains non-green for its documented reason — a seeding `UnitUnavailableException`
(date-coupled), **unrelated to the star**; its other 12 tests pass. Suite **1907 / 12,448**, 9 non-green = the
documented baseline set. PHPStan L5 (0); Pint clean.

## 2026-08-12 — **SAVE v9: the CLEANUP CHAPTER is closed** (a memory-consolidation pass — docs only)

Five passes ran after the design-parity walk closed at SAVE v8 (`e869d5d`): **`DO-INV-4`** (`e994dc6`) →
**`DO-EMAIL-1`** (`b940cda`) → **`DO-EMAIL-2`** (`d517187`) → **`DO-EMAIL-3`** (`ac502bf`) → **`DO10-4`**
(`ee6be74`). Each wrote its own §-record and dated entry; this SAVE adds only what emerged **across** them, plus
the register and RESUME reconciliation. **No product code, template or test was touched.**

**The canon is `PROJECT-STATE.md` §N.14**, nine syntheses, headlined by the one that changes how the next phase
is planned:

> ⚠️ **A CONTRAST/RENDER PASS IS BOUNDED BY THE ROLE IT RUNS AS.** No probe can measure markup a permission
> check never emitted. Eleven greys sat behind `@can('users.manage')` and were **absent from the DOM** as the
> demo operator the gates were driven as. This extends G10: *a conditional SURFACE is invisible too, and the
> condition can be AUTHORIZATION.* **Coverage is "force every state across every role that can reach it".**

The other eight: a **certified component can have un-measured defaults** (`<x-star-rating>`'s own colours
failed 3:1 — *the thing everything was migrated to drew a star you could barely see*) · **INPUT vs DISPLAY
changes the fix** (applying the display pattern to the email's five rating *inputs* would have introduced a
phantom rating) · the **toolchain false-RED pair** (`php -l` **and** `view:clear`) plus **a guard vacuous
against its own subject** (the star test asserted literals repeated from the source) · **a number that moves is
not automatically a correction** (a scratchpad name collision, not a stale figure) · **a colour has several
grep-forms** (13 named → 28 real; the `rgb()` form hid a whole 403 page) · **a re-scoping note can amputate an
item's founding scope** (`DO-INV-4` had been narrowed past `#A99E95`, the literal it was raised for) · **a
shared layout's defaults are content and can be FALSE** · **token-drift means map to the TOKEN**, with three
measured exceptions.

**State consolidated:** the grey-literal drift is CLOSED across PDFs (17 templates), emails (20 templates, all
now on-brand, **335 runs / 0 FAIL**) and the operator/owner web screens the pass could reach (28 occurrences /
9 files, mapped to tokens); the **O26 star defect family is RETIRED**. ⚠️ **"Closed" means closed everywhere
this pass could REACH** — §N.14.1 is explicit that the operator/owner realms were swept only as far as the
roles used allowed, and `DO-EMAIL-5` is the honest successor.

**Register reconciled** with two index blocks: ✅ *closed by the cleanup sequence* (7) and ⬅ *the cleanup's open
successors, grouped by kind* (7). ⚠️ **The totals are not a burn-down** — every pass opened items it could only
see once it started.

**RESUME rewritten for the BACKEND PHASE**, priority order: ⚠️ **① `DO-EMAIL-9`** — a **live §N.8d**: a security
email telling an owner their **login-email change** *"relates to your booking with us"*, with **unknown scope**
(it is the shared layout's default, inherited by every account/security template) and a **reword-vs-restructure
call to surface** · ② `DO-EMAIL-4` (the twice-defined `--vy-amber-text`) · ③ `DO-EMAIL-5`/`DO-EMAIL-6` (the
role-aware re-audit; the standalone pages) · ④ the small tail (`DO-EMAIL-7`/`8`, `DO-STAR-1` — ⚠️ a bookmark,
not a rating) · ⑤ the backend phase proper (the full register · the 6 reopened operator a11y gates · the founder
decisions incl. G13's three verdicts). ⛔ The billing/pricing go-live blocker (§G.1) remains open, untouched by
both chapters.

**Stale claims corrected in place** (§N.8b applied to our own record): the certified-engines list still
described `<x-star-rating>` as having a live remnant *and* carried its pre-fix defaults; §N.13.8, the §G-8
bullet and two runway items still read as though `DO-G8-1` were open — each now closed with a pointer, and each
annotated where "all that remains of DO10-4" turned out to be wrong.

**Recommendation: start the backend phase in a FRESH chat.** The cleanup chapter's canon is durable in §N.14
and the register; a new session should open on the rewritten RESUME rather than inherit this one's context.

## 2026-08-12 — **BUILT: the guest Help centre** (`/guest/help`) — a pure FAQ over the certified engine

A build, not a parity gate. It takes G13's `DO-G13-1` verdict, on which the founder ruled: **build the FAQ
centre; the support half is a separate backend; keep it a PURE FAQ.** Full record: **§GUEST-FAQ** in
`docs/design/MISSING-BACKEND-BY-PAGE.md`.

⚠️ **The 2026-08-07 refusal is REVERSED, and annotated in place** in `DIVERGENCE-REGISTER.md`. It refused a help
**centre** because *"its content would have to be invented"* — sound when written, **false now**:
`HelpKnowledgeBase` is curated, real, screen-linked content read by the owner Help page and the grounded
assistant. ⚠️ **The other half of that refusal still stands and was honoured in full** — the page invents
nothing and offers no support affordance.

**Reused, not forked (§N.8f):** `HelpKnowledgeBase::guestArticles()` — 10 entries / 5 categories added to the
same engine, same contract plus a `category`. The view holds **no help content**; it renders the engine, so the
FAQ and the source cannot drift the way two copies of a claim always do. A test asserts both sets keep the
shape, and that guest entries link only `guest.*` routes while owner entries link only `owner.*`.

⚠️ **Every answer was verified against the code before it was written.** The door-code answer **interpolates
`ArrivalPack::LEAD_DAYS`** rather than typing a number — `DO-G4-1` had already caught a docblock claiming "48h"
against a constant that says **2 days**, and a FAQ is exactly where that drift would strand a guest at a door.
Also verified: online check-in is not the operator's authoritative check-in · Manage creates pending requests ·
payment is hosted Stripe Checkout with no stored card · the wallet cannot overdraw · a review needs a completed
stay · deletion is a reversible 14-day schedule after which anonymised financial records remain.
**Omitted rather than guessed:** a cancellation-refund window — it is per-property (`DO-G12-1`), so the entry
points at the booking's own Manage page instead of a number that would be wrong for some guests.

⚠️ **PURE FAQ.** No phone, WhatsApp, hours, reply time or 24/7 line — **and no slot, placeholder or commented
seam for them.** None has a backend, and promising support that will not answer is the class of false claim
`DO-EMAIL-9` records. The ONE contact is the existing relay.

**Verified as the GUEST (N.14.1), both a11y axes at birth.** Keyboard: 28 controls, **0 unnamed** under strict
name computation; a real Tab confirmed `:focus-visible` fires and every custom control has a matching outline
rule. Contrast: pixel-sampled with two anchors across the populated, **forced open-accordion** and no-results
states — **0 failing runs**; the chips measured separately on their own plates (4.67 / 6.52).

⚠️ **N.14.2 earned its place within minutes:** the page reused `.vy-sr-only` — **which the guest shell does not
define.** An undefined visually-hidden class hides nothing and would have rendered the search label as stray
text. Defined locally; every other reused class and token checked to exist first.

**Guarded** by `GuestHelpCentreTest` (7 tests / 165 assertions), **mutation-proven four ways**. ⚠️ **Two
mutations passed at first and both were faults in the guards** (O32): one edit **had not landed** (caught by
grepping the anchor), and the relay assertion was **vacuous** — `assertSee(route('guest.messages'))` stayed
green with the button repointed, because the shell's nav links Messages on every guest page. Now scoped to the
relay card. The negative support assertion also fired a **false positive** first: it scanned raw HTML and hit
"PHONE" in a CSS comment in the shell — a *breakpoint* heading, and a reminder that **CSS comments ship**. It
now asserts on the visible text.

**No schema** — the knowledge set is curated code, not a table. Suite **1914 / 12,613**, 9 non-green = the
documented baseline set. PHPStan L5 (0); Pint clean.

## 2026-08-12 — **SAVE v10: the FAQ centre is BUILT, the support backend is SCOPED** (docs only · a session handoff)

A full memory-consolidation pass. **No product code, template or test was touched.** Its purpose is a
**session handoff**: after this, a fresh Claude Code session orients entirely from `PROJECT-STATE.md`'s RESUME,
§N.13–§N.15 and the DO-register.

**Folded in: the first BUILD since the walk.** `GET /guest/help` (`23bf335`) — a guest FAQ centre over the
certified `HelpKnowledgeBase`, reused not forked, with the real relay as its only contact. **Canon: §N.15.**

**Three things the build added to the canon:**
1. ⚠️ **Verify-every-promise now covers AUTHORING.** Writing a FAQ makes fresh claims about the product before
   any test exists to catch them, so **verify before writing — it costs a grep; verifying after costs a gate.**
   And a new rule: **when the true answer VARIES, ROUTE to the authoritative screen rather than pick a number**
   (the per-property cancellation window points at the booking's Manage page; the door-code answer interpolates
   `ArrivalPack::LEAD_DAYS` rather than typing the "48h" that `DO-G4-1` caught as stale).
2. ⚠️ **Three new guard traps, all caught, none of them bugs in the feature:** a **vacuous assertion can hide in
   a shared nav** (`assertSee(route('guest.messages'))` stayed green with the button repointed, because the
   shell links Messages on every page — scope link assertions to the specific element); **N.14.2 extends from
   components to reused CSS classes** (`.vy-sr-only` was undefined in the guest shell, and an undefined
   visually-hidden class hides nothing); and **an absence assertion must read VISIBLE TEXT** — the no-support
   guard false-positived on "PHONE" in a CSS comment, because **CSS comments ship**.
3. ⚠️ **Building to the matured canon at birth held, and cost little** — rendered as the guest, both a11y axes,
   0 unnamed controls, two-anchor contrast across three states including a forced-open accordion.

**The Guest-Help verdict was SPLIT by founder ruling, and the record says so precisely:** the FAQ half is
**BUILT** (reversing the 2026-08-07 refusal, whose premise the engine falsified); the **support half is SCOPED,
not refused** — so that refusal is now **conditional, not permanent**. ⚠️ Both "the refusal was reversed" and
"the refusal stands" are true of different halves; §N.15.5 exists so a future session reading either sentence
alone does not get it wrong.

**The support backend is SCOPED as a spec** (§N.15.6) so the next session builds against it rather than
re-deciding it: 3 new per-property fields → migration → operator-settings UI → a guest support block; a stored
phone/WhatsApp, a **soft operator-set reply NORM** ("usually within…", never a guarantee — the `DO-EMAIL-9`
class), and **real per-property hours** (no "24/7" unless the stored hours say so). ⚠️ **The honesty principle
is baked into the data shape: every field displays only when populated — empty means the affordance is ABSENT.**

**Register updated:** a 🏗 *BUILT since the cleanup* block (`DO-G13-1` split; the support backend as a ready
spec) and an explicit ⚖️ *awaiting a founder ruling* row for `DO-G13-2` (Documents → DEFER) and `DO-G13-3`
(Referral → DON'T-BUILD) — recommendations, not decisions, exactly as the Help verdict was before it was split.

**RESUME rewritten as the session-handoff surface**, with the priority order stated plainly and the billing
go-live blocker (§G.1) called out as outranking everything if launch is near.

**Whole-record coherence checked, §N.8b applied INWARD — three stale self-claims found and closed:** §N.14.10's
state table still carried the pre-build suite figure; `G13-VERDICTS.md` still asserted *"there is no guest help
route"*; and the G13 entry in this log still read as a pending recommendation. Each annotated in place rather
than rewritten, so the reasoning that was true when written stays legible.

**Verified:** DO-numbers contiguous · the engines list now carries `HelpKnowledgeBase` incl. `guestArticles()` ·
`DO-EMAIL-9` still flagged live · the support spec present in both the canon and the register · the suite figure
consistent (1914 / 12,613, 9 non-green = the documented set) · the billing blocker still flagged.

## 2026-08-12 — **BUILT: the guest SUPPORT BACKEND** — `DO-G13-1` is now closed in BOTH halves

The other half of the Guest-Help verdict. The founder ruled **build the backend first** — not don't-build, and
not ship-the-UI-over-nothing — and this is that backend plus the two surfaces it makes honest. Three layers, one
commit. Full record: **§SUPPORT-BACKEND** in `docs/design/MISSING-BACKEND-BY-PAGE.md`; canon in §N.15.6.

**SCHEMA.** `2026_09_22_000000_add_property_support_contact_columns` adds `support_phone` · `support_reply_norm`
· `support_hours` to `properties` — **all nullable, none with a default**. Reversible, proven by an actual
rollback and re-migrate rather than by reading `down()`. Per-property, so the tenant perimeter is
`properties.organization_id` unchanged; **no new scope was invented**.

⚠️ **NULLABLE IS THE HONESTY MECHANISM, not a convenience.** NULL is not "unset yet", it is the product state
*this property offers no such channel*, and the guest surface draws the affordance only when the column is
populated. A seeded default would ship an operational promise no operator ever made — a number that rings
nobody, an hour by which nobody replies — which is the `DO-EMAIL-9` class in the one place a guest will act on
it. Nothing is seeded, including in the demo org.

**OPERATOR UI.** A **Guest support** section on `/app/settings` → `POST /app/settings/support`
(`can:properties.manage`, the same gate as the rest of the per-property settings) → `SettingsActionController`
→ the certified `SettingsService::updateSupport`, which audits by FIELD NAME and never by value.
⚠️ **An emptied box is written back as NULL, deliberately** — clearing a phone is *withdrawing a channel*, and a
writer that "only sends what changed" would leave the guest page advertising a number the operator just took
down. Mutation-proven.

**GUEST UI.** A conditional block under "Still need help?" on `/guest/help`, **one card per property the guest
has actually booked**, each carrying the property's name — a support number is a promise made by a specific
front desk, and two desks must never be merged into one number. The properties resolve through `ResolvesGuest`
and the guest's own `lead_guest_id` relation, so a guest cannot see the support details of a property they have
never stayed at; cancelled and no-show stays are excluded. The relay stays unconditional, because it is real for
every property by construction.

**THE SHARED DERIVATION.** `App\Support\Guest\PropertySupport` is read by BOTH surfaces, so the sentence an
operator picks is byte-identical to the sentence a guest reads (§N.8f — two copies of a claim about how fast
someone replies is exactly the mock-value shape this repo keeps paying for).

⚠️ **THE REPLY NORM CANNOT BECOME A GUARANTEE, STRUCTURALLY.** The column stores a KEY into a fixed catalogue;
the wording lives in code and every phrase begins *"usually"*. The operator picks a bucket, never types a
sentence, and `Rule::in(array_keys(REPLY_NORMS))` refuses a hand-posted *"guaranteed within 1 hour"*. That is
§N.8d closed the way §N.10b prefers — a refusal that *cannot fail*, rather than a helptext asking nicely.
Nothing is measured either: the norm is what the operator says they aim for, never a statistic re-presented as a
commitment. And no "24/7" is hardcoded, defaulted or suggested — hours are free text, so if a property is
round-the-clock it is because someone typed that.

⚠️ **PREMISE CORRECTION — `DO-SUP-1`: PHONE, NOT WHATSAPP.** The scoped spec said "a stored phone / WhatsApp per
property". One number is stored and it renders as a **telephone (`tel:`) only**. Nothing in the product verifies
that a given number answers on WhatsApp, so drawing that affordance would assert a channel that may not exist
(#39) — the same shape as the reply-time promise this whole build exists to avoid. A real WhatsApp affordance
needs a second column the operator ticks deliberately, or a verification step. Logged, not smuggled in.

**GUARDED** by `GuestPropertySupportTest` (10 tests / 89 assertions), **mutation-proven seven ways** — the phone
row's gate, the card-level null return, a catalogue phrase turned into a guarantee, the guest read widened to
every property, the `Rule::in` dropped, the writer skipping nulls, and the writer taking a request-supplied
property id. Each red on its own guard, green on restore, with `php -l` and `view:clear` after every edit.

⚠️ **ONE MUTATION PASSED, AND IT WAS A FINDING (O32, redundancy form).** Removing `PropertySupport::for()`'s null
return left every row-level assertion **green** — because each row is separately gated — while the page would
have rendered an **empty, property-named card**: a placeholder by another name, which is exactly what the spec
forbids. Redundancy hid it. The guard now asserts that no support markup exists at all in the unconfigured
state, and the mutation goes red. *A passing mutation is a finding, not a formality.*

⚠️ **AND THE BROWSER CAUGHT A DEFECT THE TEST COULD NOT.** The catalogue first stored bare intervals, so the page
read **"We usually within a few hours."** — broken English that `toContain('We usually')` was perfectly happy
with. Rendering it as the guest is what found it. The phrases are now complete predicates and the guard asserts
the whole composed sentence per entry. *A prefix assertion tests a prefix.*

**VERIFIED AS BOTH ROLES (N.14.1).** As a `Property Owner` (the role holding `properties.manage`): the section
renders, the select offers only the four soft norms plus "Don't show a reply time", and two real saves through
the form wrote hours-only and then phone + norm, audited by field name. As the guest: unconfigured → **0 support
cards, 0 `tel:` links**; hours-only → exactly one row; fully populated → three rows under the property's name.
**Contrast** pixel-sampled on the real render with the anchor reading **5.18** (the published
white-on-solid-accent figure, so the instrument is sound), animations frozen by *completing* them, 0 transparent
elements before capture: labels **6.73**, values **14.83**, the dial link **5.92** — **0 failing runs**, and
greyscale-safe because every row is distinguished by its label rather than by colour. **Keyboard:** 39
focusables, **0 unnamed** under a strict accessible-name computation; the dial link is reached by a **real Tab**
(not `el.focus()`, which does not set `:focus-visible`), genuinely matches `:focus-visible`, and is named *"Call
Demo Seaside Property on +351 289 000 114"*.

⚠️ **A PRE-EXISTING DEFECT FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, NOT INTRODUCED HERE: `migrate:fresh --seed` currently ABORTS.**
`DemoSeeder` dies on a `UnitUnavailableException` — a date-coupled collision between demo stays. **Proven
pre-existing by stashing this build and re-running on a clean tree, where it fails identically** (§N.14.5's
discipline, and the reason to own a clean baseline). It leaves the demo org half-seeded: one property instead of
two, and the demo staff user with **no roles**, so `/app` is unreachable until they are provisioned by hand. The
migration added here applies and rolls back cleanly against it. **Logged, not fixed — it is nobody's regression
and it is not this build's scope, but it blocks any session that needs a demo database.**

## 2026-08-12 — **FIXED: `DO-SEED-1` — the demo seed's date rot, at the root** (+ two G13 ratifications)

`migrate:fresh --seed` had stopped completing. Raised while verifying the support backend and **proven
pre-existing** there by stashing and re-running on a clean tree. Full record: **§DO-SEED-1** in
`docs/design/MISSING-BACKEND-BY-PAGE.md`.

⚠️ **THE ROOT CAUSE, WALKED TO RATHER THAN INFERRED.** The seeder mixed **two date systems**: a today-RELATIVE
forward window (the arriving-tomorrow stay, the terminal pair, the whole analytics spread) and an **ABSOLUTE**
calendar (the showcase stays on `2026-09-xx`, five "past" statement months `2026-04`…`2026-08`, an October
accrual, the reviews, the expenses, the agreement dates). They were disjoint **on the day they were written** —
and `seedOwnerStatementHistory` carried a comment saying exactly that: *"clear of the (future-dated)
analytics-history window, so no collision"*. Time walked the relative window into the absolute one and the
comment became false. The precise collision, from the stack: the "past" **August** statement stay on **14–18
Aug**, apartment **A1**, against the analytics entry at **today+3 = 15 Aug** on the same apartment. Analytics
runs first and *tolerates* collisions; the statement history is **strict**, so it aborted the whole seed.

⚠️ **AND THE CODEBASE HAD ALREADY MET THIS EXACT FAILURE ONCE.** `seedOwnerBalanceAccrual` carries a
*"ROBUST TO DATE-DRIFT"* forward-scan added for the identical reason. **The rot was known and defended in one
place out of two** — the other had a comment instead of a guard. *A comment is not a defence; it is a claim that
goes stale (§N.8b) exactly where the guard was missing.*

**THE FIX IS AN ANCHOR, NOT A BUMPED DATE.** Three helpers now derive every formerly-absolute date:
`thisMonth()`, `showcaseMonth()/showcaseDay()` (the NEXT full month — so the showcase stays are upcoming on any
run day, which is what keeps the **#33** withheld-door-code demo honest) and **`completedMonth(n)`** (a month
that has already ENDED). The statement history reads the last of these, which makes its collision
**structurally impossible**: a finished month is strictly before today, and every colliding booking is dated
today-or-later. Also re-anchored: the waitlist, the agreement `effective_from` (now provably before the oldest
attributed night), the pending amendment, the accrual month, the example tax rate, the owner expenses (including
the **pre-agreement** row whose whole purpose is to fall before `effective_from`), and the review anchors —
which held absolute July/May dates while the availability they depend on was already published relative to today.
One shared `bookAptStayNear()` scans forward for a free window for the two stays created *after* the tolerant
analytics pass, and **throws rather than skips**: a demo that quietly loses half a statement's net is worse than
one that fails loudly. It replaced the accrual's private copy of the same idiom (§N.8f).

**WHAT THE SEED NOW PRODUCES, VERIFIED:** **2 properties** (was 1) · the demo staff user **with its `Hotel
Manager` role** (was roleless) · 41 reservations · **6 owner statements** — five `paid` in completed months, one
`finalized` for the showcase month. `/app` renders as `demo-staff` **straight from a clean seed with no
hand-provisioning**; the manual role assignment the support-backend build needed is gone. ⚠️ Not to be
mis-read: `demo-staff` is a Hotel Manager and by design does **not** hold `properties.manage`, so `/app/settings`
still needs a `Property Owner` — the role catalogue working, not a seed defect.

**GUARDED** by `DemoSeedDateRobustnessTest` (7 tests / 25 assertions): the end state, the **structural** property
(every `paid` statement covers a month that has ended; the `finalized` one is next month), a
no-hardcoded-calendar-date grep with comments stripped, and **the seed run at four time-travelled dates** — a
month end, a year boundary, a leap day and 2031.

⚠️ **THE TIME-TRAVEL CASE IS WHAT MAKES THIS A ROOT FIX RATHER THAN A PATCH.** A test asserting only "the seed
passes today" would have been green every single day before this broke. **Mutation-proven:** restoring the
original `'2026-08-01'` literal turns **6 of 7 red** — and the seventh, the 2031 date, legitimately still
passes, because a literal that far in the past no longer collides. *One date would not have caught it.*

⚠️ **AND THE STANDING CLAIM ITSELF WAS THE LESSON.** Every dated entry in this log saying *"`migrate:fresh
--seed` clean"* was true on its date. *"The seed is clean"* is a statement about **a day**; only a date-robust
seed plus a time-travelling guard makes it a statement about the code. The RESUME now says so.

⚠️ **HONEST NOTE ON THE FIGURES.** On this run the showcase statement's net is **€885.60** — the figure the
record has always carried. It is **not structurally pinned**: a drifting analytics stay can fall inside the
showcase month on some run days. Every figure stays REAL and reconciling (#17), so the guard asserts the
statement **shape**, never the constant.

### Ratified the same day — the G13 tail

- **`DO-G13-2` · Guest Documents → DEFER.** Ratified as recommended. The rollup already lives on
  `/guest/payments` (a ratified location divergence); building a second hub would reopen it.
- **`DO-G13-3` · Guest Referral → DON'T-BUILD (#39).** Ratified as recommended. Five subsystems are absent,
  including a **new guest-creation path** — a security-posture change, not a page.

⚠️ Both are now **decisions, not recommendations**, and neither is a gap. With `DO-G13-1` built in both halves,
**the whole G13 set is closed.**

### Recorded, not acted on — `DO-EMAIL-9`

The founder leans **RESTRUCTURE, not reword**: change the shared email layout's default service line and audit
which templates then need their own, rather than the per-template override `DO-EMAIL-3` used. Noted in the
register against `DO-EMAIL-9` so the next session builds against it. **Nothing was changed here.**

**BASELINE — and it MOVED, downward.** Suite **1931 / 12,745**, **7 non-green** (`BookingImportTest` ×6 ·
`OwnerUnitDetailViewTest` ×1). It was **9**: the two `StubViewsTest` failures were `UnitUnavailableException::
occupied` — **the same collision this entry fixes** — and are now green, verified in isolation (3/3) rather than
inferred from the total. PHPStan L5 (0); Pint clean.

⚠️ **TWO SELF-INFLICTED FALSE REDS ON THE WAY, both worth recording** (they extend §N.13.2's false-RED family
with a fifth and sixth source — *the environment*, not the file or the cache):
1. **A CONCURRENT TEST DATABASE.** Running the new seed guard while the full suite was still running produced
   six `SQLSTATE[40001]` **deadlocks** on the `permissions` table. Nothing was wrong with the guard; two
   processes were provisioning roles into one `vyrobel_test`. **Run the guard alone** — it is 7/7.
2. **`MAIL_MAILER=log` ON THE SUITE.** Set out of habit (Mailpit is not running locally), it turned
   `MailTransportSafetyTest` red — a test whose entire job is to assert the suite runs on a non-sending
   transport. **The override broke the very guard that exists to catch it.** The baseline above is a clean run
   with no overrides and nothing else touching the database.

## 2026-08-12 — **`DO-EMAIL-9` + `DO-EMAIL-8` CLOSED: the email footer reason is DERIVED, not defaulted**

The shared email layout ended every template with ONE hardcoded line — *"You're receiving this because it
relates to your booking with us."* — and `owner-email-change`, an owner changing their **login email**, shipped
it live. A shared layout's default copy is content, and it can be false (§N.14.8). Full record:
**§EMAIL-FOOTER-RESTRUCTURE** in `docs/design/MISSING-BACKEND-BY-PAGE.md`.

⚠️ **WHY RESTRUCTURE, NOT REWORD (the founder's call — and the reasoning holds).** Any single sentence in that
slot is wrong for *some* category, and the next template added inherits it silently. A reword moves the
falsehood; it does not remove it. So the reason is now **derived from a declared category** — a template writes
`@section('footer_reason', 'security')`, and the wording lives in the layout. **A false reason is not something
a template can type.** This is the second build in a row to reach for that shape (the guest support reply-norm
was the first); it is becoming the house pattern for copy that must stay true.

⚠️ **THE DEFAULT IS GENERIC-TRUE, AND THAT IS THE ACTUAL FIX.** A template that declares nothing gets *"…because
you have an account with us"*; an unrecognised key falls to the same line rather than rendering the raw key.
**A forgetful new template still cannot claim a booking** — which is precisely what the old default guaranteed
it would.

**THE MAPPING (all 16 extending templates enumerated):** `booking` — the six booking mails · `security` —
guest-password-reset · `email_change` — **owner-email-change**, admin-email-change · `account` —
account-deletion, verify-email, maintenance-cost-report · `waitlist` — waitlist-notification · deliberately
generic — notification, plus the two marketing templates which supply their own opt-out block.

⚠️ **A FINDING, NOT TIDINESS: `email_change` EXISTS BECAUSE FLATTENING WOULD HAVE BEEN A REGRESSION.** The
obvious move was to declare `security` on both change emails. But an email-change confirmation is sent to the
address being **ADDED**, whose reader may hold no account at all yet — so *"a security change on your account"*
is not safely true of them. `DO-EMAIL-3`'s one-off override had carried exactly that nuance, and folding it into
`security` would have been a small honesty regression dressed as consolidation. **The old test defending that
sentence is what surfaced it** — a test that looked like mechanical breakage and was not.

⚠️ **`DO-EMAIL-8` — PREMISE CORRECTION: the slot was OVERLOADED, not merely misnamed.** It genuinely held a
marketing opt-out block (`winback`, `operator-guest-message`) **and** was pressed into service as a reason
override. Renaming alone would have re-conflated them, so it was **split**: `footer_reason` (a key) and
`footer_marketing` (the opt-out block). `@section('unsubscribe')` greps to zero. A transactional email offers no
opt-out — nobody can unsubscribe from a security notice about their own account.

**VERIFIED BY RENDERING.** 11 of the 16 rendered as real Mailables — nine through the operator Email-Previews
route plus the two change emails — and each footer read as a recipient sees it. The remaining five are covered
by the enumerated declaration guard plus the layout-catalogue render. `owner-email-change` before/after is
captured: identical message, CTA and URL; **only** the footer line changes.

**GUARDED** by `EmailFooterReasonTest` (12 / 97), **mutation-proven four ways** — regress the default to the
booking line, drop `owner-email-change`'s declaration, make an unknown key render raw, restore the old slot
name — each red on its own guard. Email suites 45/45.

⚠️ **THREE INSTRUMENT FAULTS CAUGHT WHILE WRITING THE GUARD, all of known families:**
1. **`toHaveKey($name, $message)` asserts a VALUE, not a message** — the §N.8c API-misuse family in a new guise,
   and it failed loudly only by luck.
2. **A source-level scan fired on a BLADE COMMENT** quoting the old line while documenting its removal — the
   *inverse* of the CSS-comment trap: a CSS comment ships and must be scanned, a Blade comment never does and
   must be stripped first.
3. ⚠️ **A mutation verdict was briefly untrustworthy because the VERIFICATION GREP was broken** by shell
   escaping — it reported the edit had not landed when it had. Re-run with an asserted anchor in Python.
   **The check must be as trustworthy as the thing it checks** (§N.4p, applied to the instrument).

⚠️ **AND A FOURTH, THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE: `operator-guest-message` WAS CLASSIFIED WRONG.** It was left
undeclared (generic) when it is a property writing to a guest **about their stay** — `booking` is the truthful
line. The pre-existing `MarketingUnsubscribeTest` caught it, because it already pinned that template's
no-unsubscribe service-message mode. *A test that looks like collateral damage from a refactor may be encoding
a real invariant — read it before changing it.* Its two modes are now explicit: with an unsubscribe URL it fills
`footer_marketing`; without one it falls through to `booking`.

## 2026-08-12 — **`DO-EMAIL-4` CLOSED: `--vy-amber-text` reconciled to one value**

The token was declared **twice with different values** — guest `#7E5811`, owner `#804C05`. A `var()` resolves to
whichever shell is in scope, so a shared component would pick up the wrong one, and *"the amber-text value"* was
ambiguous enough to infect `DO-EMAIL-1`'s record. Full record: **§AMBER-TEXT-RECONCILIATION**.

**THE MEASUREMENT DECIDED IT.** Both values were pixel-sampled against every plate either renders on, in BOTH
realms, with three self-validating anchors all reading exactly **5.18**. Worst case: `#7E5811` = **4.65**,
`#804C05` = **5.18** — **both clear AA, so the branch is UNIFY**, and the value with the headroom wins.
`#804C05` is strictly darker, so it scores higher on every light plate; no amber-text use sits on a dark plate,
which is what lets that generalise beyond the seven sites sampled.

⚠️ **THE PROBE TRIED TO LIE ONCE.** Two owner samples sat below the viewport and `imagecolorat` returned black,
scoring them 3.29 / 2.95 — a failure that never happened. Caught because the numbers were implausible beside
their neighbours, and re-measured after scrolling them in. **An out-of-bounds read is not a measurement.**

**IT WAS ACCIDENTAL, AND HISTORY SETTLES IT:** the guest value arrived at the guest Reservation gate
(`4040b0f`), the owner value at the Owner Statement gate (`656cc34`). Two passes, months apart, each deriving an
amber for their own plates, neither aware of the other. Same intent, two answers, one name.

⚠️ **PREMISE REFINEMENT WORTH KEEPING — "declared per shell" is not itself the defect.** A scan found **8**
tokens differing across the three shells and **7 of them are deliberate**: the guest realm runs smaller radii
and a lighter shadow, `--vy-glass-border` is warm-dark on guest and white on owner/operator, and `--vy-on-grad`
was measured **separately per shell on purpose** (§N.4i/§N.4j). Per-shell theming is the design system working.
The defect was narrower: *this* token has one intent and no reason to differ. **So the guard is scoped to the
token — a blanket "all tokens must agree" rule would be false against the design**, and writing one would have
been the kind of overreach that looks like rigour and is actually a bug.

**THE DELTA** is the token definition plus the literals that must track it: the guest shell adopts the canonical
value; the two email literals (`pre-arrival`, `payment-reminder`) move to it (emails cannot read a token, but the
literal must still be *the* value or the ambiguity merely relocates — and it improves every email plate, 5.73 →
6.39 on `#FBF1E9`); the owner-remittance PDF already used it. `#7E5811` greps to **zero**. The visual shift is a
slightly deeper, less yellow amber in the guest realm. **Greyscale-verified** — the badge and figures stay
legible on luminance and wording, never hue.

**GUARDED** by `AmberTextTokenTest` (10 / 26), **mutation-proven twice**: re-adding the old guest value reds the
one-name-one-value guard; lightening the canonical value reds the AA guard on every plate.

🚩 **LOGGED, NOT FIXED — `DO-TOKEN-1`, the structural root.** Each shell re-declares the whole palette, so **any**
token can diverge this way and nothing but a test stops the next one. A shared token source is the §N.8f fix —
but it must preserve the 7 deliberate per-shell overrides rather than flatten them, which makes it a refactor
across three shells, not a contrast item.

## 2026-08-12 — **`DO-EMAIL-5` (partial) + `DO-EMAIL-6` (closed): the role-coverage re-audit**

§N.14.1 said a contrast pass is bounded by the ROLE it runs as. This turns that into a **procedure**: enumerate
the roles → identify which ones prior passes ran as → **diff** to get the permissions they lack → grep the
markup gated on those → render as a role that passes the gate, force the conditional on top of it, sample.
Step 3 is what makes it tractable: the target was **6 permissions / 12 gated blocks**, not "everything as
everyone". Full record: **§ROLE-COVERAGE-RE-AUDIT**.

**THE UNCOVERED ROLE was Property Owner / Group Admin** — every operator contrast pass ran as the demo Hotel
Manager, which holds none of `users.manage`, `settings.manage`, `properties.manage`, `billing.manage`. The other
roles hold subsets of Hotel Manager, so they expose little new markup — worth stating, because it bounds the
audit honestly rather than leaving "all the other roles" as an open-ended debt.

**FOUND, rendered live as Property Owner (anchor 5.18 on every capture):** the known `.vy-inv-lbl` **#9C9089 =
2.80**; ⚠️ **a second grey nobody had named — `#B7ADA4` = 2.00**, worse than the known one, visible only once
the modal was rendered by a role that could see it; and ⚠️ **the storefront filter keys at 1.77**.

⚠️ **THAT THIRD ONE WIDENS THE LESSON.** Those labels are not permission-gated at all — they are public, and
invisible because the page needs a **performed search** and the property needs filter **data**. **A surface can
be invisible because of DATA, not only authorization or UI state.** G10 named the conditional *style*; N.14.1
named the conditional *surface* via authorization; this is the third form. And the plate chose the token: they

## 2026-08-12 — **`DO-EMAIL-7` CLOSED: the status fill was fine; the thing beside it was not**

`--vy-hk-ooo` was logged as *"a status fill — a design decision"*. `DO10-4` had since established that a status
carried by COLOUR is **correctness** (WCAG 1.4.1), not tone, so it was re-opened **to measure, not to fix**.
Full record: **§HK-STATUS-DETERMINATION**.

**THE VERDICT ON THE TOKEN IS VERIFIED-FINE, AND NOTHING WAS CHANGED.** Rendered as a **Property Owner** on
`/app/housekeeping` with a **real** out-of-order room present (no forcing needed), anchor 5.18: every status
chip prints its **word** beside the dot, and OOO rooms are not drawn as cards at all — so `--vy-hk-ooo` renders
in exactly one place, a dot next to the words "Out of order". Colour is never the sole carrier (1.4.1
satisfied), the dot clears the non-text bar anyway at **3.31**, and a greyscale capture confirms all five
statuses read by word. ⚠️ **A flagged item that turns out to be sound is an honest close — inventing a fix for
it would have been the failure.**

⚠️ **BUT THE SAME MEASUREMENT FOUND THE DEFECT NEXT TO IT** (N.13.1's thesis, again — the risk sits beside the
thing everyone is looking at). The tally chip is `--vy-glass`, **translucent over the page gradient**, so its
plate moves with its position; and `.vy-hk-tal.is-zero` dropped **the whole chip** to `opacity: .62`, dimming a
status WORD to **2.28**. Worse, `--vy-muted` reads **6.00** on a light part of that band and only **4.25** on a
saturated part — **it fails at FULL opacity there.**

⚠️ **Two lessons in one CSS rule.** *Opacity applied to a chip dims its text* — and the empty state was already
carried by the "0" beside the word, so the dimming was both redundant and harmful. And **a token that passes
where you sampled can fail elsewhere on the same translucent band**: `--vy-muted` was wrong by **position**, not
by carelessness. The label now reads `--vy-ink` (9.38 on the worst plate) and the de-emphasis rides the dot.

Status semantics, the state machine and the data are untouched — display only. **Guarded** by
`HousekeepingStatusContrastTest` (3 / 20), which pins **both** outcomes: that every `--vy-hk-*` token appears in
a chip carrying its status word (so the verified-fine state cannot regress to colour-only), and that the dimming
never returns to the text. Mutation-proven: restoring `.is-zero { opacity: .62 }` reds 2 of 3.

## 2026-08-13 — **BILLING: two founder rulings, and PASS 1 builds the shape-aware engine to them**

⚠️ **THE §G.1 QUESTION WAS DISSOLVED, NOT ANSWERED.** It had been framed as *"which model does Vyrobel sell —
flat tier or per-unit?"* The founder ruled that **pricing is configurable DATA and the product supports BOTH
shapes**, managed from a later super-admin panel. There is no model to pick; there is a plan **engine** that
charges faithfully to whatever shape a plan declares. The "contradiction" was two hardcoded models coexisting,
not a real either/or — worth recording, because a whole go-live blocker turned out to be a framing artefact.

- **RULING 1 — configurable, both shapes.** `flat` (one price regardless of units) or `per_unit`
  (rate × the org's real units + VAT).
- **RULING 2 — per-unit prorates immediately.** A mid-cycle unit change charges the difference now, not at
  renewal. ⚠️ This makes the currently-false *"prorated"* claim on the Billing page **true for per-unit plans** —
  but the page itself is pass ③ and was deliberately left alone.

### What PASS 1 built (the engine only)

- **`plans.pricing_type`** (`flat` default, so **every existing row stays valid and charges exactly as before**)
  plus `unit_rate_minor` and `vat_pct`. ⚠️ The per-unit rate moved from global config onto the PLAN, because a
  global constant cannot express "this plan charges €9 and that one €12" — which is what a catalogue needs.
- **`Plan::quantityFor()` / `chargeFor()`** — the plan answers its own shape and what an org owes.
- **`createSubscriptionCheckout` is shape-aware** — the `'quantity' => 1` hardcode (the core gap the
  investigation found) is gone: flat → 1, per-unit → the org's real count, with `proration_behavior` set only
  where it means something.
- **`BillingService::syncSubscriptionQuantity()`** — the prorated mid-cycle re-quantify; a **no-op on flat**,
  because a flat price does not move with the rack and sending a quantity would multiply the bill.

⚠️ **THE QUANTITY IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED — the load-bearing decision.** New `BillableUnits` is the ONE source,
read by both the CHARGE path (`Plan::quantityFor`) and the DISPLAY path (`SubscriptionPricing`). A stored count
is correct only until the next unit is added, and nothing announces the drift; a charged quantity that disagrees
with the org's units is the §N.8d false-claim shape **with money attached**. There is deliberately no
`subscriptions.unit_count` column. A test asserts display and charge return the same figure.

**Proven against the FAKE Stripe client** (`STRIPE_FAKE=true`; `StripeSafetyGuard` untouched) — the fake records
the quantity, price and proration flag that *would* reach Stripe. That is not a weaker proof: the bug being
guarded lives entirely in what we send.

**GUARDED** by `BillingPricingShapeTest` (8 / 33), **mutation-proven four ways** — restore the `quantity => 1`
bug → red; make the quantity a stored copy that drifts → red; drop proration on the mid-cycle change → red;
make flat send the unit count → red. All 53 billing/Stripe tests green.

**SCOPE HELD:** no super-admin panel, no customer Billing page (③ — a half-aware page is worse than the
known-false one), no live Stripe Prices or env (②), no real org re-planned. The four seeded tier plans are
explicitly flat and unchanged.

⚠️ **STILL BLOCKING THE FLIP:** ② real Price objects of each shape + env (the rows carry `price_fake_*`; it
fails loudly, not silently) · ③ the Billing page must render FROM the plan — it currently tells a FLAT-tier org
*"Adding a unit +€9.00/mo · prorated"*, a live §N.8d · the plan-CRUD panel.

## 2026-08-13 — **BILLING PASS 3: the customer Billing page renders FROM the plan — the live §N.8d is retired**

The page rendered a per-unit view **unconditionally**, so an org on a FLAT tier was shown *"8 units × €9.00"*,
*"incl. 23% VAT"* and *"Adding a unit +€9.00/mo · prorated"* — none of which is true of a flat plan, where
adding a unit changes nothing at all. That was the live §N.8d the investigation found. It is gone.

**RENDER FROM THE SHAPE (§N.16.3).** The summary is keyed on the org's plan `pricing_type`:
· **FLAT** → the flat price, plan name, next charge. No per-unit breakdown, no VAT split, no proration promise.
· **PER-UNIT** → rate × the real unit count + VAT, the breakdown, and the proration line — **true since pass 1**.

⚠️ **THE FALSE CLAIM IS STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE, NOT HIDDEN.** The per-unit markup lives inside the per-unit
branch, so a flat org cannot render it even by mistake. "We remembered to hide it" is a discipline; "the branch
does not exist for you" is a property.

⚠️ **DISPLAY = CHARGE.** Every figure comes from `Plan::chargeFor()` / `BillableUnits` — the same expression the
CHARGE uses. The page performs no arithmetic of its own, because a second calculation is a second source, and
two sources for one number is how a page ends up contradicting the invoice. Pass 1 made the charge read one
source; pass 3 makes the display read the same one, and a test asserts the page's figure tracks a mid-cycle unit
change. **The "€88.56" headline that was docblock-labelled a PLACEHOLDER is now a real derived figure.**

**VERIFIED AS THE ROLE, BOTH SHAPES FORCED (§N.16.2 — the plan's shape is DATA).** Rendered at `/app/billing` as
a Property Owner: the FLAT org shows **€49.00/mo**, "Units on the rack 8", "Adding a unit **included in your
plan**", and no proration/VAT/× lines; the PER-UNIT org shows **€88.56/mo**, "Monthly · 8 units × €9.00",
"incl. 23% VAT" and "+€9.00/mo · prorated". A pass that rendered only the default org would have seen one view.

**GUARDED** by `BillingPageShapeTest` (4 / 16), **mutation-proven three ways**: render the per-unit rail for
everyone → red (the §N.8d claim cannot return); make the page recompute instead of reading the engine → red
(display drifts from charge); drop the per-unit branch for a per-unit org → red. All 47 billing/Stripe tests
green.

1. **`$billing` shadowed the injected `BillingService`** in `render()`, so a later `tierCards($billing)` got an

2. **A mutation that did not land was nearly recorded as proven.** M1's anchor did not match, the run passed,

## 2026-08-13 — **BILLING PASS 2 (wiring half): real Price ids, loud failures — and the tax gap nobody had seen**

**RULED: flat tiers are VAT-INCLUSIVE.** €49/€99 is the final price. Pass 3's open question is answered; the
flat view's absence of a VAT split is correct, and a flat Stripe Price is created `tax_behavior: inclusive` at
the same amount. No engine change follows from this.

### What the pass did (autonomous)

- **`STRIPE_PRICE_*` is the source of truth.** The seeder's `price_fake_*` fallback is now **dev-only**: in
  production an unset key **throws at seed time**. `startCheckout` refuses a missing **or placeholder** id
  before a session is created. Nothing silently falls back to an id Stripe has never heard of.
- **`docs/BILLING-STRIPE-PRICES.md`** — the exact specs (currency, amount, interval, billing scheme, tax
  behaviour, env key) for the founder to copy, create and paste.

### ⚠️ THE FINDING — nothing sends tax to Stripe, and per-unit would under-charge by the VAT

The checkout sends `price` + `quantity` and **no tax configuration at all** — no `tax_behavior`, no
`automatic_tax`, no `tax_rates`. A per-unit plan's engine total is `units × rate + VAT`, so with a €9.00 Price
and 8 units **Stripe takes €72.00 while the page says €88.56 — €16.56/month under-charged, silently.** That is
§N.8d at the money boundary: passes 1 and 3 made engine and page agree, and the last hop disagreed with both.

⚠️ **The two fixes are not equivalent, so the pass did not pick one.** A VAT-**inclusive** unit Price (€11.07 at
23%) works with today's code and matches the flat convention; **Stripe Tax** (`exclusive`) is correct for
cross-border and EU B2B reverse-charge but needs `automatic_tax` wired, which is a further build. Choosing has
compliance consequences. **So the app refuses**: a per-unit plan will not bill in production until
`STRIPE_TAX_BEHAVIOR` is declared. Refusing to charge beats charging the wrong amount.

### ⚠️ The honest boundary — two different claims

**PROVEN from dev, against the fake client:** the configured id reaches the call per shape · a placeholder or
missing id **throws** on the production path · a per-unit plan with no declared tax convention **throws** ·
the quantity reaching Stripe equals `Plan::chargeFor()`. Guarded by `BillingStripePriceWiringTest` (7 / 19),
mutation-proven three ways (restore the silent fallback → red; drop the tax refusal → red; send a wrong id →
red). ⚠️ Each loud-fail test **forces the production context**, because a guard that never enters the branch it
guards is vacuous — and each asserts the same plan is *fine* outside production, so the check is not trivially
always-throwing.

**NOT proven, and not claimable:** that the real Prices exist in Stripe with the right amounts. `StripeSafetyGuard`
refuses a live key outside production — by design, and untouched — so that is the founder's dashboard
confirmation, spelled out in the spec doc.

**SCOPE:** config, seeder and the pre-charge gate only. Pass 1's engine, pass 3's page and the (unbuilt) panel
are untouched.


---

## 2026-08-13 · BILLING PASS 2b — STRIPE TAX FOR PER-UNIT, AND THE APP GIVING UP A CLAIM

**RULED:** per-unit VAT reaches Stripe via **Stripe Tax — `tax_behavior: exclusive` + `automatic_tax`**, reverse
charge handled by Stripe. Flat tiers stay **VAT-inclusive** (€49/€99 final), unchanged.

**Why this was not a pricing tweak.** Under Stripe Tax the tax is **customer-dependent** — country, business
status, EU reverse charge (€0). So the engine's hardcoded `+ 23%` stopped being merely *unsent* (pass 2's
finding) and became **false for a whole class of customers**. The correct response was not different arithmetic
but **to stop asserting a post-tax total the app cannot know** (§N.8d).

**Three layers moved together** — a split would have left the page asserting a tax the checkout no longer fixes:
- **checkout** `automatic_tax: enabled` for the exclusive shape only, plus the inputs Stripe Tax requires
  (`billing_address_collection`, `tax_id_collection`, `customer_update.address` — Stripe rejects the session
  without the last one when an existing customer is passed);
- **engine** per-unit `chargeFor()` is the **pre-tax subtotal** (`units × €9`) with a new `tax_known: false`;
- **page** per-unit shows the subtotal + **"tax calculated at checkout"**, driven by ONE keyed `tax_note`
  (§N.16.3) read by all three sites on the card.

**The pass-2 refusal LIFTED for the right reason.** `STRIPE_TAX_BEHAVIOR` defaults to `exclusive`;
`assertTaxConventionResolved()` still throws when it is unset, and a test unsets it to prove production refuses
again. The guard was not removed — the correct path was built.

**⚠️ TWO MORE SURFACES WERE ASSERTING THE SAME FIXED VAT, both beside the one pass 3 fixed** (§N.13.1):
1. the Billing card's own **"Next invoice" strip** read `SubscriptionPricing`, so a FLAT org saw €49.00 in the
   headline and **"€72.00 + €16.56 VAT"** immediately below it;
2. operator **Settings → "Your plan"** priced *every* org with the per-unit formula — the demo org on flat
   Essential displayed **"Vyrobel Essential · €88.56/mo"** against a Billing page saying €49.00.

Both now read `Plan::chargeFor()`, and `SubscriptionPricing` no longer computes VAT at all: it had become a
second, divergent total for one concept (5535 vs 4500), which is exactly what §N.8f exists to prevent.

**G8 — three prior tests amended, invariants preserved:** pass 1's per-unit charge test (kept "real unit count ×
rate, derived not stored"; dropped "+ 23% VAT"; added a non-vacuity assertion that the plan still carries
`vat_pct = 23`), pass 3's page test (kept "the right view per shape"; swapped the fixed-VAT claim for the
deferral), and pass 2's refusal test (kept "an undeclared convention refuses"; it now unsets the convention
explicitly rather than relying on a default that the ruling changed).

**Flagged, not defaulted — `DO-BILL-1`:** `organizations.billing_vat_id` is collected in-app but used only for
PDF letterheads and **never sent to Stripe**. Stripe now asks again via `tax_id_collection`; a customer who
skips it there pays VAT they could have reverse-charged. Syncing it onto the Stripe customer is a follow-up.

**⛔ Founder steps remaining:** enable **Stripe Tax** + register jurisdictions in the dashboard (⚠️ `automatic_tax`
is **inert** until then — a per-unit customer would be charged the pre-tax subtotal with no tax added); create
the Prices (per-unit at **€9.00, exclusive**); fill the production env. The **super-admin plan-CRUD panel**
remains unbuilt.

Guards: `BillingStripeTaxTest` (8) — checkout on/off per shape · the flag tracks the declaration · the refusal
lifts yet still fires when unset · engine subtotal with no VAT · flat unchanged · subtotal == what reaches
Stripe · page per-unit deferral with no fixed VAT · page flat unchanged. Five mutations each red on the right
guard (drop `automatic_tax` · undeclare exclusive · re-add the hardcoded VAT · make the page print a fixed VAT ·
break subtotal-vs-Stripe). All against the FAKE client; `StripeSafetyGuard` untouched; no live key, no charge.
Suite **1987/1994** (5 non-green = the documented `BookingImportTest` set); PHPStan L5 (0); Pint clean.

## 2026-08-13 · SAVE v12 — THE BILLING WORKSTREAM IS CLOSED (docs-only consolidation)

**Chapter ⑤ closes.** The read-only investigation → pass 1 (`43862db`) → pass 3 (`615904c`) → pass 2
(`7de1f35`) → pass 2b (`9fed4a1`). **Cross-pass canon: §N.17** (seven sub-sections). **⚠️ The billing CODE is
complete and honest; the live-key flip is gated on the FOUNDER's Stripe dashboard steps, not on code.**

**The four founder rulings, all recorded in §G.1:** pricing is configurable data (both shapes) · a per-unit
subscription **prorates** immediately · **flat tiers are VAT-INCLUSIVE** (€49/€99 final) · **per-unit VAT
reaches Stripe via Stripe Tax** (`exclusive` + `automatic_tax`, reverse charge Stripe's).

**⛔ The founder's three remaining steps are DASHBOARD/ACCOUNT actions, not code:** enable Stripe Tax + register
jurisdictions (⚠️ `automatic_tax` is **inert** until then) · create the Prices · fill the production env.

**⚠️ THE HEADLINE LESSON — GIVE UP THE CLAIM, NOT THE CALCULATION.** When Stripe Tax made per-unit tax
customer-dependent, the hardcoded 23% went from *unsent* to *false*. No arithmetic could fix that, because the
right value depends on facts the app does not hold. The app stopped asserting a post-tax total and now shows the
pre-tax subtotal + "tax calculated at checkout". **Pass 2's €16.56 under-charge closed from the other end — not
by sending the 23%, but by never having claimed it.**

**⚠️ AND THE BLOCKER WAS A FRAMING ARTEFACT.** §G.1 stood open for months as a founder pricing *choice*; there
was no model to choose, only two hardcoded models coexisting. *When a blocker frames itself as "X or Y", ask
whether the fix is "stop hardcoding the choice."*

### ⚠️ A premise correction — pass 2b's cleanup verification was VACUOUS

Pass 2b reported its transient per-unit plan "reverted + verified". `Plan` uses **`SoftDeletes`**, so
`Plan::where('code', …)->delete()` soft-deleted it and `Plan::where('code', …)->count() === 0` passed **because
the same global scope hid the row from the check**. It surfaced here as a unique-key violation on a row Eloquent
insisted did not exist. ⚠️ **A cleanup check must not run through the same scope as the cleanup** — verify with a
raw query or `withTrashed()`. The leftover is now `forceDelete`d and verified with raw SQL (including that no
subscription points at a per-unit plan). *Same family as §N.4p: the verdict must come from something other than
the mechanism under test.*

## 2026-08-13 · `DO-BILL-1` — the stored VAT number reaches the Stripe customer (a money-path fix)

**The gap.** `organizations.billing_vat_id` was used for **PDF letterheads only** (pass 2b verified it by grep).
Pass 2b then turned Stripe Tax on, and Stripe Tax decides reverse charge from the **customer's** `tax_ids` — so
a business that had already given Vyrobel its number, and skipped Stripe's own prompt, was charged VAT it was
entitled to reverse-charge. The app held the answer and never passed it on.

**The fix.** `VatId` derives a **typed** Stripe tax id from a **closed** country map (`eu_vat`/`ch_vat`/`gb_vat`/
`no_vat`), returning null for anything else. `StripeTaxIdSync` is the ONE path to the customer, called from the
**three** in-app writers and **from the webhook** when a customer id first appears.

⚠️ **A premise refinement the orientation produced: the app never creates a Stripe customer** — Checkout does,
and the id arrives by webhook. So there was no pre-existing attach point, and the webhook hook is not an extra —
it is the only place a first-time customer can be reached. It also matters most: **Stripe re-computes tax on
every renewal invoice**, so a missing id would have overcharged monthly, not once.

**⚠️ The posture is asymmetric on purpose — when in doubt, CHARGE THE TAX.** Overcharging is visible and
refundable; wrongly **zero-rating** is silent and lands on the operator at an audit. So: an untypeable number is
never sent · a Stripe rejection returns false rather than throwing (a bad number must not break a subscription)
and is never treated as success · both are logged **without the value**, a customer business identifier · a
corrected number **replaces** the stale one rather than joining it.

**Reconciled with pass 2b's `tax_id_collection`, no double-set:** the stored id attaches to the customer;
Stripe's own prompt is the **fallback** for the first session, before any customer exists.

**⚠️ The guard caught the validator being too generous before it shipped.** `"not-a-vat-id"` normalises to
`NOTAVATID` — leading `NO` is **Norway** — and the body passed a bare "alphanumeric" test. Prose was one step
from reaching Stripe as a Norwegian VAT number, which is exactly the mis-typing that can be accepted and
zero-rate a taxable sale. Fixed by requiring a run of ≥4 digits. *On a tax path, an over-permissive structural
check is not a weaker guard — it is the failure mode.*

**⛔ A NEW FOUNDER DECISION — VAT VALIDATION (recorded in §G.1).** Structural ≠ valid. Implemented: send as-is
and let Stripe validate against VIES **asynchronously** (so a sale can be zero-rated before validation
completes). The alternative — require VIES validation first — is safer but is a build with a new "pending
validation" state. **Flagged, not guessed; the safe half is implemented either way.**

**Scope held:** the PDF letterhead use is untouched (asserted) · engine, page and the unbuilt panel untouched ·
display = charge = Stripe still holds — the app forwards a fact to Stripe and still asserts only the pre-tax
subtotal; it computes no reverse-charge total of its own (asserted).

Guarded by `BillingVatIdSyncTest` (8/22), mutation-proven four ways, all against the FAKE client. Billing family
**129/129**. Suite **1999/2006**, 7 non-green = the documented set. ⚠️ **One earlier run of the same commit
showed an 8th non-green that did NOT reproduce on two subsequent runs and could not be identified** — recorded
as an unexplained range-walk (§N.17.7 / the (J) 5–10 range), **not** claimed as proven pre-existing. PHPStan L5
(0); Pint clean.

## 2026-08-13 · THE SUPER-ADMIN PLAN PANEL — terms freeze, quantity stays live (the last billing build)

**Two founder rulings, recorded and built to:** **full CRUD** of plans of BOTH shapes from the platform-admin
console; **edits affect NEW subscriptions only — existing subscribers keep their terms.**

**⚠️ THE PREMISE CHECK CHANGED THE PASS.** The panel was specified as missing. It was not: `index`/`edit`/
`update`/`toggle` already existed, platform-admin gated and audited. Missing were **create**, **shape-awareness**
(`update` validated only `name` + `price`, so a per-unit plan could be saved with **no rate**), and any notion of
**sellable**.

**⚠️ AND THE RULING WAS UNENFORCEABLE — WITH A LIVE SURFACE ALREADY ABLE TO VIOLATE IT.** `subscriptions` stored
only `plan_id`, so every displayed price came from the LIVE plan row, and `update()` could already change it on
a plan with subscribers.

⚠️ **The failure mode was not the obvious one.** Stripe bills an existing subscription against the **Stripe
Price object** it was created with, and nothing here pushes a rate change to it — so an edit would **not** have
re-priced anyone. It would have changed only what Vyrobel *displays*, leaving the product quoting one figure
while Stripe charged another: **the display ≠ charge divergence, re-opened from the admin side.**

### What was built
- **`PlanTerms`** — the ONE charge calculation. `Plan::chargeFor()` now delegates to it, and a subscription's
  captured terms use the same method. Two sources, one arithmetic (§N.8f; §N.17.4 is what happens otherwise).
- **Captured terms on `subscriptions`** (+ a **backfill** for every existing row, so the ruling protects the
  customers already on the books rather than only future ones). ⚠️ **Quantity stays DERIVED, terms FREEZE** —
  billing pass 1's derived-not-stored rule inverted for the half that must not move.
- **`PlanIntegrity`** — one ruleset for create and edit; `pricing_type` a closed set; a per-unit plan needs a
  rate **> 0** (a zero rate silently bills nothing); and **a plan without a real Stripe Price cannot be
  activated**. Pass 2 catches a Price-less plan at the till; this catches it at the shelf.
- **Create (both shapes)** + a shape-keyed form, a draft banner, and the "new subscriptions only" note stated on
  the edit form itself.

### ⚠️ Enumerating writers is a losing game — bind the behaviour to the model

Capture was first wired at each **known** call site. Verifying `migrate:fresh --seed` then showed the demo
subscription with **null terms**, because `DemoSeeder` creates rows directly and was a call site nobody listed.
This is `DO-BILL-1`'s three-writers lesson (§N.18.3) recurring inside one pass — and it upgrades the remedy:
capture moved onto the model's `creating`/`updating` hooks, so **every** path captures, including ones not
written yet. ⚠️ Caught by checking the database after the seed, not by a test.

**G8 — two pre-existing `PlatformPlansTest` cases legitimately changed.** Their fixture had no `pricing_type`
and no `stripe_price_id`, and their payloads sent only `name` + `price`. The **invariants were preserved and the
fixtures amended**: the fixture now describes a plan that can really be sold, and the payloads carry the shape.

**Scope:** the engine's calculation, the customer pages and `StripeSafetyGuard` are untouched; the panel writes
plans the engine reads. No live Stripe Price is created — that remains the founder's step.

Guards: `AdminPlanPanelTest` (9/29) — super-admin only (**both** roles asserted) · well-formed-or-rejected ×3 ·
per-unit create · not-billable-without-a-Price · **edits-affect-new-only** (a plan doubled under a live
subscriber, who still bills €49.00 while a new subscription gets €98.00) · trial captures at creation · display
= charge. Mutation-proven five ways, each red on its guard; teardown verified with a **raw** query (§N.18.1).
Browser-verified as the platform admin: both shapes, a per-unit plan created end-to-end as a **draft** with the
"no Stripe Price id yet" banner.

Suite **2008/2015 · 13,079 assertions**, **7 non-green = the documented set**. PHPStan L5 (0); Pint clean;
`migrate:fresh --seed` clean (⚠️ it needs Mailpit running — a seed abort without it is environmental, not a
regression).

## 2026-08-13 · SAVE v14 — 🏁 THE BILLING BUILD IS COMPLETE (docs-only consolidation)

**Chapter ⑦ closes** with the super-admin plan panel (`f389317`). **Canon: §N.19** (six sub-sections).
⚠️ **v13 recorded the billing CODE complete; that was accurate but incomplete — one build was outstanding.
Both halves are now done, and nothing billing-related remains to write.**

### The four syntheses folded into §N.19

1. ⚠️ **AN ADMIN EDIT CAN RE-OPEN `display ≠ charge` FROM THE OTHER SIDE.** The obvious risk — an edit
   re-pricing existing subscribers — was **not** the real one: Stripe bills against the Price object the
   subscription was created with and nothing pushes a rate change to it. What an edit *would* have changed is
   only what **Vyrobel displays**, leaving the product quoting one figure while Stripe charged another. The fix
   is not "don't re-price"; it is **"don't let display and charge diverge."**
2. ⚠️ **TERMS FREEZE, QUANTITY STAYS LIVE** — billing pass 1's derived-not-stored rule inverted for the half
   that must not move. `PlanTerms` is the ONE calculation both `Plan::chargeFor()` and captured terms delegate
   to, so §N.8f survives the freeze: **one arithmetic, frozen-vs-live inputs, never two pricing logics.**
   Existing subscriptions were **backfilled** — a capture that only worked going forward would have left every
   current customer exposed.
3. ⚠️ **PUT THE INVARIANT ON THE MODEL'S LIFECYCLE HOOKS, NOT AT EACH CALL SITE.** `DO-BILL-1`'s three-writers
   lesson recurring *inside one pass*, and upgraded: `DemoSeeder` was the writer nobody listed, so capture moved
   onto `creating`/`updating` and **no path can bypass it, including ones not written yet.** ⚠️ Caught by
   **checking the database after the seed**, not by a test — a test over the known call sites would have been
   green while the seeder wrote nulls.
4. ⚠️ **WELL-FORMED OR REJECTED, AT THE SHELF *AND* THE TILL.** `PlanIntegrity` — one ruleset for create and
   edit, `pricing_type` a closed set, a per-unit rate **> 0** (zero silently bills nothing), and no activation
   without a real Stripe Price. Pass 2 catches a Price-less plan at the **till**; this catches it at the
   **shelf**.

⚠️ **AND THE CAPSTONE (§N.19.6): an invariant is only as strong as the set of ACTORS it was checked against.**
The billing passes checked the customer, the webhook and Stripe — never the platform admin, a different realm
writing the very rows the whole chain reads. **A fourth way a defect hides**, beside conditional STATE,
AUTHORIZATION and DATA (§N.16.2): **ACTOR** — the surface was neither hidden nor conditional; it belonged to
somebody the pass was not thinking about.

### ⛔ What remains — none of it code, and none of it billing

The founder's **Stripe dashboard steps** (enable Stripe Tax + register jurisdictions — ⚠️ `automatic_tax` is
**inert** until then; create the Prices; fill prod env) and the open **VAT-VALIDATION decision** (send-as-is,
implemented, vs VIES-first, a build needing a "pending validation" state — ⚠️ a session must not pick the second
unilaterally). The pre-billing tail is now the only outstanding *build* work: `DO-TOKEN-1` ·
`DO-EMAIL-5-continued` · `DO-STAR-1` · `DO-SUP-1`.

**§N.8f applied to the palette.** Four shells — guest, owner, operator and the public storefront — each
re-declared the whole palette, so every shared token had four independent definitions and any one could drift.
That is not hypothetical: `--vy-amber-text` did exactly that (DO-EMAIL-4). The 31 shared tokens now live in
`resources/views/components/design/tokens.blade.php`, included by every shell **before** its own `<style>`.

**⚠️ Inventory re-verified, with a correction.** 31 shared and 7 divergent as recorded — but **11 single-shell,
not 13** (49 tokens, not 51). The `a5212aa` inventory had drifted.

**⚠️ All 7 divergences confirmed DELIBERATE, and preserved as declared overrides.** The 5 guest tokens
(`--vy-r-lg` 18px, `--vy-r-sm` 9px, a lighter `--vy-shadow` and `--vy-shadow-accent`, a warm-brown
`--vy-glass-border`) move **consistently in one direction** — smaller, softer, warmer. *Drift produces arbitrary
differences; theming produces a direction.* The `--vy-on-grad` pair carries a **measured** justification in
source: each is computed against its own shell's page gradient (§N.4i/§N.4j), so unifying them would break AA on
one of the two. None was accidental, so none was flattened.

**⚠️ A category the inventory did not have: a DYNAMIC override.** The guest shell conditionally re-declares
`--vy-accent`/`--vy-shadow-accent` from a validated property brand accent (#98), emitted after the main style.
Not drift, not static theming — a runtime override, and correctly left alone.

### ⚠️ No visual change, proven — zero value changes across all four shells

Every palette token's **resolved** value (`getComputedStyle`, §N.8e) was captured in a real browser on the clean
worktree and again after: **guest 21, operator 41, owner 43, public 24 — parse and render agreeing exactly in
every shell**, then **0 tokens changed value and 0 were lost**. All four shells landed together; the pass was
never half-applied.

⚠️ **THE PROBE FAILED FIRST, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS TRUSTWORTHY NOW.** The initial token list was hand-typed: it
invented seven tokens that do not exist and omitted thirteen that do (`--vy-r-pill`, `--vy-peach`, `--vy-orb-*`,
`--vy-hk-*`, `--vy-shadow-sm/dark`, `--vy-muted-on-dark`). It was caught because parsed and resolved counts
disagreed. **Regenerated programmatically, and only then did the two agree.** §N.8e: when the probe is wrong,
publish nothing.

### ⚠️ One real rendering consequence, found by the proof and reported rather than buried

The base now provides **30 tokens that some shells never declared**. Inert almost everywhere — no shell's own
CSS references a token it did not declare — but page content is also inside these shells, so each was checked:
- guest `var(--vy-r-pill, 30px)` — the fallback **is** the shared value. No change.
- `guest/auth/layout.blade.php` — a **standalone** layout with its own `:root`. Unaffected.
- ⚠️ **public `booking/room.blade.php` uses `background: var(--vy-wash)`, and the public shell never declared
  `--vy-wash`** — so the declaration was invalid at computed-value time and the review-response box rendered
  **transparent**. It now resolves to `#F6EBE2`. **A latent defect the refactor fixes**: the author plainly
  intended the cream wash and it silently did nothing. Recorded as the single behavioural delta of this pass.

### G8 — three existing guards legitimately changed

`AmberTextTokenTest`, `DesignTokenContrastTest` and `OperatorOwnerGreyDriftTest` all read the **shell files** for
token values that have moved. ⚠️ **`AmberTextTokenTest`'s own non-vacuity message fired** — *"the token is no
longer declared — this guard would pass on nothing"* — which is the guard working, not failing. Amended:
the contrast and grey sweeps now compose **base + shell** (the cascade a browser actually sees), and the amber
guard's assertion went from *"≥2 declarations, all equal"* to **"exactly 1"** — *strictly stronger*, because
one-value-everywhere stopped being something to check and became a property of the structure.

**Guard:** `DesignTokenSourceTest` (4/46) — reads the **rendered response** and computes the cascade, never the

(including operator's `--vy-on-grad` staying operator's) · **the base is included BEFORE the shell's styles**,

## 2026-08-13 · `DO-STAR-1` — the Messages star: a bookmark, and the name was the defect

**Premise sharpened:** the star is in the **OWNER** realm (`/owner/messages`, `MessageStar`), not the guest relay.

### ⚠️ The conflation check — NOT conflated, and the state was already greyscale-safe

The register flagged this because DO10-4 had just fixed the RATING star. The bookmark **never touches**
`<x-star-rating>` — it is its own inline SVG — and its state is carried by the **GLYPH**: `fill="#E8A63A"` when
starred, `fill="none"` when not. **Filled vs outline is a shape difference, verified in a greyscale capture**,
so the colour-only failure DO10-4 had to fix for ratings **does not exist here**. That half is verified-fine.

### ⚠️ What was actually wrong — and it is an unusually instructive shape

`aria-label="Star"` was **static on both states**, and `aria-label` **overrides** `title` — which was correctly
computed as `"Unstar"` when starred. **A screen-reader user heard "Star" on a button that would unstar.** The
right words were already being derived and were discarded one attribute later. *The information existed; the
markup threw it away.* Fixed with `aria-pressed` plus a stable name (`"Star message"`), the standard toggle
pattern, so the state is announced rather than smuggled into a name that then contradicts the action.

### ⚠️ A second defect the measurement found — hover-only visibility (WCAG 2.4.7)

`.vy-msg-acts { opacity: 0 }` with only a `:hover` rule and **no `:focus-within`**. Measured live: the star
button takes focus (`document.activeElement`, outline `auto`) while its container is fully transparent — **a
keyboard user tabs to a real button and sees neither it nor its focus ring.** Hover-only makes a control
mouse-only in practice while leaving it in the tab order: the worst of both. Fixed by adding `:focus-within`.

**The PIN toggle is the star's twin** — same computed-then-discarded `title`, same static label — and got the
same fix; **Reply and React are not toggles** (no state) so their static labels are correct and were left alone.

### ⚠️ Two measurement notes worth keeping
