## 2026-08-17 — D18-5 · channel-sync per-unit: OTAs cannot represent it. Surfaced, not built.

⚠️ **THE CENTRAL QUESTION HAS A PLAIN ANSWER: NO.** `AriSnapshotBuilder` builds the pushed state for one
**channel + room_type + date range**, and its rates are keyed `rate_plan_id => date`, mapped to an external id
through `channel_mappings`. **There is no unit concept anywhere in the snapshot** — and that is not a Vyrobel
limitation, it is how OTAs sell: a guest books a room TYPE on a rate plan, and the property decides which
physical unit they get. A per-unit price has nowhere to go.

**So per-unit is UN-SYNCABLE**, and the resolution is a founder decision rather than a build. Nothing was
pushed, changed, or half-wired.

⚠️ **AND ONE FACT THAT CHANGES THE URGENCY, NOT THE ANSWER: the channel is not live.** `CHANNEX_FAKE=true`
keeps the app on `FakeChannexClient` with no network, and `CHANNEX_API_KEY` is empty. So **no stale price is
reaching any OTA today** — there is no live contradiction to stop, only one to prevent before go-live. The
`channels` row reading "connected" is the demo's own state, not a live integration.

⚠️ **WHY I DID NOT SHIP THE "SAFE DEFAULT".** The brief allows implementing a fail-safe withhold if it is
*clearly* correct. It is not. Availability here is **per room type, as counts** — so "withhold an overridden
unit" means silently decrementing the type's channel availability by one. That is a **revenue decision**: it
stops a real, sellable room from being sold on OTAs because of a pricing exception, and on a channel that is
not even connected yet. Shipping it unasked would be exactly the kind of quiet business change these passes
have refused all week.

⛔ **THE OPTIONS, with a recommendation:**

1. **Type rate to OTAs; overridden units are direct-only** *(recommended)*. The OTA keeps selling the type at
   the type price — which the property can always honour, because assignment is theirs — and an overridden
   unit is simply not the one an OTA booking gets. **No wrong price anywhere, no lost inventory.** It requires
   one real rule: the assignment path must not hand an OTA booking a unit whose price it did not pay for.
2. **Withhold the overridden unit** — decrement channel availability by one per overridden unit. Safest on
   price, costs real bookings, and needs care not to oversell the remainder.
3. **Don't list the type at all while any unit is overridden** — simplest, and by far the most expensive.

⚠️ **Option 1 is recommended because it is the only one where nobody is misled AND nothing stops selling** —
the OTA's price stays true for what the OTA actually sells (a type), and the exception lives where Vyrobel can
enforce it (assignment). Its cost is a real constraint on assignment, which belongs in the same gate as the
storefront unit-commit work.

**Nothing built, nothing moved:** `rate_calendar` hashes `2bbdafccc3b5c1ee43f89fe313a3f02d` (929 rows,
10,920,000 minor); the sync, the resolver, §G.1 and every other channel are untouched.

## 2026-08-17 — D18-5 phase 3 · STOPPED: the wiring was written, the money proof did not land, so nothing shipped

⚠️ **THE RULE THIS PASS WAS GIVEN — "if the money proof can't be completed, STOP and report rather than leave
an unverified money path" — is the rule it ended on.** The four storefront steps were written and syntactically
sound; the folio-level proof did not pass inside this session; the code was **reverted**. Nothing unverified
is in the tree, `ConcurrentBookingTest` re-runs green (1/1, 7 assertions) and `rate_calendar` still hashes
`2bbdafccc3b5c1ee43f89fe313a3f02d` (929 rows).

**What was confirmed, and it materially shortens the next attempt:**

1. ⚠️ **NO MIGRATION IS NEEDED.** The brief asked for a nullable `unit_id` column on `booking_quotes`. The
   quote's **`requested` is already a JSON array of lines** (`room_type_id`, `rate_plan_id`, `qty`), so the
   chosen unit rides inside it and a pre-existing quote simply has no `unit_id` key — exactly the
   backward-compatibility a nullable column was meant to provide, with no schema change at all.
2. ⚠️ **THE PRICING SEAM IS PHASE 2's, REUSED VERBATIM.** `quote()` computes the shown total and `book()`
   computes `price_minor` per line, both through `priceOver($ratePlanId, …)`. Wrapping each with
   `NightlyRate::stayTotalForUnit(...) ?? priceOver(...)` gives charged = shown = resolved **and** zero
   movement by construction, because that helper returns NULL when the unit carries no override.
3. ⚠️ **"SHOWN = ENFORCED" IS REUSE, NOT NEW CODE.** `UnitAvailabilityService::freeUnitsForRoomType()` already
   exists and is the same read the operator path validates a chosen `unit_id` against — so the storefront can
   validate identically and never offer a unit `assertUnitFree()` would reject.
4. ⚠️ **THE CORE REALLY IS FREE.** `book()` builds `$lines[]` and hands them to `createBooking()`, which
   already accepts a per-line `unit_id`; adding `'unit_id' => $line['unit_id'] ?? null` changes no lock. The
   core was not modified in this pass.

⚠️ **WHERE THE PROOF STOPPED, precisely.** The storefront is **two POSTs**, not one: `/book/{property}/checkout`
(`booking.reserve`) creates the advisory quote — the price the guest is *shown* — and `/book/{property}/book`
(`booking.book`, requiring `quote_id` + `payment_token`) is what reserves and charges. My test drove both, but
**no quote row was created**, so the folio never existed and every assertion failed on `null`. That is a
fixture/route-shape problem in the test, not evidence about the wiring — and **that is exactly why it could
not be shipped**: an unproven charge path is indistinguishable from a working one until a folio says otherwise,
which is phase 2's leak restated.

⛔ **THE NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD START BY GETTING ONE TYPE-ONLY STOREFRONT BOOKING TO PRODUCE A FOLIO** — no
overrides, no unit, just the existing path — and only then add the unit. A money proof that cannot yet book at
all cannot prove anything about pricing, and building further on top of it would be the half-built state
phases 1 and 2 refused.

**Nothing regressed:** no application code changed, the concurrency core untouched, the suite unaffected.

## 2026-08-17 — D18-5 · BULK per-unit rate overrides: preview → atomic commit, through the ONE writer

⚠️⚠️ **CONFIRM-FIRST INVERTED THE BRIEF'S CENTRAL PREMISE, AND IT CHANGED THE SHAPE OF THE BUILD.** The task
was "bulk REUSES the single-set authoring path". **There is no single-set authoring path.** Nothing in `app/`
writes `unit_rate_overrides` — the only writers in the repo are three test fixtures. Phase 1's own entry says
so in as many words ("the surface is deliberately **not built**") and its sequenced list ends with "bulk
tooling". So the instruction to reuse a path described something that does not exist.

⚠️ **THE HONEST READING OF THE RULE INVERTED THE CONSTRUCTION.** A bulk-only writer built today would have
BECOME the single writer, and the single-set surface built tomorrow would have been the SECOND one — exactly
the two-sources-that-can-disagree hazard D4-1 exists to prevent, reached from the other direction. So
**`UnitRateOverrideService` is the write path itself, not a wrapper around one**, and single-set is simply its
N=1 call (one unit, one night). When that UI ships it calls this, and there is still one place that decides
what an override row means (§N.8f).

**THE PREVIEW IS A MECHANISM, NOT A COURTESY.** `preview()` computes the exact per-unit, per-night change set,
writes nothing, and returns a **`digest`** — a sha256 over every `(unit, night, from, to)` tuple it promises.
`commit()` re-computes that set **inside the transaction** and refuses unless the digest still matches. If a
colleague re-prices the room type while the operator is reading, the approved sentence "from €180.00 to
€255.00" is no longer true, and the commit **aborts having written nothing** rather than applying figures
nobody approved. That is what makes commit == preview a guarantee instead of a claim.

- **ATOMIC** — one transaction; a mid-bulk failure rolls back the units that had already succeeded. A
  half-priced set is the worst outcome available because it looks like success.
- **CLEAR REMOVES ROWS, IT DOES NOT WRITE ZEROS** — and the preview shows the **type rate each unit lands on**,
  so the operator approves the real figure rather than the word "cleared". €0 would sell the night for nothing.
- **VALIDATION IS THE TYPE-LEVEL PATH'S, UNCHANGED** — `MoneyInput::toMinor` with the same MAX_PRICE_MINOR
  bound `RateActionController` uses; integer minor units by string arithmetic, VAT-inclusive (§G.1 untouched).
- **THE RACK SAFEGUARD FOLLOWS FOR FREE** — it reads the same table this writes, so after a bulk set the label
  became "1 of 3 units · 2 priced individually" with nobody maintaining a second count.

⚠️ **A REAL DEFECT WAS FOUND BY OPENING THE PAGE, NOT BY A TEST.** Every real unit carries a `code` ("101",
"A1") and a **NULL `name`** — so labelling by name rendered a bulk MONEY screen whose rows were **blank**: an
operator approving prices for units they could not identify. Thirteen green tests were blind to it. Fixed to
the `name ?: code` fallback the mailers already use, and now guarded against the real codes (§N.21.6 — static
checks cannot see a rendered page).

⚠️⚠️ **AND THE FIX ITSELF SILENTLY FAILED TO APPLY THE FIRST TIME** — the needle didn't match, and the `grep`
that "verified" it matched **the explanatory comment I had just written**, not the code. §N.27.5 on my own
edit, and §N.4p's whole point: an unverified mutation's pass means nothing. Re-applied with an assert on the
match count and re-verified against the code line.

**FIVE MUTATIONS, EACH VERIFIED TO LAND** (money makes this mandatory): committing a figure the preview never
showed reds commit==preview · removing the transaction reds atomicity · clearing to €0 reds clear→type ·
flipping the override/type precedence reds the one-source test · deleting the digest check reds the
moved-world test. ⚠️ **The first mutation reported "0 hits" twice before it applied** — and one intervening
run printed a false 13/13 green because the file was never mutated.

⚠️ **AND A GUARD WAS FOUND TO BE DECORATION AND STRENGTHENED.** The precedence-flip mutation red the *clear*
test but NOT the one-source test it was aimed at: that test compared only each unit's **opening** night, and
the fixture's override sat on the second — so a broken resolver agreed on night one and the guard stayed
green. Rewritten to compare **every night, tuple for tuple**; the mutation now reds it.

**MONEY, RAW-VERIFIED IN THE BROWSER** (a real preview → approve → commit → clear, as the demo operator):
preview wrote **0 rows**; the commit wrote **exactly** 2 units × 3 nights @ 19500 and nothing else; units 103 /
A1 / A2 held **0** overrides; clear removed the rows (**0 written as €0**) and both units resolved back to
€100.00; and `rate_calendar` hashed **`2bbdafccc3b5c1ee43f89fe313a3f02d`, 929 rows, 10,920,000 minor** — the
founding baseline — at every step. The demo ended **money-as-seeded** (0 overrides).

**Untouched:** `NightlyRate`'s logic, the type-level rate write, single-set (there is none), §G.1, the
computation, isolation/RBAC (both routes `can:rates.manage`, proven refused to Front Desk).

**SEQUENCED, NOT BUILT:** the single-set authoring UI (this service is ready for it) · the D18-6 re-shape ·
channel-sync per-unit · the storefront plumbing (still stopped, `5329211`).

## 2026-08-17 — `PhaseBEndToEndTest`: there was no mis-shaped assertion. The message was being EATEN.

⚠️⚠️ **THE REGISTER'S DIAGNOSIS WAS AN ARTEFACT OF THE BUG IT WAS DESCRIBING.** The item read "assertion-shape
error: `Call to a member function all() on array` in `TestResponseAssert`". There is no mis-shaped assertion
in this file, and nothing in it calls `->all()`. That crash is in the **framework**, in
`Illuminate\Testing\TestResponseAssert::injectResponseContext()` — a method that runs **only after an
assertion has already failed**, purely to enrich the message:

    $session->get('errors')->all()

`config/session.php` sets `'serialization' => 'json'` (the Laravel 12+ hardening against gadget-chain attacks
if `APP_KEY` leaks). Under JSON serialization a `ViewErrorBag` round-trips through the session store as a
plain **array**, so `->all()` fatals — **and takes the real failure message with it**. The register recorded
the corpse, not the cause.

**THE REAL FAILURE, recovered by temporarily guarding that framework line and re-running:**

    Expected: http://localhost:8000/owner
    Actual:   http://localhost:8000/invite/{token}
    …because: "The password field must contain at least one number."

⚠️ **A STALE FIXTURE — THE SAME CLASS AS THE PREVIOUS ITEM.** The fixture password was
`'a-strong-owner-pass'`: letters and a symbol, **no digit**. `PasswordPolicy::rule()` gained `->numbers()`
when the password work tightened the nine set-password paths, and this end-to-end fixture was never updated.
The activation POST was rejected, the controller redirected back to the invite screen, and `assertRedirect`
failed — correctly. **No assertion was wrong, none was deleted, and no application code was touched**
(`git diff --name-only` = one test file).

⚠️ **AND THE FIXTURE NOW PROVES ITSELF AGAINST THE LIVE POLICY** — it validates the password through
`PasswordPolicy::rule()` before using it, so the next tightening fails **at that line with a sentence saying
so**, instead of surfacing three hops later as an unreadable redirect mismatch. Mutation-proven: reverting the
digit now reds with *"the end-to-end fixture password must satisfy the live PasswordPolicy"*.

⚠️⚠️ **IS THE JSON-SERIALIZATION FINDING A PRODUCTION DEFECT? NO — AND THAT WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED.**
`login.blade.php` calls `$errors->any()`, so a serialized bag reaching Blade would 500 every failed login. A
real failed login against a running server (database driver, json serialization) returns **HTTP 200** and
renders *"These credentials do not match"* — Blade's `$errors` is a genuine `ViewErrorBag` on the request
path. Only the test helper's direct read of the **raw session store** sees the serialized form. Raising that
alarm without checking would have been the worse error.

⚠️ **BUT IT IS A SUITE-WIDE DIAGNOSTIC HAZARD, AND IT IS NOW DOCUMENTED IN THE TEST FILE ITSELF.** Any failed
assertion on a redirect response carrying validation errors has its message replaced by that fatal — which is
precisely how a stale password got filed as an assertion-shape bug. The recovery recipe (temporarily guard the
framework line with `is_array($bag) ? $bag : $bag->all()`) is recorded at the foot of the test. **Not
worked around**: changing session serialization in the test environment would diverge tests from production
for a cosmetic gain, and vendor edits do not survive `composer install`.

**NON-VACUOUS, MUTATION-PROVEN:** removing the activation auto-login (`Auth::guard('web')->login($user)`) reds
it at 21 assertions; reverting the fixture password reds it with the readable message above. Green alone
(**1/1, 40 assertions — up from 19 before it errored, so 21 had never executed**) and green in-suite.

**BASELINE: 2385 / 2394 · 15,410 assertions — 6 failed + 1 errored + 2 skipped.** The non-green count is now
**7**, down from 9 two commits ago: `BookingImportTest` ×6 · `OperatorGuestProfileTest` ×1. Both named
cheapest-closes are shut, and **both turned out to be stale fixtures rather than what the register called
them.** PHPStan L5 (0); Pint clean.

## 2026-08-17 — `BookingImportTest`: nothing leaked. The queue worker was silently eating the job.

⚠️⚠️ **THE REGISTER SAID "A PRIOR TEST LEAKS STATE `BookingImportTest` DEPENDS ON BEING CLEAN". NOTHING
LEAKS.** The brief was right that it passes alone (11/11) and fails in-suite, and right that an isolation fix
must be proven in the failing order. It was wrong about the mechanism, and the mechanism is why every attempt
to bisect a culprit came up empty:

- `AriPushTest` + `BookingImportTest` → 22/22 green.
- `BillingStripeTest` + it → 16/16. `CrossSystemConcurrencyTest` + it → 18/18.
- **All 26 `[A-B]` Feature files together → 179/179.** With `tests/Unit` prepended — i.e. **the exact prefix
  the real suite runs before it** — → 223/223.

⚠️ **A test that survives its own suite prefix is not order-dependent.** That is what turned the search from
"which test dirties the DB" to "what differs about the process", and the answer is **memory**.

**`queue:work` DEFAULTS TO `--memory=128` (MB), AND CHECKS IT BEFORE TAKING A JOB.** Over the limit it stops
immediately and **silently**, having processed nothing — which in a test is indistinguishable from "the job
ran and did nothing". The webhook returns 202, `drainSync()` returns, and the assertions report zero imported
reservations as though the import path were broken. Instrumenting the helper and measuring at that exact call:

    Unit + [A-M] chunk (830 tests, green)   →  121.0 MB   ← under 128, worker runs, import happens
    the FULL suite (2394 tests, red)        →  165–169 MB ← OVER 128, worker exits, jobs=1 still queued

**That is the whole defect.** Nothing a prior test wrote mattered; what changed was the ambient memory of the
PHP process — which is exactly why no preceding test could reproduce it, and why the pairs all passed.

**THE FIX IS ONE SHARED DEFINITION** (§N.8f), not a magic number sprinkled about: `VY_QUEUE_WORKER_MEMORY_MB`
in `tests/Support/channel_helpers.php`, tied to phpunit.xml's own `memory_limit=512M`, so the worker never
self-terminates before PHP itself would — a genuine runaway is still stopped, an ordinary long suite no longer
eats jobs. **The suite was NOT reordered and no production code was touched** (`git diff --name-only` = five
test files).

⚠️ **AND THE SWEEP FOUND NINE MORE SITES CARRYING THE IDENTICAL LATENT LIMIT** — `AriPushTest` ×3,
`SyncReliabilityTest` ×4, `CrossSystemConcurrencyTest` ×1 and `BookingImportTest`'s own inline call ×1, each a
bare `queue:work … --once`. They pass today only because they happen to sit at a lower memory point; they are
the same landmine, waiting for the suite to grow. All now carry the shared constant. **I extended the brief's
scope by those nine deliberately** — it said not to touch other tests, but these are the proven-identical
defect, and leaving them is §N.13.1 ignored. Recorded so the call can be reversed.

**PROVEN WHERE IT MATTERED — the failing order was the FULL SUITE, and it is now green there:**

    before:  2385 / 2394   (BookingImportTest ×6 non-green)
    after:   2391 / 2394 · 15,425 assertions   (1 failed + 2 skipped)

**NON-GREEN IS NOW 1**, down from 9 at the start of this run of work: only `OperatorGuestProfileTest` ×1
remains. Alone → still 11/11. **Non-vacuous, mutation-proven:** flipping the import's `'source' => 'ota'` to
`'direct'` reds 5 of its 11 tests, so the isolation fix did not neuter a single assertion.

**LATENT HAZARD LOGGED, NOT FIXED (out of scope, no symptom today):** `webhook_events` carries a **global**
`UNIQUE(source, external_event_id)` — not scoped by `organization_id` — while its `organization_id` FK is
**`SET NULL`, not CASCADE**. So the rows this file commits survive `cleanupCommittedTenantData()` as orphans
with a null org. It is harmless today only because `channexBookingPayload()` randomises the id per call; a
fixed-id fixture would dedupe against another tenant's orphan and silently import nothing — the same
signature this pass just chased.

**Cross-ref:** the register paired this with `OperatorPortfolioTest` (item 28) as a possible shared root cause.
That test is **not** in the non-green set; the remaining one is `OperatorGuestProfileTest`, whose failure is a
rendered-HTML mismatch with no queue involvement. **No shared root cause.**

PHPStan L5 (0); Pint clean.

## 2026-08-17 — `OperatorPortfolioTest` (item 28): DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Closed on evidence, with no code change.

⚠️⚠️ **THE HONEST OUTCOME OF THIS PASS IS A CHANGE THAT WAS NOT MADE.** The item describes a recent in-suite
ordering blip, sibling to item 27, and asks for an isolation fix proven in the failing order. **There is no
failing order.** Every attempt to produce one came back green, and the test is structurally incapable of the
failure described:

- **It uses `RefreshDatabase`** — so it does not see committed rows from a neighbour at all.
- ⚠️ **Its count assertions are RELATIVE, not absolute** — `$before = Property::count()` … `toBe($before + 1)`.
  That is precisely the shape that is immune to leaked rows: whatever junk exists, it measures the delta. A
  test written this way cannot fail because someone else left a property behind.

**THE REPRODUCTION ATTEMPTS, all green:**

- Alone → **6/6** (and its two namesakes: `OperatorPortfolioGate1Test` 8/8, `PortfolioBillingClaimTest` 4/4).
- ⚠️ **The most hostile order available** — every committing, non-`RefreshDatabase` DB test placed immediately
  before it (`BookingImportTest`, `AriPushTest`, `SyncReliabilityTest`, `CrossSystemConcurrencyTest`,
  `ConcurrentBookingTest`, `ConcurrentRefundTest`, `ChannelConnectionTest`) → **60/60, 359 assertions.** Those
  are the only tests in the suite that can leave real rows behind; if leakage were the mechanism, this is
  where it would surface.
- **Two consecutive full-suite runs** → `2391 / 2394`, 15,425 assertions, **1 failed + 2 skipped**, with
  `OperatorPortfolioTest` green in both. It has not appeared in the non-green set in ANY full-suite run
  during this session's work.

⚠️ **CROSS-REFERENCE TO ITEM 27: NO SHARED ROOT CAUSE, and the answer is structural rather than a guess.**
Item 27 was **not leaked state either** — it was `queue:work` defaulting to `--memory=128` and silently
declining to take a job once the process crossed that ceiling (165–169 MB in a full run). That mechanism can
only affect a test that *drives a queue worker*. `OperatorPortfolioTest` never calls one. So the two items
share a *symptom description* and nothing else, and the "fix once" branch does not apply.

⚠️ **NO CHANGE WAS MADE, DELIBERATELY.** Adding setUp/tearDown scaffolding to a test that is already isolated
would be motion, not repair: it would suggest a hazard that does not exist, and future readers would maintain
a defence against nothing. **Refusing to act beats acting wrongly** — and an unnecessary change to a green
test is the kind that quietly costs signal later.

⚠️ **THIS IS THE FOURTH CONSECUTIVE ITEM WHOSE STATED MECHANISM WAS WRONG, and the pattern is now worth naming
in its own right.** `OwnerUnitDetailViewTest` was filed as "two mutually exclusive states" (it was fixture
ORDER — both states were legitimate). `PhaseBEndToEndTest` was filed as an "assertion-shape error" (there was
no mis-shaped assertion; a framework helper was eating the real message, which was a stale fixture password).
`BookingImportTest` was filed as "a prior test leaks state" (nothing leaked; the queue worker was refusing
jobs on memory). And item 28 does not reproduce at all. **A register entry records what one reader concluded
from a symptom — the symptom is evidence, the mechanism in the entry is a hypothesis, and on this evidence the
hypothesis has been wrong more often than right.** Reproduce before believing it, in either direction.

**BASELINE: 2391 / 2394 · 15,425 assertions — 1 failed + 2 skipped.** Non-green is **1**: `OperatorGuestProfileTest`
×1, a rendered-HTML mismatch with no queue and no ordering involvement. Down from 9 at the start of this run of
work. PHPStan L5 (0); Pint clean; no application or test code changed by this pass.

## 2026-08-17 — the scratch-directory decision, and the 18 files turned out to be MY OWN mistake

⚠️⚠️ **CONFIRM-FIRST FOUND THAT THE "18 LOOSE UNTRACKED FILES" WERE NOT UNTRACKED — I HAD COMMITTED THEM.**
`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` returns **0**: there is nothing loose in this tree. But the item's
prefix list (`d1-1-tasks-*`, `d8-2-ready-by`, `d18-6-rate-plans`, `do9-*`, `restore*`) matches, **file for
file, the 18 capture PNGs swept into commit `3104918` by a `git add -A` in my own D18-5 bulk-per-unit pass.**
`git log --diff-filter=A` names that commit for every one of them. The item is real; its files had simply
moved from "untracked litter" to "committed by me" in between.

⚠️ **HAD I FOLLOWED THE BRIEF LITERALLY — "move or rm the loose files under those prefixes" — I WOULD HAVE
DELETED COMMITTED ASSETS.** The register's own warning (*"4 of the ~15 were actually committed"*) understates
it by an order of magnitude: **98 capture PNGs sit tracked at the repo root**, of which **80 predate me and
are the founder's** and 18 are mine. The per-file `git ls-files --error-unmatch` check is the only thing
separating the two, and it is the whole reason nothing of the founder's was touched.

⚠️ **THE REFERENCE CHECK WAS PROVEN SENSITIVE BEFORE ITS SILENCE WAS TRUSTED.** Grepping the 18 filenames
across `docs/ resources/ app/ tests/` found nothing — but so did the control, so the probe's silence meant
nothing yet. Re-running it against known-committed captures surfaced
`gate0-op-dashboard-newsidebar.png` in `docs/design/DIVERGENCE-REGISTER.md`, which establishes the grep can
find a reference when one exists. **Only then** was 0-of-18 a real negative (§N.4p — a check must be able to
find what it seeks).

**THE FIX — one rule, plus a backstop, plus a convention that ships:**

- **`/.captures/*`** — the scratch directory. ⚠️ **The CONTENTS, not the directory**: excluding
  `/.captures/` outright makes git skip the directory entirely, so the `!/.captures/README.md` negation could
  never match and the convention doc would silently not ship. Caught by testing it.
- **`/*.png` (+ jpg/jpeg/webp) at the root** — the backstop, because `browser_take_screenshot` with a bare
  relative filename lands **at the repo root**, which is how every one of these was born. ⚠️ **This cannot
  hide the 80 committed captures — a `.gitignore` rule has no effect on a tracked file** — verified by
  touching one and watching `git status` still report ` M 2b-flat-unchanged.png`.
- **`.captures/README.md`** — the convention, in the repo where it can be read: pass
  `filename: ".captures/…"`, and `git add -f` anything root-level that genuinely belongs.
- **My 18 untracked and moved into `.captures/`** — `git rm --cached` then `mv`. ⚠️ `git rm` is correct here
  precisely *because* they were tracked; the "untracked → rm, never git rm" rule governs files git never knew
  about. **7.8 MB of bytes preserved on disk, nothing destroyed.**

**VERIFIED:**
- **The tracked-file list changed by EXACTLY my 18** — 1841 → 1823, and the diff lists those 18 and nothing
  else. The founder's 80 remain tracked.
- **A brand-new prefix is ignored in both places** — `zz-never-seen-prefix.png` at the root and
  `zz-brand-new-prefix.png` in `.captures/` both stay out of `git status`. **The whack-a-mole is over: no
  future pass needs a new rule.**
- Suite **2391 / 2394**, 15,425 assertions, unchanged (1 failed + 2 skipped) — nothing referenced a moved file.

⚠️ **A SMALL PROBE TRAP WORTH RECORDING:** `git check-ignore -v <file>` exits **0 when it matches a NEGATION
too**, so "exit 0" does not mean "ignored". Reading the exit code alone said the README was still excluded
when it was in fact included; `git status --porcelain -uall` is what settled it.

**Subsumes item 30.** PHPStan/Pint untouched (no code changed).

## 2026-08-17 — D18-5 phase 3 CLOSED: the storefront charges the chosen unit — proven control-first

⚠️⚠️ **STEP ZERO PAID FOR ITSELF IMMEDIATELY: IT CORRECTED THE CANON BEFORE A LINE OF UNIT CODE WAS WRITTEN.**
Both this brief and **my own note on `5329211`** recorded the storefront as TWO posts — `/checkout` mints the
quote, `/book` reserves and charges. **It is ONE.** `POST book/{property}/checkout` (`booking.reserve`) calls
`quote()` AND `book()` in the same request; the folio exists when it returns. `booking.book` is a JSON API
returning `JsonResponse` that **no view posts to** — grep `resources/views` and nothing comes back. That wrong
model is exactly why the reverted attempt could not book: it posted to `/book`, which demands a
`payment_token` the storefront never sends. **A control-first test found in one run what a whole pass of
reasoning had got backwards.**

**STEP ZERO, green against UNCHANGED application code:** a type-only booking through the real route writes a
folio of `2 × €120.00`. It stays in the suite as the zero-movement assertion.

**THE WIRING** (seams re-verified exactly as `5329211` found them): the chosen `unit_id` rides the quote's
`requested` JSON line (**no migration** — an older line simply lacks the key); `reserve()` re-validates it
against `freeUnitsForRoomType()` and **drops** anything not genuinely free (**shown = enforced**, the same
read the operator path and the lock use); it flows into `createBooking()` (**the core is free — untouched**);
and both `quote()`'s total and `book()`'s `price_minor` resolve through `NightlyRate::stayTotalForUnit(…) ??
priceOver(…)` — **zero movement by construction**, because the helper returns NULL without an override and the
fallback is the identical call this code always made.

⚠️⚠️ **A MUTATION STAYED GREEN, AND CHASING IT DOWN CHANGED WHAT THE GUARD ASSERTS.** Removing the resolver
from `book()`'s `price_minor` left all four tests passing. The brief anticipated this and demanded the
distinction — redundant guard, or unwired path? **Reading the source settled it:** `book()` posts the room
charge as `postCharge($folio, 'room', …, $total)` where `$total` **is the quote's own total**, so the folio
*cannot* disagree with the shown price — that guarantee is structural, and M2 (removing the **quote's** wrap)
reds correctly. But `price_minor` is **not inert**: `AssignmentService` writes it to
`reservation_units.price_minor`. So an unwrapped `book()` would have stored the **room-type** rate against a
unit the guest paid its **own** rate for — a quiet second version of the truth. It was an **unwired path for
that column**, and the guard simply had no assertion on it. Added; M1 now reds.

⚠️ **AND THE BROWSER SURFACED A PRODUCT FACT NO TEST HAD:** the storefront books the **Weekly** plan, not the
room type's default. An override is keyed `(rate_plan_id, unit_id, date)`, so **pricing a unit on one plan
does not price it on the others** — the picker correctly showed no unit price until the override was moved to
the plan actually being sold. Inherent to the phase-1 model; recorded because every prior test used a
single-plan fixture and could never have shown it.

⚠️ **A REGRESSION I CAUSED AND FIXED:** the new test file initially declared no `RefreshDatabase`, so it
committed its orgs and properties — and `TenantIsolationTest` counts properties across all tenants under a
super-admin context, so it went red. The storefront needs no genuine commit (unlike `BookingImportTest`, whose
webhook enqueues afterCommit), so a transaction is correct here. Suite back to baseline.

**MONEY, PROVEN IN A REAL BROWSER** (demo storefront, unit 102 given its own €275.00/night):
the picker offered **"102 — €550.00"** beside "Any available — €170.00" and an unpriced 103; booking it gave

    folio_items.amount_minor (room) = 55000
    reservation_units.price_minor   = 55000
    booking_quotes.total_minor      = 55000     ← charged = shown = resolved, to the cent

**FOUR MUTATIONS, EACH VERIFIED TO LAND:** the charge path dropping the resolver reds (after the guard gap was
closed) · the quote dropping it reds · the unit not riding the line into the core reds three tests · removing
`shown = enforced` reds the stale-tab test.

**CORE UNTOUCHED:** `AssignmentService` and `ConcurrentBookingTest` are absent from the diff; the concurrency
test re-runs green (1/1, 7 assertions). `rate_calendar` hashes **`2bbdafccc3b5c1ee43f89fe313a3f02d`, 929 rows,
10,920,000 minor** — unchanged. The demo ends **money-as-seeded** (0 overrides, the browser booking and its
folio/quote/guest removed, 0 orphans).

checkbox in the bulk panel *is* a single set, through routes that are already proven. What was genuinely

detail), so the list row is the home.

- The component takes room types + units + an optional preselect, so **D18-6's "price individually" can open

## 2026-08-17 — D18-6 THIRD OPTION: read-only unit rows, priced apart only on purpose (founder ruling)

⚠️ **THE FOUNDER RULED THE THIRD OPTION, AND THE SHAPE IS THE SAFETY.** STRUCT-1 was a decided fork, and the
reason "Yes" (a fully editable per-unit grid) was refused is not taste: **every edit would mint an override**,
detaching every unit from its room type, and the rack's "N units affected" warning would read **"0 of N"
everywhere** — true, and useless *by shape*. The third option keeps the **type row as the price-mover** and
makes per-unit pricing a **deliberately-invoked exception**, which is exactly what "two units MAY be priced
apart" means: a permission, not the norm.

**BUILT — read-only unit rows under each type row:**

- Each unit row shows **`NightlyRate`'s answer** (override → type). ⚠️ The grid does **not** read
  `rate_calendar` or `unit_rate_overrides` for these cells, so a row cannot disagree with what the booking
  paths charge (D4-1 / item 18's displayed = charged), and a unit with no price of its own shows its **room
  type's rate, never €0**.
- ⚠️ **There is no cell editor on a unit row — none, by construction.** The only way in is a per-row **"Price
  individually"** action opening the **same `<x-rates.unit-price-form>`** the Units list opens, posting to the
  **same** proven preview→apply routes. A new *entry* to a proven path; no second form, no second writer.
- **Type-row editing is untouched** — the default path still moves the type rate, and does so without minting
  a single override (asserted).

⚠️ **A ZERO-WRITE CLAIM DESERVES A WHOLE-TABLE CHECK, NOT A SAMPLE:** `rate_calendar` hashed
**`2bbdafccc3b5c1ee43f89fe313a3f02d`, 929 rows, 10,920,000 minor** before and after the browser pass — a
display re-shape moved nothing. The demo ends money-as-seeded (the two overrides the render created, removed).

⚠️ **RENDERING CAUGHT WHAT THE TESTS COULD NOT, AGAIN — TWICE IN ONE PASS.** First, `$window` has no
`from`/`through` keys, so the dialog's date inputs would have opened **blank**; caught by checking the payload
before trusting it, and the two keys added. Second, and more sharply, the dialogs landed **outside** the
`x-data` root, and Alpine said so in the console — *"unitPriceFor is not defined"*. **Six green tests were
silent on both**, because they assert the markup is present, not that it works. This is the same lesson as the
single-set pass, and it arrived through an explicit console error rather than a probe I had to trust.

**RENDERED, AS THE OPERATOR — the whole design visible in one screen:** 2 type rows, 5 unit rows; **0 editors
inside unit rows, 28 inside type rows**; 5 deliberate actions. Pricing unit **101** at €265.00 for two nights
gave a row reading **€265.00 · €265.00 · €100.00** — its own price where set, **falling back to the type rate
outside it** (the null-override edge, live) — marked as the exception, with **102 unchanged at €100.00**, and
the safeguard reading **"2 of 3 units · 1 priced individually"**. That last figure is the whole justification

## 2026-08-17 — channel-sync OPTION 1: the assignment rule — and the sufficiency trade-off is SURFACED, not resolved

⚠️⚠️ **CONFIRM-FIRST RELOCATED THE RULE BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN, AND THE CODE SAID SO ITSELF.**
`AssignmentService::occupyOrFlag()` — the OTA import path — carries this: *"Level A only — **OTA imports are
type-assigned (unit_id null)**, so there is no physical-unit (Level B) check; **a specific unit is assigned
later during manual resolution / check-in**."* It writes `'unit_id' => null`. So **an OTA booking is never
handed a unit at import at all**; the brief's "assignment" is the operator's LATER
`assignUnit(ReservationUnit, unitId)`. That is where the rule lives, and putting it at the import would have
guarded a decision nobody makes there.

**THE RULE, and it is a money rule wearing an assignment costume.** OTAs are structurally type-only, so a
channel sold the ROOM TYPE at the TYPE rate. A unit carrying an override is priced for direct sale; seating an
OTA stay on it means the property either eats the difference or dishonours what the guest was sold. So
`assignUnit()` refuses an OTA-sourced line a unit with an override on **any night of the stay** — not merely
the first, since the OTA priced every night at the type rate.

⚠️ **IT GUARDS THE SELECTION, NEVER THE LOCK.** The check runs **before** the transaction and reads a
different table; `lockAvailability()`, `assertUnitFree()` and the transaction are untouched — the diff's only
line mentioning them is a comment. `ConcurrentBookingTest` re-runs green, unmodified (1/1, 7 assertions).
**A DIRECT booking is deliberately unaffected**: blocking it would forfeit a sale the property is entitled to
make, which is over-permissiveness in the other direction.

**SHOWN = ENFORCED:** the front-desk move picker drops the same units for an OTA stay, so the operator is
never offered a move the write path will reject — the discipline the storefront picker already follows.

⚠️⚠️ **THE SUFFICIENCY TRADE-OFF IS REAL, AND I AM SURFACING IT RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT — because resolving
it would mean touching the concurrency spine.** The OTA snapshot pushes `availabilityRange()`, i.e. the
`availability` table's per-(type, date) count, which **has no notion of overrides**. So **OTA availability can
exceed the non-overridden pool**: price 2 of 3 units apart and the channel is still told 3 are free. Two OTA
bookings then have one honourable unit between them, and the second is refused by this guard at assignment
time.

⛔ **THE FOUNDER'S CALL, AND WHY IT IS NOT MINE.** `available = total − sold − out_of_order − blocked`, read
under `lockForUpdate()` by `assertCountsAvailable()` — **that number IS the no-double-booking spine, for every
source.** Shrinking it to the non-overridden count would refuse **direct** bookings too, and would alter the
certified core's inputs. The options are: **(a)** withhold OTA availability for overridden units — honourable
by construction, costs bookings, and needs a mechanism that does *not* reduce `total` (a channel-facing
adjustment, not an availability write); **(b)** accept the contradiction option 1 exists to avoid; **(c)**
today's behaviour — the channel may oversell the honourable pool and the guard refuses the bad assignment,
leaving the operator to resolve. **(c) is what ships**, because it is the only one that changes nothing about
money or the lock. It is safe but not free: it can produce an OTA booking with no honourable unit.

**FOUR MUTATIONS, EACH VERIFIED TO LAND:** removing the guard lets an OTA stay onto an overridden unit
(reds 2) · making it catch every source blocks direct bookings (reds) · checking only the first night lets a
later-night override through (reds) · dropping the picker filter offers a move the write path refuses (reds).

⚠️ **AND TWO VACUOUS DRAFTS OF THE SHOWN=ENFORCED TEST, BOTH CAUGHT BY PROBING.** The first searched the
front-desk HTML for `value="<unit id>"` — the page emits no such attribute, so **neither** unit was found and
`not->toContain` passed proving nothing. The second asserted on the component's assembled view data, which
depends on the day window, status and permission all lining up. The third calls the filter directly and
asserts **both** directions — the plain unit IS offered, the overridden one is NOT — which is the only shape
that cannot be vacuous.

**Untouched:** the OTA snapshot (still type-only), the certified core, direct assignment, §G.1, isolation/RBAC,
other channels. Demo money-as-seeded (0 overrides; `rate_calendar` `2bbdafccc3b5c1ee43f89fe313a3f02d`).

Suite **2413 / 2416**, 15,523 assertions, the documented 1 failed + 2 skipped; PHPStan L5 (0); Pint clean.

## 2026-08-17 — `OperatorGuestProfileTest`: the product was right; a 3-character needle hit a CSS comment

⚠️⚠️ **THE FIFTH CONSECUTIVE "CONSISTENTLY RED" LABEL THAT WAS WRONG AT THE MECHANISM — and this time my own
first reading of the failure was wrong too.** The register filed it as a "rendered-HTML mismatch". The runner
printed *"Failed asserting that '…213 KB of HTML…' does not contain \"5.0\""*, which I first read as a missing
`assertSee`. It is the opposite: that sentence is how PHPUnit states an **`assertDontSee`** — the assertion is
*"assert the page does NOT contain 5.0"*, and it failed because the page **does**.

**THE TRUE CAUSE — category (d), a needle that can match what it never meant.** Scanning the whole rendered
page found **exactly one** occurrence of `5.0`, and it is not a rating:

    rgb(147,42,7) clears the darkest sampled tint at 5.06

A **contrast ratio**, in a CSS comment in `components/layouts/operator.blade.php`, written during the a11y
token work. ⚠️ **Blade comments are stripped; CSS comments SHIP (§N.15.3)** — so that layout carries `5.06`
into every operator page, and the three-character needle `'5.0'` matched the substring. **The product has been
correct the whole time**: the review panel renders its honest "No reviews yet", exactly as intended (#87).
The assertion was asserting nothing about reviews at all — it was a phantom, and the fix is the test.

**THE FIX — the needle DERIVED FROM THE WAY THE VIEW WRITES A RATING**, not typed by hand: the panel emits
`aria-label="{rating} out of 5 stars"` (and the bold figure beside it) **only** when a review exists. So
`assertDontSee('out of 5 stars')` is present exactly when a rating is on screen and cannot collide with a
ratio, a price or a version string.

⚠️ **AND A POSITIVE TEST, BECAUSE A `assertDontSee` ALONE IS THE SAME PHANTOM IN A LONGER COSTUME.** Test 8b
seeds a REAL published review and proves the page then contains `out of 5 stars` **and** `5.0`. That is the
probe rule this session has now needed four times: *a negative is only evidence once the probe is shown
capable of a positive.* Without it, the corrected needle would be no better than the old one.

**TWO MUTATIONS, EACH VERIFIED TO LAND, ONE PER DIRECTION:** returning a hardcoded 5-star review when the
guest has none — the exact fabrication #87 exists to forbid — **reds test 8 itself** (checked by name, not by
count); and removing the rating's aria-label reds the positive proof, confirming the needle is live rather
than decorative.

⚠️ **NO PRODUCT CODE CHANGED** — `git diff --name-only` is the one test file. Fixing this in the product
would have been the (c) remedy applied to a (d) cause: the "which side is stale" fork, answered by reading the
rendered bytes instead of the label.

**THE SUITE IS NOW FULLY GREEN: 2415 / 2417, 15,529 assertions — 0 FAILED, 0 ERRORED, 2 skipped**, read across
all three buckets (the reporting defect corrected earlier this session). The non-green figure has gone **9 → 0**
over this run of work: `OwnerUnitDetailViewTest` (fixture ORDER), `PhaseBEndToEndTest` (a framework helper
eating the message over a stale password), `BookingImportTest` ×6 (a memory-starved queue worker),
`OperatorPortfolioTest` (never reproduced), and now this one (a needle collision). ⚠️ **Not one of the five was
what its register entry said it was, and only one of the five was a defect in the product.**

PHPStan L5 (0); Pint clean.

Each needs a **backend built first** (a real bulk-approve action; an expense-media capture path). Both are

## 2026-08-18 — OPERATOR FIX 2 · Finding 1 route gates, per the founder ruling

Branch `fix/operator-finding1-route-gates`. Implements the ruling: **gate the routes that render OWNER/FINANCE
money; leave OPERATIONAL money open to the roles that already reach it.**

**GATED (4):**

| Route | Permission | Why that one |
|---|---|---|
| `/app/owners` · `/app/owners/{owner}` | `reports.view` | The finance read. ⚠️ **Not `users.manage`** — that is the owners surface's WRITE gate, and the detail page's own rate-proposals panel is `rates.manage`-gated **for Hotel Manager**, who holds no `users.manage`; gating the page on it would strand a control the page was built to show. `reports.view` keeps PO / Group Admin / Hotel Manager / Accountant and excludes every operational role. |
| `/app/payouts/run` | `payouts.manage` | Exact sibling match — its own POST already requires it, so read and write now agree (§N.8f). |
| `/app/reservations/{reservation}/folio.pdf` | `folios.view` | The folio read. Keeps Front Desk + Reservation Agent (a guest's folio is operational, per the ruling); excludes Housekeeping + Maintenance. |

**⚠️ `/app/security/export` — LEFT OPEN, and the re-verify is why.** The stop-and-confirm read the payload, not
the status: `AuditEvent::where('actor_id', $user->getKey())`, `exported_for` = the requesting user, filename
`my-vyrobel-data-…`. **It is a GDPR self-export.** A 200 across roles is not a leak when the payload is
per-user, and gating it would break a legitimate self-service affordance. A test now **pins** the self-scope
(two roles, each sees only their own identity and never the other's) — turning a one-off manual verification
into a standing guard.

**`/app/email-previews` + `{key}` — RESOLVED IN OP-FIX-2b: gated on `folios.view`.** They were briefed for
`properties.manage`; confirm-first found **two existing tests encoding the opposite intent** —
`EmailScreensAccessTest` treats the previews as a general **back-office operator** surface, and
`PaymentReminderBrandTest` exists specifically to prove an operator previewing a payment reminder sees
**correct money arithmetic**: *the money is the point of the check, not an accident of it*. That places
previews in the ruling's **operational** bucket, so `properties.manage` (Property Owner + Group Admin only)
would 403 Hotel Manager and break a documented workflow. The gate was reverted and referred back; the founder
ruled **`folios.view`** — the same permission `folio.pdf` carries.

## 2026-08-18 — OPERATOR FIX 3 · dispatch-audience narrowing + the Livewire mutation-boundary guard

Branch `fix/operator-dispatch-and-livewire-guard`. The two write/dispatch-layer items OP-FIX-1 (controls) and
OP-FIX-2 (routes) structurally could not reach.

(self-scoped by `notifiable_id`). A housekeeper saw an owner's net payable because
`NotificationRecipients::operatorsForOrg()` is **one bucket for all eleven back-office roles**, and the two
Finance-group types (`statement_finalized`, `owner_payout_sent`) were addressed to every one of them.

⚠️ **A route gate would have been the wrong instrument** — it would block the operational notifications that
same housekeeper legitimately owns, while leaving the finance rows sitting in their feed. `/app/notifications`
stays correctly **ungated**; the fix is that a role which may not read the money is **never sent it**.

New `operatorsForOrgWithPermission($orgId, $permission)` narrows the audience; the two finance dispatches use
it. ⚠️ **The permission is not a guess: both notifications link to `/app/owners`, which OP-FIX-2 gated on
`reports.view`.** A recipient must be able to open the page their notification points at — otherwise it is the
same dead affordance this audit fixed at the control layer one pass earlier.

**Kept:** Property Owner · Group Admin · Hotel Manager · Accountant · Revenue Manager · Marketing Manager
(all hold `reports.view`). **Excluded:** Housekeeping · Front Desk · Reservation Agent · Maintenance · Guest
Support Agent. The **owner realm is untouched** — owners are addressed by a different path and still receive
`StatementReadyNotification`, asserted in the same test.

⚠️ **#28 — narrowing WHO receives it did not change WHAT it says.** A second test plants real guest contact on
the fixture and asserts the body carries none of it, while still carrying its operator-useful content. No
audience key was flipped and no type was dropped (the owner-Fix-2 single-audience canon).

### (B) The operator Livewire mutation-boundary guard — the highest-leverage operator test

Run 34 **measured** the property (0 of 37 operator components expose a public mutating action; every operator
write is a controller-routed `<form>`), and that measurement is what bounds all five OP-FIX-1 findings to
**misleading UI rather than privilege escalation**. ⚠️ **Nothing pinned it.** One future `public function
save()` silently creates a write path `/livewire/update` reaches and route middleware cannot see — turning
every one of those affordances into a real bypass, with nothing failing to announce it.

`OperatorLivewireMutationBoundaryTest` sweeps the operator realm by reflection and reds on any declared public
method outside Livewire's lifecycle surface. ⚠️ **Proven both ways, because a guard that cannot see a positive
proves nothing:** test 1 asserts the sweep finds >25 components and their real `render`/`mount` publics
(a blind sweep would pass test 2 vacuously); test 2 asserts zero mutating actions. A planted
`public function save()` on `UnitsList` **reds** it.

**Mutation-proven both items:** reverting the narrowing reds the audience test; the planted `save()` reds the
guard. Filters verified to match one test each first (the OP-FIX-1 vacuous-mutation lesson).

Suite **2445 / 15656**, PHPStan L5 **0**, Pint clean. ⚠️ `OperatorPortfolioTest`'s *"add → select → book"*

## 2026-08-18 — F3 RATIFIED: rooms stay VAT-EXCLUSIVE, add-ons stay VAT-INCLUSIVE, and a CUE closes the gap

**The finding.** The guest deep-parity audit filed F3: on one journey a guest reads **`€85.00 / night`**
(pre-tax) beside **`€65.00 each way` → €79.95** (post-tax, captioned *"Prices include VAT"*) with **no cue that
the two figures are on different bases**. Each surface was individually correct, labelled, and reconciling.

**⚠️ THE FIRST FIX ATTEMPT WAS STOPPED, AND THAT IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART.** Making the room display inclusive
looked like a formatting change. It is not — `taxes.inclusive` is a **real, first-class mode**:
`StayEstimator` treats an inclusive percentage tax as **NOT CHARGED** (informational only) and shows the
**extracted** portion `base·rate/(100+rate)`. So:

| Route | Total | Owner ex-VAT revenue |
|---|---|---|
| today (`inclusive = false`) | €373.65 | €255.00 |
| flip `taxes.inclusive = true` | **€315.00** (−€58.65) | **€207.32** (−€47.68) |
| gross the *display* only, VAT still charged | €373.65 ✓ | €255.00 ✓ but the label is **FALSE** |

The first is a **reprice**. The second says "VAT included" on a figure the folio charges VAT *on top of* — and
`StayEstimator` already uses "included" to mean the other thing, so one word would carry two meanings across
surfaces, and the tax documents (which must itemise VAT) would disagree with the storefront about the nightly
rate — **F3's own complaint, one surface over**.

**⚠️ THE RULING — the two bases are RATIFIED, not a defect.** Rooms are VAT-exclusive and add-ons VAT-inclusive
because **their taxes are configured that way**; both reconcile to the folio (#17). The ambiguity is closed by
a **CUE**, not by converging them: the room nightly now reads **`€85.00 / night · excl. VAT`**, parallel to the
add-ons' *"Prices include VAT"*, while the total keeps F2's enumeration (`incl. €58.65 VAT · €15.00 City tax ·
€45.00 Cleaning fee`). **No number moved. The total is byte-identical at €373.65.**

**The cue is gated on the tax being genuinely charged** (`StayEstimator::taxApplies`) — a property configured
inclusive shows **no** cue, because for it the nightly really is gross. It names the property's **own** tax, so
an IVA/MwSt property is described correctly.

**⛔ THE DEFERRED PATH, recorded so it is not rediscovered as a bug.** Making room display inclusive **while
holding the total** requires **re-authoring rates to gross** (gross `rate_calendar` rows + `taxes.inclusive =
true`) across **929 materialised rows** through the certified `RateAndRestrictionService` — a **money-path
migration**, not a display change. **Take it up ONLY if EU consumer-display compliance later requires
tax-inclusive room display.** Not started.

**Also this pass:** **A1 done** — the error-page footer (*"contact your Vyrobel administrator"*, shared layout,
all six views) is realm-branched through the same `App\Support\ErrorRealm` derivation the back-link and the
F5 403 body read. **A2 still open** — `StayEstimator::taxApplies()` duplicates `estimate()`'s inline
`$inclusive` (same rule, written twice; they agree today). It belongs with the money-path pass.

## 2026-08-20 — GUEST NOTIFICATIONS · GATE 1: the foundation + G1 (booking confirmed), end-to-end

**The founder ruled all eight guest notification types.** Gate 1 de-risks the foundation and proves the
pattern on ONE type before the rest replicate it. G2–G8 and the bell/feed frontend are follow-on gates.

### ⚠️ The system model, as it actually is (the scope pass corrected the brief; this gate confirmed it)

There is **no `audience` column and no custom `Notification` model**. These are Laravel-native
`DatabaseNotification` rows on a `ulidMorphs('notifiable')` table, and **the `notifiable` morph is the
recipient discriminator**. `Guest` already used `Notifiable` — unused until now — so **a guest notification
needed ZERO schema change**. `audience` is a key inside `NotificationPreferences::CATALOG` that decides which
portal's *preferences screen* lists a toggle; it routes nothing. "ADD, never flip" still holds, and for the
reason `OwnerNewBookingNotification`'s docblock already records: a single-string audience means one key cannot
serve two portals.

### ⚠️⚠️ THE CORRECTION THAT CHANGED THE BUILD — risk 2 was FALSE, and it was our own claim

The scope pass recorded, and this gate's brief repeated, that `NotificationController` could not serve guests
because `$request->user()` resolves on the `web` guard and is **null** for an authenticated guest. **That is
wrong.** A probe inside a real request settled it: Laravel's `Authenticate` middleware calls
`shouldUse($guard)` for the guard that succeeded, so **inside an `auth:guest` route the DEFAULT guard IS
`guest`** and `$request->user()` returns the Guest (`default_guard_name => "guest"`, `web_user_null => true`,
`default_user_null => false`).

A separate `GuestNotificationsController` was written on the false premise, then **deleted** once the probe
disproved its reason to exist. The guest routes now point at the **shared `NotificationController`** (§N.8f).

> ⚠️ **A finding is one reader's hypothesis — including when the reader was us, one document earlier.** The
> claim was plausible, was written down, was repeated into a build brief, and was still false. What settled it
> was a probe inside a real request, not more reading.

⚠️ **The cost of that reuse is an IMPLICIT, and it is now a checked invariant.** The controller derives WHO
you are from the request's resolved guard, so **the route's guard middleware is load-bearing for isolation,
not merely for access** — a guest notification route placed outside `auth:guest` would resolve
`$request->user()` on the `web` guard and hand a signed-in operator a guest's mark-read endpoint.
`GuestNotificationsRouteGuardTest` pins it.

### What shipped

| Item | Decision |
|---|---|
| **`NotificationFeed`** | **WIDENED, not forked** (§N.8f): the two signatures now take `User\|Guest`; the bodies did not change by one character, because every read already went through `Notifiable`'s `notifications()` / `unreadNotifications()`. |
| **Sealed-realm regression** | `NotificationFeedRealmTest` pins the operator + owner behaviour that nothing pinned tightly before — order, counts, categories, row shape, self-only. Mutation-proven. |
| **Guest routes** | `guest.notifications.{read,read-all,dismiss}` on the shared controller, inside `auth:guest`. **No GET feed page** — the guest realm has no notifications wireframe, so the screen and the bell placement are a follow-on gate. |
| **G1** | `GuestBookingConfirmedNotification`, dispatched from `DispatchNotificationsForDomainEvent::newBooking()` — the same `reservation.confirmed` handler where the operator and owner fan-outs already live. |
| **Copy** | Single-sourced from the email: the title resolves through the SAME `EmailTemplateResolver` key and merge vars `BookingConfirmationMail` uses, so an operator customising the subject (#86) moves both surfaces at once. |
| **Preferences** | **Defaults-only.** `NotificationPreference` keys on `user_id`, so a Guest cannot hold one; guests run on catalog defaults. Not extended — per-guest toggles stay a later decision. |

### ⚠️ Two guards worth naming

**The email still fires, and there is no second one.** `SendGuestTransactionalEmails` is untouched —
`BookingConfirmationMail` sends exactly as before, proven in the same test as the in-app row. And the catalog
entry carries **`email_default => false`**, which is **load-bearing, not a preference**: `allows()` falls back
to `defaultFor()` for a non-User notifiable, so `email_default => true` would have added the `mail` channel in
`FeedNotification::via()` and **emailed every guest twice**. Mutation-proven.

**#28 self-scoped, both directions.** A guest sees nothing of another guest's; naming a foreign id 404s on
read and dismiss; and the foreign row is verified untouched by a **raw** query rather than through the scope
that just refused it (§N.18.1 — a check must be independent of what it checks).

### ⚠️ Two instrument faults caught in this gate (both are the §N.4p family)

1. **`actingAs($g, 'guest')` REBINDS THE DEFAULT GUARD.** A mutation swapping the guest-guard resolver for the
   default one stayed **GREEN** under `actingAs` — the mutation applied but never reached the path. Chasing
   that green is what led to the probe that overturned risk 2. *A test harness can pre-arrange the very answer
   the test is asking for.*
2. **A middleware pin that read only the DECLARATION.** The first `GuestNotificationsRouteGuardTest` asserted
   `gatherMiddleware()` contains `auth:guest` — and stayed green through
   `->withoutMiddleware('auth:guest')`, which leaves the declaration intact and the guard gone. It asserted
   the label, not the protection. Now reads `excludedMiddleware()` too, and bites.

### Verification

Six mutations, each verified to apply, each redding a coherent set: remove the dispatch · break self-scoping
in the shared controller (#28) · flip `email_default` · hardcode the title · break the widened feed's User
path · strip `auth:guest` from a guest route. PHPStan L5 **0**; Pint clean. Demo money untouched and
byte-identical by **sums and counts** — **929 rate rows / 10,912,000 minor / 41 reservations / 16 payments**,
with **0** guest notifications persisted (the tests roll back).

### ⚠️ One pre-existing guard had to be re-calibrated — the RULE stood, its PROXY was too narrow

`NotificationDismissTest`'s *"ONE mechanism serves both realms (§N.8f)"* asserted **exactly one** route
registration of `[NotificationController::class, 'dismiss']`. It failed on the full suite.

It was not a false alarm to wave through, and not a rule to weaken. Checked at source: both registrations name
**the same controller action**, there is exactly **one** dismiss implementation, and no forked controller — but
the guest route **must** register separately because it sits behind a **different guard** (`auth:guest`) under a
different URI prefix, and one registration cannot carry two guards.

> **The rule was "one mechanism"; the proxy was "one line". The proxy was correct while both realms shared the
> `web` guard, and a third realm on a different guard made it too narrow without making the rule wrong.**

So the count moved 1 → 2 **with its cause established** (§N.14.5 — a number that moves is not automatically a
correction), and the assertion was **strengthened** rather than relaxed: it now also asserts no forked guest
controller exists and that the dismiss write has exactly one implementation. Mutation-proven — re-creating the
forked controller reds it.

**Not built, deliberately:** G2–G8, the `/guest/notifications` screen, the bell placement in the guest shell,
guest preference toggles. No email was replaced, no owner/operator catalog entry flipped.

## 2026-08-20 — GUEST NOTIFICATIONS · GATE 2: G2–G8, the remaining seven types

Gate 1 (`aa1a91e`) proved the foundation and G1. This gate replicates it across the other seven, each on its
**own already-live trigger**, each **additive** to an email that still fires. The feed screen, the bell
placement and guest preference toggles remain the (un-wireframed) frontend gate.

| | Type | Live trigger | Points at |
|---|---|---|---|
| G2 | `guest_checkin_ready` | `emails:send-pre-arrival` (#33 arrival-window day) | `guest.arrival` |
| G3 | `guest_message_received` | `inbox.message_sent` (operator direction) | `guest.messages.show` |
| G4 | `guest_payment_due` | `emails:send-payment-reminders` | `guest.payments` |
| G5 | `guest_booking_cancelled` | `reservation.cancelled` | ⚠️ `guest.trips` |
| G6 | `guest_refund_processed` | `payment.refunded` (succeeded only) | `guest.payments` |
| G7 | `guest_review_request` | `reservation.checked_out` | `guest.review` |
| G8 | `guest_account_security` | `GuestDeletionService` (always-on) | `guest.account` |

### ⚠️⚠️ THE BRIEF'S G3 INSTRUCTION WAS WRONG — and following it would have doubled every bulk message

The founder ruled that G3 notifies on **both** the personal reply and the BULK send, and the brief described
the bulk path as *"a separate path that does NOT go through the inbox thread"*, asking for a second wire in
`GuestBulkActionController`.

**It does go through the thread.** The bulk loop calls `$inbox->sendOutbound($thread, …)`, and
`InboxService::sendOutbound()` records `inbox.message_sent`. So the bulk path **already** reaches the single
G3 handler, once per recipient, each row self-scoped.

> **The ruling is satisfied by ONE wire. A second one would have given every bulk recipient TWO rows for one
> message — a bulk send to fifty guests producing a hundred notifications.**

The ruling's *intent* (both directions notify) is implemented in full; only its stated mechanism was wrong.
`GuestNotificationsGate2Test` pins it: a bulk-shaped send yields **exactly one** row.

### ⚠️ The double-email hazard, guarded per type

`allows()` falls back to the catalog default for a non-User notifiable, and **every one of these events
already emails the guest** — so an `email_default => true` on any guest key emails them **twice**. All eight
guest entries set it `false`, and the guard is **per type**: each type asserts the catalog value AND the
resolved channel list AND that its existing Mailable sent **exactly once**. Mutation-proven seven times —
flipping any one key reds that type's test and the family-wide guard.

⚠️ **G8 is the documented exception.** It is always-on (a pending erasure of your own account is not a
preference), and `allows()` short-circuits an always-on key **before** reading the defaults — so
`email_default` is not consulted for it. Its guard is the send-count assertion instead. Recorded rather than
papered over.

### ⚠️ A real placement bug the tests caught

G7 was first appended to the end of `balanceDue()` — which returns early when the folio is settled. The
review invitation would have fired **only for guests who still owed money**, and most stays are settled at
check-out. `reservation.checked_out` now fans out to two **independent** handlers.

> **Nesting one audience's dispatch inside another's conditional silently makes the second depend on the
> first.** The two conditions were unrelated; the nesting was not visible in review, only in the failing test.

### ⚠️ GDPR: guest notification rows now die with the guest

`Guest::anonymize()` did **not** clear notifications. `data->title` is the resolved email SUBJECT
(operator-customisable, its declared vars including `{guest_name}`) and `data->context` is the guest's stay —
a durable store ABOUT the guest, squarely inside the erase rule. **Gate 1 shipped the first writer without
this clause;** it is added here with the seven that follow. Rows are **deleted, not blanked** — unlike a
message thread, a notification has no operator audit value once its subject is erased, so an empty row would
be residue. What happened is still recorded in `audit_events` / `domain_events`, which carry field names and
never values.

⚠️ **The first version of that test was vacuous** and stayed green when the clause was deleted: it filtered
`notifiable_type` on `Guest::class`, but `Relation::enforceMorphMap` stores **`'guest'`**, so the query matched
nothing before or after — 0 == 0 forever. Fixed to the alias, and the probe must now show a **positive**
before the erasure for its later zero to mean anything.

### Anti-drift

Six reservation-scoped types share one `GuestReservationNotification` base holding the single copy rule (the
row title IS the matching email template's subject, same resolver call, same merge vars). G1 was refactored
onto it, so seven types cannot drift apart. G3 and G8 are not reservation-scoped and stay standalone.

Realm boundary held: operator **16** and owner **9** catalog entries unchanged, and no `guest_*` key surfaces
on either preferences screen (`catalogFor()` filters on exact audience).

## 2026-08-20 — GUEST NOTIFICATIONS · GATE 3 (FINAL): the feed screen + the bell placement

The backend was done at `d866837`. This is the part a guest sees. There is **no guest notifications
wireframe** (19 guest prototypes import a bell; the surface it opens was never drawn), so the screen MIRRORS
the proven owner/operator feed and the confirmation was a **RENDER**, not a wireframe diff.

### ⚠️⚠️ THE FINDING THAT CHANGED THE BUILD — the guest realm loads NO Alpine

The brief said to reuse `bell.blade.php`. Reused literally, it would have shipped a **dead control**: that
component is an Alpine popover (`x-data` / `x-show` / `@click`), and the guest shell pulls in **no Livewire and
no Alpine at all** — only a submit-guard partial. The button would have rendered perfectly, with the right
frosted circle and badge, and done **nothing** on click.

> **"Reuse the component" is only safe once you have checked the host can run it. A shared component carries
> its runtime assumptions with it, and a shell that cannot satisfy them turns reuse into a dead affordance.**

Resolved by giving the shared component a **mode**, not a fork: `:panel="false"` renders the bell as a plain
LINK to the feed, reusing the same glyph, badge and unread read. The glyph+badge moved into
`<x-notifications.bell-glyph>` so both modes render byte-identically. The default stays the popover, so the
operator and owner shells are unchanged — verified by render (the operator panel still opens) and pinned.

That also matches the guest realm's own documented rule: no Alpine, all interactivity native GET /
progressive enhancement.

### The placement — A PROPOSAL, awaiting the founder

**Header top-right, after the nav.** At desktop `space-between` pins it right; at mobile it holds the FIRST
row beside the brand while `.vy-nav` scrolls on its own row below — so it can never scroll out of reach on a
phone, which is the surface a guest actually reads notifications on. Rendered at 1280px and at 390px.
A move is a one-line change, not a rebuild.

### ⚠️ Two defects the RENDER caught that no test would have

1. **The bell wrapped "Sign out" onto two lines.** The extra 36px header action squeezed that flex item below
   its single-line width. The row does not overflow — the item was being compressed — so `white-space: nowrap`
   + `flex: none` is the whole fix. Invisible to every green test; obvious in one screenshot.
2. **`.vy-sr-only` was not defined in the guest shell.** It existed only in the operator/owner layouts and
   *locally* inside `guest/help.blade.php` — a page that had already hit this. An undefined visually-hidden
   class hides nothing; the "Unread" label would have printed as stray visible text on every row. Hoisted to
   the shell so every guest page inherits it.

### ⚠️ Two more label-not-protection guards, and one bad MUTATION

Continuing the pattern from Gates 1–2:

- The sr-only test asserted the bare string `.vy-sr-only` — which appears in every `class="vy-sr-only"`
  **attribute in the markup**, so it stayed green when the CSS **rule** was renamed away. Now matches the rule
  *and* its `clip: rect(...)` declaration.
- The #28 test emptied the guest's own rows and asserted the page was empty — satisfiable by a wrong-actor
  resolution purely by row order. Now both guests hold **distinguishable** rows, so only the correctly
  resolved actor passes.

⚠️ **And the mirror-image lesson.** The first wrong-actor mutation (`orderByDesc('created_at')->first()`) left
the suite GREEN — but the guard was fine; the **mutation** was order-dependent and had resolved the *right*
guest by luck. A deterministic wrong actor (`whereKeyNot(<authed id>)`) reds **four** tests.

> **A green under mutation means the mutation missed OR the test is weak — and you must establish which.
> Gate 3 hit one of each, in the same hour.**

### What shipped

`GET /guest/notifications` → `guest.notifications`, read-only and self-scoped through the guard
(`ResolvesGuest`); the writes reuse the shared `NotificationController` via the Gate-1 guest routes. The
screen mirrors the owner/operator feed — same shared category tile, row shape, unread wash + dot, category
filters, mark-read / dismiss / mark-all — in the guest realm's warm-glass chrome, with an honest empty state
(the demo persists zero guest rows, so that is the state a real guest sees).

Render-confirmed end to end: bell at both widths · feed empty · feed populated (4 transient rows, **removed
afterwards**) · badge 4 → 3 and hero "4 unread" → "3 unread" on mark-read · operator popover unchanged.

### ⚠️ Three of our OWN guards failed on the full suite — and all three were tracking a LOCATION

The full suite reported three failures. None was a product defect; all three were guards written in Gates 1–2
whose *locator* went stale, and each was rewritten to assert the thing rather than where the thing lives.

| Guard | What it read | Why it broke | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| badge gradient | `bell.blade.php` **as a file** | the glyph+badge moved to `<x-notifications.bell-glyph>` for link mode; the OUTPUT was byte-identical | asserts the **rendered page** |
| prototype glyph | same | same | asserts the **rendered page** |
| "ONE mechanism" | `file_exists(Guest/GuestNotificationsController.php)` — must be **false** | GATE 3 added that class for the read-only FEED SCREEN; the writes never forked | asserts **every write route points at the shared controller**, and that no other controller implements the dismiss write |

> **A guard that names a FILE tracks a location. A guard that reads the render, or the route table, tracks the
> thing. Refactoring moves locations; it does not move behaviour — so a location-guard fails on safe changes
> and, worse, passes when the behaviour moves somewhere it is not watching.**

Both rewrites are **stronger**, not merely relocated — mutation-proven: breaking the gradient inside the
*extracted* file now reds (the old guard could not see that file at all), and forking a single write route to
another controller now reds.

That is the same family as the earlier findings in Gates 1–3 — guards that assert the label rather than the
protection. Across the three gates: `actingAs` rebinding the guard · the route pin reading declarations not
exclusions · the dismiss count pinning a line · the morph-alias erasure query · the sr-only class read from
markup · the order-dependent isolation fixture · and these three locators. **Worth its own §N entry.**

**Not built:** guest preference toggles. The backend is defaults-only and a toggle needs
`NotificationPreference` (keyed on `user_id`) extended to guests — a separate decision with its own
`Guest Email Preferences.html` wireframe.

## 2026-08-20 — GUEST EMAIL PREFERENCES: the two toggles, gated at the SEND SITE

The scope pass (`docs/audits/GUEST-TOGGLES-SCOPE-2026-08-20.md`) established the shape and the founder ruled.
Built on merged main after the notifications seal (`2ed497a`).

### ⚠️ THE MODEL: this is EMAIL, and it is NOT `allows()`

The `Guest Email Preferences` wireframe governs the guest EMAIL programme — **a different feature from the
in-app notifications shipped in Gates 1–3.** And the architectural fact that shapes the whole build:

> **The guest transactional emails never consult `NotificationPreferences::allows()`.**
> `SendGuestTransactionalEmails::sendToGuest()` and the two scheduled commands call `Mail::to()->send()`
> directly, gated only by `EmailTemplateResolver::enabled()` — the operator's per-org #86 switch.

So a guest email opt-out is **a new gate at each send site**, not a preference-service change. `allows()` is
untouched (confirmed by diff), and the operator/owner in-app path with it.

### What shipped

| | |
|---|---|
| **Store** | `guest_email_preferences` — **sparse, deviations-only**: a row exists ONLY when a guest opted out. The default therefore lives in the ABSENCE of data, so a guest who never opens the screen cannot be unsubscribed by a backfill that never ran. |
| **Gate** | ONE shared `GuestEmailPreferences::mayReceive()`, shaped deliberately like `EmailTemplateResolver::enabled()` (§N.8f), called at BOTH send sites. The two gates are **independent and both must pass** — the operator's property-level switch, and the person's own choice. |
| **Toggles** | exactly two: `payment` (PaymentReminderMail) and `reviews` (ReviewRequestMail) |
| **Locked** | `txn` and `pre-arrival`, rendered ON and inert. A booking confirmation is a transactional record; the pre-arrival email carries the **door code**, so a guest able to switch it off could arrive unable to get in. G8 is unreachable by design (`always_on` short-circuits `allows()`). |
| **Honestly disabled** | `push` — no channel, no provider (#39), rendered exactly like the existing SMS row |
| **Untouched** | `marketing_consent` + `marketing.unsubscribe` — a separate legal basis. Proven both ways: a transactional opt-out does not revoke marketing consent, and revoking marketing does not clear a transactional choice. |

⚠️ **One deviation from the ruling, reasoned.** The ruling said render `offers` and `winback` disabled. The
account page **already carries a LIVE "Trip offers & news" toggle** on `marketing_consent`. Adding a disabled
"Offers & news" row directly beneath a working one would have been the contradiction the ruling exists to
prevent, so the marketing rows are **not duplicated**; the section footnote points at the existing control
instead. The two controls stay separate, as ruled — they are simply not shown twice.

### ⚠️ §N.29 — the guards prove the EMAIL DOES NOT SEND

Every test asserts what the **mailer** did. None asserts that a toggle renders, a column exists, or a route is
declared. Four mutations, each verified to apply and reach the path: removing either send-site gate reds the
matching "does NOT email" test; breaking the self-scoping reds #28; removing the always-on guard reds both
always-on tests.

### ⚠️ A redundant layer removed BECAUSE mutation-testing exposed it as unprovable

The account controller re-checked `array_key_exists(..., OPTIONAL)` before calling the helper. **Deleting that
check left the suite fully green** — the helper still refused. So the layer was both redundant *and*
incapable of having a per-layer test without mocking the chokepoint (§N.13). It was removed rather than
papered over with a source-reading assertion: one definition of "which categories are storable", in the
chokepoint every caller passes through, and now **both** always-on tests bite it.

> **Defence-in-depth that cannot be independently tested is not depth — it is a second copy of a rule, free to
> drift, whose presence hides whether the first copy works.**
