## 2026-08-20 — ✅ DEPLOYMENT §7.6 CI: the by-hand gates become a control · the flake was never order-dependent

**The deploy track is COMPLETE.** Six items, six built (§7.1 backups → §7.6 CI).

### What §7.6 actually changes

Every gate in this project — the full suite, PHPStan L5, Pint, the money-as-seeded re-measure — has been run
**by hand** and reported in prose. That worked because one person ran them every time. ⚠️ **It is a habit,
not a control, and a habit has no failure mode that announces itself.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now runs
all four on every push and every PR, inside the §7.5 parity image.

**Founder's call: a live workflow, not a documented-only spec.**

### ⚠️ §N.29 applied to CI — each gate was VIOLATED and observed to red

A step that reports green without running its gate is the runtime form of the label-vs-protection failure.
So none of the four was taken on trust:

| Gate | Violated by | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 0 · runtime (`ops/runtime-contract.sh`) | run against this dev machine | ❌ **3 genuine failures** — see below |
| 1 · Pint | a malformed class planted in `app/` | exit **1** → removed → **0** |
| 2 · PHPStan L5 | a call to an undefined method | exit **1** (`method.notFound`) → removed → **0** |
| 3 · the suite | reverting the flake fix under the pinned token | **1 failed, deterministically** → restored → 6/6 |
| 4 · money-as-seeded | baseline moved to 17 payments | exit **1**, both figures printed → restored → **0** |

No `|| true`, no `continue-on-error`, no swallowed exit, and **no test filter** — Gate 3 is `php artisan test`
whole, with no `--parallel` (the workers share one database).

### ⚠️ The runtime is CONSUMED from §7.5, never restated (§N.8f)

Three files, one direction of authority: **§7.5** is the contract in prose · **`ops/runtime-contract.sh`** is
its **executable** form (asserts it against a live machine, exits non-zero) · **`Dockerfile.ci`** merely
*installs*, and Gate 0 runs the script inside it, so an image that drifts reds the build. The script
deliberately checks the two things `composer check-platform-reqs` **cannot** see — §7.5.1(a) the
`REDIS_CLIENT`/`phpredis` default needing an undeclared `ext-redis`, and §7.5.1(c) `pcntl`/`posix`
**functions** neutered by `disable_functions` while the extension still reports loaded — and reds on a
**MariaDB** banner, so "genuine MySQL 8" is enforced rather than requested.

⚠️ **One honest residue, recorded rather than hidden:** §7.5.6 lists the same checks in prose and this pass
was scoped not to edit §7.5, so two expressions of that list exist (one enforced, one read). They agree
today. A one-line pointer from §7.5.6 to the script would collapse them — the founder's call, and the only
§N.8f duplication §7.6 leaves behind.

### ⚠️⚠️ THE FLAKE WAS NOT ORDER-DEPENDENT — and it had been solved here twice already

`OperatorPortfolioTest`'s *"add → select → book"* has sat in the register as an **order-dependent** flake for
a year. It is nothing of the kind.

`seedScenario` codes units `U1`, `U2`… (`tests/Support/booking_helpers.php:50`), and the test asserted
`assertDontSee('U1')` on the new empty property's page. Every page carries a 40-char random CSRF token, and
`Str::random(40)` is alphanumeric — so it contains the two-character string `U1` **~1% of the time**, twice
per page. **Measured, not assumed: 212 hits in 20,000 draws = 1.06%**, matching the 0.95% this repo had
already computed. The assertion was failing on a page that had leaked **nothing**: it was testing the
**needle**, not the behaviour.

> ⚠️ **It is randomness-dependent. The token is redrawn every run regardless of test order.** The distinction
> is not pedantry: an ordering fix — deterministic sort, isolated fixtures, an explicit `orderBy` — would
> have changed **nothing**, and the test would have kept flaking with a "fix" recorded against it.

⚠️⚠️ **And this exact flake was diagnosed and fixed twice in this repo on 2026-07-17.**
`OperatorReservationsListTest:86` renames its foreign unit to `FOREIGNUNIT9`; `BackOfficeAccessTest:132`
renames to `BRUNOUNIT9` and carries the full arithmetic in its comment. `OperatorPortfolioTest` is simply the
site that sweep missed — **§N.13.1 again: the defect sat beside the flagged thing**, one file over, for a
year. A register entry is one reader's finding (§N.27.1); the remedy existed and the third site did not get it.

**The fix reuses that remedy rather than inventing one**, plus two hardenings:

1. **A leak-proof needle** — `ORIGINALUNIT9`, a string that could only appear **by leaking**.
2. **The positive first** (§N.29) — the test now asserts the code *does* render on the original property
   before asserting it does not on the new one. Without that, a needle that can never appear passes forever
   while guarding nothing.
3. ⚠️ **The worst case is PINNED.** The negative assertion runs with a CSRF token deliberately containing
   `U1`, so the 1-in-50 collision now happens on **every run**: a leak-proof needle sails through, a short
   one reds **immediately and deterministically** instead of flaking months later. The protection RUNS.

**Mutation proof:** with the token pinned, reverting the needle to `U1` fails **1/6 every time**; restoring
passes **6/6**. Assertions **29 → 31** — two added, none removed. ⚠️ **No product code touched.** It was a
fixture-and-needle defect, never an ordering bug; nothing was papered over.

### The parity image — and where it deliberately exceeds §7.5

`Dockerfile.ci` is **dev/CI only, never deployed** (production is pull-in-place, §7.3). No app code, no
`.env`, no secrets. ⚠️ It installs **one** extension §7.5 excludes — **`ext-gd`** — and that is a real
asymmetry, not drift: §7.5.2 rightly excludes gd from production (only `PlaceholderImage` uses it, reached
solely by `DemoSeeder` and one test, and production is never seeded), but that "one test" is
`tests/Feature/RoomPhotosTest.php:79`, which calls `PlaceholderImage::jpeg()` and **throws without gd**. The
**suite** needs what production does not. The contract script prints it under a separate `CI-ONLY` heading so
the sets never blur. ⚠️ **`ext-intl` is deliberately NOT installed** (§7.5.1b), so CI runs as a host without
it does and any future *unguarded* `intl` use fails here rather than in production.

⚠️ **Status: written, NOT built.** Docker is not installed on the dev machine. **Gate 0 is what verifies it** —
the first CI run either satisfies the contract or reds with the exact requirement it missed. Not assumed.

### ⚠️ Gate 0 found something on its very first run — on this machine

`upload_max_filesize` **2M** (needs ≥ 12M) · `post_max_size` **8M** (needs ≥ 14M) · `memory_limit` **128M**
(needs ≥ 256M). `php artisan serve` runs on the CLI SAPI, so these are local development's real limits.

> ⚠️ **The 8 MB guest ID upload and the 10 MB message attachment cannot be exercised on this machine at
> all** — PHP rejects the file before Laravel sees it. Those paths have only ever been tested below 2 MB.
> A local `php.ini`/`conf.d` change, so the founder's; the parity image already sets all three.

### ⚠️ THE CONTENT-HONESTY GATE — CI Gate 5, mutation-proven

**The rule in one sentence:** *the marketing ledger cannot be declared production-ready while any entry in
it is unreal (`real` null/false/absent) or unconsented (`consent` !== true on a named person) — and
production rendering filters such entries out regardless.*

**Mechanism:** `tests/Feature/MarketingContentHonestyTest.php` (**7 tests / 106 assertions**) — run TWICE
per push: as the new dedicated **Gate 5** step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` AND inside Gate 3's full suite,
so neither path can be filtered away. Same no-`||true`, no-swallowed-exit style as the four existing gates,
**whose steps are untouched** (the diff shows zero deletions in the gate steps; only the header count
comment changed 4→5). ⚠️ **Two implementations, one arbiter (the §N.18.1/§N.8f resolution):** the test
re-implements the rule in raw helpers independent of the class, and a **pinned fixture table** is the
arbiter BOTH must satisfy shape-by-shape — an agreement test turns any drift between them into a red build.

The first version passed its own three mutation proofs and was still defeasible — **§N.29 catching its own
author again, this time on the very gate built to embody it.** A 3-lens/19-verifier adversarial review of
the uncommitted diff confirmed seven real defects; all fixed in the same pass:

| # | The hole (confirmed with a concrete failing input) | The fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ⚠️ **HIGH — a closed reject-set `{null,false,absent}`:** `real: "no"` / `""` / `"TBD"` / `"false"` / a numeric string read as REAL in **both** layers (test and class shared the identical rule — code-path independence, not rule independence) | `real` is now an **ALLOW-LIST**: exactly `true` or an explicit int/float. Every rejected shape pinned in the fixture table |
| 2 | **the illustrative check was a loose substring:** `"Production ready — illustrative content replaced"` — a good-faith production declaration — kept the teeth OFF | illustrative ⇔ the status **BEGINS** with the word; merely containing it is production-declared |
| 3 | **the runtime-filter test was predicate-as-oracle**, its only independent assertions gated on customers alone (one legitimate consent would retire them forever), and figures had NO independent check | the expected output is now derived from the **raw JSON** via the independent rule and compared **unconditionally**, figures included |
| 4 | ⚠️ **the filter keyed on `environment === 'production'` exactly** — a `staging`/`prod`/`Production` host rendered every fabricated entry **unfiltered** (fail open) | inverted allow-list: only `local`/`development`/`testing` render unfiltered; every other or unknown environment **filters** |
| 5 | **a hardcoded section list:** a new ledger section (`"partners"`) would ship unguarded | unknown top-level sections now FAIL the gate (`MarketingContent::SECTIONS`) |
| 6 | a `use Tests\…` import of a class that does not exist (Pest files declare none) | dropped; the doc references the file path |
| 7 | `consent: "pending"` / `1` / `"true"` shapes unpinned | pinned refused in the fixture table (consent must be strictly `true`) |

pending, and the drawer being all-pending; **updated, not deleted**, and the drawer guard re-scoped from
pending-ness to **reachability** so a vanished row can no longer look identical to one that became a link).

**Mutations, each violate → RED → restore → GREEN:** the stats band made to render when empty (the exact
launch-day hole) → RED · a figure value taken from the design script instead of the ledger → RED · ⚠️ **CI
Gate 5 re-proven now that pages consume the ledger** → RED with all 13 entries named.

## 2026-08-21 — FRONT WEBSITE · GATE 3: two honesty audits, four pages built, six HELD

Full analysis: `docs/audits/FRONT-GATE3-HONESTY-AUDITS-2026-08-21.md`. **Built:** Switching · For Hotels ·
For Apartments · For Villas. ⚠️ **Held for a ruling:** Alternatives · Compare · the case-study index and its
three stories.

### ⚠️ AUDIT (A) — the case studies ARE the invented customers

Each story asserts a named business that the ledger flags `real: null, consent: false` (Kastellis Villas ·
Hotel Alfama Reyes · Van Dijk Stays), its size and city, a before/after narrative — Rotterdam carries a
**quantified outcome claim** (*"~20% → 50%+ share of nights arriving direct, across one season"*) — and a
direct quote. ⚠️ **And the index offers *"Want to talk to one of them?"*** — an offer to introduce a
prospect to a business that does not exist. That is where an invented case study stops being copy and
becomes a representation someone could act on.

⚠️ **What survives D1's filter: nothing — and worse, the filter cannot reach these pages at all.** The
ledger governs DATA; these pages are MARKUP. Built the Gate-2 way, three invented businesses publish
straight to production untouched by any gate. Built ledger-driven, all four pages render EMPTY — and an
empty publicly-routed, sitemapped URL is worse than no page (dead weight, a visitor landing on nothing, and
a URL that outlives its fix). **Recommended: defer until a real customer consents.** Not built.

### ⚠️ AUDIT (B) — twelve named-competitor claims, none sourced

`Alternatives` names Mews, Cloudbeds, Guesty and Hostaway. ⚠️ **The design is unusually careful here** —
it calls them *"good products with real customers"*, has a section titled *"Where we'd tell you to buy
something else"*, and carries a real disclaimer including a trademark notice. The claims are POSITIONING,
not feature comparisons, and several are self-deprecating.

**But every one is unsourced — the disclaimer says so itself: *"We have not tested these products against
ours."*** Six characterisations (B1–B4 per vendor, B5 *"the market clusters in a similar band"* — an
unsourced claim about **competitor pricing**, B6 on booking engines), plus ⚠️ **B7: the disclaimer says
"at the time of writing" with no date anywhere — unfalsifiable, and it ages invisibly.**

`Compare` is worse: ⚠️ **"Typical cost: 15–18% of every booking"** (unsourced third-party pricing) and
⚠️ **no disclaimer, no trademark notice, no date at all** while naming five companies.

⚠️ **Under the refuse-the-unverifiable rule, removing these claims does not trim the pages — it removes
their subject.** Both are held. What would make each defensible: a citation + a *verified on* date, or
softening to a non-comparative statement about ourselves, or removal.

**Recommended mechanism (a sibling of Gate 5):** a `resources/marketing/claims.json` ledger — one entry per
external claim with `source_url` and `verified_on` — rendered through, and a CI gate that **fails the build
when a claim is past review or missing a source**. Otherwise a competitor claim rots exactly the way
`MAIL_MAILER=log` fails: silently, for a year.

### ⚠️ B12 — a live pricing contradiction, and I missed it in Gate 2

`/pricing` has been live since Gate 2 advertising **Starter €6 / Pro €4 per unit / Enterprise custom**.
`config/billing.php` charges **`per_unit_minor = 900` → €9/unit** under tiers named **Essential (€49/mo)**
and **Pro (€99/mo)**. The per-unit *model* matches; the *rate* is 50–125% out and the *plan names* do not
exist in the billing system. Both sides are labelled placeholder, so neither lies — but they are **two
placeholders that disagree on the money surface**, and a prospect quoted €9 after reading €4 has been
misled by an inconsistency nobody intended. ⚠️ Gate 2 reproduced the page faithfully and never reconciled
it against the app. **Founder's reconciliation required.**

> ⚠️⚠️ **SUPERSEDED 2026-08-22 (SAVE v2) — THIS ENTRY'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS WRONG, and the way it was wrong is
> the lesson.** *"The per-unit model matches; the rate is 50–125% out"* asserts that the engine bills per
> unit at €9. **It does not.** Probed against the real rows, all four seeded plans are `pricing_type = 'flat'`
> with `unit_rate_minor` **NULL**: the engine charges **flat €49 (Essential) and €99 (Pro)**, and
> `config('billing.per_unit_minor') = 900` seeds a column **no plan uses**. The per-unit machinery exists and
> is complete; nothing runs on it.
>
> ⚠️ So the divergence was never a rate mismatch — it was **model vs model**, which is a larger error than
> the one recorded here, and it survived two further gates because the €9 figure was read out of `config` and
> repeated rather than checked against `plans`. See the `/pricing` entry of 2026-08-22, which rebuilt the
> comparison table, bound every price and tier name to the engine, and added `MarketingPriceSourceTest`.
> ⚠️ **Read a config default as a default, not as what is charged.**

### ⚠️ My own new guard caught the nav — every page was naming four competitors

The Gate-1 nav's Alternatives row described itself as *"Mews, Cloudbeds, Guesty, Hostaway"*, so **every
page on the site named four competitors** while `/alternatives` is held. A nav row cannot advertise a
comparison the site does not serve. Replaced with that page's **own section heading** (the design's words,
not invented copy); restorable when the page ships with cited claims.

### ⚠️ D13 — the ruling named two instances; a sweep found SIX

Amara Mensah ×2 (Home), Marco Reyes (How It Works **and** For Hotels), Joris van Dijk (For Apartments),
Elena Kastellis (For Villas) — **three of them on pages built this very gate.** All replaced with
non-overlapping names (Bram Hoekstra · Petar Novak · Chara Melis · Nadia Farouk) and their avatar initials.
⚠️ **A register entry is one reader's finding — sweep.** Now a permanent test, because the content-honesty
gate reads the ledger and can never see a name typed into markup.

### Verification

`MarketingSalesPagesTest` 10 tests / 256 assertions; all four marketing suites **42 / 726** green.
⚠️ **The storefront control was written STRUCTURALLY CAPABLE this time** (Gate 2's lesson): it asserts
first that an EARLY `/{locale}/{page}` really does swallow `/book/seaside-demo` — the control proving it
can produce the failure — and only then that our registration order does not. Route-name collisions checked
before naming (all four free). The total route count is pinned in **one** file, not two (Gate 2's pin went
stale here — two files asserting one fact is a second definition, §N.8f).

**Mutations, each violate → RED → restore → GREEN:** a ledger name reintroduced into a page → RED on the
D13 sweep · a held page routed without a ruling → RED on both the count-pin and the held-pages guard · a
competitor name reintroduced → RED on the competitor guard.

## 2026-08-21 — FRONT WEBSITE · GATE 3b: the scenarios rewritten, the claims gate built, the price reconciled

Full detail: `docs/audits/FRONT-GATE3-HONESTY-AUDITS-2026-08-21.md` (Gate 3b section).

### (A) A rewrite, not a badge — and the URL was part of the claim

All six conditions met on four pages. Removed: three invented business identities with their city+size
pins · **four attributed quotes** (three blockquotes plus three quoted `<h2>` headings on the index) · the
`~20% → 50%+` stat block and the `4 days → 1 afternoon` callout · **nine animated result counters** · and
the **"Want to talk to one of them?"** section with its "Ask for a reference" CTA. Added: a prominent
label immediately after each `<h1>`.

⚠️ **The slug changed: `/case-studies/…` → `/example-scenarios/…`**, and the old URLs are asserted to 404.
A URL that says "case study" re-asserts exactly what the rewrite removed. This **deliberately diverges from
the design's sitemap** — a sitemap slug is not binding once the page's identity changes — and it was free
only because nothing had shipped.

### (B) The claims ledger + CI Gate 6 — the mechanism, not the sourcing

`claims.json` holds all 12 claims with `source_url` / `verified_on` / `review_by` / `disposition`; Gate 6
refuses anything unsourced, past review, or **missing an expiry** — a missing `review_by` **fails closed**,
because that is the B7 shape in code: *"at the time of writing"* with no date can never be shown stale.
**Nine sourceable · one requires-testing (Hostaway's "without heavy setup" — soften or drop) · two
page-level safeguards.** ⚠️ Sourcing is not testing, and the founder supplies the sources: `Alternatives`
and `Compare` stay unrouted and 404 until they do.

### ⚠️ (B12) The divergence was bigger than Gate 3 reported — correcting my own finding

I reported "billing charges €9/unit". **It does not.** Every seeded plan is `pricing_type = 'flat'`
(**€49 / €99**) with `unit_rate_minor` null; `config('billing.per_unit_minor')` seeds a column no plan
uses. So the site was advertising a **pricing MODEL the system does not run** — and its four-tier per-unit
ladder cannot express two flat plans, so the grid was rebuilt from the catalogue rather than re-numbered.
Names, amounts, the per-unit-vs-flat **suffix**, the feature gates and even the headline now derive from
`MarketingPricing`, pinned against `Plan::chargeFor()` — the method that actually bills. No third price
representation remains.

### ⚠️⚠️ THE LESSON OF THIS GATE: AN HONESTY FIX APPLIED AFTER GENERATION IS UNDONE BY THE NEXT GENERATION

D13's name fix and B12's home bindings were both applied by patching generated files. **Regenerating
reverted both** — the ledger names came back, and the hard-coded prices came back — and each was caught
only because a guard existed. Both now live **in the converter**, where regeneration preserves them.
⚠️ A fix downstream of a generator is not a fix; it is a delay.

### ⚠️ Four more things the adversarial verifiers and mutation caught

1. ⚠️ **I wrote a FALSE CLAIM into the four rewritten pages** — *"Guarded by MarketingScenarioTest"* — when
   no such test existed. Stub-and-pretend, in the files whose entire subject is not claiming things that
   are not true. **The honest repair was to write the guard, not soften the comment.**
2. ⚠️ **Three LIVE routed Sales pages were carrying the same fabricated testimonials** the case-study
   ruling was written about — blockquotes attributed to ledger people, including the very `~20% → 50%+`
   claim ordered deleted. The ruling named the case studies; the defect was one page over, live.
3. ⚠️ **The claims gate was VACUOUS on the real ledger.** Its fixtures proved the predicate; nothing
   asserted the actual data was clean, so marking a real entry sourced-but-expired left everything green.
   Mutation exposed it — in the gate built to prevent exactly that.
4. ⚠️ **My first `<figure>` strip was over-broad**, eating the home gallery's wrappers and orphaning their
   captions; and my first quote-sweep needle (`<figcaption`) conflated **photo captions** with attributed
   speech. Both narrowed. *(The design itself ships 29 figcaptions against 24 figures — those orphans are
   the designer's, faithfully reproduced.)*

### Verification

Six marketing suites **59 tests / 1,261 assertions** green. Mutations, each violate → RED → restore →
GREEN: a real ledger claim sourced-but-expired → RED · sourced with no expiry → RED · a quote reintroduced
into a scenario → RED · the scenario label removed → RED. Gate 3's route-count pin and held-page set were
**updated, not deleted**, to ruling A's new truth. Seven CI gates; the existing six untouched.

## 2026-08-22 — FRONT WEBSITE · GATE 4: `/try-booking` rebuilt as an honest sandbox (D3 = (b))

### The design-vs-truth gap

The design's page was a **client-side simulation** of a booking on **"Villa Azure, Paros, Greece · sleeps
6"** — a property that does not exist — ending in a **fabricated confirmation email**, under a meta
description promising *"Make a real booking on a demo property"*. Nothing was booked, nothing was sent, and
no such email existed. What is actually true: **`seaside-demo`** is *Demo Seaside Property*, Faro · Algarve
· Portugal, with a real *Double Room* (3 units) on a real *Flexible* plan at **€100.00/night**; the engine's
quote comes from `rate_calendar`; and `BookingConfirmationMail` is a real, branded template that embeds
**five live URLs — including `arrivalUrl`, the arrival-secrets page (#33)**.

### The five constraints

Every figure now mirrors the real property; the price comes from **`BookingEngineService::priceOver()`**,
the engine's own method (⚠️ `quote()` is never called — it persists a `booking_quotes` row); the
confirmation is the **real mail**; the meta and the page copy promise nothing; and the sandbox framing sits
**above** the preview, positionally asserted, because the confirmation step is where the illusion is
strongest.

⚠️ **What could NOT be mirrored, surfaced rather than invented:** the interactive date-picking. The
simulation *was* the fabrication — 25,000 characters of flow that touched no engine and ended in a fake
email — so it was removed rather than corrected. Making it genuinely interactive means driving the live
engine, which writes. The page instead shows the real thing and links to the live storefront.

### ⚠️ Nothing written, nothing sent, nothing leaked

Reservations, quotes, folios and payments are counted before and after **two** renders and are identical;
money as seeded is unchanged. Every URL the real mail computes is neutralised before the template sees it,
on a reservation built in memory and never saved.

### ⚠️⚠️ THE GUARD I WROTE WAS VACUOUS — and mutation, not review, found it

The first version of `MarketingTryBookingTest` ran against the empty test database, where the sandbox has
no property to mirror, so **every meaningful assertion hit an early `return`**. Removing the #33
URL-defusing entirely — which really does put five `/guest/reservation/…` links, including the arrival
page, into the preview — **left the file passing.** Its own header even claimed it ran against the demo
database.

⚠️ **That is Gate 3b's lesson repeating inside the guard written to honour it.** Fixed properly: the test
seeds the demo property, and `tbAssertNotVacuous()` now **fails** when there is nothing to check.

**Three more vacuity defects surfaced in the same battery, each caught by a mutation:**

1. ⚠️ **A needle that could never match.** The page guard searched for `/guest/arrival` — the real path is
   `/guest/reservation/{id}/arrival`. The needles are now **derived from the routes themselves**.
2. ⚠️ **A needle keyed to the sandbox reference**, so a leak carrying a *real* reservation id — the leak
   that would actually matter — sailed past. Now matches the **route pattern**, not one key.
3. ⚠️ **A needle too broad**: a blanket `http://` fired on `xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"`, and a
   blanket `/guest/` fired on the footer's legitimate D9 sign-in link. A guard that cries wolf gets
   loosened by the next person; both were narrowed to what is actually forbidden.

**Six mutations, each violate → RED → restore → GREEN:** the URL defusing removed (RED, naming the leaked
path) · a live arrival deep link planted with an arbitrary id · the sandbox banner removed · the invented
property reintroduced · the engine price replaced with a literal · the sandbox made to write a quote row.

### ⚠️ The sweep found what the ruling could not reach

D3 was scoped to `/try-booking`. The **nav's own row for it** read **"A real booking, no signup"** — on
**every page**, promising exactly what the rebuilt page refuses to do. Fixed, and the sitewide sweep is now
a permanent test. ⚠️ Same shape as Gate 3b's three live Sales pages: *a ruling scoped to one page reaches
neither the chrome nor its neighbours.*

### The generation lesson, applied

Every honesty transform — the meta rewrite, the property mirroring, the copy sweep, the mail substitution —
lives **in the converter**, and a test reads the generated FILE so a regeneration that dropped them reds.

⚠️ **And it nearly bit again:** Pint auto-imported `Tests\Feature\MarketingTryBookingTest` into
`TryBookingSandbox` because a docblock referenced it — app code depending on a test class, for a test that
did not yet exist. Removed; the guard is referenced by path and was written in the same change.

### Verification

`MarketingTryBookingTest` 9 tests / 121 assertions; all seven marketing suites **68 / 1,404** green.
Route-name collision checked; the storefront proof reuses the structurally-capable `/{locale}/{page}`
control. Earlier gates' route-count and pending-page pins updated **with the ruling**, never silently.

## 2026-08-22 — FRONT WEBSITE · GATE 4b: the sandbox picker restored, read-only (D3 = (b), continued)

⚠️ **The founder's ruling: a page called Try Booking where nothing can be tried is materially weaker than
D3 = (b) asked for.** Gate 4 removed the date picking on the grounds that real interactivity means driving
the engine, and the engine writes. ⚠️ **That was true of `quote()` and not of `priceOver()`** — the
read-only half the page was already pricing from. Gate 4's own report established the possibility; the
founder ruled the picker back.

### #1 — `priceOver()` proven read-only, by reading it

`app/Services/BookingEngineService.php:309-331` is one `RateCalendar::query()->…->get()` and an in-memory
sum. No `create`, `save`, `update`, `delete` or `DB::` statement; it calls nothing that has one. ⚠️ Read,
not inherited from Gate 4's summary — **a finding is a hypothesis**. `quote()` (`:97`) persists a
`booking_quotes` row and is never called.

### #2 — ⚠️⚠️ THE NEW RISK, AND WHY THERE IS NO ORACLE

Restoring the picker means prices reach the browser somehow, and **any server path that takes a property id
prices every customer on the platform for anyone who asks** — enumeration plus competitive intelligence on
our own customers' rates.

**Taken: the page itself accepts `?from=&to=&m=`. Not a client-side precompute, and not a new endpoint.**
⚠️ A client-side picker would have had to **sum nightly prices in JavaScript** — a second implementation of
the engine's own rule ("Σ nightly, refuse if any night is unpriced"), which is precisely how two surfaces
come to disagree about money (§N.8f) — and it would have let the confirmation email show a different stay
from the total above it. Server-side re-pricing means **one `priceOver()` call, one number, both surfaces**.
There is no JavaScript on the page at all, so the picker also works with scripting off.

⚠️ **The property is a CONSTANT, never an argument.** `TryBookingSandbox::DEMO_SLUG` cannot be reached by a
request. **Mutation-proven by attack**: a second organisation's property is seeded with distinct rates, and
`?property=` / `?slug=` / `?property_id=` / `?organization=` in seven shapes leaves the page pricing the demo
property only — while still pricing it, so the refusal is a refusal and not a blank page. Making the slug
request-readable turns the guard RED immediately. Proven again **in the browser** against the dev database's
real second property. The parameterised path is rate-limited (`throttle:try-booking`, ~60 reads per request);
the plain page is `Limit::none()` so crawlers are never 429ed — observed live: 429s on the dated path while
`/try-booking` and `/pricing` stayed 200.

### #3 — framing stronger, and copy pinned to control

Interactivity raises the illusion risk, so there are now **two refusals**: the banner **above the control**
(positionally asserted — a footnote under a picked total is too late by definition) and a second one landing
**with the number the visitor just produced**.

⚠️ Gate 4 found the hero still saying *"Pick your dates"* over a picker that no longer existed. The picker is
back, so the line is true again — and **the copy and the control are now pinned as a BICONDITIONAL**,
mutation-proven in both directions: removing the picker reds ("the copy invites a date picker that does not
render"), removing the copy reds ("a date picker renders but no copy invites it"), and a non-vacuity anchor
stops `false === false` satisfying it with the whole feature gone.

### #4 — every price is the engine's

Ten ranges of differing length and start agree with an independent `priceOver()` call to the cent, and each
of the ~60 visible calendar nights is compared against a fresh single-night call. Positive controls on the
data: at least six ranges must actually price, and not all to the same figure — a flat rate would let a wrong
sum look right. Re-deriving the total from the calendar rows instead of asking the engine reds.

**Unpriced dates are refused, not filled.** No total, no confirmation, no zero — the page says how many
nights have no published rate. **Sold-out dates too**: the real published rate is shown, the confirmation is
withheld, and the calendar marks the night **Booked** from real availability.

### #5 — ⚠️⚠️ MY OWN GUARD WAS VACUOUS AGAIN, AND MUTATION FOUND IT AGAIN

Gate 4's lesson was that a guard over empty data passes while checking nothing. Writing that lesson down did
not prevent it: **"⚠️ writes nothing, however hard the picker is used" passed on an empty database**, because
with no demo property every call returns null immediately, nothing is priced, and the counts match trivially.
The loop counted its own *requests*, which is not the same as counting its *work*. Fixed with positive
controls on what was actually done — stays really priced, confirmations really rendered — and re-proven: the
vacuity mutation now reds **12 of 20** tests with diagnostic messages, and the 8 that still pass are the
genuinely data-independent ones (two needle controls, the money descriptor, the rate limiter, the generated
file, three absence sweeps). Three further tests were erroring on a null offset instead of saying why; they
now refuse with a reason.

⚠️ **And the fixture now contains the dangerous shapes, not only the happy one** — a sold-out night, a gap in
the rate calendar, varying nightly prices, and a second organisation. Each is itself mutation-proven: fill the
gap and the unpriced test reds *"the fixture has no gap"*; remove the sold-out night and its test reds;
price the rival identically and the oracle test reds *"a leak would be invisible to every assertion here"*.

### ⚠️ #6 — TWO DEFECTS THE SUITE COULD NOT SEE

1. ⚠️ **The picker rendered perfectly and could not be used.** With a check-in chosen, every later cell
   **restarted** the range instead of completing it — the halfway state carries `picked => true` and a
   placeholder check-out, and the calendar keyed off `picked` alone. "The calendar renders a pickable date"
   passed throughout. **Found by clicking twice in a browser.** A guard that follows the page's own hrefs
   through two clicks to a priced stay now exists and reds on the reintroduced defect. *A control is only
   proven by following it to its outcome.*
2. ⚠️ **The two month grids collided.** In the half-width column October's last weekday was clipped and the
   digits overlapped. Every rendered *value* was correct; the page was simply unusable. **Found in a
   screenshot.** — the standing lesson that **static checks cannot see a rendered page**, twice in one gate.

### The converter and the sweep

Every transform lives in the converter; regenerating produced a **byte-identical** file and the guards stayed
green. The sitewide sweep was re-run: the nav's row had become an **understatement** of a page that now prices
real dates and was sharpened — ⚠️ deliberately **not** to "Pick your dates", because that is an *invitation*
and belongs only where the picker is (the row renders on every page, and a test now sweeps for exactly that).

### Nothing written

30 distinct picks against the live server plus a 429 burst, and 27 in-suite exercises with positive controls.
Reservations, quotes, folios, payments, `unit_rate_overrides`, `rate_calendar` (rows **and** sum) and
`availability` identical. Money as seeded `929 / 10,912,000 / 0 / 41 / 16 / 0` unchanged throughout.

**Still refused (#39):** the design's animated "watch the rate build itself", and its *"an OTA would have
taken €X"* comparison — no OTA commission rate is modelled for a direct booking.

## 2026-08-22 — FRONT WEBSITE · GATE 5: THE DOC-TRUTH AUDIT (27 pages) — **0 BUILT**

⚠️ **Documentation is a claim about how the product behaves, and no existing CI gate can see it.** The
content ledger governs DATA; these 27 pages are PROSE ABOUT BEHAVIOUR. Every guide asserts a feature exists
and works a particular way, and a wrong one generates support burden, refund disputes and — for Security,
GDPR and Payouts — legal exposure.

**All 27 were audited against the actual product before any was built. 591 claims: 142 TRUE · 188 PARTIAL ·
220 FALSE · 41 UNVERIFIABLE, 59 critical. Not one page can publish as written, and 0 were built.**
`docs/audits/FRONT-GATE5-DOC-TRUTH-AUDIT-2026-08-22.md` + the per-claim appendix beside it.

### ⚠️ The three sharpest, audited hardest

**PAYOUTS** — `STRIPE_CONNECT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is absent (`config/services.php:184` → null) and the engine is
test-mode by design, so "Processing — submitted to the bank" describes a rail whose confirming webhook cannot
verify a signature. "Paused funds … **withdrawable on demand**" is false: there is no owner-initiated
transfer rail, and the product says so itself. ⚠️ **`DO3-3` (failed-payout retry) turned out to be BUILT** —
`owner.payouts.retry` → `OwnerPayoutService::retry()`, row-locked and idempotent; the register was stale.

**SECURITY** — four claims are security properties the product does not have: **SMS 2FA** (no provider
anywhere; every SMS surface is honestly gated), **"Admins can require 2FA account-wide"** (no tenant-level
enforcement exists — only `PlatformAdmin`'s), **"approximate location"** in the session list (there is no
geolocation in the application), and ⚠️ **a "write availability" OAuth scope** — `OAuthScopes` is read-only
with exactly three scopes, so the page tells a reader an app can be granted a write the authorisation server
refuses to issue. ⚠️ A security claim is either backed by code or it is false; it is never softened.

**GDPR** — the entire Retention section navigates to **"Settings, Data and privacy"**, which does not exist
(the operator Settings screen has twelve sections; none is it), to set a **statutory period** that is not a
setting, for a **statutory anonymisation sweep that was never built** (`guests:process-deletions` executes
*guest-requested* deletions after a 14-day grace). ⚠️ And both "automatically" claims are true **only** under
the single `schedule:run` crontab line — which the page never mentions.

### ⚠️ Seven product findings — SURFACED, NEVER FIXED

⚠️⚠️ **P-6 and P-7 are the two that most deserve the founder's attention, and neither is about docs.**
**P-6:** `RoomType::create`, `RatePlan::create` and `Channel::create` appear **nowhere in `app/`** (only in
`DemoSeeder`), and the one `Unit::create` in `app/` is the owner add-unit approval path — so a tenant
provisioned through `/signup` has a property with **no room types, no units and no rate plans and no product
surface to add any**. **P-7:** the `property_user` allow-list's ONLY write (`PropertyController.php:73`) is
gated `if ($user->propertyAssignments()->exists())`, a condition nothing else can make true, so per-property
staff scoping is **unreachable in production** and every back-office user falls to the "all properties"
branch of #38.

**P-1** No operator UI writes `units.door_code` / `wifi_ssid` / `wifi_password` / `arrival_notes`; every
reference outside the model, seeders and tests is a READ. The arrival-secrets feature cannot be populated by
a real operator. **P-2** The door code releases on a **date** (`ArrivalPack::LEAD_DAYS = 2`), not on check-in
— a deliberate design, but not what three pages describe. **P-4** The operator Channels screen ships
hardcoded third-party commission rates (Booking.com 15% · Airbnb 3% · Expedia 15% · Vrbo 8%) — ledger entry
**B5**'s class, inside the app where the ledger cannot see it. **P-5** The GDPR page names no sub-processor;
Postmark is live and an Anthropic LLM seam is declared (inert by default — a disclosure obligation before it
is switched on).

⚠️ **Verification is honest about its own gap:** nineteen adversarial agents re-checked the sharp pages and
every FALSE call and **overturned nothing**; ⚠️ **eight more died on a session limit** — the seven
`/resources` articles and `/docs/settings` — so those eight stand **un-refuted, not verified**, and it is
recorded rather than glossed.

⚠️ **Two questions are the founder's and block everything else:** whether *"we never hold client funds"* can
stand when `createPaymentCheckout` opens the Session on the **platform's own Stripe account** and owners are
paid by a `transfer` out of the platform balance; and whether the **DPA** two pages assert actually exists.

### ⚠️ Why no subset could publish

Every one of the 23 guide/article pages carries **"Guide N of 16"** / **"Article N of 7"** and each guide
renders the full sixteen-item sibling list; `/faq` announces "18 questions". **Each page asserts the whole
set exists**, so publishing two articles would put "Article 4 of 7" on a site with two — the same false-count
shape as the chrome below. Removing the counters is a *doc fix*, which is the founder's option to pick.

### ⚠️ The chrome sweep — the fourth instance, and this time already LIVE

`footer.blade.php:17` announced *"Multi-currency pricing and a documentation library — **prices in EUR, GBP
or USD**, and **sixteen written guides**"* **on every page**. Both halves false: `config/billing.php` has one
`default_currency` ('EUR') and all four plan rows are EUR; zero guides are published. `nav.blade.php:57` read
`desc="Sixteen written guides"`, likewise sitewide. **Both fixed** — the strip removed (KIND-2 is refused,
not restyled; real release notes are the Changelog's, Gate 6) and the nav description stripped of its count.

### ⚠️ The lessons this gate re-taught

⚠️ **A content sweep is blind to the absence it seeks (§N.27.1).** I swept the seven articles for `%`, `€`
and "Vyrobel", found almost nothing, and provisionally called five clean. **They are not** — the claims that
matter contain no number and no brand: *"Most operators answer no to at least two"*, *"Marketplaces treat
operator-side cancellations badly, and repeated ones affect your ranking"*, *"Most OTA contracts in Europe no
longer enforce strict price parity"*. 210 unsourced figures were extracted in total. ⚠️ And the same blindness
hid the **closing CTA card on every article**, each of which is a product claim — found only by reading.

⚠️ **Confirm-first cuts both ways (§N.27.11) — five times in one session.** `DO3-3` was built · recovery
codes exist · `payout_currency`/`fx_rate` are modelled · an editable role-permission matrix exists · all four
housekeeping CTA capabilities are real. ⚠️ **And once it saved a false product finding from reaching the
founder:** a proposed defect — *"a failed payout appears in none of the Balance page's four buckets"* — was
withdrawn on opening the file, because there is a **fifth** bucket, *Carried forward*, defined in the code as
covering exactly *"one whose only payout failed"*.

⚠️ **A needle that cannot match proves nothing.** A grep for `logoutOtherDevices` found nothing and would
have made "changing a password signs out other sessions" FALSE; the file says `changePasswordTo($password,
$currentSessionId)` and terminates every other session. **TRUE, and only opening it showed that.**

## 2026-08-22 — FRONT WEBSITE · GATE 6: the honest cookie notice (D11) + the DPA claims removed

### ⚠️ What is actually set — enumerated from the code AND read off the wire

| cookie | purpose | lifetime | set when | strictly necessary? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vyrobel-session` | the session (sign-in, a booking in progress) | 2 h | every first page view | yes |
| `XSRF-TOKEN` | CSRF protection for every form | 2 h | every first page view | yes |
| `vy_td` | remembers a device the user chose to trust, so 2FA does not re-ask | 30 d | only on ticking "trust this device" at a 2FA prompt | yes — security, at the user's own request |
| `vy_cookie_choice` | the answer to this notice | 365 d | only on answering | yes — it exists to honour a privacy choice |

Confirmed empirically: `/`, `/pricing`, `/book/seaside-demo` and `/guest/login` each set **exactly two** —
`XSRF-TOKEN` and `vyrobel-session`. **No analytics, no marketing, no third-party cookie, and no third-party
request at all** (fonts are self-hosted, F6-6). There is **no `remember` checkbox in any login form**, so the
framework's remember-me cookie is never issued through the UI — a latent path in `GuestLoginRequest`, noted.

### ⚠️ WHY THERE IS NO "ANALYTICS" TOGGLE — the design's own spec, refused

The design's Launch Checklist specifies *"Per-category cookie consent … marketing off by default"*.
⚠️ **Per-category consent cannot be reproduced faithfully, because there is exactly one category.** A
"Marketing — off" switch that stores nothing and gates nothing is the #39 shape, and here it is **worse than
no dialog at all**: a visitor who switched it off would believe they had opted out, and the first analytics
snippet added later without reading that choice would override them silently — with no failing test, no log
line and no monitor. So the notice states what is true (*"there is nothing on this notice to switch off
today"*) and records the answer anyway, because the answer is **forward-binding**.

### ⚠️ THE FORWARD-GUARD IS THE FEATURE — CI Gate 7 (the eighth gate)

`CookieConsentForwardGuardTest` reds if: a cookie reaches a browser that the disclosure does not describe ·
`app/` writes one outside the catalogue · a third-party vendor appears in a file that does not consult the
stored consent · a non-essential cookie is declared with nothing calling `CookieConsent::allows()`.

⚠️ **It is SATISFIABLE BY COMPLIANCE, deliberately.** The first version forbade every vendor outright — which
makes a wall, not a gate, and the first person who genuinely needs analytics deletes it instead of complying
(§N.17.5). Mutation-proven both ways: an ungated `googletagmanager` snippet → **RED**; the same snippet
wrapped in `CookieConsent::allows()` → **GREEN**.

⚠️ **Its own vacuity check, because check D is inert today.** Three consecutive gates shipped a fresh guard
that inherited the previous blind spot, so the forward-binding predicate is extracted and run **on every
run** against a synthetic catalogue containing an ungated `_ga`, and required to fire. ⚠️ Honest limit,
stated in the file and in CI: the vendor and cookie sweeps pattern-match, so a novel injection path escapes
them and is a review rule — but the disclosure check reads the real `Set-Cookie` of a real response and
cannot be evaded by whatever route a cookie took.

**Twelve mutations, each violate → RED → restore → GREEN:** ungated analytics · gated analytics (GREEN, the
point) · a non-essential cookie with no `allows()` caller · a cookie outside the catalogue · decline styled
quieter than accept · consent failing OPEN · the record exposed to script · the notice removed sitewide · an
open redirect · the source scanner neutered (the vacuity check) · the DPA claim reintroduced · a hardcoded
cookie count.

### ⚠️ Three defects no assertion caught

1. ⚠️ **The banner shipped a fabricated number.** It read *"3 cookies"* — neither the catalogue size (4) nor
   what a visitor receives (2) — on every page, in the chrome of the gate about not fabricating things.
   **Found in a screenshot.** Every figure is now derived from the catalogue and pinned to both the catalogue
   and the wire.
2. ⚠️ **The notice reflected the whole request URI into a hidden field**, so any query a visitor arrived with
   was echoed into the HTML. Blade escapes it, so not an injection — but needless reflected surface, and
   **found by ANOTHER gate's guard**: Gate 4b's pricing-oracle test failed with *"leaked another property's
   slug"* because this field had put it there. It carries the path only now.
3. ⚠️ **PHPStan proved the forward-binding branch was dead code** — read as a `const`, every category folds to
   the literal `'essential'`. Correct today and exactly what must not stay true. The catalogue is now reached
   through a typed accessor that declares `category` as the open string it genuinely is.

### The mechanics

Persisted and demonstrable (**choice + timestamp + disclosure version**; a record against an older version is
refused and re-prompts). **Nothing non-essential is set before the answer** — there is nothing non-essential
to set. **Decline is the same control as accept**: same route, same method, same one click, and the two
buttons carry a byte-identical style string, asserted. No checkboxes, so nothing pre-ticked. **No
JavaScript** — a server-rendered form, working with scripting off, with no client state a persistent worker
could leak. **No third-party CMP** (F6-6). **Not a modal**: `role="region"`, last in the DOM and last in tab
order, no focus trap, no `aria-modal`, no full-screen overlay — the page stays operable with the notice
ignored, which is both the accessible choice and the non-coercive one. Verified in a browser at 390px and
1200px: keyboard-only decline → recorded; reopened from the footer on another page → changed to accept;
choice shown back with its date and version; 49% / 32% of the viewport after the copy was tightened.

⚠️ **SURFACED, NOT DECIDED: the notice renders on the MARKETING shell only.** The same two cookies are set on
the storefront and in the guest/owner/operator/admin realms — the disclosure is true everywhere, but the
notice is not shown there. Extending it touches the sealed storefront (E3) and the app shells, which is a
founder call and its own change.

### ⚠️ The DPA claims — removed; Article 28 is a GO-LIVE item

The DPA does not exist. ⚠️ It appears in **no built page and no ledger entry** — only in `/docs/gdpr-and-data`
and the FAQ, both deferred by Gate 5. So the removal went into the **converter**, where a page generated
later cannot inherit it, and what survives is true (Vyrobel *is* the processor, acting on the operator's
instruction); only the assertion that an agreement sets it out is gone.

⚠️ **The converter cannot cover every path, and the gap is named.** The FAQ's copy lives inside a `DCLogic`
`<script>` the converter strips wholesale, so the transform never sees that sentence. Gate 5 recorded that
publishing the FAQ requires lifting that array into a server-rendered source — a lift that happens outside
the converter, on which day the claim returns. A sweep in `MarketingContentHonestyTest` (CI Gate 5) reds on
the phrase in any built marketing view, with its own positive control.

⚠️⚠️ **REMOVING THE CLAIM DOES NOT REMOVE THE DUTY. Article 28 requires the agreement to exist before a
customer's guest data is processed — a GO-LIVE BLOCKER, alongside the Stripe live-key flip and the
`schedule:run` crontab entry.** Not drafted here: that is legal work, not a build step.

⚠️ **Untouched, as ruled:** the *"never hold client funds"* claim (awaiting its flow-verification pass — not
published, not softened) and product findings **P-6** and **P-7**, which remain recorded in the Gate 5 audit
and are their own gates.

## 2026-08-22 — P-6 · GATE 1: THE BOOKING BLOCKERS — a real tenant can now sell

⚠️ The reachability sweep proved `BookingEngineService::search()` iterates `RoomType` rows and **no creation
path existed anywhere in `app/`**, so a `/signup` tenant reached a property they could never make sellable.
⚠️ And the application **instructed the impossible** — *"Finish setup — add units, rates & channels — to go
live"* — which is worse than an absent feature, because the tenant concludes they are failing.

### #1 The minimum sellable chain, derived from the code

`search()` (`app/Services/BookingEngineService.php:48-96`) offers a room type only when **all four** hold:
**(a)** a `RoomType` on the property with `max_adults >= adults` and `max_children >= children` · **(b)**
`minAvailable() >= 1`, which reads `availability` rows and treats a **missing row as zero** · **(c)** an
**active** `RatePlan` · **(d)** `rate_calendar` rows for **every** night (`priceOver()` returns null if one
is unpriced).

⚠️ **So the chain is larger than "three screens": a unit only becomes sellable once availability is
MATERIALISED.** `AvailabilityService::recompute()` is what does it, and `OwnerUnitRequestService:231` was the
existing precedent — reused, not reinvented. ⚠️ **`RateCalendar` was confirmed genuinely reachable**
(`POST /app/rates` → `RateActionController@apply` → `RateAndRestrictionService`); the sweep's naive grep had
been wrong about it, and re-checking cost nothing.

### ⚠️ #2 THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION — a fresh tenant completes a booking

`tests/Feature/TenantCanBecomeSellableTest.php` provisions through `TenantProvisioningService` exactly as
`/signup` does, asserts it starts with **zero** room types, units and rate plans, then goes through the
app's own HTTP paths: room type → unit → rate plan → rates → `search()` returns an offer → `quote()` →
`book()` returns a reservation with a reference. ⚠️ **No seeder, no factory, no direct model write anywhere
on that path** — a factory call would substitute for the very path being proved.

### #3 The pattern, and the wireframe

`InventoryActionController` is `PropertyController` in every respect that matters: workspace read-only guard,
`$request->validate()`, parent resolved from the actor's own scope, `Model::create()` with `organization_id`
auto-filled, PRG redirect. ⚠️ **No operator wireframe exists** for these screens (only OWNER unit ones) —
registered in `DIVERGENCE-REGISTER.md` rather than passed over.

### ⚠️ #4 Tenancy — and a FALSE GREEN mutation found in my own guard

The cross-org test looked correct and **passed under a broken scoping**. ⚠️ Two reasons, both instructive:
the 404 it observed came from **`AvailabilityService`'s own** tenant-scoped `findOrFail` deep inside
`recompute()` — *after* `Unit::create` had already run — and the "nothing landed" assertion counted rows
**inside the victim's org**, while a cross-org write auto-fills `organization_id` from the **attacker's**
context, so the row landed in the attacker's org and the victim's scope reported zero.
⚠️ **A tenancy check must be independent of the tenancy it checks (§N.18.1)** — it uses raw `DB::table()`
queries now, and **M2b (every scope in the action removed) REDs with a 302 where a 404 belongs**.

That mutation also exposed a real ordering weakness: `Unit::create` ran before the recompute, so a throw in
between would leave a unit with no availability — **inventory that exists and is silently unsellable, the
exact defect this gate removes.** Both are now in one transaction.

**RatePlan touches money**: currency is taken from the **property**, never the request, and `is_active` is
forced true or `cheapestRatePlan()` silently skips the plan. A newly created plan prices at **298.50 for
three nights at 99.50**, checked through the engine's own `priceOver()` — independent of the creation path.

⚠️ **P-7 is not depended on and not fixed.** Scoping is by ORGANISATION, which works. `resolveProperty()`
carries the note naming the one place a later P-7 fix must touch.

### ⚠️ #5 The reachability guard

A separate test states the rule directly: every entity a tenant must create has a **registered, POST,
permission-gated** route. Mutation-proven (removing the room-type route REDs it with the P-6 diagnosis), and
**extensible — the other eleven seeder-only entities are one row each.**

### ⚠️ #6 RENDER-VERIFY caught what nothing else could

⚠️ **`/app/rates` returned a 500 while the suite, PHPStan and Pint were all green.** Three directives written
as `yet@endunless`, `it@else` and `one@endif` were never compiled — **Blade ignores a directive whose `@`
follows a word character** (the `\B` rule that lets `foo@bar.com` render literally), leaving an unclosed `if`
that blew up on the next `@endforeach`. ⚠️ I made the same mistake **three times in one edit**, and it is
documented in CLAUDE.md. A render guard now asserts both screens return 200 and leak no raw directive, with
its own positive control; reintroducing the trap REDs it.

Browser-verified as the demo operator: created a room type, then a unit, saw both flashes and the new row,
and confirmed the rates page offers the plan form with the room type marked *"— no plan yet"*. The
verification rows were removed afterwards.

### #7 The guidance is now true — and the sweep found FIVE sites, not two

`OnboardingController:81` (the first sentence a new tenant reads) · `PropertyController:81` ·
`portfolio.blade.php:253` · `onboarding.blade.php:175` · `RateActionController`'s post-apply summary.
⚠️ **Channels are no longer instructed anywhere in the setup path**, because they remain impossible
(decision ④, where *remove* is still a live option).

**Out of scope and untouched:** channels · statement finalisation (⚠️ decision ② — the ledger accrues on
CHARGES not receipts, so finalisation alone would pay owners against uncollected revenue; that pair must be
fixed together) · P-7 · the seeder (money-as-seeded byte-identical).

### ⚠️ #8 Two more found while VERIFYING, not while building

⚠️ **A hidden `std_occupancy="2"` would have PUBLISHED A FIGURE NOBODY TYPED.** The room-type form carried it
as a constant to satisfy validation — and `std_occupancy` is **rendered to guests** on the public room page as
*"Standard occupancy"*. A room type sleeping 4 would have advertised 2. Found by grepping where the column is
READ before committing, not by any test. It is derived from `max_adults` now, and the acceptance test pins
**the payload the form actually posts**, not one only a test sends (§N.27.9 in reverse — a dormant input
feeding a live display).

⚠️ **THE IMPOSSIBLE INSTRUCTION HAD A SIXTH SITE.** I fixed five, then swept for the phrase instead of
trusting the count: `portfolio.blade.php:219` — *"You'll set up units, rates & channels next"* — **34 lines
above one I had already edited, in the same modal** (§N.13.1, §N.27.1). ⚠️ Left alone deliberately:
`channels.blade.php`'s *"connect one below"* points at a panel that says **"Setup required — needs your
Channex partner account"**, so it signposts an honest deferral, not an impossible action.

### #9 Verification

Full suite **2625 tests · 2623 passed · 2 skipped · 18,041 assertions**, run ALONE. PHPStan L5 **0**; Pint
clean; every view compiles; **money as seeded unchanged**; the **eight CI gates and the seeder untouched**
(0 changed files under `.github/`, `ops/`, `database/seeders/`). Browser-verified as the demo operator:
a room type, a unit **and** a rate plan created through the real forms, each flash and each new row correct;
verification rows removed afterwards and the money check re-run.

⚠️ **MOBILE, HONESTLY:** the forms add **no** overflow — the card measures exactly the width of the main
column. But the operator shell is **desktop-fixed**: at a 390px viewport `/app/units` has a 754px scroll
width and `/app/reservations`, which this gate never touched, has **850px**. That is a pre-existing property
of the realm, not of this change, and is not "fixed" here. (The console errors on `/app/units` are equally
pre-existing: demo photo URLs are absolute `localhost:8000` while the page is served from `127.0.0.1`, so
CSP `img-src 'self'` blocks them.)

## 2026-08-22 — FRONT WEBSITE · GATE 7: THE COMPANY PAGES (audit-first, with a legal boundary)

Ten prototypes audited against the code before a line was built. **147 claims, 75 FALSE.** Four pages
published with every false claim corrected; six refused, each on a ruling.
Full detail: `docs/audits/FRONT-GATE7-DOC-TRUTH-AUDIT-2026-08-22.md`.

### ⚠️ #1 The legal boundary held — structure and a cited inventory, no drafted text

⚠️ **NO PRIVACY-POLICY OR TERMS TEXT WAS WRITTEN**, and neither page is published or routed. A
plausible-looking policy is worse than none: the founder would rely on it, and so would their customers'
auditors. What was produced instead is the thing only this codebase can produce — **`docs/legal/DATA-INVENTORY.md`,
142 cited entries across five domains**, plus `PRIVACY-STRUCTURE.md` and `TERMS-STRUCTURE.md` giving the
design's own section order with what the code supports under each.

⚠️ **They are DOCUMENTS, not unrouted Blade views.** An unrouted view is dead code one route away from being
live, and the one thing these must never do is get published by accident.

⚠️ **96 of the 142 entries have no retention rule, no deletion path, or both** — the single most useful output.
Five are GDPR-material today, and the first is the worst shape a gap can take:

⚠️ **A CODE COMMENT DEFERS A GDPR CASE TO A MECHANISM THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** `Guest::anonymize()` states at
`app/Models/Guest.php:349-351` that abandoned booking quotes *"are cleared by the scheduled retention purge,
not from here."* **There is no scheduled retention purge** — the eight scheduled commands are enumerated in
`routes/console.php:15-72` and none touches `BookingQuote`. A prospective guest's encrypted email, phone and
snapshot are retained indefinitely and are unreachable by erasure, while the code reads as though handled.
⚠️ **Not an absence — an absence with a comment saying it is covered.** The next reader ticks the box.

Also: **no account deletion exists for any human account or organisation** (`SoftDeletes` is declared on
`User` and never called) · `audit_events` holds IP and user-agent permanently with no prune ·
`webhook_events.payload` retains OTA guest name/email/phone verbatim, unreachable by erasure · **backups are
an unfiltered `mysqldump`, so a restore reinstates erased data** · staff leave requests carry a free-text
`reason` (possible Article 9) with no retention and no delete route · and **`localStorage` is undisclosed
terminal-equipment storage**, in ePrivacy scope on the same footing as a cookie.

✅ Two corrections in the founder's favour, both found by re-checking: **`ops/deploy.sh:168-179` installs the
scheduler cron itself** (an idempotent append) — so the "GDPR depends on a crontab line nobody installs"
caveat is out of date; and **backups exist with a proven restore drill**.

> ⚠️ **CORRECTED 2026-08-22 (SAVE v2), and the correction matters more than the claim.** This paragraph
> originally added *"and refuses to deploy if told to skip it"*. **It does not.** `fail()` at
> `ops/deploy.sh:53` only prints to stderr; `set -euo pipefail` does not fire on a successful `printf`; the
> script's only `exit 1` is the health check at `:203`. A deploy run with `DEPLOY_NO_CRON_INSTALL=1` prints a
> red line and **completes**, leaving the 14-day erasure and the 30-day ID purge unscheduled. ⚠️ That
> over-claim was written here, carried into `docs/legal/DATA-INVENTORY.md`, and from there into the next
> session's brief — three surfaces, one unchecked sentence. Found by opening `deploy.sh` during the
> reconciliation pass. **The §7.2 scheduler heartbeat, not the deploy, is what catches the skipped case.**

### ⚠️ #2 Two findings are PRODUCT defects, not copy defects — reported, not fixed

⚠️ **NINETEEN OPERATOR SCREENS CARRY NO PERMISSION GATE, AND THREE RENDER MONEY.** The design claims *"a
housekeeper sees rooms, not revenue."* The role catalogue models that correctly and the dedicated Reports,
Insights and Guests screens refuse Housekeeping — but `routes/web.php:620` registers `/app/dashboard` with no
`can:`, and `OperatorDashboard.php:123` computes "Revenue today" unconditionally. The marketing sentence was
cut back to the two clauses that ARE enforced. ⚠️ **The gate itself is a separate change and the founder's
call.** The second is the phantom retention purge above.

### #3 The six refusals

⚠️ **`careers`** — its subject is a company that does not exist: four openings at a one-person business, a
studio in Rotterdam, published salary bands, a four-day fortnight that *"survived two release crunches"*
(**zero releases**), on-sites *"at a property that runs on Vyrobel"* (**no customers**), *"the best hires
we've made"* (**no hires**), and one role card asserting *"two operator customers"*. Removing the false claims
removes the page. ⚠️ **Nothing is discarded by refusing it** — verified, not assumed: the page has **no form
and no file input**; all five CTAs point at `/contact`, which now works. Rule #4's premise is not met.

⚠️ **`changelog`** — ⚠️ **the brief said seven entries; there are EIGHT.** Three predate the repository's
first commit (2026-07-02): 26 May, 9 June, 23 June. **Two are dated in the FUTURE** — 22 September and
6 October — and the 6 October one is presented as most recently shipped, 45 days ahead of today. Nothing has
ever shipped: zero tags across 863 commits, no deploy run, `APP_ENV=local`. ⚠️ **No labelling cures a date
that cannot have happened.** A real DEVELOPMENT log could later be derived from `DECISIONS.md`; that is a
different claim and a founder decision.

⚠️ **`demo-confirmed`** — the post-submit state of the demo booker refused with D5.
⚠️ **`privacy` / `terms`** — the legal boundary above.

### #4 Contact — built, because a form that does not send is #39

⚠️ The design's submit was an `sc-camel-on-click` handler with no `<form>`, no `action` and no endpoint —
**and `key="contact"` appears 21 times across nine PUBLISHED pages**, so it is the destination of nearly every
call to action the site makes. It now posts to a real route: validated, throttled per IP, honeypotted, and
written to `marketing_contact_messages` **inside a transaction BEFORE any mail is attempted**.

⚠️ **THE ROW IS THE SYSTEM OF RECORD; THE EMAIL IS A NOTIFICATION** — because `MailSafetyGuard` downgrades
every sending transport to `log` outside production, so a mail-only form would silently destroy every message
sent before go-live. ⚠️ It also works with **no destination configured** (`MARKETING_CONTACT_TO` is blank in
`.env.example` — the address is the founder's and no placeholder is shipped): an unset address costs the
notification, never the message.

⚠️ Refused with it: **no auto-reply** (a reply-time promise nothing keeps — the design asserted one twice),
**no demo slot picker** (D5; there is no scheduling package, no meeting provider and no invite generator, so
it would name a time and book nothing), **no support widget** (D4; it would be the first third-party request
on a site that deliberately makes none). Also removed: an invented `support@vyrobel.com`, two offices, and a
*"Quoting the GROWTH plan"* banner for a plan that does not exist.

### ⚠️ #5 The generator now refuses to finish on a silent no-op

⚠️ **THE GATE-6 DPA TRANSFORM — written explicitly so "a page built later would otherwise inherit the
sentence" — MATCHED NONE OF THE SIX DPA MENTIONS ON THE THREE GATE-7 PAGES IT WAS MEANT TO PROTECT.** It
looked like forward protection and was a record of the four phrasings one reader had seen. That is the third
silent no-op in this project (the B12 price needle, this, and Gate 7's own first draft).

So the converter gained a **reporting matcher**: it normalises the punctuation the design mixes and **records
every needle**, and the generator **exits non-zero when one matched nothing**. Mutation-proven — a
one-character change to a needle makes it refuse. It immediately earned itself three times: a needle that
no-oped because an *earlier transform in the same pipeline* had already rewritten its text; four needles left
dead by a later element cut; and a needle transcribed from a truncated dump.

⚠️ **AND IT CANNOT CATCH EVERYTHING.** Three Integrations corrections were **lost in a refactor** — the hero
still asserted a live channel sync directly above three pills reading "Not connected". A needle that was
never written matches nothing to report. **Only opening the page found it.**

### ⚠️ #6 ALL NINETEEN MARKETING PAGES HAD LOST THE DESIGN'S RESPONSIVE RULES

⚠️ The prototypes are inline-styled, but their **responsive behaviour lives in a `<style>` block — and the
converter strips `<style>` with `<script>`.** Every page kept the design's hooks (`data-h1` and `data-sec` on
all 19, `data-two` on 9, `data-bandinner` on 8) and **nothing read one of them.** The public marketing site
was non-responsive below 980px for six gates.

⚠️ **NO ASSERTION COULD HAVE FOUND IT.** The pages returned 200, leaked no raw Blade, and **did not even
overflow** — a grid squeezes its columns rather than overflowing, so `document.scrollWidth` looked perfect
while the contact card sat at 241px on a phone. **Layout does not fail loudly.** Found by taking a screenshot
at 390px.

Fixed by extracting the **114 declarations across 10 breakpoints** from the 19 masters' own stylesheets into
the shared shell — the design's rules, not invented ones, all `max-width`, so no desktop rendering changes.
Guarded and mutation-proven.

### #7 Verification

Suite green, run ALONE. PHPStan L5 **0**; Pint clean; **money as seeded unchanged**; the **eight CI gates,
`ops/` and the seeder untouched** (0 changed files). **Nine mutations, all RED**, each guard with its own
vacuity check. All four pages browser-verified at desktop and 390px, and a real POST proven end to end
through the running server.

**Out of scope and untouched:** the 19 ungated operator screens · the phantom retention purge · channels ·
statement finalisation (②) · P-7 · the seeder · **and NO SEO artifacts** — the published set is still moving,
and when the sitemap comes the storefront must end up ALLOWED and SITEMAPPED.

## 2026-08-22 — `/pricing`: THE INVENTED TIER TABLE (live · money · one source)

B12 rebuilt `/pricing`'s CARDS to read from `config/billing.php` and pinned them against `Plan::chargeFor()`.
⚠️ **The comparison table ONE SECTION BELOW, on the same page, kept a hand-drawn ladder of four invented
tiers and twelve invented feature differences** — §N.13.1 at its tightest radius yet, live, and about money.

### ⚠️ #1 The sweep found ELEVEN representations, of which B12 had bound two

⚠️ **And the sweep had to be redone twice**, each time by checking a category rather than a count: a first
pass grepped `description=` and missed the **SEO title** asserting the model in three words; probing the
rendered page then found the FAQ describing per-unit *mechanics* — a third class entirely, neither a price
nor a name.

| # | where | what | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–2 | `/pricing` cards, headline/priceNote/whoPays | price + suffix + model | ✅ bound (B12) — **and see #5** |
| 3 | `/pricing` **comparison table** | 4 invented tiers × 12 rows | **rebuilt from the config** |
| 4 | `/pricing` **Enterprise card** | a fifth tier + segment + 4 bullets | **removed** |
| 5 | `/pricing` **SEO title** | *"per-unit plans"* | bound to the real model |
| 6 | `/pricing` **SEO description** | *"simple per-unit plans"* | bound |
| 7–8 | `/pricing` **FAQ ×2** | per-unit billing mechanics | rewritten from the flat model |
| 9 | `/` teaser **prices** | €49 / €99 + suffix | ✅ **still bound — verified** |
| 10 | `/` teaser **names, bands, ladder** | Starter / Growth / "Pro & Enterprise", *"Up to 10 units"* | **bound / removed** |
| 11 | `/switching` **h2 + body + meta** | *"included on Growth and above"* | **removed** |

⚠️ **#10 IS THE SHARPEST.** Gate 3b bound the home teaser's PRICES and left its NAMES hand-written beside
them — so the page rendered **the real €49 under the invented label "Starter"**. Worse than either being
wrong alone: the number is authoritative and the label is fiction. **Binding half a representation leaves
the other half free to drift.**

### #2 A four-column ladder cannot express two flat plans

The engine charges **two FLAT tiers — Essential €49.00/mo (€490/yr), Pro €99.00/mo (€990/yr)** — every
seeded row `pricing_type = 'flat'`, `unit_rate_minor` NULL (`per_unit_minor = 900` seeds a column no plan
uses). Counted against the config, **the real differences are exactly TWO**: `channels` (Pro only) and
`team` (5 seats vs unlimited). `analytics` is on both, so it is not a difference. ⚠️ **The drawn table
manufactured ten more**, and re-numbering would not have fixed it: four columns assert three upgrade steps
and the product has one boundary. Rebuilt at the size the truth actually is via a new
`MarketingPricing::comparison()`, whose rows ARE the catalogue the paywall and `planAllows()` read.

⚠️ **IT WAS ALSO BROKEN, AND ONLY THE BROWSER SHOWED IT.** The design's `<sc-raw-table>` is not a table —
it is an unknown element with `display: inline`, so `border-collapse` did nothing and the section rendered
as **inline soup**: four tier headers jumbled over each other, check cells floating as orphaned dashes.
Zero real `<table>` elements were in it.

### ⚠️ #3 `/pricing` HAD BECOME UN-REGENERABLE — the deeper finding

⚠️ **B12's binding lived only in the GENERATED file.** The inline-PHP block and the tier loop existed nowhere
in the converter, so running the generator over `/pricing` would have **silently restored the design's four
hardcoded tiers on the CARDS too**. That is the converter's own doctrine — *a post-generation patch is undone
by the next generation* — turned on the FIX rather than the defect. Found only because Gate 7's zero-match
rule was extended to the B12 price needle and it came back a no-op.

⚠️ **AND I THEN WALKED INTO THE OTHER HALF OF IT.** Having ported the cards into `<x-marketing.plan-cards />`
and regenerated, the page came back saying *"One price per unit"* under a table correctly reading €49/€99 —
because `headline()`, `priceNote()` and `whoPays()` were **also** hand-bound and I had not checked. **Having
found one hand-edit, DIFF for the rest rather than assuming it was the only one.** All four now live in the
converter; `pxbuild.py` proves the page rebuilds without losing them.

### #4 Three real bugs found on the way, two of them latent since Gate 7

⚠️ **`_element_span()` had an off-by-length bug.** `rfind(sub, 0, i + 1)` cannot match a `<div` that BEGINS
at `i`, so a needle starting with its own tag cut the **previous sibling** — and reported success, because a
span *was* found. Fixed, plus an enclosure check that refuses a span not containing its needle. ⚠️ **The
report proves a match, not the right match** — an honest limit, now narrowed.

⚠️ **Blade compiles STATEMENTS BEFORE it strips COMMENTS**, so a directive written inside a Blade comment is
compiled anyway. An inline-PHP directive in a docblock opened a real PHP block that swallowed the block
defining `$mkTiers`, and `/pricing` 500'd. ⚠️ A sweep found **17 directives inside comments** across the
views; only that one was fatal, and `pdfs/owner-statement.blade.php` documents this exact bug **in a comment
that still contains the directive causing it** (checked: currently harmless).

⚠️ **The home teaser's prices were bound but UNMARKED**, so the new guard could not see them and counted two
price nodes where four exist. A binding nothing can find is a binding nothing protects.

### #5 The durable guard — mutation-proven, and one mutation exposed it blind

`MarketingPriceSourceTest`: no plan name the config does not define · no `data-price` value the engine would
not charge · the model wording derived from `shape()` · the rendered comparison row count equal to the gated
feature count.

⚠️ **SIX MUTATIONS, and the third one PASSED first time.** The comparison guard compared
`comparison()` against the config — the source checked against itself — so inventing a row **in the view**
left it green (§N.18.1). It now counts `<th scope="row">` in the RENDERED table. Two more holes came out of
the same run: `unit_rate_minor ?? 0` had put **"0.00" in the allow-list**, so a binding resolving to nothing
would have passed; and the vacuity check caught that `plans` is EMPTY under `RefreshDatabase`, which made the
whole price comparison run against an empty allow-list until the real seeder was added.

⚠️ **ITS LIMIT, STATED:** it pattern-matches. A price written in words, inside an image or in an SVG path is
invisible to it, as is copy in an unrendered branch. Those remain a review rule. It also deliberately ignores
product figures — a mocked folio total of €8,412.60 is not a subscription price, which is why the model check
is scoped to `/pricing` (`/modules` legitimately says "per-unit **performance**" about owner reporting).

### #6 Verification

Suite green, run ALONE. PHPStan L5 0; Pint clean; **money as seeded unchanged**; the **eight CI gates, `ops/`
and the seeder untouched**; **`config/billing.php` NOT modified** — the page conforms to it. Six mutations
RED. Render-verified at **1440px and 390px**: the table is a real `<table>`, 337px wide inside a 339px
wrapper at phone width — **no horizontal scroll, readable rather than merely present** — and the design's own
`[data-cmp] { font-size: 12px }` rule survived regeneration, confirming the restored responsive CSS holds.

**Out of scope and untouched:** the GDPR gaps · the 19 ungated operator screens · ② and the accrual pair ·
SEO finalisation · P-7 · the held pages.

### ⚠️ #7 A postscript: the new guard's own instrument ate the page

⚠️ The guard passed alone and FAILED in the full suite, reporting *"/pricing renders no price node"* about a
page that renders two. The cause was its own helper: `pxText()` opened its strip on `<script` **anywhere in
the HTML** — including the literal text `` `<script>` `` that a **CSS comment in the marketing shell was
shipping into every page**. The match then ran to the next real closing tag and removed the whole body.

⚠️ **A CSS comment goes to the browser; a Blade comment does not.** Gate 7's own responsive-CSS note was
therefore publishing markup-looking prose onto 19 pages, and the first thing to read it was a guard written
one gate later. §N.27.5 — *a source-scanning guard reads its own needle* — for the **fifth** time in this
project, and the first time in a stylesheet.

Both ends fixed: the comment spells the tag names as words, and the helper requires a real tag boundary.
⚠️ `pxText()` now has **its own vacuity check** (`pxTextIsSane()` plus a length floor on a real page),
because every assertion in the file reads its output — a stripper that removes too much makes all of them
vacuous while they still report green.
