## 2026-08-22 — STOREFRONT SEO (D10): the direct-booking pages made findable

⚠️ **The gap, stated plainly.** Vyrobel's core promise is commission-free DIRECT bookings, and the direct
booking pages carried a bare `<title>` and nothing else — no description, no canonical, no OG/Twitter, no
structured data — and appeared in no sitemap. Every marketing page that ranks was pointing at a site whose
actual product pages a crawler could not find or interpret.

**Founder ruling applied:** index ALL tenant storefronts by default.

### What shipped — additive only, on a sealed money-carrying surface

- `App\Support\Storefront\StorefrontOffer` — the ONE definition of "sellable, and at what price". A thin
  probe over `BookingEngineService::search()` (the P-6 Gate 1 chain: capacity · availability · an active
  rate plan · a price for every night), read by BOTH the page's `Offer` and the sitemap's inclusion test, so
  the two cannot disagree (§N.8f).
- `App\Support\Storefront\StorefrontSeo` — the ONE builder of `<head>` + JSON-LD.
- `<x-public.seo>` — the single emitter. The storefront shell gained ONE prop (`:seo`, default null →
  byte-identical prior output) and suppresses its own bare `<title>` when a payload arrives, so there is
  exactly one title element per page.
- `GET /sitemap-storefront.xml` — route-generated, `runAsSuperAdmin`, cached 10 min.
- ⚠️ Checkout and the booking confirmation are now `noindex, nofollow`. **They were indexable by default
  before this pass** — a confirmation page carries a real reference and a real guest email.

### ⚠️ The three traps, and what was actually done about them

1. **`aggregateRating` / `starRating`.** Emitted ONLY from the certified `ReviewRating` helper and only on
   `has_reviews === true`; `starRating` only when the tenant set one (it is NULL for every property this
   product creates). ⚠️ Note this is a REAL rating where real published reviews exist — not a refusal to
   emit one. The refusal is of the *fabricated* kind: mutation M1 planted a default and two tests went RED.
2. **Price from the engine (B12).** ⚠️ **AND CORRECTED MID-PASS:** `search()` returns the room-only,
   VAT-EXCLUSIVE subtotal (the ratified F3 basis), which is NOT what the page displays. Quoting it would
   have advertised a figure lower than anything a guest can pay. The quoted figure is now the GRAND TOTAL
   via the certified `StayEstimator` — the same estimator the browse card, the checkout breakdown and the
   folio use. Verified equal to the cent against the rendered page (€152.05 / €268.90, and €264.10 on the
   room page).
3. **Only sellable properties sitemapped**, mutation-proven in BOTH directions.

### ⛔ SURFACED, NOT DECIDED

- **Tenant opt-out / foreign canonical.** The ruling is index-all-by-default, so no opt-out was built. Note
  that `organizations.custom_domain` already exists as an unused nullable column — the natural home for this
  when it is decided.
- **`APP_URL` is load-bearing** and re-flagged for go-live: every canonical, `og:url` and sitemap entry
  resolves against it, and a wrong value mis-canonicalises the whole storefront SILENTLY. Observed live this
  pass — serving on `:8901` with `APP_URL` at `:8000` produced CSP-blocked images from the mismatch.
- **The EU consumer-display question is untouched.** Room rates remain VAT-exclusive on display (ratified
  F3); the structured data now quotes the all-in total, which is the stricter of the two. If EU display
  compliance later forces the page itself inclusive, that is the deferred 929-row rate migration, not this.

**NOT this pass:** the marketing sitemap, `robots.txt` and marketing JSON-LD (SEO finalisation is LAST, once
the page set stops moving — the storefront was CONFIRMED already ALLOWED: `robots.txt` disallows only
`/admin`) · the 27 docs · `Alternatives`/`Compare` (ruled DROP) · D4/D5 · ②/accrual · GDPR.

Suite **2662 / 2660 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed · 18,497 assertions** (+16 tests, +133 assertions);
PHPStan L5 **0**; Pint clean; **money as seeded byte-identical**; the eight CI gates untouched.

## 2026-08-23 — TWO RULINGS ratifying `d94452f`, and the money pin's DATE-FRAGILITY fixed

### ⚠️ RULING 1 — COLLECTION RISK: **HOLD UNTIL COLLECTED** (a risk allocation, chosen)

⚠️ **This is a FOUNDER DECISION ALLOCATING COLLECTION RISK BETWEEN THE PLATFORM AND THE OWNER — not an
implementation default.** An owner is paid when the money has actually been collected from the guest. **The
platform does not front the owner.** When a pay-on-arrival guest never pays, the owner waits; Vyrobel does
not carry that receivable on the owner's behalf.

The alternatives were surfaced in `docs/audits/OWNER-COLLECTION-GATE-2026-08-23.md` §5 and **not** taken:
release pro-rata with the folio's collection ratio, or have the platform front the owner and carry the
bad-debt risk. ⚠️ Recorded as a choice so a future reader does not mistake it for the way the code happened
to be written.

**Ratifies** `App\Support\Owner\OwnerCollection` and the gate in `OwnerStatementService::claimable()`.

### ⚠️ RULING 2 — FINALISATION TRIGGER: **OPERATOR ACTION** (a money-event control)

A human closes a period: `POST /app/owners/{owner}/close-period`, gated `can:payouts.manage`, audited.
Not a scheduled close and not automatic on period end — **closing a period is the act that makes money
payable, so it takes a deliberate, attributable human decision.**

⚠️ **TWO FOLLOW-UPS REMAIN OPEN and are NOT resolved by this ruling:**
1. **A booking that lands after its period closes.** Today it flows to the next statement as a prior-period
   adjustment, via the straggler path `claimable()` already had. That is behaviour, not yet a decision.
2. **Whether a finalised statement may be REOPENED, and by whom.** ⚠️ Nothing reopens one today —
   `finalize()` locks. No mechanism exists, and none was built.

⚠️ `d94452f` was held unpushed pending these two rulings. **It is now ratified.**

### ⚠️⚠️ THE MONEY PIN WAS BORN FRAGILE — the audit

`ops/money-as-seeded.sh` red on 2026-08-23 for a reason unrelated to any code change. The audit:

**When it began, and the ordering that explains it:**

| commit | date | what |
|---|---|---|
| `f9142c8` | **2026-08-12** | the demo seeder was made **date-relative** on purpose — and its docblock recorded the consequence: *"the demo's exact money figures depend on the run day … it is simply no longer a constant."* |
| `895dea5` | **2026-08-20** | ⚠️ **the money pin was written as six CONSTANTS — eight days later**, against a seeder that had already said it could not promise constants. |

⚠️ **The pin was born fragile.** It was never wrong about the data; it was wrong about the contract.

**Which values move — MEASURED, one fresh process per date** (a first batch probe was caught producing an
artefact — it reported the seeder *throwing* on today's date, which a fresh-process run disproved; §N.31.2):

| figure | verdict |
|---|---|
| `rate_calendar` COUNT | **DATE-INVARIANT** — a fixed 180-day window |
| ⚠️ `SUM(price_minor)` | ⚠️ **DATE-DEPENDENT** — 10,912,000 / 10,916,000 / 10,920,000 / 10,926,000 / 10,928,000. The **weekend uplift** means a window starting on a different weekday holds a different mix of Fri/Sat. |
| `unit_rate_overrides` | **DATE-INVARIANT** (0) |
| ⚠️ `reservations` | ⚠️ **DATE-DEPENDENT** — 40 / 41 / 42. `seedAnalyticsHistory` *skips a stay on collision*, and whether it collides depends on the run day. |
| `payments` | **DATE-INVARIANT** (16) |
| `rate_seasons` | **DATE-INVARIANT** (0) |

⚠️ **10,912,000 recurs on three unrelated dates.** The old pin passed by COINCIDENCE as often as by
correctness — so *"it has always been green"* was never the evidence it looked like.

### ⚠️ WERE PRIOR "MONEY BYTE-IDENTICAL" CLAIMS SOUND? — **Yes, with one honest caveat.**

- The script compared all six figures as one string, so it was a **real check against real data**, never
  vacuous. On the three days the pin lived (2026-08-20 → 08-22) the figures genuinely matched; those passes
  earned their green.
- Claims made **before** `895dea5` were by-hand measurements, not this script.
- ⚠️ **THE CAVEAT:** because `SUM(price_minor)` can drift *and drift back*, a green was always weaker evidence
  than it appeared. Nothing false was reported — but the confidence was over-stated by the form of the check,
  and the gate was destined to red on a calendar boundary rather than on a defect.

### ⚠️ THE SEEDER IS RIGHT; THE CHECK WAS WRONG

Date-relative seeding is a **deliberate product property**: `showcaseMonth()` keeps the demo's stays genuinely
upcoming on any run day. ⚠️ **Anchoring the seeder would make the demo age** — a prospect would open a
storefront full of bookings that already happened, and the "#33 door code still withheld" demo needs a
genuinely future stay. **That product consequence is why the seeder was not touched.**

**The options, and what each stops catching:**

| option | trade-off |
|---|---|
| (a) anchor the seeder to a constant date | deterministic — ⚠️ **but the demo ages and looks dead.** Rejected on product grounds. |
| (b) make the CHECK date-aware | seeder untouched; the check carries the complexity. ⚠️ **Adopted.** |
| (c) split invariant from dependent, and drop the dependent two | ⚠️ **stops catching a changed RATE PRICE and a changed BOOKING SET** — the two most valuable signals. Kept only as the weaker fallback mode. |
| (d) before/after within a pass | drift cancels — ⚠️ **but stops catching drift that accumulates ACROSS passes.** Rejected. |
| ⛔ a pin computed from the seeder's own logic | ⚠️⚠️ **VACUOUS — the source against itself**, the `/pricing` comparison guard's failure (§N.31.1 shape 8). **Not adopted.** |

**Implemented (b):** an optional `VY_SEED_DATE` in `DatabaseSeeder` freezes "today" for a seeding run.
⚠️ **Unset — the normal case — nothing about the demo changes.** The gate then has two modes and says which
it ran: **FULL** (seeded at the reference date, all six asserted; **CI now sets it**) and **INVARIANT** (four
figures, and loudly states that a changed price would not be caught). The expectations remain **hand-measured
constants**, never derived from the seeder.

**Re-pinned `929 / 10928000 / 0 / 42 / 16 / 0` at reference date 2026-09-01, every number attributed:**
`SUM 10,912,000 → 10,928,000` and `reservations 41 → 42` are **the reference date, not a code change**.
⚠️ Separately, the demo's September owner statement moved (gross 100,000 → 46,000, net 82,000 → 37,720) under
`d94452f`'s collection gate — 54,000 of demo September comes from folios never paid, so it is correctly held.
**That is the gate working**, and it is not one of the six figures.

**Mutation-proven:** ⚠️ **roll the date forward (2026-10-15, 2027-02-14) → still GREEN** · delete a payment →
RED · change a rate price → **FULL reds, INVARIANT passes** — which proves the documented limitation rather
than merely asserting it.

## 2026-08-23 — THE SEEDER BLOCKER: `migrate:fresh --seed` failed on a narrow date window

⚠️ **A CONTAINED BUG, not a product decision** — determined at source, not assumed.

### What actually collided (the brief's hypothesis was wrong)

The brief proposed the **analytics** seeder's collision-skip as the suspect. ⚠️ **It is not involved.**
`seedAnalyticsHistory` books entirely FORWARD (`today->addDays(2…132)`); it can never touch a past month.

⚠️ **The real collider is the REVIEWS history.** Its stays are booked at `today − {27,35,42,53,75}` days via
`bookAptStayNear()`. On 2026-08-23 the `today − 42` spec lands on **2026-07-12 → 07-15** (apartment unit 0,
source `ota`) and overlaps `seedOwnerStatementHistory`'s plan entry `[1, 22000, 14, 4]` — `completedMonth(1)`
= July, day 14, 4 nights = **2026-07-14 → 07-18** — on the **same unit**. Throw site
`AssignmentService::assertUnitFree()` → `UnitUnavailableException::occupied()`.

**Reproduced 3/3 on 2026-08-23, and 3/3 green on 2026-08-22 / 09-01** — deterministic in both directions.

### ⚠️⚠️ THE SAME BUG, FIXED TWICE WITH A PREMISE INSTEAD OF A MECHANISM

The loop's own comment records the history, and it is the finding:

1. Originally the months were literals with a comment claiming they were *"clear of the (future-dated)
   analytics-history window, so no collision."* **That became false as today advanced.**
2. It was fixed by switching to `completedMonth()` with a new claim: *"a month that has ended is strictly
   before today, and **every colliding booking is dated today-or-later**."*
   ⚠️ **Also false** — the reviews stays are dated in the **past**.

⚠️ Meanwhile the two sibling seeders have a **mechanism**: `bookAptStayNear()` scans forward, and its comment
explicitly names *these* statement stays as what it is avoiding; `seedOwnerBalanceAccrual` carries a
forward-scan *"ROBUST TO DATE-DRIFT"*. **This loop was the only one exempted — on an assumption.**
⚠️ **So collision-avoidance between exactly these two seeders is the DOCUMENTED INTENT, which is what makes
this a contained bug rather than a demo-layout decision.**

### The fix

`bookStatementStayInMonth()` — the same mechanism, **clamped to the month**. ⚠️ The clamp is load-bearing: a
stay sliding into the next month would land in a different statement period and **silently move the demo's
money**. The planned day is tried first, so on a non-colliding date nothing moves at all. An exhausted month
**throws** rather than skipping — a silently missing statement month would change every figure after it.

⚠️ **AND A SIDE-EFFECT CAUGHT AND CLOSED:** the first draft prepared the rate calendar for every candidate it
tried, so abandoned windows left rows behind and `rate_calendar` drifted **929 → 930…935 on exactly the dates
the fix repairs** — breaking the date-invariant the money pin documents (`b6bcbba`). It now **reads
`reservation_units` first** and only writes a calendar for the window it commits to. **929 on every date.**

### The date sweep — before and after (each a fresh process)

| seed date | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-22 | ✅ 929 | ✅ 929 |
| **2026-08-23 / 24 / 25 / 26** | ⚠️ **exit 1 · 749** | ✅ **929** |
| 2026-08-31 · 09-01 · 09-14 · 09-30 · 10-15 · 12-31 · 2027-01-01 | ✅ 929 | ✅ 929 |
| **2027-02-28** | ⚠️ **exit 1 · 749** | ✅ **929** |
| **2027-03-01** | ⚠️ **exit 1 · 745** | ✅ **929** |

⚠️ **The brief reported 08-23/24/25. The sweep found SIX failing dates** — 08-26 and two in 2027 as well, one
with a *different* partial count (745), i.e. it aborted at a different point.

### 3 · ⛔ PROPOSED, NOT BUILT — a regenerate-and-diff CI gate

It would make the whole class impossible: no post-generation edit could survive a build.

⚠️ **THE OBSTACLE IS REAL AND VERIFIED:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` uses sparse-checkout with
`!docs/design/front/` in **both** jobs (`:58-64`, `:140-146`), deliberately excluding the 102 MB masters. **CI
cannot regenerate anything today.**

| option | cost | what it would STOP catching |
|---|---|---|
| **Include the masters for one job** | +102 MB clone on that job only | nothing — full coverage |
| **A separate scheduled job** (nightly) | full clone, off the PR path | a bad edit merges and is caught later, not at review |
| **Local pre-commit / a `make` target** | free in CI | anything a contributor skips — unenforced by construction |
| **Hash-based** (commit a per-page hash of the generated body) | tiny; no masters needed | ⚠️ **a change to `convert.py` itself** — the hash would be regenerated from the new converter and agree with it (source-vs-itself, §N.31.1 shape 8) |

⚠️ It touches the clone-cost decision, which is the founder's. **Proposed only.**

## 2026-08-23 · ⚠️ FOUNDER RULING — the arrival-secret REVEAL gate stays `units.manage`

**Ruling.** Revealing a stored door code or wifi password remains gated on **`units.manage`** — the same
permission as editing the unit. ⚠️ **Recorded as a ruling, not as an implementation default**: cluster E
shipped it that way and surfaced the question, and the founder has now chosen it deliberately.

**Reasoning.** ⚠️ **A reveal is arguably the MORE sensitive capability of the two**, because it is *silent*
where an overwrite is *detectable*: change a door code and it stops working and somebody complains within a
day; read one and the only trace is an audit row nobody routinely opens. A separate permission would express
that difference — but it is administrative overhead while tenants are effectively single-operator, and a
permission nobody is ever granted separately is a permission that only makes the role catalogue longer.

**⚠️ Revisit trigger.** **When tenants have real staff** — which is the same moment per-property scoping
(cluster J, `property_user`) starts to matter, and for the same reason: both are about *which of several
people* may do a thing, a distinction that does not exist while there is one person.

**What was built alongside it (`ArrivalSecretRevealedNotification`).** A reveal now notifies the **unit's
owner**. ⚠️ **The notification says THAT a reveal happened and never WHAT was revealed** — who, when, which
property and unit, and which FIELDS held a value. ⚠️ A notification is the worst possible destination for a
credential: it lands in the `notifications` table *and*, on the mail channel, in an inbox — unencrypted,
indefinitely, outside every guard cluster E built around the column.

**⚠️ Always-on, following precedent, not by fresh decision.** `account_security` (owner) and
`guest_account_security` are already `always_on`; a credential to your own building being read belongs in
that class. ⚠️ **Surfaced rather than assumed**: if the founder wants it suppressible, that is a change to
this ruling, not a bug.

⚠️ **The owner is on the UNIT (`units.owner_id`), not the property** — properties carry no owner column. So
the notification targets the unit's owner, which is also the more precise target: a reveal is per-unit.

**⚠️ No owner is not an error.** Operator-owned inventory (hotel rooms) has `owner_id = null`, and an owner
may have no linked user. Both resolve through `$unit->owner?->user?->notify(...)`, so **nobody is notified
and the reveal itself is unaffected** — the operator asked for a credential and must still get it. Both
paths are tested.

## 2026-08-24 · ⚠️ `not_a_claim` — and the one row it uncovered

### Where it landed, and why it is not where it semantically belongs

⚠️ **`not_a_claim` is a `disposition` value, not a `kind`** — even though *"this row is not a claim"* plainly
describes what the row **is**, which is `kind`'s job.

⚠️ **The reason is mechanical and decisive:** `pageIsCleared()` decides whether a row participates in
blocking by reading **`disposition` alone**; `kind` only ever affects *how* a participating claim is
evidenced. Putting it in `kind` would force the blocking decision to consult **two fields** — ⚠️ **a new
overload replacing exactly the one this constant removes** (§N.8f). **One question, one field.**

⚠️ **Every `not_a_claim` row carries a recorded reason**, enforced by the gate. Without it the label is an
assertion rather than a judgement — *as unfalsifiable as the overload it replaces* — and it becomes a
permanent "nothing to do here" that a real claim can be filed under.

### The re-classification — judged by ELEMENT, not by reading

⚠️ **29 rows carried `disposition: remove`.** Rather than eyeball each, the test applied was structural:
**what element does the text sit in?** A heading, nav label or card `<span>` states nothing a reader can act
on; a `<p>` is prose.

| bucket | n | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| text **gone** from the page — a genuinely executed removal | **1** (`S1-078`) | stays `remove` |
| text present, **heading / nav label / card span** | **26** | → `not_a_claim`, each with its reason |
| ⚠️ text present, **body prose that asserts** | **1** (`S1-182`) | ⚠️ **restored to `publish`** |

### ⚠️⚠️ THE FINDING — `S1-182` was mis-filed as noise

On `/resources`, inside a `<p>`:

> *"What owners actually want to see, in what order, and why the line item most likely to cause an argument
> is the one you explain worst."*

⚠️ **This is not a heading. It asserts two things about owners**, neither sourced. It was filed `remove` as
a "card blurb" — and `remove` being non-blocking meant **an unsourced population claim stopped blocking its
page.** ⚠️ **Restored to `publish`; `/resources` blocks again**, which is what it should always have done.

⚠️ **It is not an "unexecuted removal"** — nothing ever ruled it removed. It is a **misclassification**, and
the only reason it surfaced is that this pass judged every row individually instead of bulk-relabelling.
**A bulk re-label would have made it permanent.**

⚠️ **SLICE 2 (clusters F and G) WAS NOT STARTED.** The instruction was to stop on a row of this kind, and
the reasoning holds: slice 2 files more dispositions, and it should not file them on top of a ledger whose
filing has just been shown unreliable.

## 2026-08-24 · ⚠️ MONEY PATH — REFUND ATTRIBUTION: DEFAULT TO OWNER, ALLOW AN OVERRIDE (invariant #74)

⚠️ The first product change in this arc, on the certified append-only owner ledger, so the posture inverts:
built so it **cannot** move money wrongly.

**How the listener decides, established before anything was written:** `AdjustOwnerLedgerOnRefund` loads the
refund `Payment` by `domain_event.subject_id`, requires `status === 'succeeded'`, and calls
`OwnerAttributionService::attributeRefund`, which returns 0 when no `owner_ledger` row exists for that
reservation+currency. Idempotency key: `refund:{paymentId}:{ownerId}`. ⚠️ **So the choice had to live on the
refund `Payment` row** — nowhere else is in the listener's reach.

### ⚠️ ZERO MOVEMENT BY DEFAULT — proven on the whole table

`owner_ledger` **29 rows · net 465360 minor** before and after, per owner; `payments` with a non-null
`refund_borne_by`: **0**. Nothing was back-filled, so every existing row is NULL and therefore owner-borne
**by construction rather than by inspection**. The certified owner-accounting suite (**283 tests**) is green
**UNAMENDED**.

### The column, and why it is not a JSON key

`payments.refund_borne_by`, nullable, closed set `owner|operator` on `Payment::BORNE_BY`, refused at the
controller boundary. ⚠️ `metadata` already carries the refund REASON — descriptive, and harmless if absent.
**This value decides whether money moves**, and a JSON key can go absent, misspelled or wrong-typed with
nothing announcing it. NULL = OWNER-BORNE: the ruling, and the fail-safe direction.

### Ordering, and no way back

`Payment::create()` runs **inside** the transaction; `domainEvents->record('payment.refunded')` fires **after
commit** — so the value is on the row before the listener can read it. ⚠️ There is **no edit route, no admin
flip, no retroactive re-attribution**: a flag that changed money already posted would make the ledger
disagree with itself silently. A wrong choice is corrected by an adjustment through the certified path.

### ⚠️ THE MUTATIONS — all six caught

Remove the listener guard → RED · flip NULL to operator → RED · remove the closed-set check → RED (a
`borne_by=nobody` post reaches the column) · drop the value from the create array → RED · idempotency holds
in both states · ⚠️ **#27 still refuses an over-refund with the override set.**

⚠️ **AND A FALSE RED WORTH RECORDING.** The full suite failed `TenantIsolationTest` — *"9 is identical to 2"*
— while passing in isolation. ⚠️ **The certified test was right and my test file was wrong**: every Feature
file declares `uses(RefreshDatabase::class)` **itself** (it is commented out in `Pest.php`), mine omitted it,
and seven leaked properties inflated a cross-tenant count. **A clean-baseline run proved the branch caused
it.** ⚠️ The rule held exactly as intended — the certified test was not amended; the new file was fixed.

### The permission, chosen by reading the matrix

`payments.refund` — already the gate on the refund route. ⚠️ Whoever ISSUES the refund is the one who KNOWS
the cause; gating the choice more tightly would mean the person who knows cannot record it and someone who
does not know decides. Admitted roles are exactly those that can already refund. The audit records the
choice **only when one was made** — recording "owner" on every untouched refund would claim a decision
nobody took.

### The control

Renders only where `OwnerAttributionService::isOwnerAttributed()` is true — ⚠️ **the same test the refund path
uses (§N.8f), extracted rather than duplicated**, since a second definition would eventually disagree with
the one that decides whether money moves. "The owner" is **checked by default and stated in words**:
absorbing a refund is deliberate, never the result of leaving a control alone.

### ⚠️ The doc corrected in the SAME pass

Batch 1's sentence ("deducted from the owner's share") became false the moment this shipped.
`guide-refunds` now: **AUDIT-FALSE 11 owed / 11 done / 0 still / 0 unmatched · LEDGER 6 rows / 0 blocking ·
CORRECTED YES · CLEARED YES.**

**What the page already shows for an OWNER-borne refund:** the `adjustment` ledger row renders through

into `OwnerBookingDetail::absorbedRefunds()` — where a future reader meets it — because an unexplained
asymmetry gets "tidied" and the tidy would be the defect:

  show **one deduction twice on a money page**;
- an absorbed refund **posts nothing**, so it cannot join a gross→net list without either a zero line —
  implying it was weighed in the arithmetic when it was not — or moving a figure, which is forbidden.

⚠️ **The two cases are represented differently because they ARE different: the breakdown answers "what
changed your net"; the note answers "what happened that did not."**

the note; **#17 holds to the cent with the note rendering** (`gross + deductions == net`, asserted while an

two absorbed refunds list, the owner-borne one stays a single `Adjustment` and is **not** duplicated into the
note. ⚠️ **None → the note is absent entirely**: silence is the honest empty state, and a zero row would read
as a deduction that had been weighed.

inside the boundary it already enforces — no second definition of "this owner's booking". ⚠️ Amount and date

⚠️ It states the fact and the effect, **no reason** — the column records WHO bore it, never WHY, and

## 2026-08-24 · ⚠️ MONEY PATH — THE OWNER FOLLOWS THE UNIT ON A MOVE (invariant #76)

### ⚠️ ESTABLISHED FIRST: THERE IS NO EFFECTIVE DATE, AND NONE WAS INVENTED

`AssignmentService::assignUnit()` writes `unit_id`, records `reservation_unit.moved` with
`from_unit_id`/`to_unit_id`, and audits it. ⚠️ **That is the entire move record — there is no effective date,
no `moved_at`, nothing that says which night the guest actually changed rooms.**

⚠️⚠️ **SO THE MID-STAY SPLIT IS NOT IMPLEMENTED, DELIBERATELY.** A `now()` or the audit row's timestamp
standing in for the move date would be a fabricated fact that lands on someone's payout — the invented-`15:00`
class, except this one moves money. **An already-arrived booking is left exactly as it is, and the gap is
reported rather than guessed at.**

**WHAT IS MISSING, precisely:** a `reservation_units.moved_effective_date` (or a dated move record), captured
**at the moment the operator performs the move**, with the operator stating **which night the guest first
slept in the new unit**. ⚠️ **AND THE HAZARD THAT COMES WITH IT:** such a date would be operator-settable and
**backdatable**, which on an append-only ledger is a **money-manipulation surface** — an operator could shift
nights between two owners after the fact. **That is a founder decision, not an implementation detail.**

### ⚠️ NOTHING WAS INVENTED — THE CERTIFIED METHOD EXISTED WITH NO CALLER

`OwnerAttributionService::reattributeReservation()` already reverses the live version as a **whole
transaction** and attributes a fresh one, and its reversal already stamps `prior_period_adjustment` from
`PeriodLockGuard::isSealed()`. ⚠️ **It simply had ZERO callers — which is exactly why the money never
followed.** The fix is a listener on `reservation_unit.moved` that calls it, and nothing else.

### ⚠️ ALL FOUR TRANSITIONS, EACH PROVEN

| transition | behaviour | proven |
|---|---|---|
| same owner → different unit | ⚠️ **PROVEN NO-OP — not one new row.** Reversal + identical re-post is churn the owner can SEE | ✅ |
| owner A → owner B (pre-arrival) | A reversed to **exactly 0**, B holds A's former net, ledger sum unchanged | ✅ |
| owner → operator-owned | owner's share reaches **0**; ledger sum for the booking becomes 0 | ✅ |
| operator-owned → owner | the owner **gains** an attribution where there was none | ✅ |

⚠️ Ownership is read as `units.owner_id` — the same resolution the attribution itself uses (§N.8f).

### ⚠️ A FALSE GREEN CAUGHT — AND IT WAS MY MUTATION THAT WAS WRONG

Removing `Event::listen(…, ReattributeOwnerOnUnitMove::class)` left every test **passing**. The edit applied
(1 → 0 occurrences), so it was not the §N.4p "edit didn't apply" case. ⚠️ **Laravel auto-discovers
`app/Listeners`, so the explicit registration is redundant and removing it changes nothing.** Mutating the
**listener body** instead turns 3 tests RED. ⚠️ **A mutation that targets a redundant registration proves
nothing, and reporting the first result as a pass would have been a false green on a money path.**

### The rest

**Locked period:** proven explicitly — with A's period sealed through the service date, **every reversal
carries `prior_period_adjustment = true`** and the sealed statement's own figures are untouched.
**No back-fill:** no migration at all; `owner_ledger` **29 rows · net 465360**, unchanged.
**Idempotent:** moving A→B→A returns exactly to the starting position with the ledger sum preserved.
**Audited:** `assignUnit()`'s existing `reservation_unit.moved` audit row carries from/to unit and actor.
**Arithmetic:** the signed sum is preserved on every owner-to-owner move — money is **moved**, never created
or destroyed. It legitimately falls to zero only when the unit becomes operator-owned.

**Certified owner-accounting suite: 324 tests green, UNAMENDED.**

### ⚠️ THE DOC RE-CORRECTED IN THE SAME PASS — THIRD TIME THIS PATTERN HAS RUN

Batch 3 wrote *"the earnings stay with the unit that was originally booked"* — true that morning, false the
moment this shipped. It now states both halves honestly: the earnings follow the unit before arrival, and
stay put after it **because nothing records which night the guest changed rooms**.
`guide-checkin`: **AUDIT-FALSE 14 owed / 13 done / 0 still / 1 unmatched · LEDGER 2 rows / 0 blocking ·
CORRECTED YES · CLEARED YES.** `guide-statements` and `guide-payouts` make no claim about moves — unaffected.

## 2026-08-25 · ⚠️⚠️ THE MID-STAY SPLIT — ESTABLISHED, **NOT BUILT**, AND HERE IS WHY

⚠️ Rule #1 said: establish whether the certified attribution can express a split, and **if extending it is
required, report what that touches BEFORE touching it.** It is required, it touches something dangerous, and
this pass therefore stops at the report.

### ⚠️ EXPRESSIBILITY: THE MONEY LAYER CAN ALREADY DO IT

`attributeAtVersion()` **already loops over `activeLines`** and attributes **each line to its own owner**
(`$unit->owner_id` per line, its own `ManagementAgreement`, its own `service_date`). Two owners on one
reservation is not a new shape — **group bookings already produce it.**

⚠️ **And the arithmetic trap is already solved by certified code.** `Money::allocate()` takes floor shares and
**hands out the leftover minor units by remainder** — it is exactly "compute one side, derive the other"
generalised to N, it never loses a cent, and the attribution **already calls it with NIGHT weights**
(`$roomTotal->allocate($weights)` where weights are nights when lines are unpriced). ⚠️ **No new arithmetic
needs writing, and none should be.**

### ⚠️⚠️ SO WHAT BLOCKS IT IS NOT THE MONEY — IT IS THE INVENTORY, AND IT WOULD LOCK A GUEST OUT

To make the money split, the stay must be expressed as **two sequential lines** — `[check_in, effective)` on
the old unit, `[effective, check_out)` on the new. That means `AssignmentService::assignUnit()` stops
mutating one line's `unit_id` and starts **splitting the line**, inside the availability lock, with `sold`
net-zero across the two.

⚠️⚠️ **AND SIX SURFACES READ `reservationUnits->first()`:**

| surface | what breaks after a split |
|---|---|
| ⚠️⚠️ **`ArrivalPack.php:44`** | `first()?->unit` returns the FIRST segment — **the room the guest MOVED OUT OF**. The guest would be shown the **wrong door code** for the rest of their stay. |
| `PreArrivalMail` | pre-arrival email carries the old unit's code |
| `PaymentReminderMail` · `ReviewRequestMail` · `OperatorInbox` · `ReviewService` | name the wrong unit |

⚠️ **That is the "guest standing at a door that will not open" failure — created by this change.** Batch 3
existed to remove exactly that class of defect; shipping the split naively would manufacture a real one.

⚠️ `PerformanceMetrics` is **safe**: room-nights are summed over lines **overlapping the range**, and two
sequential non-overlapping segments sum correctly. Checked, not assumed.

### ⚠️ THE TWO OPTIONS, FOR A RULING

**(A) SPLIT THE LINE.** Touches the certified single inventory write path + all six `first()` surfaces, each
of which must become date-aware. ⚠️ **Largest blast radius, and it puts the #33 door code in play.**

**(B) ⚠️ KEEP ONE LINE, RECORD THE MOVE.** A `reservation_unit_moves` row (line, from-unit, to-unit,
**effective date**, **stated-at**, actor) and `attributeAtVersion()` splits that ONE line's room revenue
across the segment owners by nights via the existing `allocate()`. ⚠️ **Inventory is untouched**, and
`assignUnit()` already updates `unit_id` to the NEW unit — so **`ArrivalPack` keeps showing the correct,
current door code.** ⚠️ It extends certified MONEY code instead (one loop learns that a line can span two
owners), which is the narrower and more reviewable change.

⚠️ **B is the recommendation** — it keeps the guest-facing #33 surface correct by construction and confines
the change to one method, whose reversal, versioning, idempotency key and `prior_period_adjustment` stamping
already work per-owner.

### What was NOT done, deliberately

⚠️ **No code was written.** No effective-date column, no UI, no split arithmetic — because rule #1's whole
point is that *"I extended it and the suite passed"* proves the OLD behaviour survived, not that the NEW
shape is right. ⚠️ **The `guide-checkin` sentence stays accurate** ("the earnings stay where they were,
because nothing records which night the guest changed rooms") — it is still true, so it was not touched.

## 2026-08-25 · ⚠️ MONEY PATH — THE MID-STAY SPLIT (invariant #77)

⚠️ The previous pass established expressibility and STOPPED, reporting Option A (split the line — touches
the certified inventory path and six `reservationUnits->first()` readers, **including `ArrivalPack`, which
would have shown a moved guest the door code of the room they left**) against Option B (keep one line,
record the move). ⚠️ **The brief was re-sent unchanged, which is a reaffirmation, so B was built as
recommended.**

### ⚠️ EXPRESSIBILITY — THE CERTIFIED CODE COULD ALREADY DO MOST OF IT

`attributeAtVersion()` already loops lines and attributes each to its own owner, and `Money::allocate()` is
already a remainder-exact N-way allocator. ⚠️ **So no new arithmetic was written.** The extension is one
loop learning that a LINE can span more than one owner.

⚠️⚠️ **THE EXACTNESS IS BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY HOPE.** The line-level `allocate()` is untouched — an
unmoved booking attributes **byte-identically** to before — and a segmented line then sub-allocates **its
own part** with the same allocator. Each level distributes exactly what it was given, so
Σ(segments) == the line's part == the room total, at every ratio. **Nothing is computed twice and hoped to
agree.** Proven across **30 combinations** (5 totals incl. 100003, 99999 and 7 minor units × 6 boundaries).

### ⚠️ WHAT THE MUTATIONS FOUND

Six mutations, each **proven to change behaviour**: one cent removed → RED · segment suffix dropped (A→B→A
key collision) → RED · date bound removed → RED · N segments collapsed → RED · moves ignored → RED.

⚠️⚠️ **AND ONE CAUGHT MY OWN TEST.** The "both dates" mutation (`stated_at` = the effective date) **PASSED**,
because the assertion was `statedLateDays() >= 0` — **satisfied by `stated_at` merely copying the effective
date, which is exactly the shape that makes backdating undetectable.** Strengthened to an exact 5-day gap;
the mutation now REDs. ⚠️ **A vacuous assertion on a manipulation signal is worse than none, because it
reads as coverage.**

⚠️ **A second real bug, found by a failing test:** `from_unit_id` was read via `getOriginal('unit_id')`
**after** `update()`. Eloquent syncs originals on save, so it returned the NEW unit and **the first segment
was attributed to the owner the guest moved TO.** Now captured before the update.

### The rest

**Bounded by arithmetic at the boundary** (`AssignmentService`, not the UI): refused on/before check-in,
on/after check-out, and in the future. ⚠️ **Forward-dating is NOT a real case** — a move can only be stated
for a night that has happened, and this surfaced concretely when fixtures booked wholly in the future could
not express a mid-stay move at all.
**Both dates stored** (`effective_date` + `stated_at` + `stated_by_user_id`), and the audit row carries both.
**Defaults to today**, rendered only once the stay has started; **gated by `reservations.assign`** — the same
permission as the move, held by Super Admin, Hotel Manager and **Front Desk**, who are the people who
actually know which night the guest changed rooms.
**Sealed periods**: proven marked on **both** owners — the one losing nights and the one gaining them.
**N segments**: three-segment stay proven; **A→B→A merges** (A holds 40000 across two segments, B 20000) —
which only works because the idempotency key carries the segment.

**Certified owner-accounting suite: 300 green, UNAMENDED.**

### ⚠️ THE BOUNDARY, IN ONE SENTENCE, IN THREE PLACES

*"The first night the guest slept in the new unit — nights before it stay with the old unit; that night and
after move with the guest."* Identical in the migration/service comments, the move form, and `guide-checkin`.

### The doc, re-corrected a FOURTH time

`guide-checkin`: **14 owed / 13 done / 0 still / 1 unmatched · 2 ledger rows / 0 blocking · CORRECTED ·
CLEARED.** `guide-statements` **CORRECTED but NOT CLEARED** (1 unsourced ledger claim) and `guide-payouts`
both — neither needed a change: their "adjustment"/"carried forward" language already describes the
prior-period path correctly.

## 2026-08-25 · ⚠️⚠️ THE CHECKOUT BALANCE BLOCK — BUILT, MEASURED, AND **REVERTED**. STOPPED AND REPORTING.

⚠️ The block was built exactly as ruled — guarded at the convergence point, reading the same `FolioTotals`
the folio screen renders, with credit and zero passing — and its own six tests passed. ⚠️ **Then the full
suite measured what it costs, and rule #6's stop condition was met: an existing, shipped behaviour moved.**

### ⚠️⚠️ THE BLOCK MAKES A DELIBERATELY-BUILT FEATURE UNREACHABLE

**`BalanceDueNotification` exists.** It is a real operator notification, preference-gated
(`NotificationPreferences: 'balance_due' => ['label' => 'Balance due at checkout', 'group' => 'Front desk',
'default' => true]`), dispatched from `DispatchNotificationsForDomainEvent:258` **on
`reservation.checked_out` when the folio has a balance**, with two tests pinning it — including one that
charges €200, pays nothing, checks out, and asserts the notification fires.

⚠️ **The product was designed on the premise that checking out with money owed is a NORMAL, EXPECTED,
NOTIFIED event.** A hard block makes that feature permanently dead code: the state it announces becomes
unreachable. ⚠️ **Amending that test to accommodate the block would have silently deleted a shipped
feature — which is why this stopped instead.**

### ⚠️ THE CHURN NUMBER — 10 errors across 3 files, and the demo seed is one of them

| broken by the block | why it matters |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ **`DemoSeedDateRobustnessTest`** (6) | **`migrate:fresh --seed` FAILS** — the demo seeder checks out a stay with **€332.10 owed.** Rule #6 called this out in advance: if the seeder checks out an unpaid folio, that is a finding about how the product is modelled. **It does.** |
| ⚠️⚠️ **`NotificationWiringTest`** (2) | the two tests that pin `BalanceDueNotification` — **the feature above** |
| `StubViewsTest` (2) | consumes the same demo seed |

⚠️ **The number is not "a few fixtures needing a payment". It is the demo world plus a shipped feature.**
**Unpaid checkout is normal in the modelled world.**

### #1 · The bill-to-account question — answered, and the answer is NO

⚠️ **No bill-to-account, invoice, deferred-settlement, company-account or payment-terms concept exists
anywhere.** `corporate` is a value in the `reservations.source` enum — a **booking channel**, not settlement
terms. Nothing keys "this balance is legitimately unpaid".

⚠️ **So the block, as ruled, forbids corporate and group business where settlement follows departure** —
and it does so with no exemption available, because there is nothing to exempt.

### What was built (and is reverted, not lost)

Guard in `CheckOutReservation::handle()` — the single convergence point (`FrontDeskService::checkOut()` is
its only caller; the controller is that method's only caller). Read through `FolioTotals::for($folio)`, the
**same** computation `ReservationDetail` renders. `balance_minor <= 0` passes, so **credit and zero both
check out cleanly**; integer minor units throughout. Message: *"€150.00 is still owed on this folio. Take
the payment, or post an adjustment or void the charge if it should not stand, then check out."*

### ⚠️ WHAT THE BLOCK LOOKS LIKE IN PRACTICE — and the three options, costed

- **The one-cent case** — a rounding remainder of €0.01 blocks a departure. The guard is `> 0`, so it
  cannot distinguish it from €500.
- **6am departure with an open bar tab** — the guest is gone; the agent cannot close the stay, so the room
  stays "in-house", housekeeping is not triggered, and the unit is not released on the board.
- **The corporate case** — impossible to complete at all, per #1.
- ⚠️ **What an agent with a guest waiting actually does:** records a fake payment, or voids the charge.
  **Both are harder to audit than the balance being caught**, and the second destroys revenue data.

| option | cost |
|---|---|
| **(a) supervisor override** | a real, keyed, audited exemption — who allowed it and why. Honest, but it is a new permission + an audit surface, and it re-opens "who may approve". |
| **(b) a small threshold** (e.g. under €1) | fixes only the rounding case. ⚠️ It is a *policy number* that will be wrong for someone, and it does nothing for the corporate or 6am cases. |
| **(c) build bill-to-account first** | the honest fix: a keyed settlement-terms state on the reservation, so the block fires only where money is genuinely unaccounted for. Largest, and it is a product feature rather than a guard. |

⚠️ **Recommendation: (c), with the block shipping after it.** Blocking before there is any way to express a
legitimate unpaid balance converts a data-quality guard into a business restriction, and the product already
disagrees with it in the form of a notification built for exactly that state.

### The doc was NOT changed

`guide-checkin` currently says *"Check the balance before you complete a checkout — nothing stops a checkout
with money outstanding."* ⚠️ **That is still true, so the fifth re-correction is not yet due.** Correcting it
to describe a block that was reverted would have been the fabrication this whole arc exists to remove.

## 2026-08-25 · COMPANY ACCOUNTS — THE HONEST MINIMUM (invariant #78)

### #1 · What existed: **nothing**, and nothing was overloaded

⚠️ No company-account, receivable, invoice or settlement-terms concept exists anywhere. The adjacent things
that turned up were all **left alone**: `organizations.billing_company` is the OPERATOR'S OWN subscription
billing identity; `owners` is the property-owner party; and ⚠️ **`reservations.source = 'corporate'` is a
BOOKING CHANNEL — how the booking arrived, not how it settles.** Overloading it would have been one field
answering two questions.

### ⚠️⚠️ #4 FIRST, BECAUSE IT DECIDED THE WHOLE DESIGN

**`OwnerCollection::reservationIsCollected()` is literally `FolioTotals::for($folio)['balance_minor'] <= 0`.**

⚠️⚠️ **So if billing to an account had reduced the folio balance, the collection gate would have counted it
as collected THE INSTANT it was billed** — and the payout engine would have released money to owners that
nobody has received, out of the operator's own working capital, surfacing months later as an untraceable
shortfall.

⚠️ **That is why this posts NOTHING.** No payment, no charge reversal, no adjustment. The balance is exactly
what it was, which gives all three properties at once and needed **no change to the collection gate at all**:

1. **The debt stays visible** — the folio still reads owed, as billed to an account rather than settled.
2. **It is not collected** — proven: `reservationIsCollected()` is false before AND after billing.
3. **The owner ledger moves by exactly zero** — row count and signed sum both unchanged.

⚠️ When the company pays, the ORDINARY `FolioService` path records it, the balance reaches zero, and the
owner becomes payable **then, through the existing mechanism** — proven. No parallel settlement path exists.

### #2 · The minimum built, and what a fuller version would add

**Built:** `company_accounts` (org-scoped) · a **keyed** `folios.billed_to_account_id` + `billed_at` +
`billed_by_user_id` · `CompanyAccountService::bill/unbill/outstandingFor` · guards (cross-org refused,
settled folio refused) · audit on both transitions.

⚠️ **The account owes no stored total.** "What does this company owe us?" is the **sum of the real folio
balances** billed to it, through the same `FolioTotals` the screen renders — so there is nothing that can
drift from the folios it is made of. **That is why no receivables ledger was built.**

**NOT built, deliberately:** invoicing/PDFs · payment terms or aging · credit limits · dunning · a
company-facing statement or portal · a receivables ledger. A fuller version would add: an invoice document
and number series, net-N terms with an aging bucket view, a credit limit checked at billing time, a chase
queue, and a company portal to view and pay.

### ⚠️ #5 · WHAT IS NOT BUILT AND MUST BE REPORTED PLAINLY

⚠️⚠️ **There is no operator surface yet — no route, no screen, and therefore NO PERMISSION GATE.** The
service enforces org isolation and the settled-folio refusal, and both are mutation-proven, but a boundary
gate cannot exist without a boundary. ⚠️ **The block pass must add the route gated on `folios.manage`**
(Super Admin · Hotel Manager · Front Desk · Accountant — the people who already take payments and manage
folios, and billing to an account is a folio settlement decision). **Reported rather than claimed.**

⚠️ **Un-billing is a NEW STATE, not a reversal** — because nothing was POSTED to reverse. The folio's own
balance never moved, so there is no ledger entry to correct, only an attribution to withdraw; it is audited
the same way billing is, so a debt cannot move back without a trace.

### #6 · The checkout path is untouched

`BalanceDueNotification` still fires on an unpaid checkout (`NotificationWiringTest` **9/9, UNAMENDED**).
The demo seeder's money is unchanged; `owner_ledger` is **29 rows / net 465360**, the baseline.

### ⚠️ A real defect found while building

`CompanyAccount::is_active` defaulted only in the DB, so a **freshly created account read as CLOSED** until
refreshed — and the billing guard would have refused it. Defaulted on the model so the object and the row
agree from the moment it exists.

### #7 · The doc: **NONE**

`guide-checkin` still says *"nothing stops a checkout with money outstanding"* — **still true, because the
block was not built.** No page claims company billing is impossible, so nothing went stale. Nothing was
changed, and no register moved.

## 2026-08-25 · THE SUPERVISOR CHECKOUT OVERRIDE (invariant #80)

### #1 · Its own permission — `reservations.checkout_override`

⚠️ **Deliberately NOT `folios.manage`.** That set includes **Front Desk**, and an override every agent holds
is not a supervisor override — it is a second checkout button. Verified against the matrix: **Super Admin ·
Hotel Manager** are the only roles holding `reservations.checkout` *and* the supervisory permissions
(`reservations.cancel`, `reports.view`, `rates.manage`), so those two hold it.

⚠️⚠️ **THE 6AM COST, STATED PLAINLY:** with no manager on shift, a front-desk agent **still cannot release
the room**. The stranded-room case that motivated this is fixed only when a supervisor is reachable. That is
the direct price of "supervisor", and it should be read here rather than discovered on a night shift.

### #2 · A keyed reason, and the rate is answerable

`CheckoutOverrideReason`: `rounding_residue` · `guest_departed` · `disputed_charge` · `settled_offline` ·
`other`. ⚠️ **The first two come from the cases measured live last pass** (the €0.01 residue; the departure
that never released the room). ⚠️ **`other` requires a NOTE and is counted separately** — refusing an unlisted
case would push agents into miscategorising, which corrupts the very count this set exists to produce, so a
high `other` rate is itself the finding that the set is wrong.

⚠️ **`CheckoutOverrideStats::since()`** answers *"how many, and why?"* — count, checkouts, **rate**, by-reason
breakdown, and total minor units overridden. ⚠️ **The rate is the honest measure of the block**: if it runs
at forty percent the block is doing nothing, and that is now visible rather than assumed otherwise. ⚠️ **On
the demo data the answer is 0 overrides** — the seeded unpaid departure goes through the *company-account*
exemption, not the override, which is the shape you would want.

### ⚠️⚠️ #3 · It moves no money

Proven: the balance is **still €200 owed** after an override, `owner_ledger` row count and signed sum
**unchanged**, `BalanceDueNotification` still fires, and `reservationIsCollected()` — literally
`balance_minor <= 0` — **still reads FALSE**. ⚠️ **It permits an ACTION; it does not resolve a DEBT.**
`migrate:fresh --seed` clean, `owner_ledger` **29 rows / net 465360**.

### ⚠️⚠️ #4 · The deliverable is the ROOM, and the whole chain is asserted in one test

blocked → ⚠️ **no housekeeping task, unit not dirty (the stranded room)** → override → checked out →
**`GenerateDepartureCleanTask` fires** → task exists → ⚠️ **`units.housekeeping_status === 'dirty'`** → **and
the balance is still owed.** An override that completed the checkout but left the unit un-flipped would have
fixed nothing, so the flip is asserted rather than assumed.

### #5 · Audited — the amount as well as the act

`reservation.checkout_overridden` carries reason, note (when `other`), **`balance_minor` at that moment**, and
currency, plus the actor and time the recorder already stamps. ⚠️ **A €0.01 override and a €900 override are
different events and must not look alike in six months.**

⚠️ **It is an ACT, NOT A STATE** — passed per checkout, never persisted. A test walks every folio column and
fails if any `override` column appears: a standing "may check out unpaid" flag would be a permanent hole.

### #6 · The doc — sixth correction, third in three passes

`guide-checkin` now states the override, that it is a manager action, that the reasons are a fixed list so
they can be counted, and ⚠️ **that it releases the room but settles nothing — the balance stays owed exactly
as it was.** That last clause is the point: a reader who thinks an override clears the balance is exactly how
an override becomes a write-off.

### #7 · Six mutations, all through the fixed harness

free-text reason accepted → RED · `other` note requirement dropped → RED · audit removed → RED · amount
dropped from the audit → RED · supervisor permission check removed → RED · ⚠️ **the trap: making the override
settle the balance → RED.** ⚠️ **No anchor misses; the harness would have refused to report one as a pass.**

## 2026-08-25 · RESTRICTIONS ARE ENFORCED AT BOOKING (invariant #81)

### #1 · The store's scope, and each restriction's verified shape

⚠️ **Scope: `(room_type_id, rate_plan_id, date)`**, unique. ⚠️ **Every shipped writer keys it room-type-level
with `rate_plan_id = NULL`** (`RateActionController`, `OwnerRateService`) — and the rate-grid badge reads
exactly that. ⚠️ **So the engine reads the same key the badge renders (§N.8f); if it looked anywhere else the
bug would simply move — the badge saying one thing and the refusal another.**

| restriction | shape, verified |
|---|---|
| `min_stay` | judged on the **ARRIVAL date's row**; a stay shorter than it is refused. A minimum on a *later* night does not govern the stay — proven. |
| `stop_sell` | **every night** `[check_in, check_out)`. ⚠️ The departure date is excluded — nobody sleeps that night — proven. |
| ⚠️ `closed_to_arrival` | forbids **STARTING** on that date; a stay **passing through** is untouched. |
| ⚠️ `closed_to_departure` | forbids **ENDING** on that date; passing through is untouched. |

⚠️⚠️ **CTA AND CTD ARE PROVEN BOTH WAYS** — the forbidden case refused *and* the pass-through case permitted.
A refusal-only test cannot distinguish a correct implementation from an inverted one, and the two inversion
mutations (applying each to every night) both go RED.

### #2 · Every creation path — one convergence point

`ReservationCreateController` (operator) · `BookingEngineService` (guest storefront) · `NewReservation`
(Livewire) · `GroupBookingService` · `DemoSeeder` — ⚠️ **all funnel through `AssignmentService::occupy()`**,
which `createBooking()` and `createGroupBooking()` share. ⚠️ **Enforcement sits INSIDE that locked core,
immediately after the availability lock and beside the out-of-service guard** — the same point, the same
transaction, never a second gate that could disagree with them.

### ⚠️ #3 · Zero movement where nothing is set

⚠️ **Absent means unrestricted, never a default.** No row, or a null column, enforces nothing — an empty
result returns before any check runs. A null `min_stay` read as anything but "no minimum" would silently
close inventory nobody chose to close; the mutation that defaults it goes RED.

⚠️ **Seeded restrictions: ZERO.** So **0 seeded bookings violate a seeded restriction**, `migrate:fresh
--seed` is clean and `owner_ledger` is **29 rows / net 465360** — unchanged. ⚠️ **That is also a finding: the
demo never demonstrates restrictions at all.** Not changed here — it is not ruled, and it would move the
money-as-seeded baseline.

### #4 · No back-fill, proven

Enforcement is at CREATION only. A restriction added **after** a booking exists leaves it `confirmed` —
asserted directly, because a retroactive refusal would cancel real stays.

## 2026-08-25 · THE RESTRICTION OVERRIDE, FINISHED (invariant #83)

### ⚠️⚠️ #1 · THE ACCEPTANCE TEST NOW PASSES — removing a grant REDs

⚠️ **Last pass, removing Front Desk's `reservations.restriction_override` grant broke nothing and the harness
correctly reported "NO TEST COVERS THIS". It now turns tests RED.** That was the single condition this pass
had to meet.

⚠️ **The gate lives where the override is CONSUMED** — `AssignmentService::occupy()` — not on a route. That
is the single convergence point for **every** booking path: the operator create controller, group bookings
(`createGroupBooking` funnels through `occupy()`) and the public storefront. A route-only check would have
left the other callers ungated.

⚠️⚠️ **AND IT SURFACED A REAL FOOTGUN, LIVE.** The first version failed because **a null spatie team makes
`can()` fail SILENTLY TO FALSE** — it does not throw, it answers "no". `occupy()` runs from jobs, commands
and the seeder as well as requests, so it cannot rely on `SetTenantForWebRequest`. ⚠️ **The team is now set
from the reservation's own organization and restored afterwards**, the same discipline `StaffRoster` already
uses for exactly this reason. ⚠️ **Without it the gate would have refused legitimate operators in every
non-request context — a fail-closed bug that looks like a working gate.**

### #2 · The override is offered ONLY after a refusal

⚠️ **There is no override field on a first attempt** — asserted by fetching the create page and checking
`restriction_override_reason` is absent from the HTML. ⚠️ **A pre-tickable option gets ticked out of habit,
the block stops firing at all, and the override RATE — the only signal that says whether the restrictions
themselves are right — becomes meaningless.**

**The flow:** attempt → refusal listing **every** breach → the operator picks a keyed reason **with that list
on screen** → resubmit. ⚠️ **If the operator cannot override, no picker is rendered at all**; the refusal says
*"You cannot override a restriction. A manager or someone on the front desk can."* — because an offer that
fails on submit teaches people the system is broken.

### ⚠️⚠️ #3 · SEEN == WAIVED, mechanically

The breach list travels back in `restriction_override_seen`, and the service **re-evaluates on submit** and
compares fingerprints. ⚠️ **If the set changed — someone edited the rate grid in between — it REFUSES AGAIN
with the NEW list.** Proven with a changed set: shown only a minimum stay, a closed-to-arrival added
meanwhile, refused. ⚠️ **This makes "informed" mechanical rather than hopeful, and makes the audit's waived
list provably the list the operator read.**

### ⚠️⚠️ #4 · A guest can never override

Proven: an unauthenticated caller supplying a valid override reason is **refused**, and ⚠️ **no audit row is
written** — the permission is checked **before** the audit, so no row can record an act that was not
permitted. **Which paths can:** the operator create controller and group bookings, both only with the grant.
**Which cannot:** the public storefront (`BookingEngineService` never sets the field and has no operator
user), the seeder, and any future job or import.

### #5 · Zero movement

No override → byte-identical: a breaching booking is still refused and **no audit row is written**.
`owner_ledger` **29 rows / net 465360** · **42 reservations** · **4 seeded restrictions** — all unchanged, and
the computed seeding window is untouched.

### ⚠️ #7 · WHAT A RESERVATION AGENT ACTUALLY SEES — reported, NOT widened

⚠️ **The dead end is now real rather than theoretical.** A Reservation Agent takes a phone booking that
breaches a minimum stay and gets: the refusal, the full breach list, and *"You cannot override a restriction.
A manager or someone on the front desk can."* ⚠️ **They can start a booking and cannot finish it — they must
hand it to someone else or leave it.** ⚠️ **Not widened: the ruling named Front Desk.**

### ⚠️ TESTS I AMENDED, AND WHY

⚠️ **Five tests in the previous pass's `RestrictionOverrideTest` now act as a permitted operator.** They
passed **unauthenticated** before — which is precisely the defect this pass closed, so their old shape was
only green because nothing was checked. ⚠️ **No assertion's meaning changed.** Reported rather than done
quietly.

### #6 · The doc — fifth correction in five passes

*"Anyone who can take a booking can override"* became false the moment the gate worked. It now reads **"When
a booking is refused, a manager or someone on the front desk can override it"**, keeps the sentence that an
override **does not change the restriction**, and states the override follows a refusal. Channels
**untouched**.

### Mutations

⚠️⚠️ **Remove Front Desk's grant → RED (the acceptance test)** · gate bypassed → RED · seen-vs-waived skipped
→ RED. All through the fixed harness; no anchor misses.

## 2026-09-22 · APPLY 01 #1 — R7: A STAY THE GUEST IS PHYSICALLY IN MAY NOT BE TERMINATED

**Founder ruling.** `checked_in → cancelled` and `checked_in → no_show` are refused on every path. This is
the first pass in the audit programme that changes behaviour rather than measuring it.

### The implementation decision, and why the obvious one is wrong

⚠️⚠️ **`checked_in` was NOT added to `TERMINAL_STATUSES`.** That is the one-line version of this ruling and it
is a defect. Measured before choosing: four unrelated readers of that constant would have changed behaviour
silently — `GuestDeletionService`'s active-stay query (GDPR), `OwnerBookingDetail`'s upcoming-check-in flag,
`BookingImportService::modify()`'s **R6 permission** (which the founder ruled the other way and which must
stay), and the `CANCELLABLE` partition assertion. The exception's message would also have lied: *"already
`checked_in` and cannot be marked cancelled"* reads as though the stay were over.

**So: a second constant, `AssignmentService::IN_PROGRESS_STATUSES`, and a second exception,
`ReservationInProgressException`.** #29 bounds a **second** termination of a **finished** stay; R7 refuses a
**first** termination of an **unfinished** one. `TerminateGuardTest` now asserts the two sets stay **disjoint**
— because the union-based partition assertion alone would pass if somebody merged them.

### Three layers, none redundant

| layer | behaviour | why it cannot be the only one |
|---|---|---|
| `AssignmentService::terminate()` | **throws**, before the transaction | authoritative; covers `cancelReservation()`, `markNoShow()` and every caller of both |
| `ReservationLifecycleController::CANCELLABLE` | **flash**, and the detail screen hides the button | without it the operator gets an exception where a sentence belongs |
| `BookingImportService::cancel()` | **no-op + audit row** | it runs on the retrying webhook path; a throw there is a poison message |

⚠️ The controller reads the exception's `messageFor()` rather than hand-typing the sentence — two copies of
one refusal is exactly how the controller and the service came to disagree about `checked_out` in the first
place.

### ⚠️⚠️ THE FOURTH CALLER, FOUND BY SWEEPING THE DIFF RATHER THAN THE BRIEF

`GuestDeletionService::eraseNow()` cancels a guest's live bookings on a **cron**, wrapping each call in
`catch (Throwable)`. The new refusal would have been **swallowed**, the live stay skipped — and
`reservationsToCancel()` would have gone on counting it for the account screen, the scheduled-deletion email
and the confirmation copy. **The erase would have kept working while the warning started lying**, silently,
on a path nobody watches. The predicate now excludes `IN_PROGRESS_STATUSES` and the guest-facing copy was
corrected: it used to promise the erase cancels *"a stay already under way"*, and now states that a stay you
are checked into is **not** cancelled. Deleting an account does not evict a guest from a room.

### ⚠️⚠️ WHAT THE RULING COSTS — REPORTED, NOT DECIDED

🔬 Measured three independent ways (the `app/Actions/Reservations/` inventory · every write of
`status => 'confirmed'` · every lifecycle route): **the product has no reverse-check-in.** There is a
`ReverseCheckOut` (R3, `checked_out → checked_in`) and nothing that walks `checked_in` back.

So `checked_in` now has **exactly one operator exit, `checked_out`**, and **a check-in recorded in error can
no longer be undone** — previously an operator cancelled it. The brief's proof step *"reverse → cancel →
allowed"* **could not be run**, and that is stated in the test file rather than quietly omitted.

⚠️ The refusal therefore names **check-out**, the exit that exists, and says plainly that reversing a
check-in is not built. Naming a control that does not exist is the same defect as a fabricated figure (#39).

**Open as `R9` (founder's, not a session's): build `checked_in → confirmed` on R3's
disclose-what-cannot-be-undone pattern?** R3 already ruled the mirror case permit-and-reverse.

### Tests amended, each with its reason

1. `TerminateGuardTest` — `checked_in` removed from the "first cancellation from every non-terminal status"
   dataset. It asserted, by name, the behaviour the ruling removes. **Not deleted:** the same transition is
   now asserted in the opposite direction, with its inventory consequence.
2. `TerminateGuardTest` — the partition assertion widened from `enum − TERMINAL` to `enum − (TERMINAL ∪
   IN_PROGRESS)`. The old dichotomy ("every status is either terminable or terminal") was true until the
   ruling created a third state. **Widened, not deleted** — the property it defends is unchanged.
3. `GuestAccountTest` — `expect($text)->toMatch('/already under way/i')` **inverted** to assert the opposite
   sentence, so a revert of the copy goes red rather than shipping a warning that over-states the erase.

### Mutation

⚠️ Emptying `IN_PROGRESS_STATUSES` reddens **five** tests across **four** layers (service cancel · service
no-show · controller flash · OTA no-op · the partition). No new test passes vacuously.

## 2026-09-22 · APPLY 02 #2 — THE `.view` DELETE IS **WITHDRAWN** (R-PHANTOM STANDS)

⚠️⚠️ **A WITHDRAWAL, NOT A REVERSAL.** APPLY 01 #3 instructed a delete of six `.view` permissions that
**R-PHANTOM had already ruled KEPT three days earlier**, with the explicit clause "no seeder or role-table
churn", ✅ BUILT and pinned green. The six are *exactly* the six `.view` members of R-PHANTOM's seventeen —
an identity, not an overlap.

⚠️ **The distinction is load-bearing for anyone reading this in a year.** A reversal is a founder changing his
mind on new evidence; a withdrawal is a question that should never have been put to him. Only the second
happened. Recorded so the register does not show a three-day self-contradiction that did not occur.

**Nothing was deleted.** All seventeen stay; the pinned census is unchanged at **264 / 52 / 14**; the
documentation half already existed in `docs/PHANTOM-PERMISSIONS.md`.

🔬 **What the measurement actually found** — both methods agreed nothing *reads* the six, and that was still
the wrong question. Three of them are Shape C, *"enforced by a ROLE allow-list rather than by a permission"*:
`External Owner` holds exactly one permission (`owner_portal.view`) and `Guest` exactly one
(`guest_portal.view`). Deleting them empties both roles in all three tenants. **A permission whose
enforcement is structural is not an unused permission.** Cost had it proceeded: 52 → 46, 264 → 231.

### ⚠️⚠️ THE PROCESS RULE

**A brief proposing a change is not authority to make it if the register already rules on it. Check the
register BEFORE doing the work, not after** — checking afterwards cost a pass; checking first would have cost
a paragraph.

⚠️ **And the upstream half, recorded because a rule aimed only at the executor would be a false lesson: ask
what is already ruled in an area before putting a question to the founder.** The question reached him already
answered, and he answered it again the other way because nobody had told him he had.

See `docs/AUDIT-SUMMARY.md` §4 (the R-PHANTOM row and the note beneath it) for the full measurement.

## 2026-09-22 · APPLY 02 #3 — R9: REVERSE-CHECK-IN (`checked_in → confirmed`)

⚠️ **Numbered R9, not R8.** The brief and APPLY 01 both called it R8; 🔬 R8 was already `tentative →
confirmed` (ruled 2026-09-20, built FIX 54, pinned by a test). Renumbered before anything shipped. **The same
process rule the `.view` withdrawal earned, firing again the same day — check the register for the NAME too.**

**Why it exists:** R7 blocked `checked_in → cancelled` and left `checked_in` with one exit, `checked_out`,
which refuses while a balance is owed. A clerk who checked in the wrong row faced a waiver and a recorded
stay that never happened. R9 is the door R7 needed — the two are one decision, recorded so neither is
"simplified" without the other.

### 🔬 What a check-in actually writes — MEASURED, not read

Diffed every table across a real call: `reservations.status` (**the only column that moves**) plus one row
each in `reservation_status_history`, `domain_events` and `audit_events`. **Nothing else — no folio item, no
availability row, no housekeeping task, no email.**

⚠️⚠️ **That zero is the safety argument.** The feared defect — *a reverse that undoes the status but leaves a
charge behind is a money bug wearing a fix's clothes* — cannot occur, because a check-in posts no charge.
The same diff proves **no listener acted** on `reservation.checked_in`: one that did would have written a row.

### What reversing does to each

Status → `confirmed`. The history row is **appended to, never deleted** (#7) — the stay really was checked
in. A `reservation.checkin_reversed` event is appended to both streams. **Inventory is untouched and must
be**: the nights were occupied at BOOKING time, so `confirmed` holds the same lines; reaching into the single
inventory write path from a status operation is the F-18 shape.

⚠️ **Disclosed rather than undone** (R3's precedent): charges posted since check-in — with **real figures or
no line at all** (#39) — and the guest's own completed online check-in.

**Permission:** `can:reservations.checkin`. 🔬 Measured rather than assumed symmetric — its holders are
identical to `reservations.checkout` (Super Admin · Property Owner · Group Admin · Hotel Manager · Front
Desk). No new permission invented; that would ship a role-catalogue change nobody ruled on (#30).

### Proven four ways

(a) the reversal with every side effect read back · **(b) ⚠️ reverse → cancel → ALLOWED, unit released — the
step that could not run when R7 shipped, with a control proving cancel is still refused *before* the
reversal** · (c) refused from all five other statuses, row unmoved · (d) **two OS processes racing**: exactly
one wins, the loser is told, and the loser's *reason* is asserted (an assertion that something failed is not
an assertion that it failed correctly).

🔬 **Mutation-proven 3/3:** removing `lockForUpdate` makes BOTH processes reverse.

⚠️ The concurrency test lives in its own file **without `RefreshDatabase`** — 🔬 measured: that trait's
uncommitted transaction hides the fixture from other processes, and both workers died with "No query
results" while the race proved nothing and looked like a guard failure.

### Reported, not fixed

**Neither R3 nor R9 has a UI entry point.** 🔬 The only reference to `app.front-desk.reverse-checkout` in
`resources/views` is inside its own confirmation page. Both are URL-only. R9 matches R3 rather than diverging
from it; closing the gap is a build nobody ruled on.

## 2026-09-24 — ⚠️ RULING REVERSED: the platform console now wears the product's own design system

**THE PRIOR DECISION, AND WHY IT IS NOT A BUG.** The super-admin realm shipped with *"a cohesive 'control-room'
admin design system — deep-slate + indigo, deliberately DISTINCT from the warm tenant glass but as polished"*
(recorded above, and again in `<x-admin.shell>`'s own docblock). The argument was real: the highest-privilege
realm in the product should never *look* like a tenant portal, because looking like one is how somebody forgets
which realm they are in. ⚠️ **It was a deliberate, recorded design decision, not drift — and a future reader
finding the two palettes diverged should NOT "fix" it back.**

**THE FOUNDER RULED THE OTHER WAY**, in these words: *"this separate admin panel … color is not matching to the
theme, it also have the same color as the other roles, similar color similar icons similar cool animation similar
stuff similar button — every single thing in terms of design wise should be the same."* The concern was flagged in
one paragraph and the ruling was reaffirmed, so the panel was rebuilt. **The distinct-realm argument is retired,
not forgotten:** if it is ever wanted back, the rollback is one commit, and the substance of the case is the
paragraph above.

**HOW IT WAS DONE — one indirection layer, no per-view churn.** `<x-design.tokens />` now loads FIRST in both
admin layouts, and the `--ad-*` token **names are kept** while their **values are remapped** onto the canonical
`--vy-*` palette. So ~90 `.ad-*` rules and all nine admin views kept working while the whole realm recoloured.
The product's own recipes were copied, not re-invented: `--vy-bg` + the three drifting orbs and the shimmer
streak, frosted glass (blur 22 / saturate 1.15), `--vy-grad` pill buttons, the operator's 24×24 stroked nav
icons, its account chip, and the canonical **flat-peach avatar plate** (DO-RESTORE-5) rather than white-on-gradient
initials — a gradient has two worst cases at opposite ends and no single text colour clears both.

**⚠️ THREE DEFECTS THE REMAP EXPOSED — none of them cosmetic, none found by looking:**

1. ⚠️⚠️ **`--ad-danger` WAS NEVER DECLARED**, while `.ad-pill--suspended` and `.ad-btn--danger` both read it. An
   undefined custom property makes the declaration invalid at computed-value time and CSS drops it silently — so
   a suspended customer's status chip had been rendering as ordinary body ink, in a console whose whole job is
   to show account state at a glance.
2. ⚠️ **`--vy-glass-border` / `--vy-shadow` / `--vy-shadow-accent` are PER-SHELL OVERRIDES, not shared tokens.**
   `tokens.blade.php` deliberately carries only what is identical everywhere. The first pass referenced all three
   without declaring them — cards with no border and no shadow, silently.
3. ⚠️ **`.ad-field-label` is used in `customers/show` and defined nowhere**, so the re-auth label rendered at body
   size. Same family as the `.vy-sr-only` note already in the shell: *defined, not assumed.*

⚠️⚠️ **THE INSTRUMENT IS THE POINT.** All three were found by a **token/class resolution check** — extract every
`var(--x)` and every `class="ad-…"`, subtract what is actually declared, report the remainder — not by reading the
CSS and not by looking at the page. ⚠️ **An undefined CSS custom property or class name has no error surface at
all**: no console line, no 500, no failing test, and a page that renders "fine" to a glance. It is the CSS analogue
of the dead-code sweep, and it should be run on any shell that declares its own tokens.

**STRUCTURE — the double heading.** Every admin page repeated the shell's topbar title as its own in-content `h1`.
Invisible while the topbar title was 15px; a blatant double-heading at the product's 28px. All ten views adopted
the operator's convention: the topbar carries the title, an optional breadcrumb and a subline; pages start at
their content. ⚠️ `PlatformAdminGate0Test` (security group) asserts `"Platform console"` to prove the console shell
rendered — that string moved onto the sidebar's section label, **so the assertion stayed true rather than being
weakened to match a redesign.**

**HONESTY.** Presentation only — no controller, route, model, policy, migration or test was touched. Suite
**3745/3745 (26675 assertions)**, PHPStan L5 **0**, Pint clean. All ten admin pages browser-verified at 200 with
exactly one `<h1>` each and no raw Blade. Live at `rel_L @ fedfcd8e`; exposure battery unchanged
(**REFUSED=7 · LAYER-ANSWERED=46 · SERVED=0**); `.htaccess` drift check green. ⚠️ The money gate ran in
**INVARIANT mode (4 of 6 figures)** — the local seed date is unset, and *that run is not the money-as-seeded gate*;
it is quoted here with its own mode, as the script demands.

**⚠️ ONE DEFECT FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED — it is not ours and it is not new.** On an auth page taller than
the viewport the page background stops at the fold and leaves a white band. 🔬 A **control run proved the
operator's own `/login` does exactly the same** at a short viewport, so it is product-wide and pre-existing, not
introduced by this change. Fixing it means touching ~10 unrelated auth pages, which is a separate decision.

**Addendum, same day — the dropdowns.** The founder followed up: *"drop down in text boxes are not that cool.
It should be also cool enough like the other panels."* ⚠️ **The premise was not quite right, and saying so
mattered: the other panels use NATIVE selects too**, so "matching" them would have meant leaving these plain.
What was wanted was *better*, so the admin's four selects were given a real treatment — `appearance: none`
(the line that actually surrenders the OS widget; everything else is decoration the browser paints over), the
same frosted field as `.ad-input`, the operator account-menu's own `M6 9l6 6 6-6` chevron, a hover that lifts
the fill, and a focus state that recolours the chevron to the accent. 🔬 Measured 36px — byte-for-byte the
height of the input beside it. 🔬 Behaviour proven intact, not assumed: the pricing-shape select still drives
its JS (per-unit swaps the field to "Rate per unit").

⚠️ **TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED.** (1) A `data:` URI cannot read a custom property, so the chevron
colour is a **literal** — `#5F5853` / `#932A07`, verified equal to `--vy-muted` / `--vy-accent-text` but which
will **not** follow a future re-measure of either. Named in the file; it is the one drift the token layer
cannot prevent. (2) The **open** dropdown list is still the OS popup. `option` styling is honoured on
Windows/Linux and ignored by macOS; a genuinely themed popup needs a JS listbox, and that accessibility debt
is not worth it for four dropdowns.

⚠️⚠️ **CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT READ AS DRIFT: the admin is now AHEAD of the tenant shells on this
one control.** 66 selects across 35 non-admin files are still native. Levelling them up is a real pass, not a
copy-paste — the property and workspace switchers are deliberately borderless selects inside a frosted pill
and MUST be exempted from any blanket `select` rule. Offered to the founder; not done unasked.
