## 2026-09-24 — ADMIN 01 · PHASE 1 — the platform console: nothing silent · kill switches · audit · roles

**Scope, as briefed** (ADMIN 01 + the Phase-0 addendum + ADMIN 02 "build now, walk later"): a health board as the
first screen · the €297 fixed · L14 · database-backed kill switches · the one door hardened · the audit ledger made
append-only in fact · "Suspend" relabelled · the typed "96 of 142" removed · the owner-sessions defect measured
and recorded · four admin roles with every gate mutation-proved · the 12-character admin password rule.
⚠️ `is_internal` moved INTO Phase 1 from Phase 2: the board's "no customers yet" and the €297 fix both need it.

**THE ONE DOOR (`PlatformQuery`) — hardened, not replaced.** `read()` is now read-only at the DATABASE CONNECTION
(`PlatformWriteGuard`, `beforeExecuting`) — Eloquent, query-builder and raw-SQL writes all refused — and lifts BOTH
refusal scopes: `OrganizationScope` via `runAsSuperAdmin`, `OwnerScope` via a new admin-guard-gated
`OwnerContext::liftForPlatformConsole()`. `mutate()` refuses to run without a written reason. The two stray
`withoutGlobalScopes` calls are gone and a tokenised guard test fails on any new one in the admin realm.
⚠️⚠️ **CORRECTION TO PHASE 0, MEASURED:** Phase 0 said an admin also signed into an owner account "gets silently
undercounted". **On the HTTP path that does not happen**, for two independent reasons: `auth:admin` makes the admin
the DEFAULT guard for the request, and inside the door there is no tenant context, so `actorIsOwnerLinked()` answers
"not linked". The old door narrows in ONE condition only — an owner context already ACTIVE when it runs (the
singleton outlives a request in a long-running worker). `PlatformDoorTest` measures all three conditions, with a
control that reproduces the narrowing; the lift is defence in depth, not the fix of a live leak.

**THE AUDIT LEDGER.** `platform_admin_actions` refuses UPDATE / DELETE / TRUNCATE / REPLACE at the model AND at the
connection — each layer proved on its own, because both throw the same exception and a combined test stays green
when either is deleted. New nullable `reason` column; every console WRITE route requires one (`AdminReason`) — a
structural test sends each of the 16 write routes a payload valid EXCEPT for the reason. Self-service account
actions are the one deliberate exception. A DB-level trigger is PROPOSED, not done (KNOWN-LIMITS L17).

**ROLES.** `platform_admins.role` (nullable; NULL FAILS CLOSED; existing admins backfilled to `owner` — one row on
production). One matrix, `PlatformAdminRole`, read by the route gate (`EnsurePlatformCapability`) and the UI
(`PlatformAdmin::may()`). Owner = everything · Support = tenants + support tools · Billing = revenue + plans ·
Analyst = read-only. A structural test fails on any console route without a gate; a behavioural test proves every
gate by a role that must be refused (>40 refusals).
⚠️ Interpretation stated: Analyst "read-only everywhere" includes the Admins and Integrations screens (read), not
support tools; Support has no view of revenue.

**ADMIN ACCESS.** Invite (the invitee sets their OWN password from a one-time link — only its SHA-256 is stored;
shown once, never emailed, because mail is `log`), change role, revoke, restore, force sign-out. Floors: the last
active Owner can be neither demoted nor revoked; nobody revokes themselves; every change needs the actor's current
password and a reason. ⚠️ **Sessions are tracked by the app** (`platform_admin_sessions`, keyed by a random value in
the session data) because production's `session.driver` is `file` — so force sign-out and revocation are enforced on
the next request on any driver. A revoked admin with a live session is now refused (before: carried on until expiry).

**THE PASSWORD RULE** — `PlatformAdminPasswordPolicy`, at creation, invitation and change: 12+ characters, mixed
case, a number AND a symbol. ⚠️ **The union of the two old bars, and the suite is why:** the first version copied the
creation bar alone and silently DROPPED the symbol the change form used to demand — PasswordCompositionTest (path
6/9) caught `StrongPass12` being accepted where it had been refused the day before.

**KILL SWITCHES** (`platform_settings`): sign-ups (all) · sign-up with Google · with X · sign-in with Google · with X.
A missing row is ON; an unreadable table is ON (logged). Read per request, 30 s cache busted on write. Enforced at
the signup form AND its submit (a form or social stash from before a flip cannot provision), and at the social
callback where the outcome is known; `/login` hides a provider button only when both its switches are off. Turning
a SIGN-IN switch off shows how many passwordless single-provider accounts it strands and requires a second
confirmation, enforced server-side. No switch is read by any `/admin` path.

**THE HEALTH BOARD** (`/admin`): mail · queue · scheduler + dead-man's switch · server errors (daily log, origin only,
no route group — said on the card) · live release (read from the layout; no deploy button) · silent config (names
only — `ConfigInventory`, now ONE class the CLI script also calls) · switches · exposure battery (GREY by design).
Four states; a check that throws is GREY, never green. Calibrated: mail `log`/`array` is RED.

**THE €297.** The "recurring plan value" summed list prices over active AND trialing subscriptions — on production,
three free trials of Vyrobel's own orgs. Removed, not relabelled: the Overview shows "No live billing yet" until
Phase 4 computes revenue from charges, excludes internal orgs by default, and says "No customers yet" in words.

**L14 CLOSED** — proven by behaviour, A/B, on a cached config with the value only in `.env` (see KNOWN-LIMITS).
**L16 RECORDED** — on production, "sign out other sessions" and a password reset end no session, and the reset's
audit row says they did. Not fixed, as ruled. **"96 of 142" removed** from the live records; it was a stale hand
count of a broader thing than it was quoted as.

**PROOF.** 31 mutations, 31 caught, every file restored byte-identical. Pint clean · PHPStan L5 0 · the full suite
(its count is whatever the run prints). ⚠️ Two earlier suite runs DIED AT LOAD on a duplicate test-helper name this
phase introduced — one of them was nearly read as a pass from a truncated tail. A scan for duplicate global test
functions now exists; the lesson is the standing one: a result you did not see is not a result.

**DEPLOYED 2026-09-24 — `rel_N @ 7fa23cde`** (L12k; three additive migrations run from rel_N while rel_M served —
`/`, `/login`, `/signup`, `/admin/login` all 200 throughout; boot check on the target; swap 4 ms; rollback =
`ops/release.sh rollback rel_M`). **Public checks: PASS 11 · FAIL 0 · COULD NOT MEASURE 0** — both providers' redirects
and buttons, `/signup`, 16 anonymous `/admin` GETs → login, 4 anonymous POSTs refused, the neutral invite page, 151
routes free of 5xx, battery SERVED=0. The three Phase-0 orgs marked `is_internal` by id prefix READ from the survey
(the script refuses any other set), each read back; a probe sign-up (`ADMIN-P1 PROBE (not a customer)`) accepted,
its rows read back (1 user · 1 property · a trialing subscription), marked internal by exact name. Customers on the
platform: **0**. Kill switches read ON with zero rows. `Hash::check` of the known default against admin@vyrobel.com
is still TRUE (control: a random string → false), so **break-glass will ship dormant** (ADMIN 02).
⚠️ **Three deploy-script defects, found by running them, none by reading:** `release.sh` called a migration
"pending" because its NAME contained the word (`…add_pending_email…`) — now matches the status column only;
`mark-internal.php` died at boot because Pint turned an FQCN into a `use` import placed BELOW its first use, and PHP

## 2026-09-24 — ADMIN 01 · PHASE 2 — tenants: directory · triage · a REAL suspension · archive · protected tenants

**Scope, as briefed** (ADMIN 01 §Phase 2 + the addendum's #1/#5/#7 + ADMIN 02's loop). ⚠️ `is_internal` was built in
Phase 1 (the €297 needed it); Phase 2 carries ONE additive migration — three nullable `organizations` columns:
`signup_source`, `lifecycle_lock`, `suspended_from_status`.

**SUSPEND IS NOW REAL.** 🔬 Until today `status = suspended` closed the storefront and nothing else (Phase 1 relabelled
the button until this landed). Now `RefuseSuspendedOrganization` refuses the organisation's STAFF (`/app`, every route,
billing included), its OWNERS (`/owner`), owner API tokens (JSON 403) and — registered as a Livewire PERSISTENT
middleware — the next component update from a page opened before the suspension. A plain explanation page (the ONE
branded error layout, given an optional actions slot): sign out, contact Vyrobel, or switch to another organisation
the person also belongs to (the switcher is the one route let through). The rule is ONE definition,
`TenantLifecycle::refusesAccess()`: suspended, archived, or unreadable (fails closed).
⚠️⚠️ **It touches no money** — proven by a test that snapshots reservations, reservation_units, folios, folio_items,
payments, owner_ledger and availability for the org and requires them identical after. Guests keep their own pages
(no `guest/`, `book/`, webhook or `/admin` route carries the gate — asserted structurally).
**The reservation warning**: the detail page counts in-house and upcoming stays (COUNTS, never rows), and a
suspension or archive of a hotel with any is refused until the admin ticks that they have seen them — server-side.
**Reactivate** restores the status it had before (`suspended_from_status`), so a trialing hotel stays trialing.

**ARCHIVE** = soft delete, only of a suspended organisation, reversible (restore → still suspended, on purpose).
⚠️⚠️ **Three defects archive would have introduced, found by audit before it existed:** (1) `TenantProvisioningService`
checked slug uniqueness against LIVE organisations only while the `slug` UNIQUE index covers archived ones — the
next signup with an archived org's name would 500 (mutation-proved: SQLSTATE 1062); (2) `ResolvePublicProperty` read
the org's status without trashed rows, got NULL, read that as "not closed" and would have REOPENED an archived
hotel's storefront; (3) the storefront sitemap would have kept advertising it. All three now read `withTrashed`.
⚠️ Stated, not changed: `SendPreArrivalEmails` / `SendPaymentReminders` iterate `Organization::all()`, so an archived
organisation's guests get neither email — consistent with archive, and moot while mail is `log`.
No hard delete, no prune — a structural test refuses a destroy/force/purge/prune route name and any `forceDelete`
token in the console's code.

**PROTECTED ORGANISATIONS** (`lifecycle_lock`): `baseline` refuses EVERY console write (suspend · reactivate ·
archive · restore · internal · assign-plan), and each refusal is written to the ledger as `platform.customer.refused`
so it can be SEEN — `DemoSeeder` sets it on tenant one, and the `security.baseline_tenant_guard` organisation is
locked even with no column set. `confirm` needs the organisation's EXACT name typed — for production's `Vyrobel
Internal`, set by `ops/host/mark-internal.php protect` (by name, read back, refuses to change an existing lock).

**DIRECTORY / DETAIL / TRIAGE.** Directory: name · status · plan · signed up with · verified · created · last sign-in ·
properties · users · internal; search, five filters, sortable, paginated; archived hidden unless asked. Detail adds
the account holders (name, email, role, verified, last sign-in — Vyrobel users, never guests), the lock, and the
console's own actions against the org with their reasons. Triage: three counted buckets with their definitions on
screen — unverified 7+ days · never signed in · created with X (surfaced, never acted on) — customers only unless
asked; ONE predicate (`applyBucket`) feeds both the counts and the directory's filtered list.
⚠️ **Definitions stated, because they are choices:** "verified" = at least one active member confirmed an email;
"last sign-in" = the latest COMPLETED sign-in — 🔬 the signup session does not stamp `last_login_at`, so "never
signed in" means "never came back after signing up"; "upcoming" = not terminal, not checked in, stay not yet ended
(UTC date).
**SIGNUP SOURCE** is recorded from the public signup only (`email` / `google` / `twitter`); an unknown value is
refused as NULL; no backfill — historical rows read "Unknown", never "email".

**THE LEDGER** — `PlatformQuery::mutate()` writes its row BEFORE the action runs and the row can never be edited, so
an action that throws now gets a second `<action>.failed` row; the ledger no longer claims what did not happen.

**PROOF.** 24 mutations, 24 caught — each by the test aimed at it, named in the run; every file restored
byte-identical. Pint clean · PHPStan L5 0 · the full suite green on this run (3852/3852, 2026-09-24 — a dated figure, not a pin) ·
money gate FULL: six figures and the four row digests identical to Phase 1's.

**DEPLOYED 2026-09-24 — `rel_O @ 1152752b`** (L12k; one additive migration run from rel_O while rel_N served — `/`,
`/login`, `/signup`, `/admin/login` 200 throughout; boot check on the target, every `/app`, `/owner` and `api/owner`
route carrying the gate except the signed owner email-change link, by design; swap 3 ms; rollback =
`ops/release.sh rollback rel_N`). **Public checks: PASS 11 · FAIL 0 · COULD NOT MEASURE 0** (17 anonymous admin GETs

Probe sign-up `ADMIN-P2 PROBE (not a customer)` accepted and read back — ⚠️ **`signup_source = email`, the first

## 2026-09-24 — ADMIN 01 · PHASE 3 — support tools, and BREAK-GLASS built, proved and shipped DORMANT

**Scope, as briefed** (ADMIN 01 §Phase 3 + ADMIN 02 "the password — off the build, on one feature"). One additive
migration: a NEW table, `break_glass_sessions` (platform-owned: `target_organization_id`, deliberately not
`organization_id`, so it can never carry the tenant scope or be read or deleted by the tenant it records).

**SUPPORT TOOLS** (Owner + Support; account holders only, never guests; every action a reason, via `mutate()`):
lookup by email — the ledger records WHICH user was found, never the address typed · unlink a provider — through the
PRODUCT'S OWN floor (`SignInCredentials::mayUnlink`), so it is refused exactly when it would leave no way in · mark an
email verified — the DEPLOYMENT.md "mail is down" procedure as a button, `forceFill` (the column is not fillable and a
mass-assign drops SILENTLY — mutation-proved) and READ BACK from the database · resend verification / send a password
reset — the real code paths, and while mail is `log` the result says **NOT DELIVERED** in words; never a success.
`MailDelivery` is now ONE definition of "mail discards", read by the health board and by these buttons.

**BREAK-GLASS** — requires a reason, a fresh TOTP (step-up, rate-limited; a failure is on the ledger), a chosen
organisation that is not archived, a VERIFIED back-office user there, and no tenant login in the same browser. Grants
30 minutes. The admin stays signed in as themselves; each /app request BORROWS that user's view (`setUser`, request
only — never a login, and the `verified` gate is satisfied, not skipped). VISIBLE: a banner injected into every HTML
page whatever its layout. AUDITED: start, every page (path + status), every refused write, end. TOLD: at the end —
by hand, at expiry, or by the per-minute sweep — every active back-office user gets an ALWAYS-ON in-app notice naming
the admin, the time and the reason (synchronous, so a parked queue cannot swallow it). A suspended organisation may be
looked at (suspension refuses its own people, not support). Expiry is enforced on every request, not by the cron.
⚠️⚠️ **READ-ONLY, TWICE, EACH LAYER PROVED ALONE:** (1) `RefuseWritesDuringBreakGlass` refuses every non-GET from a
browser holding a session — /app, every Livewire action, /owner — outside /admin (the brief's rule); (2)
`EnterBreakGlassSession` runs each page inside `PlatformWriteGuard::readOnly`, so a page that WRITES while viewed is
stopped at the connection — and nothing lands in the tenant's history as if their own user did it. 🔬 The whole back
office was walked in a session: no parameter-free /app page 500s; the maintenance pages CREATE their settings row on
first view (a write on GET — an existing product behaviour, not changed here) and show the read-only notice instead.
**Tenant one**: break-glass reads it; a write attempt into it is refused and its rows are unchanged — tested.

⚠️⚠️ **TWO ORDERING DEFECTS, BOTH INVISIBLE TO A GREEN TEST UNTIL THE HARNESS WAS MADE HONEST:**
1. Laravel SORTS route middleware by its priority list, and `auth` outranks the web group's `SubstituteBindings` — so
   `auth` was moved AHEAD of `EnterBreakGlassSession`. On a real request a support admin would have been sent to
   /login before the session was read. The suite was green because `actingAs($admin, 'admin')` had made `admin` the
   default guard, so `auth` passed on the admin. Fixed with `prependToPriorityList`; every break-glass test now resets
   the default guard to `web` after starting a session, as a real request has it.
2. Fixing (1) pulled `EnterBreakGlassSession` ahead of layer 1, so the refusal ran INSIDE the read-only scope, its own
   audit insert was refused, and the page came back as layer 2's — layer 1 was silently gone. A second priority rule
   puts it first; the layer-1 test now asserts layer 1's OWN wording, so layer 2 cannot stand in for it.
⚠️ **AND A MISDIAGNOSIS OF MY OWN, CORRECTED:** I read the maintenance pages as 500s and "fixed" a wrapped-exception
render path. The failing array was the write-on-view list, not the error list — they were never 500s. The chain walk
stays (a write from INSIDE a Blade template really is re-thrown wrapped in a `ViewException` — read in vendor), now
pinned by a test that renders a wrapped refusal; the comment that claimed it fixed the maintenance pages was removed.

**DORMANT** (ADMIN 02): `config/platform.php` → `break_glass.enabled = false`, a LITERAL (never env, never runtime).
While off: every break-glass route is a 404, no button, a leftover key is cleared and /app is not entered. 🔬 On the
host, `Hash::check('123456', <admin hash>)` is still TRUE, so it stays off. **Switching it on is one line and a
separate deploy**, after the founder changes the password and the check returns false.

**PROOF.** 24 mutations, 24 caught — each by the test aimed at it, against a green baseline (a first run was
discarded: its baseline was red, so its "catches" proved nothing). Pint clean · PHPStan L5 0 · full suite
3873/3873 on this run (2026-09-24 — dated, not a pin; the first run was 3870/3873 and caught three real things: an
unread flash key, and two catalogue-size pins that move WITH A REASON — the operator catalogue grew by the always-on
`support_access` notice, 16 → 17, written beside each pin) · money gate FULL: six figures + four digests unchanged.

**DEPLOYED 2026-09-24 — `rel_P @ 7440b720`** (L12k; one additive migration — the new `break_glass_sessions` table —
run from rel_P while rel_O served, `/`, `/login`, `/signup`, `/admin/login` 200 throughout; swap 4 ms; rollback =
`ops/release.sh rollback rel_O`). Boot check ON THE HOST: `config('platform.break_glass.enabled')` reads **false** from

stores each VERIFIED event in `webhook_events` with its full payload and organisation → `BillingWebhookService::applyInvoice()`
moves only status and period and records **no amount anywhere**. So the paid invoice is the only record of what was
charged, and `PlatformRevenue` sums only PROCESSED `invoice.paid` rows — never `price_minor`, never `per_unit_minor`,
never `vat_pct` (a test gives the plan an absurd list price and asserts it never reaches a figure). MRR / ARR per
currency (never summed across currencies) · new / expansion / contraction / churned per organisation, this month vs
last · trial-to-paid · failed payments · past due. Customers only unless asked. 🔬 **Production today: 6 subscriptions,
all trialing, none live-billed, zero Stripe events** — the page says **"No live billing yet"** in words.
⚠️ **A DESIGN FLAW CAUGHT BY ITS OWN TEST:** the first version put a charge "on a monthly footing" by dividing by an
average month in seconds — a 30-day monthly invoice counted as 101.46% of itself, February ~108.7%: a monthly plan's
MRR would have wobbled with the calendar. Now: the interval Stripe STATES on the line; failing that the period
bucketed (week / month / quarter / half-year / year); only an odd period by its exact length.
⚠️ **Not built, stated:** "comp a plan / extend a trial" — the brief ALLOWS it, it does not require it; it is

recorded step). "Added a property" is not a stage — sign-up creates it — and that is MEASURED (organisations with no

and hotel names only, never a guest (a test asserts four guest names never reach the page). (2) A REQUEST REGISTER
for requests arriving by email / letter / phone / a hotel: kind, subject (an account holder BY USER ID — the email is
looked up and NOT stored; a hotel's guest BY ORGANISATION ONLY), channel, received, **due in one month** (Art. 12(3)),

## 2026-09-25 — ADMIN 03 — every console page, four ways (functionality · design · content · fonts)

A quality pass, not a feature pass: no new feature, no redesign, the console's own design language. 28 GET routes
listed from the route file; 38 views walked (the signed-in pages and their states — empty, internal, found, not found —
plus the invite page, the public `/status`, the 404) at 1440 desktop and 390 phone, 76 screenshots. ⚠️ NOT walked: the
2FA challenge, 2FA setup and the email-change link — each needs the founder mid-sign-in or a mailed link (dark mode: the console and the product support none —
excluded once, not per page; ⚠️ the public `/status` DOES carry a dark block, found while fixing). The walk came first;
fixes second; the register grouped by ROOT CAUSE, so one fix closes many sightings.

**S1 — the console told the admin something untrue (3), each fixed, tested and mutation-proved:**
- **F1** the audit log's default "Changes & sign-ins" view listed nine kinds of PAGE VIEW — `READ_ACTIONS` was a hand
  list nobody updated after Phase 1. Extended, and `AuditReadActionsAreCompleteTest` now scans the code (tokenised) so a
  new `->read('platform.*')` that is not in the list fails the suite.
- **F2** the overview said "0 on trial" beside "8 in free trial", and the directory's "On trial" filter could never match:
  a free trial lives on the SUBSCRIPTION (signup sets the account status to `active`). Filter, plan column, overview and
  detail now read the subscription; the two statuses are labelled apart ("Account status" / "Subscription", in words).
- **F3** the privacy desk printed "Next due: UTC" — a timezone with no date (`?->format().' UTC' ?? '—'` — the `??` never
  fires because the concatenation is never null). Now "Nothing scheduled".

**S2/S3 — fixed at the root, once:** the shell renders the notice and EVERY validation error once (F12 — eleven pages
each showed only the first error; their copies removed) · shell CSS for phone: header stacks, table cards scroll
themselves, label/value lists shrink, long values wrap (F4/F5) · tabular digits and non-wrapping times (F16/F17) ·
`App\Support\Platform\ActionLabel` — ONE place an action key becomes words, the key kept in reach (F6) ·
`<x-admin.time>` — ONE way a moment is printed: absolute UTC on screen, relative in the title (F7, 20 sites; the health
board's error hour now says its hour and zone) · the glossary (F8 — "Organisations", "Statistics", no "tenant" in copy)
· the ledger rows for a published announcement and a posted incident now NAME the row they created (F13 — the id is
minted before `mutate()`) · plurals (F14) · cohort months "Sep 2026" (F18) · the privacy form's visible labels (F19) ·
the kill switch's wording at zero lock-outs (F20) · "marked as in progress" (F21).

**Refused or reclassified — say which, never silently:**
- ⚠️ **F20's zero-count confirmation is KEPT.** Only its words changed. Requiring it at zero is deliberate (the count can
  change between loading the page and pressing the button); dropping it would weaken a kill-switch guard.
- ⚠️ **F10 WITHDRAWN — a probe artefact.** "Auth inputs render Arial 13.3px" came from `querySelector('input, select')`,
  whose first match is the hidden `_token` input (always the browser default). Every visible input carries `.ad-input`
  → Inter. The instrument, not the page.
- **F11 DELIBERATE** — `/status` uses the system font by its own rule: no request of any kind, so it renders when the
  asset pipeline is what is broken (as the error pages).
- **F8's "11 American spellings" was a SOURCE pre-read** that counted comments and identifiers; on rendered copy there
  are none. Nothing to fix; recorded.
- F15 (label sizes) matches the product (`/app` uses the same 10.5px uppercase labels). The audit log keeps

## 2026-09-25 — SESSIONS 01 — sign-out means signed out (L16 CLOSED) · and FINISH 01 Part C, the small backlog

Run unattended by the founder's ruling (FINISH 01): no password or 2FA of his typed, nothing asked, probes only.

### B1 — the causes, MEASURED before any fix (per guard)

| behaviour | what the code did | what production did (rel_V, `file` driver) |
|---|---|---|
| change password (web) | `User::changePasswordTo` → rotate remember token + `ActiveSessions::terminateFor` (DELETE rows) | deleted 0 rows — **B stayed signed in (200)**, live, two real sessions of one probe |
| password reset (web) | same shared path | same — nothing reached the other sessions |
| "sign out other sessions" (owner + operator) | DELETE rows + rotate token (operator carried its OWN copy of the query) | deleted 0 rows, said "You have no other active sessions" — **B stayed in (200)**, live |
| hotel Security page session list | reads `sessions` rows | always empty (0 rows; 414 session FILES on disk) |
| guest password change/reset | rotate remember token only | **ended NO other session, on ANY driver** — a code gap, not a driver one |
| admin session list / force sign-out | app-tracked `platform_admin_sessions` | worked, driver-independent — ⚠️ but force sign-out on YOURSELF ended the caller's own session too |
| remember-me | web + admin issue none (`LoginRequest` omits it); guest does, token rotated on change/reset | web/admin: no cookie to steal (measured: `Set-Cookie` = session + XSRF only); guest: already rotated |
| `AuthenticateSession` | applied NOWHERE | so a session never noticed its password changed, on any guard |

⚠️ **Owner API tokens (Passport): a password reset does NOT revoke them** (`changePasswordTo` never touches the OAuth
tables; production holds 0 live tokens). Revoking protects a hacked owner and breaks their integrations — **the
founder's ruling, reported not decided.**

### B2 — fixed at the root, all layers (`rel_W @ 3cd72c26`)
- `SESSION_DRIVER=database` on production — the shared `.env` edited on the host (backup kept, 600), baked into rel_W's
  config cache at staging (L14); rel_V kept `file` until the 3 ms swap. `sessions` already existed (additive: none).
  **Proven by behaviour**: a fresh sign-up after the swap created its `sessions` row.
- `EndSessionsOnPasswordChange` (Laravel's AuthenticateSession) on the web group → a password change or reset is fatal
  to every OTHER session on web, guest and admin, whatever the driver; the session that made the change stays in. It
  stands aside for a break-glass request (nothing is written to the web session — it is not a login).
- `ActiveSessions::signOutOthers` — the ONE "sign out others": rows deleted + `logoutOtherDevices()` re-hash (driver-
  independent; it refuses loudly unless `web` is a session guard) + remember token rotated. The operator copy is gone.
- Guest change/reset now end other sessions (hash layer + rows). Admin force sign-out on YOURSELF ends only your OTHER
  sessions. With the database driver a break-glass session would have been filed under the VIEWED hotel user
  (`auth.driver` is a singleton resolved at save time) — the default guard is handed back to `admin` first.
- ⚠️ A `Login` listener to clear a "stale hash" was written and REMOVED before commit: every sign-out in the app
  invalidates the session (checked), so no real path leaves one — its docblock claimed "measured" and was not.
- ⚠️ Rollback = `ops/release.sh rollback rel_V` — returns sessions to FILES and signs everyone out a second time.

### B3 — proven the way an intruder meets it
13 tests (`SignOutMeansSignedOutTest` + one in `PlatformBreakGlassTest`): the four scenarios per guard, the ORDINARY
case (you stay signed in where you changed it) in every one, per-layer tests for the two sign-out-others layers.
Mutation set `sessions-01` (8): all land and are caught. ⚠️ Two instrument traps met: the break-glass test was blind
twice (the `auth.driver` singleton survives between test requests; the test process reuses one session handler whose
"row exists" flag makes the second write an UPDATE of nothing) — caught by the harness (S01-M7 NOT CAUGHT), fixed by
asserting what `DatabaseSessionHandler::userId()` reads at save. Four suite reds were the HARNESS (`actingAs` switching
accounts inside one session) → `TestCase::be()` forgets the previous account's hash; the product check was not touched.

**Scope, as briefed** (the part that needs nothing from the founder): move the three older `.env` backups out of the

production. ⚠️ Two defects surfaced on the way and were fixed: sign-up never sent the FIRST verification link, and the
mail log recorded every NOTIFICATION as "unknown".

1. **Backups — MOVED.** `public_html/.env.bak.pre-google` · `.env.bak.pre-rotate2` · `.env.bak.pre-twitter` →
   `~/domains/vyrobel.com/env-backups/` (dir 700, each 600), beside this session's own two (`.env.bak-mail02-…`,
   `.env.bak-sessions01-…`). sha256 identical before and after; names, sizes, modes and digests only — never contents.
   The only `.env*` left under `public_html` is the live `.env`; none under any release's `public/`; nothing in the app,
   the deploy scripts or the host's own scripts names the old paths. ⚠️ They were never web-reachable — every request
   is rewritten into `current/public/`, and `<FilesMatch "^\.">` denies dotfiles (read from `.htaccess`).
2. **`.env` — ONE shared file, measured; KNOWN-LIMITS L15 was a misreading.** `public_html/.env` (600, owner
   `u545270279`) is LINKED into all 25 releases; none holds a copy. L15's "777" is each SYMLINK's own mode, which
   Linux ignores (`stat -L` → 600). The web process runs as the owner — 🔬 the cache files a live sign-up request wrote
   are owned by `u545270279`. ⚠️ **Beside it, a real one, fixed:** 9 old releases kept their cached config (a compiled
   copy of `.env`) at 644; all 24 are 600 now, digests unchanged. **By result:** front door PASS 12 · FAIL 0 · CNM 0
   and a real sign-up accepted. ⚠️ **A deploy re-does it rather than undoing it:** `stage` (and `recache`) refuse a
   release whose `.env` is not the link and re-apply 600 to the shared file every time — a hand edit in hPanel's file
   editor may rewrite it wider. 🔬 On rel_Z: `.env → ../../public_html/.env · shared file mode 600`.

   rebuilt (L14) and `stage` refuses a commit that is already live; `recache` builds a release of the SAME commit with
   config and routes rebuilt from the current `.env`, and checks the live release's cache is untouched.

## 2026-09-26 — ADMIN 04 · create and update organisations from the console, and each one's sign-in activity

**Asked by the founder:** in the console's Organisations, create an organisation, update one, and see when each one's
people last signed in — "the exact details". **His rulings (asked, 2026-09-26):** a console-created founder gets a
set-password link by email, which also verifies the address; name, country, language and billing are editable —
currency and the web address are NOT; sign-ins show time, user, IP and device.

1. **Sign-in activity** (organisation page): the last successful sign-in (exact UTC time, who, device, IP) and the last
   25 sign-ins, failed attempts and lockouts for its staff and owners, within `login_activity`'s 90-day window — the
   rows the Activity page already shows platform-wide, narrowed to one organisation. Never a guest (by construction:
   a success must name a `user`; the guest realm records no address). Devices in words (`DeviceLabel`: "Chrome on
   macOS", an unknown agent shown as itself). Read inside the page's existing audited read.
2. **Update details** (`POST admin/customers/{id}/details`, tenants.manage): name, country (an ISO code through the ONE
   `Countries` list — the column is char 2; a name is normalised, an unknown value refused), language (the app's own
   list), billing email / name / VAT / city (the operator's Settings limits). Reason required; the baseline refuses and
   a protected organisation needs its name typed; the ledger records WHICH fields changed, never their values; every
   value read back. A changed VAT number reaches Stripe (`StripeTaxIdSync::push`) as it does from the operator's two
   screens. ⚠️ Found: those two operator writers disagree on limits (company 255 vs 160, VAT 64 vs 40) — the console
   uses the stricter; the drift itself is recorded, not fixed.
3. **Create** (`GET admin/customers/create` — registered BEFORE `customers/{organization}`; `POST admin/customers`):
   through `TenantProvisioningService` — roles, founder as `Property Owner` with NO password, first property, trial —
   `signup_source = console`, optionally internal. The founder's link reuses the invite machinery
   (`OwnerInviteService::issueFounderActivation`, role `founder`: hashed single-use token, 7 days; redeeming sets the
   password, verifies the address, assigns no second role) and the invite email with founder wording (sent by
   "Vyrobel", not by the hotel). REFUSED before anything is written when the link could not reach the founder: mail
   discarding, an address that can never receive mail, an address an account already holds. Ledger: the intent with
   the reason, then the result with the new id, then the link.

**AN INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW before deploy** (29 agents: four lenses — security, correctness, contracts, test
adequacy — and one skeptic per finding, defaulting to refuted): 23 reports survived, **11 distinct defects**, all fixed
and each pinned by a test:
- the "last sign-in" came from the same 25 rows as lockouts, so a burst of lockouts — which anyone who knows an address
  can cause from the login page — hid every real sign-in → its own query;
- attempts at the PLATFORM CONSOLE's login with a member's address showed as that organisation's → the staff and
  owners' own realm (`web`) only; the tenant login records lockouts, not per-attempt failures;
- the 90-day window was claimed but not applied → applied in the query;
- a Stripe outage after a VAT change 500'd a save that had landed and logged it as failed → the save stands, the
  ledger stays true, the admin is told;
- a language outside en/pt/es/fr set on the operator's screens was reset to `en` by an unrelated save → the stored
  value round-trips; billing values the operator's Billing screen allows longer no longer block an unrelated save;
- the founder-link ledger row said "sent" when the send failed → `.failed`;
- the signup funnel's typed columns dropped the new `console` source, so the columns no longer added up to "All" →
  built from the ONE list of sources;
- the founder email's "ignore this" line said no account exists → a founder wording;
- a founder's pending link appeared in the operator's own pending-invite lists → excluded.
Two reports were refuted by their skeptics. The every-console-write-needs-a-reason test caught the two new routes
unregistered; they are now held to it.

## 2026-09-26 — ADMIN 05 · delete an organisation permanently, and one field system for every console form

**THE RULINGS (the founder, 2026-09-26).** (1) The organisation screens become full CRUD: create and update (ADMIN 04),
suspend and archive (ADMIN 01), and now **DELETE — "delete everything, always"**: one deliberate, Owner-only action that
erases an organisation and everything it owns. ⚠️ **This replaces, for this one action, the standing "no hard delete"
ruling** (§ADMIN 01 Phase 2 — the entry is left as written; this is the pointer). Archive stays the reversible option,
and nothing deletes on a timer (no prune). (2) **"Every console form"** gets the redesigned fields — dropdowns, inputs,
choices and switches — tested in a browser.

**DELETE — what it does** (`POST admin/customers/{id}/delete` · `tenants.manage` AND the new `tenants.delete`, Owner
only · `OrganizationDeletion`):
- Asks for the admin's password, the organisation's exact name typed, an acknowledgement and a written reason; refuses
  a protected organisation (the lock), and anything not suspended or archived first.
- **Refuses before touching anything** while money is moving at a third party — live Stripe billing, an open card
  payment or hold, a payout in transit, a payout run in progress, a payment notification being processed — or while
  another organisation's rows point into this one (a cascade would take them). The service re-checks on its own, so a
  caller that skips the console still cannot delete (tested per layer).
- **One transaction:** rows reachable only through a parent go first (amenity links, a guest's notifications, sessions,
  security-log rows, reset tokens); then every table with an `organization_id` — READ from the schema at run time,
  never a typed list — then the organisation row; then the people whose ONLY link was this organisation. A
  **post-condition** re-reads every organisation table and rolls the lot back if one row survives. Files (media — which
  carries guests' ID scans — brand logos, avatars) are removed only after commit; one that cannot be removed is
  counted and logged, never fatal.
- **Kept:** the platform's own records — the append-only console ledger (the intent with the reason, and the result
  with counts), break-glass sessions, privacy requests.
- The confirmation screen says exactly what goes before asking for anything (records, tables, reservations, guests,
  payments, invoices, accounts deleted and kept, files) — or shows the refusal instead of the form.

**FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT — three defects, each now pinned by a test and a mutation:**
- ⚠️⚠️ **Laravel 13's `Schema::getTables()` with no argument lists EVERY database the connection can see** — on the dev
  machine five (225 names for 100 organisation tables), so the confirmation screen counted each table once per copy.
  🔬 The SAME call was in the retention meter (`RetentionCoverage::liveTables()`), and the shipped
  `resources/data/data-inventory.json` (TONIGHT 01 #3) named six tables — `bookings`, `tickets`, `information`,
  `packages`, `gateways`, `tenants` — that only OTHER projects' databases on the dev machine hold. Its drift test could
  not see it: it regenerated through the same list. Both calls are now scoped to the connection's own database, the
  file is regenerated (meter unchanged: 144 categories · 2 strict · 40 lenient), and an independent read
  (information_schema, `DATABASE()`) pins both. 🔬 **Production was never affected**: its database user sees ONE
  database (147 tables), measured 2026-09-26.
- ⚠️⚠️ **"Belongs to no other organisation" is not the same as "no other organisation's records name them."** Five
  foreign keys into `users` CASCADE (shifts, leave requests, signed amendment acknowledgements, message reactions and
  stars) and the rest set null — so deleting a FORMER member of another organisation would have deleted that
  organisation's history. A person is now kept whenever any other organisation's row references them, read from the
  schema's foreign keys.
- The confirm prompt showed the organisation's name through an UPPERCASE label while the check is exact — an admin
  typing what they saw was refused. The name now shows as stored, in all three type-to-confirm prompts (the two older
  ones had the same flaw).

**THE FIELD SYSTEM** (`resources/views/admin/partials/fields.blade.php`, included once by both console layouts): one look
for inputs, choice chips (radio buttons), switches (checkboxes) and a **searchable dropdown** — progressive, never a
replacement: every control stays the native element the form posts. Searchable: the country lists (with flags) and
every organisation picker (audit filter, privacy desk, break-glass) — and the announcement audience becomes a
searchable **checklist** (a native multi-select drops every earlier choice on a plain click). Browser-tested
(Playwright, 1280 px and 390 px): keyboard (↑/↓/Home/End/Enter/Esc/Tab), outside click, no-match, the posted values,
no sideways scroll. Found in the browser: the open list was translucent enough for the labels beneath to read through
it (now opaque); its chevron differed from the plain dropdowns' (now the same glyph); a plain dropdown in a form had
lost its surface to the shell's chevron rule (restored); the filter bar's searchable picker did not match its
neighbours (now the bar's own look); a screen reader heard the label but not the value (now "Country: Portugal").

**TWO INDEPENDENT REVIEWS before deploy** (a data-safety adversary, and a silent-failure hunter; both read-only) —
every finding verified against the code or the schema before acting; all real ones fixed and pinned by a test and a
mutation:
- ⚠️⚠️ **a failure AFTER the commit** (the permission-cache flush, a log write) was reported as "Nothing was deleted —
  rolled back", written to the append-only ledger as `.failed`, and skipped the file removal — guests' ID scans left on
  disk with no record → nothing after the commit can throw; each step reports what it could not do; a refusal is a
  typed `OrganizationDeletionRefused`, and any other failure CHECKS whether the organisation still exists before
  claiming nothing was deleted;
- ⚠️⚠️ **races**: the people, the files and the refusal were read before the transaction with no lock → the
  organisation row is locked first, then the open payouts (a payout mid-transfer is waited for, then seen), then the
  people (someone accepting another organisation's invite waits, instead of being cascaded with their new membership);
  the lifecycle bounds (protected, suspended-first) are re-checked by the SERVICE under the lock;
- ⚠️ **a tenant with more than 65,535 guests could never be deleted** (every guest id was bound into one statement;
  🔬 reproduced by the reviewer: error 1390) → subqueries, and bounded chunks of 1,000;
- **the security-log cleanup** would also have erased a platform admin's own console sign-in history at the same address
  → narrowed to the tenant realm's attempts;
- **a KEPT person's notifications about this organisation** (guests' names) stayed in their feed → notifications now
  name their organisation (stamped on every new one), and a deletion removes the ones that name it or link to its
  records — never their others;
- **three columns name a person without a foreign key** (`audit_events.actor_id` and four more) → a former member
  named only there keeps their account; a drift test fails on a new such column not in the list;
- **files**: a failure was mostly not logged (the disks do not throw), a missing file counted as "removed", and a file
  two tenants share (seeded demo photos) would have been deleted from under the other → confirmed-gone per file, missing
  and shared counted apart, failures logged with their paths and written to the ledger; a guest ID upload whose rows do
  not land now removes its bytes;
- **the counts** under-reported (cascaded rows counted 0) → the result is the pre-deletion count the post-condition
  proves gone, the same the preview shows; Stripe ids (customers, subscriptions, connected accounts) are written to the
  ledger to close by hand;
- **refusals that can never clear said "try again in a few minutes"** → each names its source and age, and calls it
  stuck after 30 minutes; the announcement form could widen a targeted notice to every tenant after a failed submit →
  choices restored, the contradiction refused, the audience named in the notice; the result ledger row can no longer
  500 a completed deletion; a failed `.failed` write no longer replaces the original error;
- **the field script** now builds each control off the page and swaps it in last (an error leaves the plain select
  working), shows a required field's own message instead of the browser's bubble on a hidden element, chooses on click,
  mirrors `disabled`, and repaints after the back/forward cache.
**Not fixed, recorded** (`KNOWN-LIMITS` L19): an open Stripe Checkout page is invisible to the refusal — 🔬 DORMANT on
production (fake Stripe client, no key, placeholder prices — measured 2026-09-26), and a go-live prerequisite before the
Stripe flip; a replaced brand logo's old file is never deleted (pre-existing, so a deletion cannot find it); queued work
for a deleted organisation fails harmlessly or completes.

**PROOF (pre-deploy).** `Admin05DeleteOrganisationTest` 24 tests and `Admin05ConsoleFieldsTest` 4, plus the widened
one-permanent-path guard (all of `app/`), the meter's own-database pin and the ID-vault orphan test. Mutation set
`admin-05` **47/47** landed and caught; the full harness **234/234**. Full suite **3,992/3,992 on MySQL 8.4.10 AND on
MariaDB 11.8.9** (READ COMMITTED; ⚠️ MariaDB's test database was first brought up to date — eight migrations had not
reached it since the engine gate last ran, 2026-09-22), then **3,993/3,993** on MySQL with the L19 pin. PHPStan L5 0 ·
Pint clean · money gate **MONEY AS SEEDED · FULL** (`929 / 10928000 / 0 / 42 / 16 / 0`, row digests identical — tenant
one only, as the script says). Browser (Playwright, pages rendered through the app): every enhanced control at 1280 px
and 390 px — keyboard, click, search, no-match, the checklist, a required field's own message, the posted values; no
sideways scroll, no script errors.

**⚠️⚠️ FOUND AT THE DEPLOY PREFLIGHT — A TWO-MINUTE PAGE, VISIBLE ONLY ON PRODUCTION.** Before swapping, the staged
release (`rel_AD @ 9bbccc12`) was run read-only against production (MariaDB 11.8.9): the delete preview took

TIMES the new path on the real host is what caught it — keep doing it for anything that reads the schema.** The fix's own gates: suite **3,995/3,995** (MySQL 8.4.10) · the
delete tests on MariaDB 11.8.9 **81/81** · PHPStan L5 0 · Pint clean · its two new mutations and the two that ride the key
read **4/4** caught (`admin-05` is now 49).

✅ **LIVE on `rel_AE @ 1ede4c63` (2026-09-26, swap 6 ms).** 🔬 Preflight from the staged release, read-only against
production: the delete preview of a probe organisation **188 ms** (was 117,704), the refusal 42 ms, and the one-query
key read equal to the framework's answer for **all 266 foreign keys** on production's MariaDB (the framework's own read
took 124 s to compare). Public checks **12 PASS · 0 FAIL · 0 could not measure**. 🖥 The console's sign-in page, live,
carries the field system (no script error, no sideways scroll at 390 px). ⚠️ **NOT YET DONE — the signed-in live pass**

## 2026-09-27 — ADMIN 06 · what a deletion must never run over, what it must count, and what it leaves behind

**Why.** ADMIN 05's permanent delete "refused while money was moving", but with one known hole (B19). Production runs
test-mode Stripe only, so nothing was at risk. Once live keys go in, every gap between a deletion and money becomes a
real one. ⛔ **This must be live before any live Stripe key** (`STRIPE-PRODUCTION.md`, top).

### #0 — what ADMIN 05 built, read before changing it

**B19** was written in three places: `KNOWN-LIMITS` **L19**, `GO-LIVE-REQUIREMENTS` **B19**, and the pin
`Admin05DeleteOrganisationTest` › *L19 — starting a subscription checkout writes NOTHING*. **PW-SIGNUP PROBE has not been
deleted.** The before-measurements exist (27 September: backup, per-organisation counts and fingerprints, the preview).
No after-count was taken, because there has been no deletion, and none is reconstructed here.

**Every refusal the deletion had BEFORE this pass** (A = `Admin05DeleteOrganisationTest`):

| Condition | Where checked | Test | Mutation |
|---|---|---|---|
| a protected organisation | console `destroy()` + service `delete()` | A › *the protected organisations can never be deleted…* · *the SERVICE holds its own bounds…* | A05-M17 · A05-M33 |
| not suspended or archived | console + service | A › *refuses — and deletes NOTHING — without every confirmation…* · *SERVICE holds its own bounds* | A05-M19 · A05-M34 |
| password · typed name · acknowledgement | console | A › *without every confirmation* | A05-M20 · M18 · M21 |
| a written reason *(row added by review 2, D-R2-13: the table left it out)* | console (`AdminReason::from`); `PlatformQuery::mutate()` also refuses an empty one | A › *without every confirmation* | ⚠️ none before · now **A06-M77** |
| only an Owner (`tenants.delete`) | route | A › *protected organisations can never be deleted, and only an Owner…* | A05-M24 · M25 |
| live Stripe billing | service `refusal()`, read by console first and service again | A › *refuses while money is moving at a third party* | A05-M1 · M3 · M22 |
| another organisation's rows point in | service | A › *records point into this one* | A05-M2 |
| a card payment or hold open | service | ⚠️ **none** | ⚠️ **none** |
| a payout in transit | service | ⚠️ **none** (the test named it, but only planted a subscription) | ⚠️ **none** |
| a payout run in progress | service | ⚠️ **none** | ⚠️ **none** |
| a webhook being processed | service | A › *a refusal says whether to wait or to act* (wording only) | ⚠️ **none** |
| a schema read that misses a table every schema has | service | ⚠️ **none** | ⚠️ **none** |
| already deleted | service | ⚠️ **none** | ⚠️ **none** |
| a surviving row (post-condition, rolls back) | service | A › *survives the sweep* | A05-M6 |

Six refusals had no test, or no mutation behind their test. **Every one now has both** (below).

### #1 — every Stripe object an organisation can own, and whether a deletion could run over it

| Object | Recorded here | Could a deletion run while it was live or pending? | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer | `subscriptions.stripe_customer_id` | yes, and it still does: a customer alone charges nothing | reported in the deletion record, to close by hand · ❓ ruling (a) |
| Subscription | `subscriptions` | refused only in 4 named states | refused in **any state but cancelled** |
| Saved card | **not stored** (hosted Checkout, SAQ A; `card_token` is a gateway token on a payment row) | — | — |
| **Checkout Session (B19)** | ⚠️ **was not recorded** | **yes, invisible** | **recorded** (`stripe_checkout_sessions`); refused while open |
| Payment | `payments` | refused while pending/authorised | same, plus test + mutation |
| Card hold | `payment_authorizations` | refused | same, plus test + mutation (the authorisation alone refuses) |
| Refund | `payments` (type refund) | refused, but as "a card payment" | refused **as a refund**, with a test |
| Dispute | ⚠️ **was not recorded at all** (the event was answered `202 ignored`) | **yes, invisible** | **recorded per Stripe dispute id** (`payment_disputes`), ordered by the event's own time; refused while any is open |
| Invoice (subscription) | not stored; Stripe holds it (the app sees `invoice.paid` events, pruned after 90 days) | covered only by the subscription | covered by the subscription + the #2 hold |
| Connect account | `organizations`/`owners`/`payouts`/`payments` account ids | yes: an account alone moves nothing | reported, to close by hand · ❓ ruling (a) |
| Payout | `payouts` | refused only while `processing` | refused while **processing, pending or held** (and `held` joins the lock) |
| Transfer | `payouts.external_ref` | covered by `processing` | same |

**Late webhooks.** Every event either endpoint could not place used to be answered `202 ignored` with no trace. That
covered a dispute or refund for a payment that is gone, a transfer to a payout that is gone, and an account no owner
holds. Now each one is **recorded** in `webhook_events` with its reason and answered **202**, never dropped. The status
is `failed` where the event shows it was ours (it names one of our organisations, or it is a dispute) and `ignored`
where it names none (a subscription invoice's PaymentIntent, an operator account's update), so the daily
reconciliation stays a list of real problems. Unsigned events still get a 400. Tested on both endpoints with signed
events, after a real deletion. ⚠️ **A narrow window remains:** an event arriving *while* the deletion commits can hit the
`webhook_events` foreign key once and get a 500. Stripe's retry then finds the payment gone and records it with a 202.

**B19: why record rather than refuse for 24 hours.** The app creates every Checkout Session itself, and Stripe returns
the session's own `expires_at` and `livemode` at creation. So the refusal can be exact: it lifts the moment the page is
paid or expires, not a blanket day later. 📖 Stripe's docs (read 2026-09-27): a session expires 30 minutes to 24 hours
after creation, 24 by default. A session with no reported expiry counts as open for the full 24.

### #2 — ⚠️⚠️ A HOLD PENDING HIS LAWYER, NOT A POLICY

Until the lawyer rules on how long, and where, money records must be kept, **a deletion refuses any organisation with
LIVE-mode money records**: a card payment, a refund, a payout, or live Stripe billing (whose invoices Stripe holds).
**Test-mode records never block.** Non-Stripe records (`livemode` null) don't block either; see ruling (b). Whether a
record is live comes from **Stripe's own `livemode`**, now stored when the record is written: from the object Stripe
returned, or from the signed event that settled it. ⚠️ **Stripe's Refund object carries no `livemode`** (the SDK
declares none), so a refund takes the mode of the payment it refunds. Found by PHPStan while this was built.
**Existing rows:** 🔬 production held **no** Stripe money record of any kind when measured: no payment, authorisation,
payout, webhook event or invoice, no Stripe subscription or customer id, no Connect account; 15 subscriptions, all
trialing with no Stripe id. So no existing row's mode needs proving, and the hold blocks nothing today. **He removes
this hold when the ruling comes.** It is one method, `OrganizationDeletion::liveMoneyRecords()`.

### #3 / #3b — files, and a preview that counts what actually goes

**Files.** Read first: every file the app stores is named by a `media` row, except an avatar (`users.avatar_path`) and
a brand logo (`properties.brand_logo_path`). ADMIN 05's deletion removes all three after the commit, and names a file
it could not remove. 🔬 **Proved locally** on a disposable organisation with a photo, a private upload, a brand logo
and the founder's avatar on the real disks: the preview said 4 files, the deletion removed 4, and **0 were left**.
**Replaced logos** are now removed once the new one is saved, never one another property still shows. 🔬 **Production
held 0 brand logos** (none referenced, none on disk), so there was nothing to quarantine.

**The preview.** 🔬 For PW-SIGNUP PROBE it said **17 records in 5 tables**; the deletion removes **232**. It counted only
tables with an organisation column. Now the preview and the deletion share **one plan**
(`OrganizationDeletion::plan()`), which counts every row: the organisation's own, the rows a foreign key cascades away
(its roles' permissions, an account's Google/X sign-ins), the rows removed through a parent, and the accounts that
belong nowhere else, with theirs. The screen shows it grouped in plain words, with every table listed. **The test that
keeps it honest** measures every table in the database before and after a real deletion. For a fresh signup, and for
an organisation with bookings, guests, staff and every indirect link, the preview equals what went, **table for
table**. Mutations that drop any one table, a whole group, or the cascades are caught. ⚠️ The plan follows **one**
level of cascade. That is exact while no cascaded row is itself the parent of a cascade, which is true of today's
schema. A deeper chain **refuses** rather than confirm a number it cannot count. 🔬 The delete rules live in
`REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS`, which is read **once**, never per table (the 118-second lesson).

### #4 — the three tests MySQL ran and MariaDB didn't

They were ADMIN 05's last three: the L19 pin, the one-query key read held equal to the framework's, and the
no-per-table-read pin. They were **added after** the full MariaDB run (3,992), and passed on MariaDB in the targeted
delete run (81/81). **No test in the suite skips by engine.** 🔬 The only skips are machine-dependent (the session-memory
index) or route-dependent. This pass runs the full suite on both engines.

### #5 — where a sign-in link goes

The founder's set-password link is **emailed only** (`OwnerInviteMail`). The console notice says it was "handed to the
mailer" and never shows it. It is stored only as a sha256 hash, is single-use, and lasts **7 days**. Creation is
**refused while mail is discarded** (`log`/`array`), so a link was never written to a log. 🔬 Production's logs,
measured 2026-09-27: **no mail body and no link in any file.** The only 5 "/invite/" lines are refusals of
`/app/owners/invite/preview`. **0 links are still valid.** ⚠️ **Fixed:** the link stayed valid for 7 days even after
the founder set a password another way (a reset), and redeeming it would have **overwritten** that password. Now it is
refused, both on the page and under a lock in the service. Test + two mutations.

### #6 — the three laptop-only check files

`ops/exposure-battery.sh`, `ops/htaccess-drift-check.sh` and `ops/reference/public_html.htaccess`. They existed on the
server only as **hand copies from 2026-09-21**, older than git. `release.sh stage` ships only what changed between two
commits, and these had not changed since the release layout was built from that hand-copied tree, so no deploy ever
corrected them. 🔬 Measured: **4 of 1,395** deployable files on `rel_AE` differed from git at its own commit: these three,
plus `ops/ps-check.sh`, which never shipped. **Fixed in `release.sh stage`:** every deployable file on the live release is
checked against git at the live commit (sha256), and each one that differs or is missing ships from git. The server's
copies now come from git, through the deploy.

### 🔍 The adversarial review (9 agents; 16 findings, the 6 most severe verified, every one read)

**Fixed:**
- **Disputes were last-event-wins on one column per payment.** A late redelivery of an older "open" event re-opened a
  finished dispute, and the deletion then refused forever. One dispute closing hid another still open on the same
  payment. 📖 Stripe (read 2026-09-27): a payment can carry more than one dispute; `lost` can later become `won`; events
  are not delivered in order. Now there is one row per dispute (`payment_disputes`), and an event older than the last
  one applied changes nothing.
- **Recording every unplaced event as `failed`** would have turned the reconciliation red with routine events that are
  not ours. It is now `failed` or `ignored`, as above.
- 🔬 **Pre-existing, found by the new reclaim test:** an event first recorded unresolved (no organisation) and delivered
  again once it could be placed met the unique index on a row its tenant scope could not see. Every retry got a 500, and
  the event was never applied. `once()` now adopts that row for the organisation placing it.
- **A test-mode event before go-live could pin a reused subscription row to test mode**, hiding live billing from the #2
  hold. Now live wins.
- **The count's premise missed two shapes:** a table the plan clears directly as a cascade parent, and one row reachable
  by two cascades. Both now refuse; neither exists in today's schema.
- **The founder-link lock held nothing under READ COMMITTED** (a `FOR UPDATE` whose WHERE tests the password releases a
  non-matching row). The row is now locked by its key and the password read after.
- **A logo save that failed after the property row named the new logo deleted that logo.** It now stays.
- **`release.sh` would have refused a drifted file renamed since the live commit.** It is now shipped only where it still
  exists.
- **The runbook never subscribed the endpoints to the dispute and checkout events**, so none of this would have received
  anything. The event lists are fixed.

**Recorded, not built:** 📖 **L20 / GO-LIVE B20** — a guest's card payment page cannot open with real Stripe under the
SDK's pinned API version. This is pre-existing and was read, not run.

### ❓ For his ruling — written down, not guessed

- **(a)** Should an existing Stripe **customer** or **Connect account**, with no money moving, refuse a deletion? Today
  they are listed in the deletion record, to close by hand.
- **(b)** The hotel's own **tax invoices** (`invoices`) and **cash or bank payments** are not Stripe records and carry no
  `livemode`, so the #2 hold does not cover them. Should it?
- **(c)** A **failed** payout with no retry means an owner is still owed money, but it is not "pending", so a deletion
  does not refuse on it.
- **(d)** A **staff invite** to an existing account that is not active (invited or deactivated) sets that account's
  password on acceptance. This is pre-existing and is the re-invite design; an active account is refused.
- **(e)** After a subscription is **cancelled**, an **open Stripe invoice** can remain at Stripe. It is not recorded here.
- **(f)** Removing a **replaced logo** (as briefed) breaks the logo image in guest emails **already sent** with the old
  one, once a mail client's image cache lapses. Keep old logos for email history instead?
- **(g)** *(added 2026-09-29, review 3)* A **test-mode** Checkout page's `checkout.session.expired`, arriving after its
  organisation was deleted, is recorded `failed` (its metadata names the organisation): one red reconciliation row for a
  page that moved no money. Should it be `ignored`? (A live page cannot reach this state: the deletion waits for Stripe's report.)

## 2026-09-29 — Remove a property from the Portfolio (the founder's request; design approved the same day)

**Asked:** "on /app/portfolio there must be an option to delete property … works fine … very cool design."
**Ruled by him, the same day (two questions):** *what delete means* → **safe removal**: the certified archive-not-destroy
removal (task #98) — bookings, invoices and payments always kept — gone **right away** when nobody is staying and nothing
is booked ahead, otherwise open until the last checkout and cancellable until then. *The design* → approved as written.

**What was built.**
- **On each Portfolio card** (only for `properties.manage`): a quiet remove control beside Edit, opening a confirmation
  rendered from the SAME read the action acts on (`PropertyRemovalService::outlook()`), so the screen can never promise
  "right away" while the action schedules. It shows the path — *Today → Stays open until the last checkout on X →
  removed* — or the single step *Removed as soon as you confirm*; what is **kept** (bookings, guest history, invoices,
  payments, statements) and what **goes** (its storefront page, its channel connections, the card — no restore); and the
  property's name typed to confirm (checked as typed, and again on the server). A property that is **leaving** shows a
  warm-grey hatched band, "Leaving 8 Oct", the date and **Keep this property**. Its only property explains itself and
  offers **Add a property**.
- **Routes:** `POST /app/portfolio/{property}/remove` and `/keep` — `can:properties.manage`, the property resolved only
  inside the person's access (the `property_user` allow-list, #38; outside it is a 404), refused in a read-only
  workspace, audited by the service.
- **In the service** (so Settings holds them too): **the last remaining property cannot be removed**
  (`isLastRemaining()` — one already leaving does not count), and **`removeIfClear()`** archives at once only when no
  guest is checked in, whatever their dates, and no stay ends today or later.
- ⚠️⚠️ **A GAP IN THE NIGHTLY RULE, FOUND WRITING THE COPY AND CLOSED:** `effectiveDateFor()` saw only stays whose
  checkout is today or later, so a guest **still checked in past their checkout date** was invisible, and the nightly
  pass archived the property from under them — what F-57's ruling ("no guest is archived over") forbids. Now a checked-in
  guest holds it open until tomorrow, re-asked each night. The one definition moved, not a second one (F-57's own rule).
- **Also fixed on the same page:** the Portfolio printed every notice twice.

**Rulings touched, said plainly.**
- ⚠️ **F-58 (2026-09-19): "a pending removal visible on its own Settings page is enough — no portfolio-wide list".**
  Removal now starts from the Portfolio, and the approved design shows a leaving property's state on its card. Read as
  updated by his approval of 2026-09-29 for this surface; the F-58 pin (Settings still shows the date and the cancel)
  stays green. If he wants the card silent, it is one block in the view.
- **F-57** is extended in the direction it ruled (checked-in guests), never reversed.
- **Fixtures, not rules:** two existing tests removed an organisation's ONLY property; each now gives the organisation a
  second one (`secondProperty()`), because the service refuses the last one by design.

**Found by the suite's guards, not by the author:** the dialogs' ids were built from `$loop->index`, and the `>` inside
`->` cut every tag short for the accessible-name census and the dialog-focus contract (they read to the first `>`); a
bare
`1fr 1fr` grid; and — before any test ran — a `run@if` glued to a word (the Blade trap in `CLAUDE.md`), now guarded by
`assertNoRawBlade()` in every rendered state and proved by mutation PR-M14.

**Not done, recorded:** the property Edit action on the same page resolves the property through the tenant scope only,
not the person's property allow-list (#38) — a staff member scoped to some properties could edit another by id. Outside
this request; his call.

## 2026-09-29 — Portfolio: "Open" goes into the property · the Add/Edit dialogs' fields (the founder's report; design approved)

**Reported:** "when we click on Open nothing is working" · the Add and Edit dialogs' dropdowns "look very pathetic, very
basic — should be cool, modern and minimal".

**Open — root cause, reproduced in a browser before any change.** The card's Open posted to the top-bar property switcher,
which stores the choice and redirects BACK — so the Portfolio reloaded at the same scroll position, with no message, and
only the small "Working here" tag moved (🖥 measured: same URL, `scrollY` 0, no notice). The switch worked; nothing showed
it. **Fix:** the switcher accepts one optional destination from a FIXED list (`open=dashboard` → `app.dashboard`, never a
URL — an arbitrary destination would be an open redirect); the card's Open asks for it and lands on the property's
Dashboard with "You're now working in X.". The top-bar switcher sends none and still keeps you where you are.

**The fields.** Type → three choice tiles with an icon each (Hotel · Villas & apartments · Guesthouse / lodge); Status
(Edit) → an Active | Inactive toggle; Time zone → a searchable dropdown over all ~420 zones, each with its offset now
(`App\Support\Time\TimezoneOptions`), filtering by name or offset ("baku", "utc+4"), ↑/↓, Enter, Esc, Tab. Two small
operator components, `components/operator/choices` and `components/operator/combobox`, on the console field system's
contract (ADMIN 05): PROGRESSIVE — the real radios and the real `<select>` stay in the form, so the posted fields,
validation and every existing test are unchanged. The list opens in the flow under its field (not floating), so the
dialog's focus trap and its scrolling keep working; Esc closes the list first and the dialog only when the list is shut.

**Found on the way, by the guards and the browser, not by reading:** a `<x-…>` component tag written inside a CSS COMMENT
in the layout is compiled by Blade even there — every page 500'd until it was reworded (and the comment now says so); the
shared `.vy-input` later in the sheet reset the combobox's right padding, so its chevron overlapped the offset; "Guesthouse"
overflowed its tile at 390 px.

**Proof.** `PortfolioOpenAndFieldsTest` (5, each written to fail first where it could) · mutation set `portfolio-fields`
5/5 · 🖥 walked in a real browser: Open → the Dashboard with its notice; Add with the Hotel tile and "utc+4" → saved
`hotel` / `Asia/Baku` (read back from the database); Edit opened on the property's own values and saved `villa` /
`inactive`; Esc and Enter behave; no sideways scroll and no overflowing tile at 390 px; 0 console errors.
**The keyboard guard's reasoned exemption.** `KeyboardReachabilityContractTest` flagged the list's options (a click on an
`<li>`). It is the ARIA listbox pattern — options are not tab stops; the search box drives them (↑/↓, Enter, Esc) and
points at the active one with `aria-activedescendant` — so an allow-list entry was added WITH ITS BACKING STRING (the
Enter handler); mutation PF-M6 removes that handler and the guard goes red again. The exemption cannot outlive the
keyboard path it describes.

## 2026-09-29 — Guests: the page rebuilt — centred dialogs, a sortable table, row Edit and Erase (the founder's report; design approved)

**Reported:** "the Add guest modal is not in the centre — the Edit modal should be too", "the design of this page … is so
messed", "the data table should be so advanced, so good", "the filter should be very smooth and minimal and modern", and
"we should have an option to edit and delete the guest as well".

**The dialogs — root cause, measured before any change.** Every dialog on the page (Message, Add tag, Erase, Add guest) and
the profile's Edit centred itself with an INLINE `display: flex` beside `x-show`. Alpine's `x-show` hides by writing
`display: none` and shows by REMOVING the inline display, so the first hide erased the flex and each dialog came back as
`display: block` in the top-left corner (🖥 the Add guest panel's centre sat at 260,242 in a 1280×900 window; its backdrop
computed `block`). All now centre with the shared `.vy-modal-backdrop`, whose display lives in a class. 🖥 After: every
dialog on both pages centres at 640,450. **The same pattern sits on 45 elements in other screens** (rates, units, security,
owner pages…); `XShowInlineDisplayContractTest` holds the Guests pages at zero and the rest at a ceiling of 45 so it can
only fall. That sweep is its own pass, asked for separately.

**The page.** One toolbar: search that follows the typing (placeholder now honest — *name, city or exact email*; the
encryption note is behind an ⓘ), All · In-house · Upcoming · VIP with live counts, Select, Add guest. The table sorts by
**Guest** (surname, first name), **Stays** (most first) and **Last stay** (latest first), each through an allow-list
(`GuestsList::SORTS`; a `?sort=` outside it falls back to the name, so the URL can never order people by a column the page
does not show). **Lifetime is not sortable**: it is per currency, and ranking EUR against USD would invent a rate (#17).
**Last stay sorts by the date the column SHOWS**, computed in SQL exactly as the PHP computes the cell (in house → today;
otherwise the latest non-cancelled booking's arrival if ahead, its departure if not; never-stayed last in both directions)
— sorting by check-in alone would put a long stay that ended last before a short one that ended sooner. Pages of 25, 50 or
100 (anything else → 25); a real footer ("1–25 of 312 guests · A–Z by surname") OUTSIDE the table — the old pager sat inside
`<tbody>`. Every link keeps every other setting. The header stays in view while scrolling (desktop).

**Smooth, and still #20.** Every control is an ordinary GET link or form that works with no script. The page's script only
fetches the SAME URL and swaps the two marked regions (filters, results) in place, pushing the URL to history (Back works),
so every change still runs every middleware. Anything unexpected — an error, a redirect elsewhere, a missing region — falls
back to loading the page normally.

**Edit and Erase on every row** (a ⋯ menu: Open profile · Edit details · Erase personal data). Edit is shown only with
`guests.manage`, Erase only with `guests.erase` (Property Owner / Group Admin), the same permissions the routes require
(#30, "never invite a 403"). Both come back to the list the operator was on — the way back is REBUILT from the list's own
allow-listed settings (`GuestsList::returnUrl()`), never taken from the request as a URL, so it cannot be an open redirect.
Erase is the certified `Guest::anonymize()` with ERASE typed and checked on the server (never a delete — #28); its dialog
says what goes and what is kept, from one shared partial used by the bulk Erase too. An edit the server refuses reopens with
what was typed and says why inside the dialog.

**Found on the way, before shipping:**
- ⚠️ **An Edit from the list would have wiped the guest's stay preferences.** The profile update reads "no preferences in
  the request" as "none ticked" (right for the profile, whose form carries every chip). The list's Edit does not show them,
  so it sends `keep_preferences=1` and the server leaves them untouched — proven both ways by a test (GL-M11, GL-M22).
- ⚠️ **The old footer called every filter but VIP "flagged at risk"** — In-house and Upcoming included. Gone with the footer.
- ⚠️ **A test was passing on the wrong element.** `UnwiredControlsTest` asserted the manager sees "Add guest" through
  `Livewire::test()`, which skips the middleware that sets the permission team — so `@can` answered a silent false (the #30
  note) and the button never rendered; the assertion matched the Add guest DIALOG's heading, which was not gated. 🔬 A probe
  confirmed team=NULL → `can()`=false. The test now renders through the real route and looks for the button itself.
