## 2026-09-29 — Maintenance: the board rebuilt like Guests — centred dialogs, a drawer on the right, a sortable table, row Edit and Cancel (the founder's request; design approved)

**Asked:** "https://vyrobel.com/app/maintenance — now work the same sort of things on the same page" (the Guests rebuild
the same day), then "Yess go ahead" to the design.

**The dialogs and the drawer — the same root cause as Guests, measured.** New work order, Assign and the detail drawer
each placed themselves with an INLINE display beside `x-show`, which Alpine erases on the first hide: 🖥 New work order at
260,330 in 1280×900, and the drawer on the LEFT (x 0–440) although it was drawn to sit on the right. All now use the shared
`.vy-modal-backdrop`; the drawer is a dialog whose backdrop carries `.vy-drawer-backdrop` (aligned to the end, full
height). 🖥 After: every dialog centres at 720,450 in 1440×900 (New work order measured on three openings in a row, the
work order page's two on two each, the rest once); the drawer sits at x 980–1440, full height, on each of two openings. The work order page's **Reassign** and **Mark resolved** had the same inline display and no
Escape, no role and no name (the keyboard guard's allow-list recorded them "REPORTED, not fixed"): both are now real
dialogs — centred, named, Escape and a click outside close them — posting exactly what they posted before (the pinned
`parts` / `time_spent` fields did not move).

**The page.** The five figures stay as figures (Active · Urgent · Awaiting parts · Out of order · Resolved in 7 days).
One toolbar: search that follows the typing (issue, unit, category, technician), Costs report and Settings (now gated like
their routes — both are `maintenance.manage`; the old toolbar offered them to every role, a 403), Select, New work order,
and the filters as chips with the REAL count of what clicking each shows, inside the current search: All · Active · Not
started · In progress · Urgent · Awaiting parts · Out of order · Resolved. The bare status dropdown is gone. A table:
work order (with its out-of-order and awaiting-parts marks and category), unit, priority, status, technician, time to
target, reported. It sorts by **priority** (the order the board always had: urgent first, ties newest first), **time to
target** (by the very deadline `MaintenanceSla` computes for the column; a closed one, with no target, goes last both
ways), **reported** and **unit** (A–Z, natural) — through an allow-list in `App\Support\Maintenance\MaintenanceListParams`,
like Guests. Pages of 25, 50 or 100; a real footer outside the table that says what the board holds — "open, and resolved
in the last 7 days" (the old line said "from the last 7 days" while listing open work of any age). Every link keeps every
other setting; the same in-place updates as Guests, from ONE shared script (`partials/operator-list-script`, which the
Guests page now uses too, so the two cannot drift).

**Row actions (a ⋯ menu).** Open details (the drawer) · Open full record · Edit details · Assign / Change technician ·
Start work · Mark resolved · Cancel work order — each only where the ticket's state and the viewer allow it: nothing that
writes on a closed ticket (the old board offered **Assign on a resolved one**, which the service refuses), nothing that
writes for a role without `maintenance.manage` or while the workspace is read-only; those see the two Open items. Select
keeps Export, Assign and Resolve for the selection; bulk Resolve now says in a dialog what it does (no cost recorded; each
unit back on sale unless another open work order holds it) instead of a browser `confirm()`.
- **Edit is new** (`MaintenanceService::updateDetails`, route `app.maintenance.update`, `can:maintenance.manage`): title,
  description, category and priority, ONLY while the work is open or in progress — a resolved work order's title is already
  on the owner's expense line, and a cancelled one is history. Not the unit, not out-of-order: those move a room's
  availability and keep their own paths. The audit and the event name the fields that changed and record the category and
  priority values; the title and description are free text and are never copied. The edit and both records land in one
  transaction. **Edit checks the property allow-list (#38)** — a manager scoped to one property gets a 404 on another's.
- **"Delete" is Cancel**, the honest one: the work order is kept, as cancelled, with its history; no cost is recorded; the
  room goes back on sale unless another open work order still holds it. The dialog says exactly that.
- Every action started from the board comes back to the board as it was — the way back is REBUILT from the board's own
  allow-listed settings (`MaintenanceListParams::returnUrl()`), never taken from the request as a URL.
- An edit the server refuses reopens with what was typed, and says why inside the dialog.
- **New work order** gets the Portfolio's searchable picker for the unit, the category as five tiles, the priority as a
  segmented choice, and the out-of-order switch with its "check the rack" warning. It still starts on the first unit, as
  the old dropdown did.

**Found on the way, before shipping:**
- ⚠️ **A width breakpoint clipped the table.** The shared sticky-header rule turned sideways scrolling off above 1100 px; this
  table is wider than the Guests one, so at 1180 px its last two columns — Reported and the ⋯ menu — were cut off and
  unreachable (🖥 995 px of table in an 877 px card, the card clipping). Now sideways scrolling is the default everywhere,
  and the list script marks the frame `is-roomy` only when the table MEASURES as fitting; only then does the header stick
  (🖥 1180 px: scrolls, ⋯ reachable; 1440 px: sticky, holds at the top after 700 px of scrolling). The Guests page uses the
  same rule now.
- ⚠️ **Alpine's string `:style` erased the work order page's controls.** A `:style` given as a STRING replaces the whole
  style attribute (an object merges into it). 🖥 The "Notify the front desk" switch rendered 16×6 px (its style read back as
  the bound background alone); the Reassign dialog's people lost their row layout; the update composer's Note / Progress /
  Part ordered tabs and its Post update button lost their padding. All 14 sites on that page are now objects with the same
  values; a new guard (`AlpineStyleBindingContractTest`) holds both Maintenance pages at zero and the **10 other sites**
  (schedule, notification preferences, owner units and reports, housekeeping, maintenance settings, email previews) at a
  ceiling. Not fixed there: its own pass, asked for.
- The Mark resolved dialog's Parts cost field stuck out past the dialog's edge once the panel was the shared card (the
  panel's padding plus the form's own) — the form no longer pads itself, and the cost row's columns can shrink.
- Category labels broke mid-word in five tiles ("Plumbin|g"), and on a phone the dialogs' two paddings left 250 px of a
  350 px dialog (the priority read "Norm|al") — tiles centre their label and never split a word; on a phone the board's
  dialogs pad themselves once.
- ⚠️ **Found by the independent review of the diff (one finding at its bar):** the board's Mark resolved never sent
  `notify`, and the controller reads a missing key as "do not notify" — so a work order resolved from the board never told
  whoever reported it, silently, while the same action on the work order page does by default (the old board's inline form
  never sent it either). The dialog now carries the same "Notify the front desk" switch, on unless turned off, where
  someone reported the work order; bulk Resolve says plainly that nobody is notified. 🖥 Walked: switch on by default,
  `notify=1` posted, the feed notification stored.
- "1 units blocked" → "1 unit blocked". A phone toolbar button wrapped; the fifth figure sat alone in half a row; a link
  and a button in the toolbar stood 38.8 / 35.5 px — each measured, each fixed.

**Not changed, reported:** creating a work order (`store`) resolves the unit through the tenant scope only, not the
person's property allow-list — the same shape as D-EDIT-SCOPE on the Portfolio (DEC-i); Edit here does check it, and
every other maintenance write and the work order page itself resolve the ticket by the tenant scope only, as before
(D-MT-STORE, DEC-j). The
older flash lines still say "Ticket …" where the page now says "work order".

**Divergence from the #89 exact match** (`docs/design/DIVERGENCE-REGISTER.md`): the wireframe's list had no sorting, no page
sizes, no row menu, no Edit or Cancel, and KPI tiles that filtered; the founder asked for the Guests treatment, so the
board is now a deliberate divergence.

**Proof.** `MaintenanceBoardRedesignTest` (18) and `AlpineStyleBindingContractTest` (3), written to fail first where they
could (the redesign test was RED — 11 failures and 6 errors — before any view or component code); the x-show guard now
holds both Maintenance pages at zero (ceiling 45 → 39); `KeyboardReachabilityContractTest` lost three allow-list entries
whose shapes are gone and states the checkbox/title separation for the table; `MaintenanceBoardViewTest` pins "1 unit
blocked"; mutation set `maintenance-board` (26; MB-M3 first flipped one side of the sorting comparator, which leaves an
inconsistent comparator that proves nothing — it stayed green; flipped on both sides it is caught). 🖥 Walked in a browser on tenant three (desktop 1440 and 1180, phone 390):
created a work order from a filtered, sorted view and came back to it; edited it (the audit names `title`, `priority`,
never the text); assigned, started from the drawer, resolved without a cost, and cancelled an out-of-order one (the room
stayed off sale — another open work order holds it, as the dialog said); bulk-assigned two and undid it; search, chips,
sorting, Back; Escape and focus back to the opener; 0 console errors. The Guests page re-walked on the shared script.

## 2026-09-30 — Units: the page rebuilt like Guests and Maintenance — aligned add dialogs, a sortable table, Pause / Resume, room types as cards (the founder's request; plan approved)

**Asked:** "https://vyrobel.com/app/units — on this page in Add inventory sector, text and label is mess, `Kind` word is down
and its dropdown is small. And `Add room type` word is also down. All these text and boxes must be well aligned. Fix it. …
do the similar sort of advanced work … the same work which you have done with the previous two pages." An 8-part plan was
put to him; he answered "Yes, all of it".

**Why the form was misaligned — measured, four causes.** (1) The labels used `.vy-label` and the edit dialog's fields
`.vy-inp`; no stylesheet defines either class, so the labels rendered as 16 px body text and the edit boxes unstyled. (2)
Each field carried a 15 px bottom margin, so a button placed beside a field sat 15 px lower than it (🖥 718 vs 703 in
1440×900) — "Add room type is also down". (3) Kind was a native dropdown whose height the browser decides (🖥 43 px beside
41 px boxes in Chrome; Safari draws it differently again) — "its dropdown is small". (4) The two forms shared one card with
different column counts, so nothing lined up across them.

**The add forms.** Add room type and Add unit are toolbar buttons that open centred dialogs (the shared
`.vy-modal-backdrop`; 🖥 centred at 720,450 in 1440×900): styled labels, one box height, paired fields sharing a top edge, and
the buttons in the dialog's footer. Kind is four tiles (Room · Apartment · Villa · Dorm). Add unit chooses its room type
through the Portfolio's searchable picker, which shows each type's kind and how many it sleeps; the sleeps field suggests that
figure. Each room type card has its own Add unit button, which opens the dialog with that type chosen. A refused add
reopens its dialog with what was typed and says why inside it.

**A setup guide instead of the bottom card.** While a property has no room type or no unit, the page shows three numbered
steps — add a room type, add a unit, give it prices (a link to Rates) — the done ones ticked. It steps aside once both exist.
A role that cannot add sees the steps and a line saying which permission it needs.

**The page.** Five figures: Units · Bookable (active and in service — the same test `AvailabilityService` applies) · Paused ·
To clean · Out of order. One toolbar: search as you type (unit code, name, room type, kind, owner), Export, Select, Add room
type, Add unit. Chips with the real count of what clicking each shows, inside the current search: All · Bookable · Paused ·
To clean · Out of order. The table sorts by **unit** (natural order: A2 before A10), **room type** and **sleeps**, through an
allow-list (`App\Support\Unit\UnitListParams`, like Guests and Maintenance); ties fall back to the unit and then the id, so a
row can never appear on two pages. Pages of 25, 50 or 100 and a footer outside the table. Every link keeps every other
setting, and the shared list script changes the view in place. **"Export · Soon" and "Filters · Soon" are gone**: the filters
are the chips, and Export is real — a CSV of the current view (`GET /app/units-export`, `can:units.view`) or of a selection
(POST), audited `unit.exported` with the count. Its columns are what the table shows; **it never carries a door code, wifi
password or arrival note** — the rows the page's script reads carry only whether each exists.

**Row actions (a ⋯ menu).** Edit unit · Price individually (the shared per-unit price form, unchanged) · Arrival info · See
its work orders (the Maintenance board searched for the unit's code) · Pause / Resume. Each item appears only where its
route would allow it: edit and pause need `units.manage`, pricing needs `rates.manage`, and neither is offered while the
workspace is paused (the routes refuse it). Arrival info keeps its own rules, as before: offered to `units.manage` even in a
paused workspace, because its route has no pause guard. Every action started from the list comes back to the list as it was
— the address REBUILT from the list's allow-listed settings (`UnitListParams::returnUrl()`), never taken from the request.

**Pause / Resume.** "Take out of service" / "Return to service" are now **Pause** / **Resume**, with a Paused tag on the row —
the owner portal's words for the same switch (`OwnerUnitStatusService`), and no longer the name of the maintenance
condition in the next column ("Out of service"). The dialog says what it does: bookings already taken are kept, nothing is
deleted, it is recorded. **Bulk:** Select mode can export the selection, or pause or resume several units — through the
same service as the single action (`OwnerUnitStatusService::setManyByOperator()`): the same write and the same audit row
for each unit, each affected room type's availability recomputed ONCE after all its units have moved, and the whole
selection in one transaction — all or nothing. Only units in the person's properties; units already in the asked-for state
are counted and left alone: "Resumed 3 units · 1 already taking bookings." New route `app.inventory.units.bulk-active`,
`can:units.manage`, refused in a paused workspace.

**Room types as cards:** cover photo, kind, how many it sleeps, "N units · M bookable", Add unit, and the photo strip with
its existing controls (cover, reorder, remove, add).

**Found on the way, before shipping:**
- ⚠️ **A duplicate unit code on Add was a 500.** `units` is unique on (property, code); Edit had a validation rule for it and
  Add did not, so the database was the only check (🔬 the test was RED with a 500 first). Add now refuses it with a sentence,
  scoped to the room type's property, and reopens the dialog with what was typed.
- An empty sub-line under each unit code kept its height (CSS `:empty` cannot match an element holding Livewire's block
  markers and the whitespace around them) and pushed the code off centre; the line now renders only when it has content.
- ⚠️ **Found by the independent review of the diff (one finding at its bar):** the first bulk Pause/Resume called the single
  action once per unit, and each call recomputes the unit's WHOLE room type for a year of nights — 🔬 ~0.5 s and 1,098
  queries each, measured locally on tenant three. A page of 100 selected units meant ~100 identical recomputes (~50 s here,
  slower on the shared host) with nothing around the loop, so a request cut off part-way would have left some units paused
  and no notice saying which. Now the service writes and audits every unit, recomputes each affected room type once, in
  one transaction; a new test counts the recomputes (one per room type) and proves a failure changes nothing — no unit, no
  audit row. 🖥 Walked after the fix: three units across two room types paused and resumed from Select mode, one audit row
  per unit per action, tonight's availability equal to the units on sale in both room types.
- The setup guide told anyone who could not add to "ask an administrator" for the "manage units" permission — including a
  manager in a paused workspace, who holds it. The line now shows only when the permission is what is missing; a paused
  workspace has the shell's own "Workspace paused" banner.
- The shared list script now focuses the first menu item that is showing, not the first in the page's markup — a change made
  on reading the code (a hidden item cannot take focus), not after a measured failure. 🖥 Checked after it: focus lands on
  the first visible item on the Units, Guests and Maintenance menus, and returns to the ⋯ button on Escape (measured on
  Guests and Maintenance).

**Not changed, reported:** Add unit finds the room type through the tenant scope only, not the person's property allow-list
(#38), while every other unit write checks it (D-UNIT-STORE, DEC-k) — the same question as DEC-i and DEC-j. The SINGLE
Pause/Resume (shared with the owner portal's pause) is still not in a transaction: if its recompute failed, the unit would
stay flipped with no audit row (D-UNIT-SINGLE-TXN — read, not seen happen). The per-unit price form keeps its own styling
(it is shared with Rates).

**Divergence:** there is still no prototype for this screen; `docs/design/DIVERGENCE-REGISTER.md` records the rebuild.

**Proof.** `UnitsListRedesignTest` (18), written to fail first where it could (the review's bulk test and the setup-line
check were both RED before their fixes); the x-show guard now holds the Units page at zero (ceiling 39 → 35, 🔬 scanned:
exactly 35 left); the route-gating census gained the two new write/export routes; the contrast guard reads both new panels.
Mutation set `units-list` (31): 31 landed and caught, 0 not caught, 0 did not land — including a recompute moved back into
the loop, the transaction removed, and the permission line shown on a pause. ⚠️ **The first full MySQL run was 4,105/4,107:**
`MutationSetsStillLandTest` errored twice because the new set's top-level `$rows` (a file path) overwrote the `$rows` of
the function loading it — a required file runs in its caller's scope. The harness and the suite now load each set through
one shared `loadMutationSet()` (its own scope; a probe test proves a set's variables cannot reach the loader, and the
guard stays green with the old name put back); the set's variable is renamed as well.
🖥 Walked in a browser on tenant three (desktop 1440, phone 390): added a room type from a sorted view and came back to it;
added a unit from its card (type chosen, sleeps suggested); a duplicate code refused with the sentence and the dialog reopened
with the typed values; edited a name; paused one (the Paused tag and chip), bulk-paused two and bulk-resumed four ("Resumed
3 units · 1 already taking bookings"); set arrival info (the stored code never appears in the page; Reveal showed it, as
before); opened Price individually centred; followed See its work orders; exported the CSV (text/csv, the table's columns,
no secret). At 390 px: no sideways page scroll, the dialog fits, the tiles two by two. 0 console errors or warnings.

## 2026-09-30 — DEC-k ruled: Add unit finds the room type inside the person's properties, like every other unit write

**Asked:** after the Units report named DEC-k — "Adding a unit doesn't check which properties the person is allowed to
access, while every other unit action does" — he answered: "Fix this issue too". Ruled; D-UNIT-STORE closed.

**What was wrong.** `InventoryActionController::storeUnit()` looked the room type up through the tenant scope only
(`RoomType::query()->findOrFail(...)`). The organisation boundary held, but inside it, staff limited to some properties
(the `property_user` allow-list, #38) could add a unit to another property's room type by posting its id — 🔬 the new test
got a **302 and a created unit** where a 404 was due. The Units page never offered that room type, and every other unit
write (Edit, Pause / Resume, bulk Pause / Resume, Arrival info and its reveal) already resolved inside the person's
properties.

**The fix.** An `accessibleRoomType()` beside `accessibleUnit()`, with the same rule — `PropertyContext::readIds()`: every
property the person may access when "All properties" is selected, otherwise the one they are working in (the same set the
Units page reads, so the dialog offers exactly what the write accepts). Another property's room type is **not found** — a
404, not merely hidden — and nothing is created; the room type's own property still decides where the unit goes.

**Proof.** A new test in `UnitsListRedesignTest` pins it three ways: a manager limited to property A is refused B's room
type (404, no unit); the same manager still adds to A; a manager allowed everywhere, with "All properties" selected, still
adds to B — so the rule narrows to the person's properties and locks no one out of their own. Mutation set `units-list`
now 33: UL-M32 (the helper loses its narrowing) and UL-M33 (Add unit goes back to the plain lookup) both caught.

**Not changed:** DEC-i (Edit on the Portfolio) and DEC-j (creating and working maintenance orders) — the same question on
other screens — stay his to rule; they were not in the ruling. **Found beside it, reported, not changed:** the same controller's
three rate-plan writes on the Rates page — add, edit, on/off sale (`storeRatePlan`, `updateRatePlan`, `setRatePlanActive`,
`can:rates.manage`) — find their room type or rate plan through the tenant scope only (D-RATE-PLAN-SCOPE, DEC-l; read, not
probed). They are rate writes, outside a ruling about Add unit.

## 2026-09-30 — Photos: the public disk answers at /media, so an uploaded photo shows (KNOWN-LIMITS L12p's `/storage` 404, worked around)

**Asked:** "https://vyrobel.com/app/units — on this page, when I add photo, the preview is not available. Fix it. … verify
it if it's fixed. If it's fixed, okay. If it's not fixed, then please fix it, ship it live and make sure that everything is
working fine."

**Verified first — it was not fixed.** 🔬 On production five room photos sat on disk (`storage/app/public/room-photos/…`),
and each one's address, `https://vyrobel.com/storage/room-photos/…`, answered **404** from outside (cache-busted, so the
origin and not the CDN's copy). The cause was already on record as KNOWN-LIMITS **L12p**: the document root IS the
application root, so `public_html/storage` is the real storage folder — logs and the maintenance bypass secret — and the
server's `.htaccess` refuses every `/storage…` path (`RedirectMatch 404`) before its rewrite runs. Laravel's public disk
used exactly that address, so every uploaded image failed — room photos, and equally logos, avatars, housekeeping,
maintenance and unit-request photos. L12p said it would "fail SILENTLY"; it did.

**The fix — on the app side; the server rule is not touched.** The public disk's address is now **`/media`**
(`config/filesystems.php`), which no server rule refuses, served by `PublicMediaController`:
- registered in `bootstrap/app.php` **outside the `web` middleware group** — an image never starts a session (a database
  write on production) or sets a cookie;
- **images only**: the extension must be jpg/jpeg/png/webp/gif AND the file's own bytes must say so (`finfo`) — a document,
  a hidden file, a folder (never a listing) or anything else is a 404;
- **only the directories the app writes photos, logos and avatars into** (`SERVED_DIRECTORIES`); the path pattern admits
  no dot segment, so nothing can climb out of a listed directory or the disk;
- `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400` — a day in the viewer's browser, never at the CDN: nothing PHP answers is
  publicly cacheable here (`HtmlIsNeverPubliclyCacheableTest`, L12k/L12m — a `public` first draft of this header went red
  on the full suite, and edge-caching images is a deployment decision, not this fix's) — and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
Every surface that shows these images is fixed by the one address change — the Units cards, the booking storefront, brand
logos, avatars, housekeeping and maintenance photos, owners' unit-request photos.

**Deliberately not served: owner message attachments** (images, PDFs, Office files, CSV, text). They are documents in a
private owner–operator conversation on the same public disk; they 404 on production today and still do. Whether they may be
public by address like the photos, or should go through a signed-in route that checks the viewer is in that conversation, is
his decision (`OPEN.md` D-MEDIA-ATTACH, DEC-m).

**Proof.** `PublicMediaTest` (3), RED first (the photo's address was `/storage/…` and `/media` served nothing): an uploaded
room photo gets a `/media` address that serves its exact bytes as `image/jpeg`, with no cookie, and the Units page shows
that address; refusals — a text file, a text file named `.jpg`, a real image in `message-attachments`, a hidden file, two
folders, four climbs out of a directory or the disk (plain and `%2e%2e`), a missing file; and a guard that reads `app/` for
every upload directory and fails if one is on neither list — a new photo feature can no longer 404 silently. `RoomPhotosTest`'s
address expectation moved from `/storage/photos/` to `/media/photos/` (the behaviour changed; the check did not weaken).
Mutation set `public-media` (6): back to `/storage`, any directory served, the disk's extension-based type check, dot
segments let through, the route inside the `web` group, an upload directory unaccounted for — all 6 caught. 🖥 Walked
locally on tenant three: a photo added on Units showed at once as the card's cover and its thumbnail (800×520 decoded;
its address 200 `image/jpeg`, no `Set-Cookie`), the booking storefront showed it, 0 console errors or warnings.

**Gates (each read from its own output, 2026-09-30):** the first full run **4,111/4,112 on MySQL 8.4.10** (tree `2ed2651b86f1c993`, 19:37–19:52 Baku — the `HtmlIsNeverPubliclyCacheableTest` refusal above, answered with `private`) · **4,112/4,112 on MySQL 8.4.10** (30,122 assertions, tree `41f113a1016595f1`: this code with the entry and the memory written, before these figures were filled in; 19:53–20:08 Baku) · **4,112/4,112 on MariaDB 11.8.9** (the same tree, 20:24–20:39 Baku; advisor-platform's dev server still stopped, checked at 20:24) · mutations **432/432 across every set** (`public-media` 6/6; baseline 227/227 green; 20:09–20:24 Baku) · money gate FULL unmoved (`929 / 10928000 / 0 / 42 / 16 / 0` · digest `a0e1e01d92d608f6 / cc588f6bb9562863 / 2f5598c92aadf105 / 9bac428a1b859297`, tenant one, local, reseeded 20:39–20:40 and read at 20:40 Baku) · PHPStan 0 · Pint clean.

## 2026-09-30 — DEC-m ruled: owner message attachments open only for the people in that conversation, signed in — and the inbox shows them

**Asked:** after the photos report named DEC-m — owner message attachments "don't open on the live site … they're private
owner–operator documents … my recommendation is to let only people in that conversation open them, after signing in" — he
answered: "Fix this issue as well". Ruled; D-MEDIA-ATTACH closed.

**What was wrong.** 🔬 `OwnerMessageActionController` stored each attachment on the PUBLIC disk and the owner's conversation
linked to its public address — which production refuses (`/storage`, KNOWN-LIMITS L12p), so no attachment ever opened; and
which, had it worked, anyone holding a link could have opened. 🔬 The operator inbox — the side the owner sends them TO —
never showed attachments at all: its transcript rows had no files.

**The fix.**
- **Stored on the PRIVATE disk** (`MessageAttachments::DISK = 'local'`); older rows keep the disk they record, and are served
  the same way. Production held no attachments, so nothing needed moving.
- **Opened only through two signed-in routes behind one controller** (`MessageAttachmentController`):
  `owner.messages.attachment` in the owner portal — the portal's own gates, then the **owner scope on the thread**: that owner
  and the team they added, exactly who can read the conversation — and `app.inbox.attachment` in the back office — the inbox's
  own permission `can:guests.view`, then the organisation's threads. A thread outside the viewer's conversation is **not found**
  (404, never a 403 that would confirm the file exists); each realm's door refuses the other realm's people.
- **A photo shows in place; every other file downloads** under the name it was sent with (made safe for the header — `%`, path
  separators, control characters); the choice is made by the file's own bytes (`finfo`), never its name. `Cache-Control:
  private, no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
- **One definition of an attachment row** (`MessageAttachments::rows()`), used by the owner's conversation and the operator
  inbox, each linking to its own route; the inbox now shows each file under its message — a photo thumbnail or a file chip
  with name and size.

**Proof.** `MessageAttachmentAccessTest` (4), RED first (the file landed on `public`; neither route existed): stored privately
and never publicly; the owner opens both files through the signed-in link (photo inline `image/png`; the PDF a download, its
real bytes, under its own name with a `%` in it); a teammate of that owner opens it; another owner of the organisation, an
owner of another organisation and a signed-out visitor do not; inbox staff see and open both; a role without the inbox is
refused; staff of another organisation get a 404; each realm's door refuses the other realm; another file's id through the
door is not found. `OwnerMessagesRichTest` now expects the private disk (the behaviour changed by his ruling; the check did not
weaken). Mutation set `message-attachments` (7): back to the public disk, the conversation check removed, the inbox permission
removed, every file inline, the links back to the disk address, a browser-cacheable document, the inbox not showing them — all
7 caught (the `collection` / `mediable_type` filters are left out as equivalent mutants, and the set says why). 🖥 Walked
locally on tenant three with a test owner: the owner sent a PDF and a photo — the photo showed at 800×520 in the owner's
conversation and in the inbox, the PDF downloaded as "Plumber invoice.pdf" on both sides, staff at the owner door were bounced
to their dashboard; 0 console errors or warnings.

**Gates (each read from its own output, 2026-09-30):** **4,116/4,116 on MySQL 8.4.10** (30,178 assertions, tree `ffb0b2200eb4da6d`: this code with the entry and the memory written, before these figures were filled in; 21:09–21:25 Baku) · **4,116/4,116 on MariaDB 11.8.9** (the same tree, 21:41–21:56 Baku; advisor-platform's dev server still stopped, checked at 21:41) · mutations **439/439 across every set** (`message-attachments` 7/7; baseline 230/230 green; 21:25–21:40 Baku) · money gate FULL unmoved (`929 / 10928000 / 0 / 42 / 16 / 0` · digest `a0e1e01d92d608f6 / cc588f6bb9562863 / 2f5598c92aadf105 / 9bac428a1b859297`, tenant one, local, reseeded 21:56 and read at 21:56 Baku) · PHPStan 0 · Pint clean.

## 2026-10-01 — Rates: the page rebuilt — every dialog centred, all fourteen nights, click or drag to edit, and every operation checked (the founder's request; plan approved, DEC-l included)

**Asked:** "https://vyrobel.com/app/rates — on this page table design must be better, texts must look good. And all texts and
boxes must be well aligned … the kind of work which you have done in the past three, four pages … every single operation
should be also working fine. So test every single thing on this page and fix all of them. After completion, ship them live
and verify it on MCP Playwright." A 9-part plan, with DEC-l (the property allow-list on the rate writes) inside it, was put to
him; he answered "Yes, all of it (Recommended)".

**What was wrong — measured before anything changed (🖥 1440×900, tenant three).** Every dialog opened in the top-left corner
(Bulk edit centred at 280,242: `x-show` erased the inline `display` that centred them). The grid was 1,320 px wide in a
1,148 px card and hid its last two nights. One row of controls mixed 34, 36 and 43 px boxes. The season and add-plan inputs had
no visible box, and "Add a rate plan" printed 16 px labels (`vy-label`, a class no rule defines). On a phone the figures went
2 + 1 and a plan row squeezed its buttons.

**What was wrong underneath — each proven by a test that failed first (`RatesPageFixesTest`).**
- Bulk edit and per-unit pricing were headed with the whole fortnight but posted the editor's dates, which started as ONE
  night: "raise 10%" over what looked like two weeks changed one night.
- A paused workspace — which the shell says is read-only — could still save and APPLY a season, and applying writes prices.
- Switching Refundable off still made a refundable plan (`$data['is_refundable'] ?? true`: an unticked box sends nothing).
- "All room types" meant every room type in the organisation: a bulk change made while looking at one property repriced the
  others.
- A 100% decrease was accepted and wrote €0 nights; bulk edit's `max(0, …)` could price a night at zero.
- A maximum stay, closed-to-arrival or closed-to-departure could not be set on its own (the "choose at least one thing" check
  ignored them), though the booking guard enforces all three.
- The grid shaded Saturday and Sunday; every price rule on the page (bulk "weekends", the weekend uplift, a season's "Fri/Sat
  nights") means Friday and Saturday nights.
- Every write jumped to the edited date and dropped the room-type filter; refusals arrived as plain notices, not alerts;
  "Jump to rates" searched every plan in the organisation; "Pacing · next 14 days" counted the window on screen, not the next
  14 days; the derived-plan note was a fixed "Non-refundable −10% and Weekly −15%" whatever plans existed.
- Pricing units individually and creating a rate plan left no audit trail; the paused sentence on the rate-plan writes said
  "adding inventory … until ." (no date on record printed nothing).
- The refusal to edit an applied season was set as an error nobody rendered; only a season's price error was ever shown.

**DEC-l — ruled and fixed.** Every rate write finds its room type, plan or season inside the person's properties through ONE
rule, `App\Support\Rates\RateScope` (the `PropertyContext::readIds()` rule the unit writes use since DEC-k): the grid editor,
bulk edit, per-unit preview and apply, the four season writes and the three rate-plan writes. Another property's id is a 404,
and "All room types" is the room types on screen.

**Found in the browser walk, and fixed.** A second rate plan could be added but never priced: the grid prices each room type's
MAIN plan (STRUCT-1), yet the success message sent the operator to the grid. The storefront skips a plan with an unpriced night
(`BookingEngineService::cheapestRatePlan`), so it sat unused. Now "Set rates" offers the plan where a room type has more than
one base plan (server-checked: a base plan of the ONE room type chosen, never a derived plan, never across "All room types";
stay rules stay room-type-wide), every plan row shows what it charges this fortnight ("Priced on 4 of 14 nights this fortnight ·
€99.00") and a Set prices button, and the message says so. Also: a long price ("€1,250.00", 68 px) ran into the next night —
it now steps down a size (`RatesGrid::rateFit`); the tall editor's buttons fell below the fold — the dialog footers now stay in
view; on a phone the shared 11 px input padding clipped select text; "Priced 2 units individually across 6 nights" counted rows
(now nights); "Updated rate + minimum stay" (now a sentence); the preview printed raw ISO dates; and after a drag across
nights the next single click on a night did nothing — a drag that ends on another night sends its click to the row, so the
"ignore this click" flag stayed set (now cleared once the drag's own events are done; 🖥 re-walked: drag, then click, opens
that night).

**The page.** One Alpine scope for the page (`vyRates`), the season dialogs in their own declared scope (F-20's shape), and
every dialog on the shared centred backdrop — the nine inline displays on this page are gone (`XShowInlineDisplayContractTest`
ceiling 35 → 26, the rates view and the unit price form added to its fixed list). A toolbar of 40 px controls; four figures,
the fourth "Next 14 days" from today. The grid: all fourteen nights at 1440, a sticky first column and header, today marked,
Friday and Saturday nights shaded, and one cell design — the price, what is left, a thin booked bar, and every rule the booking
guard enforces (Min · Max · No arr. · No dep.) — whose four states the legend names with the cells' own classes. Click a night,
or drag across nights, to open "Set rates & availability" (nightly price, minimum and maximum stay, open or closed, arrivals,
departures, derived plans) with a live summary. Bulk edit has its own dates (the window by default), change tiles, Every night /
Fri–Sat / Sun–Thu, and a live sentence of what it will do. The per-unit form (shared with the Units page) always shows its dates.
Seasons: a styled form whose every refusal is shown in plain words, a status chip per season, and Edit only on a draft; the
two-step and R-SEASON are unchanged. Rate plans: On sale / Off sale chips, Set prices, Rename and Take off sale as real buttons,
and an Add rate plan dialog with a working Refundable switch.

behaviour, none weakened: `OperatorRatesTest`, `OperatorRatesGate1Test` and `BulkUnitRateOverrideTest` now expect a refusal as

## 2026-10-01 — Owners: the page rebuilt — Add owner as a centred dialog with the password on its own row, a list like Guests and Units, invites resent and cancelled, and a unit's owner never changed by an invite (the founder's request; plan posted and executed)

**Asked:** "https://vyrobel.com/app/owners — on Add owner page, modal design and buttons are mess, cancel and send invite
buttons look bad, confirm with your password and its box is not well aligned. Fix all of these problems, these are the few
issue, also modify the entire design of this page like previous page and make it more creative and operational and easy to use
and fully functional the same way we worked on last 4 pages. build a plan for this page and execute it." A 7-part plan was
posted and executed as he asked, without a further question.

**What was wrong in the dialog — read in the old source.** One flex row held Cancel, the "Confirm with your password" label, the
password box, its error and Send invite side by side, in a panel of its own (`vy-inv-*`) rather than the shared dialog. Now:
the shared centred dialog (`.vy-modal-backdrop` › `.vy-modal.vy-modal-card`, focus trapped, Escape closes), role tiles,
name and email side by side, the units as chips, the commission as one segmented choice, the password on its own full-width
row ("Confirm it's you") with what it is for under it, and Cancel and Send invite together in the foot at one height (🖥 42 px
each, same top, at 1440 and 390). A refusal reopens the dialog with what was typed and says it beside the field; the box at
the top carries only refusals with no field; focus lands where the person has to act.

**What was wrong underneath — each with a test that failed first (`OwnersPageFixesTest`).**
- ⚠️⚠️ **An invite could move a unit away from its owner.** The dialog offered units that already had an owner, and
  acceptance wrote the new owner over whoever owned the unit then — and a unit's owner decides who is paid for it. Now the
  invite refuses such a unit with a sentence naming it and its owner, acceptance only assigns units that still have no owner,
  and a resend drops a unit that gained an owner meanwhile (each layer has its own test).
- The units offered came from every property in the organisation; they are now inside the person's properties (the
  `readIds()` rule of DEC-k and DEC-l).
- The "Invite sent" screen said "You can resend it any time from the owner's row" and there was no resend anywhere. Invites now
  have **Resend** (a fresh link; asks for your password, as sending does) and **Cancel** (the link stops working; the owner
  record made for the invite and never activated leaves the list; an active one is never removed). A founder's set-password
  link (ADMIN 04) is not this page's to touch: a 404 here, and the service refuses it too.
- An invite made a way into the organisation and recorded nothing. `owner_invite.sent`, `.resent` and `.cancelled` are now on
  the trail — which invite, its role, unit count, rate and expiry, **never the address** (the PII rule for `audit_events`).
  `OwnerInvite` needed a morph alias to be recorded at all.
- A paused owner read **Ready** and was counted in "ready to pay". Statuses now follow what the payout run does: a held payout,
  missing tax details or a missing payout account → **On hold, with the reason**; lines the booking channel has not confirmed
  → **Needs review** (the KPI said "draft statements"; the statement is closed — the label now says what it is); a pause →
  **Payouts paused**, left out of Ready to pay with the figure saying so. The menu offers Pause or Resume from the preference
  itself (it read it off the pay status, which says "paused" only while money is due).
- The side panel said "Statements finalize 1st of the month" — nothing does; a statement closes when someone presses Close
  period — and "Payouts sent 3rd business day", true only while the automatic run is on. It now says each of those as it is.

**The page.** Four figures that agree with the rows (Owners · Ready to pay · On hold with its amount · Needs review); the shared
list (search, chips that count what clicking them shows, sortable columns, pages, a row menu: Open owner · Copy email · Pause or
Resume payouts · Send the invite again); **Invites waiting** with Resend and Cancel; a CSV of the owners in view (formula-safe,
recorded, `reports.view`) whose link takes the view's address when clicked (it sits outside the regions the list swaps in place);
the rail: the payout run's money (its link only for `payouts.manage`), how owners are paid, the owner portal's adoption. Every
write comes back to the list as it was. At 390 px the row menu stays pinned at the right edge while the table scrolls.

**Found by reading, NOT fixed here — outside this page and on a money path, so his call (`docs/memory/OPEN.md`):**
- ⚠️⚠️ **D-PAYRUN-TENANT.** "Run payouts now" (`PayoutRunActionController::runNow` → `PayoutRunService::run()` with no owner
  list) selects owners with payable work in **every** organisation, under super-admin. 🔬 Verified in the test database with a
  throwaway probe (deleted after): an operator in organisation A pressing it created **and paid** a payout for organisation
  B's owner ("2 created · 2 paid"). It runs only while `PAYOUT_ENGINE_ENABLED` is on.
- **D-PAUSE-MANUAL.** Only the automatic run reads a pause (`dueOwnerIds`); the payout run page lists a paused owner as ready
  and creates their payout by hand. The Owners page says exactly that in the pause dialog; the owner detail page's "Amounts
  accumulate and carry forward until resumed." is unchanged.
- **D-UNITS-EXPORT.** The Units page's Export link has the same stale-address shape fixed here.

**Tests.** `OwnersPageFixesTest` (17) and `OwnersPageRedesignTest` (9), new. Moved with the behaviour, never to make a check
pass: `OperatorOwnersPayableStateTest`'s three "1 draft" label checks now read the new label with the same counts (one was a

## 2026-10-02 — Payouts: "Run payouts now" stays inside its organisation (A11), "Last run" shows only this organisation, and a pause stops every payout (DEC-n ruled); the Units export follows the view (A12)

**Asked:** "Lets work on next steps." The plan put to him — Part 1 A11 with the "Last run" leak and the "until ." wording,
Part 2 DEC-n, Part 3 A12 — was answered "Yes, all of it (Recommended)", and **DEC-n was ruled "Yes, a pause stops every
payout (Recommended)"**.

**A11 — fixed.** "Run payouts now" called `PayoutRunService::run()` with no owner list, and `run()` with none selects owners
with payable work in EVERY organisation, under super-admin (the daily automatic run's mode). 🔬 `PayoutRunScopeAndPauseTest`,
RED first: organisation A's click created and paid organisation B's owner. Now the button names its own organisation's owners
(the engine's selection read through the tenant scope), starts no run when there are none and says so, and the engine's
every-organisation mode stays for the daily run (its tests call it so on purpose). **Found while fixing it, and fixed:** the
manual run key was `manual:<timestamp>`, unique across the platform, and a run whose key exists is handed back as it is — two
organisations' runs in the same instant would have been ONE run, the second doing nothing and reporting the first one's
figures (🔬 under the suite's frozen clock). The key now carries the organisation.

**The "Last run" leak — found by reading, fixed.** Run rows carry no organisation, and the payout run page showed the newest
one — another organisation's created/paid/held counts (🔬 RED first: A's page read B's "2 created"). It now reads only what
this organisation's own payouts record: the newest payout a run created here, and the payouts that run created here ("Last
run here"); the platform-level run status is no longer shown on a tenant page.

**DEC-n — ruled and built: a pause stops every payout.** One definition (`OwnerPayoutPreference::isPaused()`), one refusal
(`PayoutsPausedException`) in `OwnerPayoutService`: `createFromStatement()` (after the idempotent return, before anything is
written or carried forward), `pay()` (inside the row lock, before the rail, beside the tax hold — the row is left exactly as it
was) and `retry()`. The engine never selects a paused owner (`PayoutRunService::owners()`, named or not) — two layers, each
mutation-proven on its own. The payout run page lists a paused owner's statements under **Payouts paused** with the way to
resume; a paused owner's waiting payout shows "Paused" instead of Mark paid; Create payouts, Mark paid and Run payouts now skip
them and say how many **owners** (the walk caught the first version counting statements: "2 paused" for one owner). The
owner portal's retry says "Your payouts are paused in your payout preferences — resume them, then try again." instead of "no
longer in a failed state". The words: the Owners page's pause dialog, its row reason and notice, and the owner page ("No payout
is created or sent until resumed — closed statements stay owed.", replacing "Amounts accumulate and carry forward until
resumed."). The owner portal's own pause already said "pausing stops your payouts entirely" — now true; unchanged.

**Also fixed:** the payout run's read-only refusal ended "…read-only until ." for a cancelled workspace (no resume date).
**A12 — fixed:** the Units Export link takes the view's address at the click, as on Owners.

**Not changed, noted:** the payout run offers "Run payout (test mode)" while `PAYOUT_ENGINE_ENABLED` is off, a button that can
only refuse (it says why) — pre-existing, the same on production (D-PAYRUN-BUTTON).

**The independent review** (read-only, the whole diff) found the cross-organisation paths, the money paths (the pause check
sits inside the payout lock without touching the double-transfer guard), the skip counts and the Blade clean — and **one real
gap, fixed:** the owner portal's "Retry payout" button is decided by `PayoutRecovery::isRetryable()`, the ONE rule read by the
button and the write alike, and it did not know about pauses — so a paused owner was offered a button the service then refused
(🔬 RED first). The rule now includes the pause, and the banner says "Your payouts are paused in your payout preferences below —
resume them to try this payout again." Its one sub-threshold note is recorded, not changed: "Last run here" takes its time from
the newest run that CREATED a payout here, so a later run that only paid older payouts does not move that time (no tenant or
money effect).

**Tests.** `PayoutRunScopeAndPauseTest` (11, new), `OwnerPayoutRetryTest` +2, `UnitsListRedesignTest` +1 — each RED first
except two added after the code to give each layer its own test, both proven by the mutation set. One existing mutation
(UL-M28) re-anchored to the moved Units link; no test was loosened. Mutations `payout-run-scope` 26/26. ⚠️ **The full
run of every set caught a weakening this pass caused elsewhere:** OW-M32 (the Owners side panel claiming automatic payouts)
survived, because the new pause-dialog sentence "…paid again from the payout run…" contained the words the panel's test
searched the whole page for. The test now reads the panel only (and asserts both what it says and what it must not); OW-M32 is
caught again.

## 2026-10-03 — The owners module: the owner's page rebuilt, four faults behind its dialogs fixed, the payout run asks first, unit requests reviewed in dialogs

**Asked:** "https://vyrobel.com/app/owners — on Add owner page, modal design and buttons are mess, cancel and send invite
buttons look bad, confirm with your password and its box is not well aligned. Fix all of these problems … all the sort of work
you have done in the previous pages … in this module … make a proper plan … maybe there are some creativity enhancement
advancement you can do … make sure everything works very well … test everything with MCP playwright … ship everything live."
The Add owner dialog was rebuilt on 2026-10-01 and measured unchanged (V, a screenshot this pass); what he described — the
password box under a shouted label with no border, Keep and Remove at two sizes — is the **Remove owner** dialog on the owner's
page (`/app/owners/{owner}`), measured in the browser before any change. The 5-part plan was posted and executed.

**1 · The owner's page, rebuilt.** The owner and every action on them in one bar under their name (Change commission · Pause or
Resume payouts · Close a period · Remove owner — each only for the role its route accepts); the figures; net to owner,
statements, payouts, the agreement, units and rate proposals; and a rail with how they're paid (the commission now and any
change waiting to start, the pause, the schedule, the masked payout account), the owner portal (a waiting invite sent again or
cancelled from here — the Owners list's own writes, coming back to this page) and the team's notes. Seven dialogs, all the
shared centred one: Change the commission · Pause/Resume · Close a period (dates in words — "Closed up to 30 Sep 2026", and a
live "1 Oct – 31 Oct 2026 · 31 days" line) · **Remove owner — "Confirm it's you" with the password on its own full-width row,
Keep owner and Remove owner at one height (both 42 px, measured)** · Propose a rate change · Send the invite again · Cancel the
invite. 80 inline styles are gone — every display is a class.

**2 · Four faults found behind those dialogs, each verified RED first and fixed:**
- ⚠️⚠️ **The commission change decided against TODAY's agreement, not the one that governs its start day.** Two changes in one
  month left two open-ended owner-wide agreements starting on the same day, and the payout maths (`ManagementAgreement::
  resolveFor()`) takes whichever row the database returns first; setting the rate back to today's wrote nothing, so the waiting
  change still came into force. Now ONE rule, `App\Support\Owner\CommissionChange`, read by the page and run by the write: a
  change starts on the first of next month (today, for an owner with no agreement in effect — see the review below); the latest
  change wins; one that would only have started that day is ended ("Replaced before it started", "Never applied" in the
  history); it never overlaps a change already planned for later (it ends the day before).
- ⚠️⚠️ **A commission change dropped the management fee.** The new agreement copied only the payout schedule and currency, so a
  fixed fee, the contract term and any attribution rules ended with the old agreement. Every term in
  `AgreementAmendmentService::TERM_KEYS` (made public — the list the amendments already use) now carries forward.
- ⚠️⚠️ **"Owner portal access" in Edit owner.** An unticked checkbox posts nothing, so the box could never switch access off; and
  the write set the linked login's status from the field, so a hand-made `portal_active=0` switched off ANY linked login —
  including someone who also works for the organisation, the case `OwnerLoginLifecycle` spares on removal — and `portal_active=1`
  opened an invited login nobody had set a password for. The field is no longer read; the checkbox is gone. **Whether access
  should be switchable here is his: DEC-o.**
- **Every refusal on the page closed its dialog and said nothing** (a wrong password or name in Remove owner, a period ending
  before it starts, a commission out of range, a proposal's dates the wrong way round). Each dialog now reopens with the reason
  beside its field and what was typed (`_form` names the dialog).

**3 · The payout run.** D-PAYRUN-BUTTON fixed: with `PAYOUT_ENGINE_ENABLED` off, "Run payouts now" is shown disabled with the
reason underneath ("The automatic payout engine is switched off …") instead of a button that could only be refused. Every write
on the page now asks first in the shared dialog — Create payout(s), Mark paid, Mark all paid, Run payouts now — saying what it
records and that Vyrobel moves no money ("Vyrobel records the payout and its statement as paid — it does not send money"); the
focus lands on Cancel, so an Enter pressed twice cannot record money. The forms still post without the script (the confirm sits
in front of the real form, and the double-submit guard still takes the confirmed post). 20 inline styles are gone.

**4 · Unit requests, rebuilt.** Chips that count what clicking them shows (Waiting · Approved · Declined · All — Withdrawn only
when there is one; the waiting ones first), each request a card with its photos and everything the owner filed, and Approve and
Decline in the shared dialog — saying what happens (the unit, the owner, that their proposed rate is not applied, whether they
will be told). ⚠️ **DEC-k applied to approving:** the unit is created only in a property the person works in
(`PropertyContext::readIds()`, the set the dialog offers) — 🔬 RED first, a manager limited to one property created a unit in
another by posting its id (302 and a unit); now a 404 and nothing is written. Applied as the rule he ruled for every unit write on
2026-09-30 and stated in the report so he can object. A8: the page's two x-show + inline-display forms are gone (26 → 24).

**5 · The Owners list.** When every unit already has an owner, Add owner says so in one line instead of a row of units that
cannot be picked. ⚠️ **A false sentence of mine (2026-10-01) corrected:** the unit picker's hint said "you can give units later
from the owner's page" — no screen does: a unit's owner is written only when an invite is accepted (or a requested unit is
approved) and cleared only when the owner is removed (V, every writer read). It now says "an owner is given existing units only
in their invite". **Whether an existing owner should be given units from their page is his: DEC-p** (it touches money —
attribution keys off a unit's owner).

**Asked of him (not decided here):** DEC-o (portal access switched from the owner's page — and if so, does their team go with
them, and does someone who also works here keep their login?) · DEC-p (giving an existing owner units later).

**The independent review** (read-only, the whole diff) found nothing critical or high; its medium findings, each checked in the
code and fixed or recorded:
- **Fixed — the rule ended only the newest agreement covering the start day**, so rows an older write had stacked stayed active
  beside the new one. Every active owner-wide agreement covering that day is now closed (a save also collapses an old stack —
  carrying the NEWEST row's other terms).
- **Fixed — an owner with no agreement in effect** (an invited one, say) got a change from the 1st only, and stays before then
  were worked out with no agreement — a zero for the owner, kept for good. A change for such an owner now starts **today**.
- **Fixed — the portal tests passed for the wrong reason:** posted without a commission, they were refused by validation before
  any write. They now send a valid commission; the mutation puts the old block back after validation, where it sat.
- **Fixed — "bookings already made keep their rate" was not always true:** earnings are worked out when a booking is made, later
  for one imported without them, and again when a booking moves to another owner's unit. The words now say "worked out".
- **Recorded, not changed — DEC-q:** rate proposals (propose, and accepting an owner's counter, which applies the rate) do not
  check the person's properties, while every other rate and unit write does (DEC-k, DEC-l) — a manager limited to one property
  can propose for another's room type. Pre-existing; his ruling, like DEC-i and DEC-j.
Also from the review, fixed: a lock so two saves at once cannot stack agreements; a fixed end date kept, not dropped; the
payout confirm can no longer fail open (unreadable text still asks); "waits until you mark it paid" says "or the next automatic
run" when the engine is on; the decline notice no longer claims the owner was notified; "is told in their portal" says
"unless they've turned these notices off"; a removed owner's unit request can only be declined (it created a unit owned by an
archived owner — pre-existing); the net-to-owner card's "incl. X% commission" names the rate of that statement's period, not
today's; two comments that overstated what works without JavaScript. Recorded, not changed: per-unit agreements are outside
the owner page's commission rule (nothing creates them today), and an amendment the owner acknowledges is written open-ended
without a "planned later" bound (`AgreementAmendmentService`, pre-existing). Three of the review's tests were written with
their fix rather than before it (the collapse, start-today and fixed-end cases); each is proven instead by a mutation that puts
the old behaviour back (OM-M42–M45).

**Tests.** `OwnerPageFixesTest` (19), `OwnerPageRedesignTest` (5), `PayoutRunPageTest` (6), `UnitRequestsPageTest` (9), +2 on
the Owners list; two needles in `OperatorControlGateTest` re-pointed to the new markup (the gate itself unchanged); the x-show
ceiling lowered 26 → 24. Mutations `owner-module` 48/48.

issues on this page and fix everything … ship everything live and then verify it via MCP playwright on the server."

**Why no booking could be made (🔬 read-only on production, 2026-10-04, his workspace "Vyrobel Internal — TEST TENANT").** Its
first property ("Internal Test Property") has **no rooms**; the other ("Villa Azure Lumière") has rooms with a rate plan and
**no price on any of the next 60 nights**. The wizard is a focused screen without the app's shell, so it has no property
switcher; under "All properties" it quietly used the first property and said "No units are free for those dates". On the
second property every room type showed "no rate set. Set a rate first →" — a link to the Rates page that threw the booking
away. No server error was logged: the page was not broken, it was a dead end. 🔬 Reproduced locally on tenant three (a second
property with no rooms, a room type with no price): the same two dead ends.

**1 · Which property.** Under "All properties" (a READ roll-up — a booking belongs to one property) the wizard asks "Which
property is this booking for?", each choice with its rooms ("5 rooms", "No rooms yet", "No rooms open for booking"), through
the app's own switcher (`app.property.switch`), saying the rest of the app follows. With more than one property the top bar
shows "Booking into [property]" as a picker. A property with no rooms — or none open for booking — gets one card that says so
and links to Units, instead of the whole wizard and "no units are free".

**2 · A missing price, set here.** For a person who holds `rates.manage`, a room type with no price for the stay shows "No
price for these nights yet" and a "Price a night" field: it posts **the Rates write itself** (`app.rates.update`, the same
rules, `RateScope`/DEC-l, the read-only guard) for exactly the stay's nights on the room type's main plan, and comes back to
the wizard on the same dates — "Price set — €140.00 a night for these 3 nights. Pick a unit to continue." (`return=new-reservation`
is a fixed token; the way back is built from two checked dates, never a URL). Anyone else is told "No price is set for these
nights … ask someone who manages rates". A room type with no rate plan says so (with a link to Rates for those who can).

**3 · A refusal keeps the booking.** Every refusal of the booking write now returns everything entered (unit, plan, party,
guest name, extras, arrival, rules, source, note, payment) and reopens at the step to fix (dates and units → 1, guest → 2,
payment and restrictions → 7). ⚠️⚠️ **Never a new guest's email or phone (#28):** they are neither flashed nor rendered; the
page says they were not kept and asks for them again, and Confirm says so once more if they are still empty. The restriction
override now appears over the WHOLE booking (it used to appear over an empty wizard, so choosing a reason resubmitted no unit
and no guest), with each rule in words ("Arriving Tue 20 Oct, a stay must be at least 5 nights" — not `min_stay on 2026-10-20`)
and a banner in words. Each value restored is re-checked against what the page offers now (a unit no longer free, another
property's unit, an extra that is not this property's: dropped).

**4 · Steps that check themselves.** Picking check-out loads what's free straight away (no "Check availability" button). Next
— and the stepper — refuse to pass an unfinished step and say what is missing beside it ("Pick a unit for these dates to
continue.", "Enter the guest's first or last name.", "That email address doesn't look right …" by the server's own test,
"Use a dot for cents …", "Say why in the note …"). Enter in a field moves to the next step; it never books.

**5 · The money as the folio charges it.** The unit's price came out of the DISPLAYED text (`preg_replace('/[^0-9]/', …)`) and
was printed with a hardcoded "€"; every figure is now the server's minor units, in the stay's own currency, through
`MoneyFormatter`'s symbol. A unit's own price (D18-5's per-unit override, which the write charges) is shown on its card ("Own
price · €350.00") and used by the estimate. The estimate now uses **the folio's taxes and fees** (`StayEstimator::taxApplies` /
`feeApplies`, per the stay's currency): it used to add an included VAT a second time and leave out the cleaning fee. A deposit
or "Full amount" follows the total while nobody has typed over it (it kept the figure of the moment it was chosen).

**6 · Design.** The room types as cards ("€123.00 a night · €369.00 for 3 nights"), units as keyboard-pickable cards (a real
radio, `vy-sr-only`, with a focus ring — it was `display:none`) showing "Sleeps 2"; a summary with dates, party, unit and guest;
a review step with "Change" on every line; returning guests with their stays ("1 stay · guest since 2026" / "No stays yet" —
two "Lena Walk"s were identical rows); sentence-case labels; one card per state; phone layout (one month per block, its own
label, units two across, full-width Next). Every inline style is gone (the two `x-show` + inline display sites with them: A8
24 → 22); the page's CSS moved into the layout as its own `vy-nr-` block, and the dead `vyn-` rules it used went (only
`.vyn-grid3`, used by Settings and Notification preferences, stays). The draft: this tab only (sessionStorage), never a guest
name, never payment, credit or the rules answer; across a date change only the party size; the rest only for the same stay,
with "Picked up where you left off".

## 2026-10-04 — Calendar: the New reservation dialog rebuilt — each name with its own box, the guest's name kept out of the address, rooms with no price said, and an empty night that starts a booking

**Asked:** "Now fix these issues "https://vyrobel.com/app/calendar?start=2026-09-28&days=14 — on `+New reservation~ page, the
design is messed, guest first name, last name, and their boxes are not well aligned." and also do additional works the way you
did for previous pages."

**Why the names and boxes did not line up (read from the code; the same view was live).** The guest row was one CSS grid of
three columns (`1fr 1fr 116px`) holding five pieces: the "First name" label, its box, the "Last name" label, its box and the
adults stepper. So the first line read "First name · [box] · Last name" and the second "[box] · stepper": the "Last name" label
sat at the end of one line and its box at the start of the next, under "First name". The dates had no labels at all. How it
came about: the wireframe (`docs/design/raw/Operator Calendar.html`) has ONE box, "Name or existing guest", beside the adults;
the build split it into two names and gave each a label, inside a grid sized for three pieces.

**1 · Each name with its own box.** The Owners dialogs' structure: First name and Last name side by side, each label directly
above its box, both boxes 42 px; Check-in, Check-out and Adults on the next line, each labelled; the adults count announced
when it changes. 🖥 Measured after: each label's left edge equals its box's (435/435 and 719/719 px at 1440).
**Correction to the plan:** it said the labels would no longer be all in capitals. They kept the app's small capital dialog
labels (`.vy-field-label`), as the Owners, Guests and Units dialogs show them, so the dialogs read alike.

**2 · The shared solid dialog.** The see-through glass panel (one of A9's five) is now the shared card: the Owners dialogs'
head (an icon, "New reservation", the property and what this dialog is for), the foot always in view, focus on First name,
the trap, and Escape or the backdrop closing it cleanly — Escape used to leave `new=1` in the address, so a reload reopened it.

**3 · ⚠️⚠️ The guest's name kept out of the address (#28).** "Check rack" is a GET and carried `gf`/`gl`: the guest's names went
into the browser's history and the server's access logs, which no erase reaches. They now stay in this browser tab
(sessionStorage) and travel only in the booking's POST; they come back only across the dialog's own "Check rack" (a `kept=1`
marker, never the name), only for the person who typed them, and any other way in starts empty and clears them.

**4 · Nothing it does not do.** It said "Matches an existing profile if the guest has stayed before" — every booking from here
creates a new guest — and that "the guest gets a confirmation email" — it asks for no email, so none is sent. Both are gone;
the fine print says what it does: books straight away as a new guest, no extras, payment or email, and a stay rule such as a
minimum stay sends you to the full form, with the booking kept.

**5 · No dead ends.** A room type with free units and no price for the dates was dropped without a word ("No units are free
(and priced)") — the dead end he hit on the full form this morning. Now it is listed: "No price for these nights yet", with
"Set a price in the full form" for someone who manages rates (the full form's price box) or "Ask someone who manages rates";
a room type with no rate plan says so, with the Rates page for those who can add one. A property with no rooms gets one card
and "Go to Units" — or, when it has rooms that are all paused or out of service, says that.

**6 · The money as the booking charges it.** The dialog showed the room type's price; a unit with its own price (D18-5) is
charged that price by the booking write, so the figure shown could differ from the figure charged. Each unit now shows its
own (one query for all of them). When the folio will add the property's taxes or fees (judged in the stay's currency, as the
write does), it says "Room only — the property's taxes and fees are added on the folio."

**7 · Dates.** Check-in defaulted to the calendar's first day — on his link, 28 September, six days back. It is now today in
the property's timezone, or the week's first day when that is later; the date boxes refuse earlier days. Check-out on or
before check-in, a past check-in and a stay over 90 nights are each named (each used to say nothing was free). A past
check-in is refused by the server too: Confirm posts its own form, which a box's `min` never checks. An impossible date such
as "2026-02-31" is dropped, not read as 3 March.

**8 · NEW — click an empty night to book it.** On a unit's row, a "+" on each night a booking could start (from the property's
today, not under one of its bookings or blocks, and only where the room type has a room to sell) opens the dialog for that
night with that unit picked. The bars stay clickable and draggable above it; the blocks keep their tooltips. Out of the tab
order and hidden from screen readers — the toolbar's New reservation is their way in. Only for someone who may book, never in
a paused workspace.

**9 · Smaller.** "Agent" is now "Travel agent", as the full form names it; the units are a radio group (one choice, said as
one); "today" on the calendar is the property's own day, so the marked column and the first bookable night agree; the drag
hint is one sentence (inside the old note "Drag a booking" sat in one column and the rest in another); the notice is a
`vy-flash`. The dialog has no inline style (the rack view 19 → 8: what remains is mostly the bars' grid positions), and the
41 dead `.vy-newres-*` rules are gone.

**Found on the walk, mine:** ⚠️⚠️ a comment inside the dialog's `x-data` said "Check rack" in double quotes. The first quote
ended the HTML attribute, Alpine received half an object, and every binding in the dialog failed — 38 console errors — while

## 2026-10-04 — New reservation, the second pass: a saved season applied from the booking, a way out of a property with no rooms, four steps, each night's price on the calendar, and only true sentences

**Asked:** "https://vyrobel.com/app/reservations/create — on this page there is functionality issues. it is not possible to do
reservation. Fix it … deeply analyze this page … build a proper plan … to make the design more cool, advanced, minimal and
operational … ship everything live. And test it on MCP Playwright." With a standing change of method: **no GitHub push per task —
work locally, ship live, push only at the very end when he says** (memory `feedback-ship-live-push-at-end`).

**Why no reservation could be made (🔬 read-only on production, 2026-10-04 15:14 UTC).** His workspace has never had a
reservation, and nothing was attempted today (0 reservations ever; today no guest created and no audit row; 0 errors logged on
3 and 4 Oct). Its
working property, "Internal Test Property", has no rooms; the page stopped there with only a small "Booking into" picker. Its
other property, "Villa Azure Lumière", has 3 units and **no price on any night, ever** — though on 28 Sep he SAVED a season,
"Winter", €200 a night from 28 Sep to 31 Oct on the Double room's plan, and it was **never applied** (`applied_at` NULL): a season
writes nothing until Apply, and the booking page said only "No price for these nights yet". (The plan named "350" on the other
room type reads like a price typed as a name; it has none.)

**The plan (posted; executed):**
1. **A way out of a property with no rooms** — the card lists the properties that can take a booking, each a one-click switch
   (the app's own `app.property.switch`).
2. **A saved season, applied from the booking** — a room type whose missing nights a saved, unapplied season would price says
   so ("Winter · €200.00 a night · 28 Sep → 31 Oct — saved but not applied yet") with **Apply Winter…**, which opens the Rates
   page's own **"Apply this season?"** disclosure (one shared partial, one builder `SeasonApplyFacts`, straight from
   `SeasonalRateService::preview()`): what it overwrites, that it cannot be undone, what somebody negotiated (R-RATE: it tells),
   what another season wins. Only "Apply and overwrite those nights" writes — the same `app.seasons.apply` (`rates.manage`, the
   property limit, the paused guard, R-SEASON's precedence order; untouched) — and it comes back to the booking on the same dates
   with the Rates page's own sentence of what was written and what the stay still lacks ("Winter applied — 30 nights rewritten
   across 2 units. Pick a unit to continue."). A season is offered only if it prices at least one night still without one.
3. **Seven steps became four** — Stay (dates, party, unit and its plan) · Guest (who, and the arrival time) · Extras (only where
   the property has some) · Confirm (the review, the house rules, source and note, the email, the payment and the wallet
   credit). Refusals reopen at the step holding what was refused (`NewReservation::STEP_*`; payment → Confirm, guest → Guest).
4. **The calendar carries each night** — the main rate of the cheapest room still free, "—" when none has a price, "Full" when
   nothing is left, today marked in the property's timezone — from the availability rows and each room type's main plan
   (`RoomType::primaryRatePlan()`), one read for a year (plain date range, no models; `Availability::left()` the one formula).
5. **Only true sentences** — house rules say "Not set" where the property set nothing (it said "Not permitted" for pets and smoking
   on a property with no policy, printed the stored codes "on_request"/"not_allowed" on one that had one, and "As per booking
   terms" over a real cancellation policy; now the Settings words via `PropertyPolicy::ruleLabel()` and the stay's own
   free-cancellation date via `CancellationPolicy`); no claim that the rules go out with the confirmation (they don't); the
   arrival sentence says how directions really reach the guest — and that email isn't being sent from Vyrobel yet, where it
   isn't (`MailSafetyGuard::isSending`; production's mailer is `log`), the pre-arrival email switched off, or a stay too soon for
   it (`ArrivalPack::LEAD_DAYS`); "Email the confirmation" cannot be ticked without an address; the done screen draws the self
   check-in code only for a guest who can sign in to use it (the guest portal is claimed by email).
6. **Smaller** — country as a list of every country by name (`Countries::everywhere()`, ICU names; the code is what is stored), the
   "price set" note only on the Stay step, the summary's "Paid now / Left to pay", a bar with the estimated total on a phone, the
   unit's plan chosen under the unit.

**Found on the walk:** none of my own beyond the review's — and one the suite caught: ⚠️ I made `steps()` a PUBLIC static on
the Livewire component, which `/livewire/update` could call (the boundary guard, `OperatorLivewireMutationBoundaryTest` — the
same slip the Guests pass recorded); it is private now; two tests of mine were wrong first (the shared
